caption: Numerous tiny, pale to off-white, cup-like fruiting bodies scattered across a dark, uneven surface. Some areas display fine, white, cottony mycelium. The fruiting bodies are small, round, and appear embedded or slightly raised, with a smooth to slightly textured surface.

Large, irregular cap with maroon and yellowish tones, showing bruising, cracking, and velvety texture. Thick, robust stem partly covered in soil, with visible yellowish to brownish hues and white mycelial patches at the base.

Numerous minute, black, rounded to slightly irregular dots scattered across a pale, dry, fibrous surface. The dots are slightly raised and irregularly dispersed, with no visible mat or additional structures at this magnification.

A thin, crust-like layer with a granular, finely textured surface. Color transitions from reddish-brown to lighter brown, forming a matte, continuous film without distinct fruiting bodies or visible margins.

Two mushrooms with slender, off-white stems and brown caps covered in small, whitish, scaly patches. The larger cap is expanded with an uplifted, irregular margin and visible white gills, while the smaller cap is convex and densely scaly.

Numerous upright, slender, greenish-gray stalks with fine, powdery surfaces, each topped by a smooth, pale cream cup. The stalks cluster densely, forming a bushy mat with muted green-gray and off-white tones.
No visible fungal structures are present. The image shows a dense clump of slender, upright green leaves with smooth surfaces and no apparent discoloration or pustules.

A small, solitary mushroom with a smooth, pale brownish to tan convex cap. The margin is even, and the slender, pale stem is mostly hidden by moss and vegetation. Gills are not visible from this angle.

Delicate mushroom with a thin, whitish stem and a smooth, conical to bell-shaped cap. The cap is pale grayish to off-white with subtle brownish tones and distinct radiating striations. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the cap.

Rough, cracked bark surface densely dotted with numerous tiny, black, rounded fruiting bodies partially embedded in the substrate. The black spheres are scattered individually, contrasting against the pale, lichenized bark with no visible pores or clustered formations.

A single mushroom with a robust, elongated white stem and a smooth, white cap with a slightly uplifted margin. The underside reveals closely spaced, white to off-white gills radiating from the stem to the cap edge.

White mushroom with a smooth, convex cap showing damage at the margin. The gills are white, closely spaced, and radiate regularly from a central, smooth white stipe. Overall appearance is crisp and uniform.

Two slender mushrooms with convex to conical brown caps showing pronounced radial striations. The caps are smooth and moist. Stems are long, thin, pale brownish, and fibrous with subtle longitudinal lines. Pale brown, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps.

Two small, white, ovoid to conical caps with faint pinkish-brown speckling and smooth surfaces. The caps are closed with even, unbroken margins, supported by slender, short white stems. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped and delicate.

A delicate mushroom with a slender, white, slightly fibrous stem and a small, conical to bell-shaped cap. The cap is pale brown to tan with pronounced radial striations, giving it a ribbed appearance. The margin is even and not flared.

Dense clusters of upright, slender, pale greenish-gray stalks with granular to irregularly rounded tips, some topped with small, clustered, pale structures. The surface is granular to slightly scaly, giving a frosted appearance, and the stalks emerge from a similarly colored basal mat.

A single mushroom with a slender, curved white stem and closely spaced, pale gills radiating from the center. The cap margin is striate, echoing the gill pattern beneath. Soil clings to the base of the stem.

A dense, whitish, fuzzy mat of fine, hair-like filaments spreads irregularly across a yellow-green surface, creating a powdery and slightly granular texture with radiating structures visible under magnification.

Reddish-brown, crust-like patch tightly adherent to the surface, with a granular to cracked texture and scattered pale grayish areoles. Margins are diffuse, blending gradually into the surrounding area. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible.

Tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered on decaying wood, yellowish to light brown, flat to slightly convex with smooth, moist-looking surfaces. Each apothecium is only a few millimeters wide, appearing sessile and loosely clustered.

Delicate mushroom with a smooth, pale beige to light tan conical cap featuring distinct radial striations. The cap is slightly translucent, and the slender, elongated stem is pale grayish and centrally attached.

Pale beige to light brown cap with a smooth, moist surface and faint radial striations near the grooved margin. Cap is conical to broadly convex with a small central bump. Underside shows widely spaced, white to pale cream gills and a slender, white, fibrous stipe.

Pale yellow to cream, tightly adherent crust with a rough, cracked, and granular surface. The margins are irregular and blend into the substrate, with numerous small fissures and a bumpy, continuous texture.
Tall, slender white stem supporting a conical, pale cap with a distinct brownish apex. The cap has fine radiating striations and translucent, uneven margins with minor splitting.

A small, fragile mushroom with a long, slender white stem and a smooth, convex light brown cap. The cap margin is even, and pale gills radiate from the stem underside. Some soil clings to the fibrous base.

Blackish, irregularly shaped, and slightly sunken fruiting bodies scattered across tan to brown wood. The stromata have a rough, granular surface with some powdery patches, blending gradually into the surrounding tissue.

Mushroom with a convex to slightly flattened, light brown cap featuring paler, irregular margins and a darker center. The dry, fibrillose surface leads to closely spaced brownish gills. The slender white stipe shows soil remnants at its base.

Small mushroom with a conical to convex cap, pale cream to light tan, darker at the center, and a distinctly striate margin. The cap surface is smooth and slightly silky. The slender, cylindrical stem is white to pale cream, with soil at the base.
Rough, cracked bark surface densely covered with green, leafy moss. No visible fungal fruiting bodies or crusts are apparent; the dominant features are bark fissures and moss growth.

Long, slender white stem with soil at the base. Light brown cap with frilly, irregular margin and prominent, crowded gills underneath. Cap surface appears fibrous or scaly. Upright, solitary structure.

Two mushrooms with tan, convex to flat caps showing fibrillose texture and marginal splitting. The gills are pale, closely spaced, and radiate from a centrally attached, white, fibrous stipe. One specimen is cut to reveal the internal structure.

Delicate mushrooms with slender white stems and pale grayish-brown, conical to bell-shaped caps showing fine radial striations. The upturned specimen reveals closely spaced, white, translucent gills attached to the stem. The overall appearance is fragile and dainty.
Upright, branched pale green structures with a granular surface, topped by irregular, contorted, flesh-colored to tan lobes. The base forms a crusty, granular mat spreading across the surface.

Convex to slightly flattened caps with vivid pinkish-red color and pale patches. Smooth, moist surface, even margin. White, closely spaced gills and a robust, cylindrical white stipe. Both mature and immature fruiting bodies are present.

A solitary mushroom with a conical, brown cap featuring prominent radial striations and pale streaks from margin to center. The cap margin is striate and slightly wavy. The slender, smooth stem is white to cream with a slightly bulbous base.

Cream-colored, closely spaced gills radiate from a central, pale fibrous stem. The gills are smooth, with minor discoloration and moisture spots. The cap margin is slightly undulate and pale with subtle brownish tinges. No veil or ring is visible.

Two mushrooms with long, slender white stems and brown, scaly caps. The larger cap is broadly convex to flat with uplifted edges and exposed white gills, while the smaller cap is rounded and closed. Stems are fibrous and slightly curved.

Dense clusters of brownish, granular tissue with numerous dark, sharply pointed, elongated spine-like structures projecting prominently, creating a striking contrast against the pale background. The overall texture is rough and irregular, with compact, amorphous masses.

Numerous small, elongated, pale tan to light brown pustules with smooth margins are scattered in irregular rows along the green stem. The pustules are slightly raised and have a powdery or granular texture, appearing oval to elliptical in shape.

Irregular, closely-adhering patch with a pale yellowish to off-white color. Surface is granular, warted, and rough, featuring visible fissures and an indistinct, blending margin. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible.

Pale gray to bluish-gray crust forming irregular, contiguous patches tightly adherent to the surface. Texture is granular to slightly areolate, with diffuse margins blending into the background and a matte appearance. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible.

Crustose thallus with a pale, off-white to yellowish granular surface, scattered with numerous small, black, rounded perithecia slightly raised above the uneven background. Some reddish-brown and yellowish tinges are visible among the rough texture.

Pale creamy to yellowish-white crust with a distinctly granular, rough surface. Irregular polygonal areoles are separated by shallow fissures, giving a cracked, uneven texture. No visible reproductive structures.

Crustose thallus with a rough, uneven surface in brown, gray, and white tones, interspersed with yellowish-green tinges. Scattered small, black, rounded structures dot the cracked, granular surface with irregular, patchy margins.

Convex to slightly depressed caps with vivid red surfaces, irregular white patches where the skin is missing, smooth texture, and some debris. White, closely spaced gills and stout white stems are visible.

Numerous small, black, circular to irregular spots scattered across a rough, light brown to grayish branch surface, some surrounded by faint reddish discoloration. The branch features prominent longitudinal ridges, two large sharp thorns, and a patch of exposed darker wood.

A dense layer of tiny, translucent to whitish, disc-shaped fruiting bodies tightly clustered on the surface, each with a smooth margin and slightly raised, gelatinous texture, creating a fine, beaded appearance.

Patchy greenish-yellow surface with a granular texture, scattered with numerous small, dark, rounded structures embedded across the uneven thallus. No distinct veins or ridges are visible, and the surface shows slight undulations.

Minute, translucent to pale yellowish, round to slightly oval fruiting bodies with smooth, entire margins. Surfaces appear moist, gelatinous, and reflective, with uniform coloration and no visible reproductive structures. The apothecia are loosely grouped and vary slightly in size.

Tightly adherent, irregular patches with a finely cracked, areolate surface. Colors range from pale gray to grayish-brown with subtle reddish-brown areas. The granular, slightly rough texture blends into the stone, and no prominent fruiting bodies are visible.

Pale greenish to off-white crust with a distinctly granular, cracked surface forming irregular, bumpy patches. The texture appears rough and uneven, with no clearly defined margins visible in this close-up view.

Dense cluster of small, round to oval, disk-like structures with brownish centers and distinct pale to white margins. The apothecia are tightly packed, overlapping, and form a textured, uneven patch with some granular or powdery areas.

A solitary mushroom with a conical to bell-shaped, pale beige cap featuring a slightly darker apex and smooth, striate margin. The dry cap surface is finely textured. The slender, straight stipe is pale tan and fibrous. Gills are not visible.

Two irregular, mature fruiting bodies with velvety reddish-brown caps, yellowish and pale damaged areas, and uneven, wavy margins. The cut surface shows pale yellow flesh with blue-green bruising. The thick stem is partly visible with soil attached.

Numerous tiny, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies, pale yellowish to whitish and some light brown, scattered irregularly on dark, rough wood. Surfaces are smooth, slightly translucent, and less than a millimeter in diameter, standing out against the fibrous background.

Small, upright, pale greenish to whitish stalks with shallow, cup-shaped tops. The cups have irregular, slightly scalloped edges and a granular surface. The structures are clustered and delicate, lacking any fuzzy or cottony texture.

Elongated, slightly raised, pale yellow-orange pustules embedded in the green plant surface, arranged mostly in single rows. The pustules have a smooth, waxy texture and lack visible spore masses or powdery deposits.

Delicate, white to off-white mushrooms with smooth, convex to nearly flat caps and striate margins. Gills are white, closely spaced, and attached to slender, smooth, white stems. Clustered fruiting bodies show fragile, translucent appearance.

Small, circular fruiting bodies with greenish-yellow coloration, each featuring a darker central disc and a finely textured, fuzzy margin. The surfaces appear minutely granular, and the apothecia are closely clustered together.

Numerous tiny, translucent to whitish, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth margins are scattered irregularly across a dark, rough, and uneven surface. The discs are slightly raised and vary in size, often appearing in loose clusters.

Pale yellow to off-white crust with a granular, cracked surface. The texture is rough and uneven, formed by tightly packed, small, rounded granules. No distinct margin or reproductive structures are visible in this close-up view.

Numerous tiny, translucent to whitish discs scattered across dark wood, some nearly spherical, others slightly lobed or flattened, with smooth, glistening surfaces and entire margins. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped but not densely packed, each only a few millimeters wide.

Crustose surface with a rough, cracked texture in pale grayish-brown, scattered with numerous small, black, rounded, slightly raised dots. The dots are irregularly distributed and embedded, giving a granular, uneven appearance.

Delicate mushrooms with slender, white stems and small, conical to bell-shaped caps that are pale grayish-brown and slightly translucent. The white gills are widely spaced and radiate from the stem. Caps are smooth with even margins.

A solitary mushroom with a conical, light brown cap featuring pronounced vertical striations. The cap appears smooth and slightly translucent at the margin. The slender, white stem is smooth with a faintly fibrous texture. No gills are visible from this angle.

Pale whitish to yellowish-green crust tightly adheres to the surface, displaying a rough, granular to areolate texture with numerous small, bumpy projections. Scattered dark, elongated structures are visible across the uneven, irregularly margined thallus.

Deep red cap with large, irregular white patches where the surface has peeled away. Cap margin is uneven and chipped. Gills are white, closely spaced, and attached to a thick, white stem. Texture appears smooth and brittle.

Numerous small, rounded fruiting bodies with dark central discs and pale to whitish, slightly raised margins are densely clustered, creating a granular, textured surface against a mottled greenish and yellowish background.

Two small mushrooms with convex, pale white caps featuring pronounced striate margins and smooth, moist surfaces. The crowded white gills are visible beneath, and the slender, straight stipes are pale and slightly fibrous. A brown slug rests atop the foremost cap.

Cylindrical wood surface densely speckled with numerous small, dark, rounded to irregular spots. The brown, textured background features a prominent circular indentation with a darker center, contrasting with the scattered dark fruiting bodies.
No visible fungal structures or fruiting bodies are present in this image; only a sunlit forest floor with dense green herbaceous plants and leaf litter is seen.

Slender mushrooms with elongated, white stems bearing brownish fibrils and soil at the base. Caps are conical to convex, smooth, brown to gray-brown with paler margins. Gills underneath are closely spaced. Arranged in a loose group.

Two small, black, spiky tufts with radiating, filamentous projections cluster on a whitish, fuzzy surface. The tufts are compact, with irregular margins and individual dark setae extending outward in various directions.

Delicate mushroom with a convex, pale brown cap featuring a darker center and striate, paler margins. The gills are white to pale cream and closely spaced. The slender, translucent white stem is slightly curved and fragile, measuring about 5.5–6 cm tall.

Cluster of mushrooms with smooth, dome-shaped to slightly convex dark brown caps, lighter at the margins. Surfaces appear shiny. Two upturned caps reveal closely spaced, pale brown gills. Stems are mostly hidden by caps and leaf litter. Caps overlap in a tight group.

Delicate mushroom with a pale gray to off-white, centrally depressed cap featuring pronounced striations and scattered brown dirt. The slender, curved stem is also pale and has soil clinging to its base. Gills are not visible in this view.

Two delicate mushrooms with long, slender white stems and bell-shaped, grayish-brown caps. The caps have a fibrous, striate texture and slightly inrolled margins. Pale to light brown gills are visible underneath. Soil clings to the base, highlighting their fragile appearance.

Slender mushrooms with elongated whitish stems and small, smooth, tan to light brown conical caps. Caps show faint striations near the margin and are slightly translucent. Gills are pale and closely spaced, visible beneath the cap. No ring is present on the stem.

White mushroom with a moderately robust, slightly curved stem and a smooth cap showing faint striations along the margin. The cap is gently undulating at the edges, with closely spaced white gills visible beneath. Some soil debris rests on the cap.

Slender green leaves display elongated, linear orange streaks running parallel to the veins. The orange streaks are fine, powdery, and granular, forming continuous lines along the leaf surfaces and creating a striking contrast with the green foliage.

Granular, pale green crustose mat with slender, upright stalks topped by small, rounded, pale brown to tan discs. The stalks and discs cluster in irregular groups, with a rough, slightly bumpy texture covering the wood surface.

Two mushrooms with long, slender, white stems and convex, pale beige to tan caps showing a slightly scaly texture. The gills underneath are crowded, off-white to pale cream, and the cap margins are even. No veil remnants or volva are visible.

Numerous tiny, circular, disc-shaped fruitbodies with a translucent, whitish to pale gray color and a smooth, slightly frosted surface. Some are attached to the substrate by fine, transparent threads, scattered across a dark background.

Underside of a delicate mushroom showing white, closely spaced gills that are adnate to slightly decurrent. The slender, pale stem is smooth, and the cap margin is even. The overall structure appears fragile and finely detailed.

Smooth, dark brown caps with a moist sheen, convex to slightly depressed. Gills are pale cream, closely spaced, and decurrent onto sturdy, pale brown cylindrical stipes. Both cap and gill surfaces are clearly visible among green moss.

A small mushroom with a smooth, pale tan conical to convex cap featuring a slightly darker center. The margin is even, and the slender, elongated stem is light brown and smooth. Gills are not visible from this angle.

Numerous minute, blackish, rounded to slightly irregular structures are scattered and slightly raised above a rough, cracked surface. The fruiting bodies blend subtly into the substrate, with no sharply defined margins. Scale indicates very small size, under 1 mm.

Two small, fragmented white pieces with thick, fibrous stipes and some attached soil. One fragment shows closely spaced white gill remnants. Surfaces are mostly white with slight brownish discoloration. No intact cap or margin is visible.

Numerous tiny, black, disc-like structures scattered irregularly across a fibrous, pale brown stem. The fruiting bodies are minute, rounded, slightly sunken, and smooth, appearing almost embedded in the plant surface.
A tiny, light to medium brown, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth to slightly textured surface sits atop a slender brown twig. The margin is even, and the fungus appears solitary.

Numerous minute, black, conical to subglobose fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across a pale, slightly textured surface. The fruiting bodies are small, dark, slightly raised, with rough, granular texture and pointed to rounded apices.

Tiny, yellow to yellow-brown cup-shaped bodies with smooth inner surfaces and finely granular or minutely hairy exteriors, closely grouped on wood. Margins are even, and the cups appear slightly translucent.

Mushrooms with convex, matte red caps showing cracked margins, robust white cylindrical stems, and off-white, closely spaced gills. Sectioned specimens reveal a solid, chalky white interior and fibrous, wrinkled stem texture.

Two slender mushrooms with smooth, light brown, conical to bell-shaped caps and long, thin, pale stems. One stands upright while the other lies on its side, exposing closely spaced, pale gills beneath the cap. The overall appearance is delicate and fragile.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, pale off-white to faintly greenish caps, some with surface debris. Stems are robust and white. One specimen shows closely spaced, white gills beneath the cap. Cap margins are smooth.

A resupinate, crust-like surface with a rough, granular texture and an indistinct margin. The coloration is brown to reddish-brown, featuring scattered, irregular depressions and holes across the patchy, continuous growth.

Two slender mushrooms with white stems and small, pale, ovoid to conical caps. The caps show faint longitudinal striations and smooth margins, appearing closed and slightly textured. Both fruiting bodies are closely grouped and emerging from dark soil.

White, rounded cap with a distinctly scalloped margin and smooth, matte surface. Some soil and organic debris adhere to the cap. The thick, white stem is partially visible beneath the cap. The overall appearance is robust with irregularities on the cap edge.

Small, blackish, roughly circular to irregular fruiting bodies with rough surfaces and central openings are scattered and slightly raised on pale, dry wood. Some areas show a whitish coating or residue around the fruiting bodies.

Numerous tiny, translucent to whitish disc-shaped structures scattered and clustered on dark wood. The discs are smooth, slightly raised, moist-looking, and sessile, lacking visible stalks. Arrangement is irregular, with denser clusters and some isolated individuals.
Small, black, rounded to irregular bumps scattered across a pale, hollow, cylindrical surface. The dark fruiting bodies are slightly raised and contrast with the granular, roughened background.

Numerous small, round to slightly oval, red to orange-reddish structures with smooth surfaces are clustered and scattered across a dark, rough, textured background. The fruiting bodies are uniform in size and vividly colored, standing out against the substrate.

Dark, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies densely covered with long, stiff, radiating hair-like setae, forming a tangled, bristly surface. The structures are closely grouped, sessile, and display a dark brown to nearly black coloration.
A single, circular sporocarp about 1 mm wide with a smooth, well-defined margin and a finely granular, metallic or silvery-brown surface, embedded in rough woody substrate.

A single, minute, roughly spherical fruiting body with a granular, powdery surface. Its color is grayish-brown to olive-brown, blending with surrounding particulate matter. The structure is solitary, lacks a visible stalk or margin, and appears embedded among debris.

Numerous slender, upright, stalked sporangia densely clustered, each elongated and cylindrical to ovoid. Sporangia range from dark brown to black, with smooth, glossy surfaces, supported by thin, hair-like stalks. Color varies from lighter brown to nearly black, forming a loose aggregation across the wood surface.
Numerous small, white, upright cylindrical or club-shaped structures with smooth surfaces and some slightly swollen tips, densely clustered and evenly spaced along a brown, fibrous substrate.

Delicate mushroom with a white, bell-shaped cap featuring a scalloped, lacy margin and finely granular surface. The long, slender stem is brownish to reddish, slightly curved, and fibrous, with white granular deposits and soil particles at the base.

White, convex cap with a slightly scaly texture and brownish streaks. The robust white stem shows a prominent reddish-brown stain along its length. Partial veil remnant is visible near the top of the stem. Gills are not visible in this view.

Clusters of tiny, ovoid to subglobose fruiting bodies on slender dark stalks, ranging in color from pale yellow to light brown and glossy reddish-brown, with a smooth, shiny surface and a three-dimensional, outward-projecting arrangement.

Dense clusters of small, brown, oval to cylindrical fruiting bodies stand upright on slender, dark stalks. The sporangia have a smooth to slightly textured surface and are closely packed, forming a cohesive patch on the decaying wood.

Convex to broadly flattened caps with undulating, inrolled margins; dry, velvety, light brown surface with a darker center. Densely packed, pale tan gills and a short, robust, soil-coated stipe, slightly paler than the cap.
Minute, globose fruiting body with a dark, roughened surface, surrounded by granular greenish and whitish material. The sporocarp appears solitary and embedded within a heterogeneous, crumbly matrix.
Numerous small, dark brown to black, slightly raised, oval to irregular spots scattered densely across a pale, woody stem. The spots are distinct and vary slightly in size and shape.

Dense, dark brown to nearly black, fuzzy tufts with a distinctly hairy, bristly surface. The globose to irregular structures have a cottony appearance, emerging in clusters from a striated, woody substrate.

White, dome-shaped cap with a smooth surface and shallow grooves. The elongated stem is white with a fibrous texture and shows a distinct pinkish-brown discoloration along its length. No gills or ring are visible.

Numerous small, black, roughly spherical to irregular structures densely scattered across a pale, granular background. The dark bodies appear matte to slightly rough, closely grouped, and vary in size, forming compact aggregations without visible stalks or caps.

White, smooth, convex to nearly flat caps with faint brownish tones. Stems are thick and white, some with soil at the base. Gills are closely spaced and pinkish, visible on overturned specimens. Cap margins are smooth.

White convex caps with scattered brownish scales, robust white stems with slightly bulbous bases, and free gills that are pinkish to reddish. Cut sections reveal white internal flesh and smooth cap margins. Texture appears dry.

Clustered, upright fruiting bodies with white, powdery stalks supporting dark, cylindrical to ovoid heads. The heads have a granular, delicate surface and display a striking iridescent sheen with blue and purple hues.

Dark, granular surface with irregular, patchy lighter areas. Fine, thread-like elements are scattered across the matted, uneven texture. No distinct fruiting bodies or prominent hair-like structures are visible.

Numerous tiny, upright, white cylindrical or club-shaped structures densely cover slender brown stems, creating a bristly, spiky appearance with a strong contrast between the white fruiting bodies and the brown substrate.

Numerous tiny, upright, spike-like structures with white bases and dark tops densely scattered across a moist, decaying green leaf and surrounding debris. The slender fruiting bodies create a striking contrast against the leaf’s surface.

Delicate, upright fruiting bodies with slender, dark, thread-like stalks topped by elongated, glossy, dark brown to nearly black, club-shaped sporangia. The structures are minute and closely grouped, with smooth, lustrous surfaces and slight variation in height and orientation.
A single, tiny, round fruiting body with a granular, roughened surface in grayish to dark brown tones, set against a textured background and surrounded by faint, thread-like filaments.

Cluster of minute, irregularly shaped fruiting bodies under 1 mm wide, grayish-brown with granular, encrusted surfaces and scattered white granules. Several display open, cup-like or urn-shaped forms with dark interiors and thin, uneven margins. Subtle greenish-yellow hints are visible in some areas.
Dense, dark purplish-brown powder coats the stamens and petals, forming a thick, granular, fuzzy layer over the pinkish-purple floral organs, giving them a dusty appearance.

Pale tan to light brown caps with smooth to slightly fibrillose surfaces. Gills are closely spaced, attached, and cream to light brown with wavy margins. Stipes are slender, pale, and faintly fibrillose.
Dense clusters of slender, upright stalks with pale, almost white bases and dark, rounded tips cover a decaying leaf, creating a bristly, textured surface with striking color contrast.

The flower’s center is overtaken by a dark, powdery, granular mass, replacing the usual reproductive parts. The surrounding petals remain pink and intact, while the infected area appears deep purplish-brown to black and dusty.

Dense, dark purplish-brown powdery masses coat the anthers and inner parts of the pink flower, forming irregular, granular deposits that follow the contours of the floral structures. Some petals show discoloration and deformation near the fungal growth.

Close-up of a green leaf surface with a prominent central vein, scattered fine hair-like trichomes, and smooth texture. Brownish areas are visible along the vein, but no distinct fungal structures or spots are apparent.

Small, black, rounded, and slightly raised fruiting bodies scattered across a textured, reddish-brown wood surface. The fruiting bodies appear smooth and somewhat shiny, contrasting with the lighter background.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, smooth yellow caps, some tinged green at the edges. Thick, sturdy yellow stems. One specimen shows closely spaced, pinkish-lilac gills beneath the cap. Caps appear moist with debris adhering to the surface.

Numerous irregular, angular to rounded brown spots scattered across glossy green leaves, many with faint yellowish halos. The lesions vary in size and are distributed widely on the leaf surfaces. No visible fruiting bodies are present.

Slender, elongated white fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded tips stand atop delicate, dark, hair-like stalks. The translucent sporangia are grouped in small, loose clusters, giving a delicate and moist appearance against the substrate.

A cluster of minute, globose to subglobose bodies with dull brownish to olive tones and a granular, slightly rough surface, scattered among greenish and yellowish detritus. No distinct stalks or sharply defined margins are visible.

Numerous small, upright, cylindrical to club-shaped fruiting bodies with dark, almost black heads atop slender, pale stalks. The sporangia are densely clustered and emerge from a fibrous, decaying substrate, with smooth surfaces and straight, delicate stalks.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to flat caps, each covered in coarse, dark brown spiny scales. Stems are long, slender, and similarly scaly. Gills are crowded, pale to light brown, and attached to the upper stem.
Highly magnified view of a rough, mottled surface with brownish to grayish tones. Scattered, tiny dark dot-like structures are visible, embedded irregularly in the granular, uneven bark-like texture.

Irregular brown lesion with a rough, granular center, sharply bordered by a vivid red margin and a yellow halo, blending into green leaf tissue. Leaf veins radiate from the spot, and the border is distinctly demarcated.

Cluster of small, rounded, bright pale yellow structures with a moist, gelatinous, and translucent appearance. The surface is irregular and lobed, forming a dense, compact mass with scattered smaller clusters nearby.

Patchy, darkly pigmented growth with a granular to filamentous texture, displaying black and brown hues. The surface is uneven and mottled, with lighter areas interspersed and fine, hair-like structures visible throughout.
A thin, whitish to pale, crust-like layer tightly adheres to the wood surface, with a finely granular to slightly velvety texture and a diffuse margin blending into the substrate.

Convex, light brown cap with a velvety texture and subtle radial fibrils. The margin is slightly inrolled and uneven, with minor surface cracking. The short, slender stem is pale and fibrous. No gills are visible from this angle.

Numerous small, black, slightly raised spots are scattered irregularly across a smooth, light brown cylindrical stem, creating a pockmarked appearance. The spots vary in size and are the most prominent feature on the otherwise unblemished surface.

Irregular, dark brown to nearly black patches cover the surface, displaying a granular to slightly hairy texture. The growth appears dense and patchy, with bristly structures visible, contrasting against the lighter wood beneath.

Single young fruiting body with a convex cap, darker brown margin, and paler cream center. Smooth, slightly moist surface. Pale, closely spaced gills visible from the side. Cylindrical off-white stem, heavily coated with coarse soil at the base.

Numerous upright, slender sporophores with cylindrical to club-shaped forms, each topped with a white, powdery or crystalline coating. Densely clustered and emerging from dark, brownish plant material, the white tips contrast sharply against the background.

Extensive, white, crust-like patch with a dense, cottony upper margin and a smooth to minutely poroid surface. The margin is irregular and diffuse, blending into the substrate, with embedded organic debris.
Tiny, dark, rounded to irregularly shaped structures with a granular surface, closely attached and scattered across a pale, rough substrate. No distinct margins or reproductive features are visible.

A dense, continuous white to grayish-white mat with a distinctly fuzzy, hairy texture. Fine, hair-like structures project outward, creating a fringed margin. The surface is uniform and tightly appressed, with no visible fruiting bodies or caps.

White to pale brown caps with frilled, fluted margins and subtle pinkish or brownish centers. Caps appear finely fibrous or slightly scaly. Stems are white, slender, and smooth, with a faint ring zone. Fruiting bodies shown at various stages, from convex to expanded forms.
Close-up of a brown surface densely covered with irregular, raised, silvery-white fibrous scales that glisten, creating a rough, spiky texture with uneven distribution across the cap.

Numerous minute, bright reddish-orange, globose to slightly oval fruiting bodies are scattered and clustered across a dark, rough, textured surface. The fruiting bodies have a smooth surface and vivid color, standing out against the background.

A solitary mushroom with a long, slender stipe densely covered in coarse, brownish scales. The convex cap is pale with prominent spiky brown scales, creating a rough, textured appearance. The cap margin is even, and the gills are not visible.

Numerous tiny, black, nearly spherical to irregularly shaped bodies scattered and clustered on rough, fibrous wood. The dark, granular structures contrast sharply with the lighter substrate, creating a dotted appearance. No large fruiting bodies are visible; only minute, discrete, slightly raised elements are present.

Numerous tiny, upright stalks each bear a dark, nearly black sporangium with a distinct pale or whitish tip. The sporangia have a powdery or granular texture and are scattered in loose clusters against a green background.
A single, tiny, rounded fruiting body slightly raised above the surface, brownish-gray with a smooth to subtly granular texture and a sharply defined margin, nestled in a substrate crevice.
Clusters of glossy, ovoid to cylindrical sporangia on slender dark stalks, ranging in color from pale cream to reddish-brown and dark brown, densely grouped on a wood surface.

Two small mushrooms with convex, pale yellow-tan caps featuring distinctly striate margins. The caps are smooth and dry. Slender, elongated pale stems support the caps, and the smaller mushroom shows widely spaced gills underneath.
Pale beige to grayish caps with darker, moist-looking centers. Caps are funnel-shaped with scalloped, undulating margins and a smooth, shiny surface. Fruiting bodies are clustered closely together.

Cluster of delicate mushrooms with pale pinkish-beige, moist, smooth caps featuring wavy, ruffled margins. Caps are convex to slightly depressed in the center. Slender, similarly colored stems and widely spaced, pale gills are visible beneath.

Minute, solitary fruiting body with a white, finely textured, matte surface. Cup- or goblet-shaped with an even, slightly upturned margin and a short stipe merging smoothly into the cup. Delicate and powdery in appearance.
No visible fungal structures or features can be observed; only green and brown plant stems and leaves are present.

Two mushrooms with slender, curved pale stems and conical to bell-shaped tan caps. The cap surfaces appear fibrillose or slightly scaly. Crowded, pale gills are visible beneath the caps. One specimen is larger, both show some soil on the base.

Irregular, crust-like patches with wrinkled, maze-like textures in shades of white, brown, and dark gray. Cottony or felted white areas intermingle with convoluted surfaces, blending diffusely into the substrate. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Thin, pale, and slightly translucent structure tightly pressed to a surface, with a folded margin. Numerous small, dark, rounded spots are scattered across the smooth to slightly granular, flat, and elongated surface.

Numerous small, black, flask-shaped to conical fruiting bodies are scattered and partially embedded in the brown bark, each with a tiny black dot at the tip. The bark also shows greenish patches and a matte texture.

Elongated green stems with linear, white, fuzzy or powdery patches partially enveloping the surface. The white growth follows the stem’s axis, has irregular margins, and a soft, cottony texture. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Granular, powdery greenish-gray surface forming irregular, compact patches. The texture is finely granular and uniform, lacking distinct lobes or margins, and appears tightly adherent. No visible reproductive structures.
A small, irregularly rounded, deep rusty brown fungus with a distinctly warty, coarse, and granular surface. The fruiting body is compact, somewhat lobed, and has a rough, uneven exterior.

Minute, whitish, nearly spherical to slightly flattened fruiting bodies scattered along dry, brownish moss leaves and stems. The apothecia are smooth, discrete, and lack visible stalks, with entire, regular margins and a simple, rounded appearance.

Irregular, swollen, white to pale green gall-like growths with a smooth to slightly powdery surface distort the leaves and young shoots, creating blistered, conspicuous patches scattered among the green foliage.

Minute, dark, pin-like fruiting bodies with slender black stipes and rounded, slightly roughened, powdery heads. The structures are spaced apart, emerging from a pale, fibrous-looking surface, with a softly blurred background highlighting their fine detail.

A resupinate, crust-like layer tightly appressed to wood, with a smooth to slightly uneven, off-white to pale cream surface and a firm, somewhat granular texture. The margin is indistinct and blends gradually into the substrate.

Pale cream to light tan, thin-walled cup-shaped bodies with wavy, irregular margins. Outer surface appears slightly granular, while the inner surface is smooth and lighter. No visible stipe; delicate and fragile appearance.

Rounded, compact fruitbody with a finely granular brown exterior. The cut half reveals a white, fleshy, and subtly marbled interior. Surface appears slightly rough and the overall shape is subglobose.

Extremely small, delicate fungus with a slender, upright, translucent white stem topped by a minute, rounded, slightly bulbous head. The surface appears smooth, and the fruiting bodies are solitary and sparsely distributed.

Predominantly white, cottony to granular surface with wrinkled, tessellated patches and scattered brownish areas. Texture varies from smooth to slightly rough, with intricate, maze-like patterns and irregular, patchy margins.

Two mushrooms with smooth, convex to slightly flattened caps in medium brown with a subtle pinkish hue, faint radial striations, pale well-spaced gills, and slender, smooth, pale cream to light brown stems. One specimen is sharply focused, the other partially visible.

Two mushrooms with smooth, striate caps: one pale whitish with a brownish center and a slightly curved white stem, the other uniformly dark brown. Both have moist, slightly fibrous surfaces and are nestled among green grass and moss.
A brown to black, slightly sunken and water-soaked lesion is visible on the stem, sharply contrasting with the surrounding healthy green tissue. No visible sporulation or fruiting bodies are present.

Creamy white wedge with irregular blue-green veins and patches. The marbling appears as diffuse, branching streaks embedded throughout, giving a mottled appearance. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible, only fuzzy streaks within the cheese matrix.

Irregular, dark brown to blackish spots with diffuse, uneven margins scattered across a granular greenish-yellow surface. The spots are slightly raised and form a mottled pattern, blending subtly into the background.

Leaves display irregular, dark brown to black necrotic patches with grayish discoloration. Affected areas appear dry, brittle, and curled, with some holes and thinning. Lesions are scattered, varying in size, and some coalesce into larger blotches.

A tiny, upright fungus with a slender, smooth, pale stem supporting a rounded, beige cap densely covered in fine, crystalline or granular textures. The cap appears velvety and delicate against a blurred background.

Numerous small, round, gray-green fruiting bodies with a powdery, granular surface are tightly clustered in bark fissures. The fruiting bodies are compact, slightly roughened, and partially embedded, contrasting with the cracked, weathered bark.
Numerous small, rounded to irregular, brownish-reddish structures densely clustered together with a slightly fuzzy, velvety surface and indistinct margins blending into the surrounding earthy matrix.

A single, sharply defined dark brown to blackish spot with an irregular, angular outline and subtle concentric zoning. The lesion is slightly sunken, dry, and matte, contrasting distinctly with the surrounding green leaf tissue.

Dark brown to olive, moist, gelatinous lobes with wrinkled, undulating surfaces and thin, irregular, somewhat translucent margins. The thallus appears glossy and flexible, forming a loosely attached, leafy cluster. A yellow-green moss is visible among the lobes.

Two small, pale cup-shaped bodies with well-defined margins, each densely covered in long, dark, bristly hairs, giving a fuzzy appearance. The surface is delicate and the fruiting bodies are closely grouped.

Leaf displays numerous irregular dark brown to black spots, some merging into larger necrotic patches and elongated streaks, set against a yellowed background. Surface is smooth with visible water droplets; spots are unevenly distributed and vary in size.

Slender, white, translucent stems topped with small, grayish-brown caps densely covered in white, fuzzy, hair-like tufts. Fruiting bodies are delicate, feathery, and scattered, with some appearing elongated and stringy, emerging directly from the substrate.

Clusters of small, white, translucent spherical bodies with a frosted, crystalline texture are scattered irregularly on the mossy wood. The delicate fruiting bodies have smooth margins and vary slightly in size and shape.

Small, circular fruiting body with a smooth, pale cream disc. The margin is distinctly fringed with prominent, dark brown, hair-like bristles. Surface appears slightly reflective. Additional similar bodies are scattered in the background.

Numerous tiny, slender, upright fruiting bodies with a pale green to yellowish hue are scattered across the decaying wood, appearing as delicate, bristle-like stalks. The wood shows fibrous texture and dark patches, with dense clusters of these minute structures.

Numerous tiny, blackish dot-like structures scattered across a discolored, browning leaf. The leaf surface appears mottled and rough, with visible tissue damage, holes, and areas of necrosis, especially along the veins and midrib.

Dark brown to blackish, wrinkled and convoluted mass with a leathery, irregular texture. The surface is coated with granular or crystalline particles, and small greenish-yellow structures are scattered throughout. Margins are uneven and lobed, giving a compact, irregular appearance.

Small, pale cream disc-shaped bodies closely grouped, each with a prominent fringe of coarse, dark, spiky hair-like structures around the margin. The smooth, slightly reflective surfaces lack visible stalks.

Small, rounded, pale cream fruiting bodies with a moist, slightly translucent surface, densely covered in long, stiff brown hair-like structures that create a spiky, fuzzy appearance. The margin is distinctly fringed with these brown setae, and the bodies are clustered together.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, rounded to slightly irregular patches with a granular texture are scattered in clusters across a pale, textured surface. The flat fruiting bodies have indistinct margins and are closely attached, with some fine, hair-like elements visible.

Numerous minute, dark brown to nearly black, irregularly rounded clumps form tight, granular nodules scattered densely across a pale, rough surface. The bumpy clusters have indistinct margins that blend into the background, creating a pattern of dark aggregations.

Roughly oval section with a dark brown to nearly black, fibrous outer layer and a lighter brown, marbled, porous interior. The cut surface reveals a dense, labyrinthine, granular texture with a distinct contrast between the exterior and interior.

Numerous minute, slender, upright fruiting bodies with a pale greenish-yellow hue emerge from the wood surface, forming a fine, brush-like covering. The stalks are smooth and delicate, lacking visible caps or discs at this magnification.

Small, delicate fruiting bodies with ovoid to cylindrical caps, whitish to pale gray, covered in shaggy, fibrous veil remnants. Margins are irregular and fringed. Thin, short, pale stems support the fragile caps. Arrangement is scattered, with individual mushrooms emerging from the substrate.

Small, round, smooth, brown to reddish-brown globose fruiting bodies clustered closely together on a fibrous plant stem. The fruiting bodies appear moist and slightly translucent, lacking visible stalks or prominent openings.

Greenish to olive thallus with a rough, granular surface and numerous small, wart-like outgrowths. A prominent, cup-shaped apothecium with a paler interior and granular margin blends into the thallus.

Rounded, irregular fruiting bodies with mottled brown and off-white, granular surfaces. Cut specimens reveal dense, spongy interiors ranging from pale cream to olive-brown. Surfaces appear matted with soil, and some show signs of damage or predation.

Numerous tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with white to pale pinkish, slightly translucent surfaces and fine, even margins are scattered densely and in small clusters on a light brown stem. The delicate, smooth texture is accentuated by a subtle moist sheen.

Slender, white, smooth stipe supporting an elongated, conical cap with grayish to bluish-gray tones. The cap surface is covered in prominent, shaggy, white to grayish scales, with an uneven, slightly tattered margin. Base attached to dark debris.

Four mushrooms with reddish to brown velvety caps, yellow pores, and slender stems showing reddish to yellow hues. Cut surfaces and bases display distinct blue-green staining. Largest specimen is about 10 cm long.

The leaf displays irregular, purplish-black to brown patches and spots, mainly along the midrib, with tiny, dark, dot-like structures scattered across the discolored, slightly raised areas. Healthy tissue remains green, with some yellowing at the infection margins. The surface appears moist, enhancing contrast.
Numerous small, white, fuzzy patches scattered irregularly across a green surface. The patches vary slightly in size and have a cottony or downy texture, appearing to emerge from the surface.

Slender, fragile white stems support small, narrowly conical to cylindrical caps with a fine, powdery or frosted coating. Fruiting bodies appear at various stages, some closed and others expanding, all with a delicate, almost translucent structure.

A small, ovoid cap with a grayish to dark surface, densely covered in fine, white, hair-like or feathery structures, giving a whiskered appearance. The stipe is mostly hidden by the surrounding substrate.

Subglobose to irregular bodies with rough, matted brown surfaces, scattered whitish patches, and adhering soil. Cross-sections reveal a spongy, labyrinthine interior ranging from olive-brown to pale tan. Texture appears firm and compact, with no visible stipe or cap.

Leaf surface covered with numerous irregular blackish spots and streaks, especially along veins and margins. Tissue appears yellowish-green, mottled, curled, and desiccated, with jagged edges and a papery, wilted texture.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, pale disc center. The margin is distinctly fringed with long, dark, hair-like bristles radiating outward, creating a spiky appearance. The contrast between the pale interior and dark, bristly edge is striking.

Pale whitish to grayish, powdery surface with a cracked, areolate texture. Numerous small, round, brown, slightly raised apothecia are scattered irregularly and stand out against the crustose background.
A mottled, rough surface with tan, brown, and green hues is visible. The texture appears uneven, with no distinct fungal structures or fruiting bodies apparent in the field of view.

Small, nearly spherical cup with a smooth, pale cream disc. The margin is distinctly lined with long, thin, brown bristles, giving a bristly appearance. Surface appears moist and solitary against the substrate.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with pale, cream-colored discs. Margins are densely fringed with stiff, brown, hair-like setae radiating outward, creating a spiky appearance. Surfaces appear moist and slightly reflective, with fruiting bodies closely grouped.

A small, hemispherical fruiting body densely covered with long, stiff, brown, hair-like spines radiating outward. The surface beneath the spines is pale to light brown and mostly obscured by the dense bristles.

Numerous small, circular, bright yellow-orange discs with smooth, glossy surfaces and conspicuous, straight, fine hair-like setae radiating from the margins, giving a fuzzy appearance. Fruiting bodies are clustered and vary in size, with some appearing more mature and others still developing.

Tiny, smooth, glossy, reddish-brown spherical fruiting bodies scattered and occasionally clustered on a pale, striated plant stem. The fruiting bodies are distinctly rounded and uniform in color, standing out against the light background.

Tiny, pale, disc-like to cushion-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, moist, translucent to whitish surfaces. Scattered in small groups along the substrate, lacking visible stipes, with even, rounded margins and a soft, gelatinous appearance.

Numerous tiny, rounded fruiting bodies with pale cream to off-white smooth discs, each distinctly fringed by long, brownish, hair-like bristles around the margin, scattered and clustered on a dark, moist surface.

Small, irregularly shaped, dark brown to nearly black thalli with a wrinkled, lobed, and somewhat shiny surface. The margins are undulating, and the thalli overlap compactly among scattered granular particles.

Small, disc-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, pale cream to light tan surface. The margin is densely fringed with prominent, straight, brown hair-like setae radiating outward, creating a striking spiny appearance.

Numerous minute, slender, whitish to pale, hair-like fruitbodies stand upright and scattered along a dark cylindrical surface. The fruitbodies are very thin, straight to slightly curved, with pointed tips and a smooth appearance.

Densely scattered, tiny, dark, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies cover a rough, pale gray to light brown cracked surface, creating a speckled, mottled appearance. The fungal structures are embedded or slightly raised above the substrate.

Tiny, delicate fruiting bodies with pale cream, fan-shaped to spatulate caps. Caps are deeply lobed, radially pleated, and have thin, wavy margins. Smooth to slightly fibrous surface. Supported by thin, wiry, pale stipes, scattered among moss.

Smooth, convex cap with pale yellow to ochre color and finely striate margin. White, cylindrical stipe with a prominent membranous volva at the base. No visible annulus; surface of stipe appears slightly fibrous.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with thin, fragile walls. Surfaces are white to translucent, displaying a delicate, lacy or reticulate pattern. Some cups appear partially collapsed or broken, revealing intricate internal structure. The arrangement is scattered and clustered.

Numerous tiny, upright, club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded to slightly pointed tips. They are pale greenish to yellowish and scattered irregularly across decomposing wood, emerging directly from the surface.

Mushrooms with convex to irregularly lobed, light brown caps featuring splits and fissures. Gills are densely packed, broad, and dark brown. Stems are slender, cylindrical, pale brown with longitudinal streaks and reddish-brown discoloration near the base.
Numerous tiny, slender, upright, whitish to pale hair-like fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across the surface of decaying wood, giving a delicate and sparse appearance.

Numerous tiny, white, needle-like fruiting bodies stand upright in scattered and clustered groups on a dark, decaying substrate. The delicate structures are slender, unbranched, and smooth, giving a fine, hair-like appearance against the rough, fragmented surface.

Broad, moist cap in deep burgundy to purplish-red with a smooth margin. Gills are closely spaced, broad, and rich reddish-purple. Slender, slightly curved stipe is pinkish to reddish-brown, paler at the base with visible mycelial threads.

Foliose thallus with overlapping, irregular lobes in pale to medium green. Surface densely covered in small, rounded, wart-like protuberances, giving a granular, uneven texture. Margins are undulating, and darker speckling is scattered across the thallus.

Densely compact, granular thallus with a rough, uneven surface. Numerous small, rounded granules cover the dark greenish to olive-brown surface. Several disk-like apothecia with slightly raised margins and dark centers are scattered among embedded mineral particles.

Dark olive-brown to blackish, rough and granular masses with irregular lobes. Surface densely dotted with small, cup-like structures, giving a pebbly, uneven texture. Compact, clustered fragments with some lighter greenish patches and indistinct margins.
Cluster of small, nearly spherical bodies with yellowish-green to olive tones and a granular, powdery surface. The fruiting bodies are tightly packed, rounded, and display a fine, uneven texture.

Small, rounded, translucent to whitish cup-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across a granular brown surface. The apothecia are sessile, smooth-margined, and slightly glistening, with some darker, possibly mature structures interspersed irregularly.
A small, delicate fruiting body with a slender, pale, slightly curved stem and a conical cap densely covered in pale, shaggy, fibrous material. The cap appears oval and no gills are visible.

Extensive, crust-like patch with a pronounced white, cottony to woolly margin blending into a beige, wrinkled, and uneven central area. The edge appears soft and fibrous, while the center is denser and more compact.
Numerous tiny, slender, upright fruiting bodies emerge from decaying wood. They are pale to whitish, hair-like or pin-shaped, smooth in texture, and scattered in loose groups across the dark surface.

Numerous tiny, round, pinkish-brown nodules densely cluster across the dark, moist soil surface. The smooth, globose fruiting bodies are irregularly distributed, forming subtle mounds that contrast with scattered green moss and soil particles.

Two subglobose to ovoid bodies with rough, soil-encrusted, mottled brown surfaces. One is cut open, revealing a dense, marbled, compact brown interior without visible pores or capillaries. Margins are irregular and not sharply defined.

Tiny, circular, white to pale cream discs with a faint peach tint, each edged with fine, hair-like cilia. The smooth, slightly translucent surfaces are scattered irregularly along a dried, light brown stem.

Small mushrooms with reddish, cracked caps revealing pale flesh beneath. The cut specimen shows a pale blue-green pore surface and slight blue staining in the context. Slender, reddish stems display surface texture. Pores are small and angular.

Clusters of small, round to irregular, yellowish-green fruiting bodies with a moist, translucent appearance and smooth to slightly granular surfaces, scattered across a dark, textured woody background with tiny black spiky structures.

Small, delicate, white cup-shaped fruiting bodies with a netted, reticulate surface, clustered densely on dark decaying wood. The structures appear fragile and papery, with well-defined margins and a scattered yet locally dense arrangement.

Delicate, slender, upright structures with a fine, hair-like appearance. White to cream in color, slightly fuzzy or velvety surface. Thin, unbranched or sparsely branched fruiting bodies emerge in small, scattered groups from the dark background.

Large, broadly convex to nearly flat cap with a pronounced central depression. Light brown surface with a darker brown center and margin, scattered fine black specks, and a subtly textured, matte appearance. Margin is slightly undulate.

Subglobose, irregularly rounded fruiting bodies with a rough, patchy brown to tan outer surface. The cut specimen reveals a pale, spongy, homogeneous interior. No stem or external reproductive structures are visible.

Slender, wiry white stalks curve upward from brown, striped fruit remains, each topped with a small, rounded, pale pinkish head. Fine, root-like threads cluster at the stipe bases. The fruiting bodies are scattered and distinct against a green, veined background.

Minute, round, brownish to reddish globose structures clustered and scattered on a pale, smooth surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly translucent with a smooth texture, appearing in small groups and individually. Some darker, possibly older structures are also present.

Delicate, slender, thread-like fruiting bodies emerge sparsely from the surface, mostly white to pale and semi-translucent. The structures are thin, hair-like, and gently curved, with smooth surfaces and no distinct caps or branching visible.

Several minute, thin, elongated, translucent to whitish fruiting bodies stand vertically, hair-like and delicate, with smooth surfaces and no visible caps or branching, sparsely distributed on a dark, fibrous substrate.

Dense patch of dark, irregularly lobed thallus with a wrinkled, convoluted surface. The leathery, opaque texture ranges from dark brown to nearly black, with uneven, curled margins and interspersed yellow-green mosses.

Scattered across the green, palmately lobed leaf are irregular, slightly raised brown to blackish spots with darker centers and lighter brown margins, highlighting the textured, minutely hairy leaf surface.

Irregularly oval, subglobose bodies with rough, patchy, dark brown to blackish outer surfaces encrusted with soil. One specimen is cut open, revealing a mottled brown to yellowish-brown, granular interior. Surfaces appear dry and uneven, lacking visible reproductive structures.

Numerous small, rounded to slightly flattened fruiting bodies clustered in bark crevices, grayish-green to olive in color with a granular or powdery surface, sessile and closely attached to the rough, cracked bark substrate.

Irregularly lobed, convoluted thallus with a shiny, moist, gelatinous surface in dark brown to blackish tones. The texture appears translucent and wet, with uneven, curled margins. Bright green moss shoots are interspersed throughout the mass.

Delicate fruiting bodies with slender, whitish stems and small, irregularly funnel-shaped to lobed caps. Caps are pale tan to off-white with wavy, split margins and a slightly darker center. The surface appears smooth and fragile, with a translucent quality.

Dark brown to blackish, leathery thallus with irregular, overlapping lobes. Surface is matte and wrinkled, dotted with numerous small, round, lighter disc-like apothecia. Margins are undulate and irregular, closely interspersed with greenish-yellow moss.

Numerous tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with pale cream to yellowish tones, each on a slender stalk. The cups have smooth, slightly translucent margins and shallow, open discs, scattered across the plant stem surface.

Crustose thallus tightly adherent to the surface, grayish and granular with a rough, cracked texture. Numerous tiny brownish dots are scattered across, and the margins are irregular, blending into the substrate with occasional greenish tinges.

Granular, uneven surface with a warted texture in olive-green, brown, and black tones. Scattered small, circular, dark-rimmed discs are visible among white crystalline particles. The structure is compact and tightly adherent, lacking visible lobes or leafy extensions.

Tiny, delicate fruiting body with a convex, white, slightly fuzzy cap atop a slender, translucent stem that fades from white near the cap to brownish at the base. The stem is smooth and tapers gently toward the substrate.
Tiny, pale to off-white disc-shaped fruitbodies clustered together, each with a smooth, moist surface and a striking fringe of long, dark, bristle-like hairs encircling the margin.

Scattered, irregular white powdery patches form fine, fuzzy growths on the green leaf surface, contrasting with the leaf’s natural fine hairs. The white areas appear patchy and delicate, giving a subtle, frosted look to the leaf.

Numerous tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with pale pinkish to light brown centers and distinctly white, fuzzy, hairy margins. The discs are flat to slightly concave, densely grouped, and have velvety edges with smoother centers.
Small, pale cream to light yellow fruiting bodies clustered together, each with a moist, somewhat translucent surface and distinctly surrounded by prominent, dark, bristly hairs along the margin.

Slender, upright fruiting body with a long, slightly curved white stem and a small, cylindrical pale gray cap. The cap is vertically striated and covered in white, floccose to scaly remnants, giving it a textured, frosted appearance.

Slender, elongated white stems topped with small, grayish-brown oval caps coated in fine white powder. Some caps show a partially collapsed margin, and the surface appears slightly fibrous or fuzzy. Fruiting bodies are at various stages of development.

Delicate, thin, white to pale thread-like structures stand upright and scattered on a dark brown surface. The fruiting bodies are minute, unbranched, hair-like, and smooth, with no visible caps or complex features, emphasizing their fine, filamentous appearance.

Tightly clustered, white, cup-like fruiting bodies with a delicate, net-like surface pattern resembling a honeycomb. The texture appears fragile and papery, with irregular, crenulate margins and a contiguous, sessile arrangement on the substrate.

Numerous small, rounded, pale cream to off-white fruiting bodies densely covered with prominent, stiff brownish hairs, forming bristly clusters. The moist surface and coarse setae are especially noticeable around the margins of each structure.

Numerous tiny, white, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with fine, radiating hair-like structures cluster densely on a fibrous brown surface. Each fruiting body appears soft, fuzzy, and delicate, giving a spider-web-like appearance.

Delicate, fan-shaped caps that are white to off-white with finely scalloped, wavy margins. The thin, somewhat translucent surface appears smooth, and the short, pale stem attaches laterally. Small fruiting bodies emerge among green moss.
Tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with a whitish to pale pink hue, each distinctly fringed with fine white hairs around the margin, scattered along a dead stem.

Tiny, white, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with prominent fringes of fine, hair-like filaments radiate from the margins. The delicate, fuzzy structures are scattered and clustered on a brownish substrate, giving a soft, airy appearance.
Numerous tiny, round to slightly irregular, dark brown to black, glistening dots scattered singly and in loose groups across a pale, striated, fibrous stem surface.

Irregular, crust-like patches tightly appressed to the surface, white to pale gray with a brittle, cracked, chalky texture. Brownish to dark areas appear where the surface breaks, exposing underlying spore masses. The patches are serpentine and scattered, lacking stalks or prominent structures.

Slender white stems support convex to conical, light brown caps with darker centers. The cap surface is finely fibrillose with striate margins. Undersides reveal closely spaced, pale gills. Mushrooms are clustered, emerging from dark soil.

Numerous tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies are scattered irregularly across the dark, broken plant stems. The discs are minute, round, slightly raised, and smooth, standing out starkly against the dark background.

Irregular, vein-like patches with a white to translucent, gelatinous and moist appearance, forming interconnected networks across decaying leaves. The texture is glossy, with diffuse margins blending into the substrate and no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

One mushroom shows a convex, brown cap with a finely textured surface and darker center. The other, viewed from the side, has a slender, smooth pale stem and a cap with broad, well-spaced, pale cream to pinkish gills.

Two mushrooms with smooth, convex to slightly flattened caps showing a darker brown center fading to a lighter brown margin. One cap is viewed from above, the other from below, revealing pale, closely spaced gills and a slender, pale stipe.

Whitish, powdery coating forms irregular, diffuse patches on plant leaves and stems, giving them a fine, dusty texture. The fungal growth appears as pale, superficial areas without distinct fruiting bodies.

Numerous small, blackish, circular spots are scattered irregularly across a reddish-brown, smooth, hard surface. The spots are slightly raised and well-defined, contrasting with the underlying grain patterns. No visible mycelium or other structures are present.

Two gelatinous, bright yellow-orange fruiting bodies with a moist, jelly-like texture. The upper one is irregular, lobed, and wrinkled with small dark spots, while the lower is rounded, smoother, and semi-translucent with undulating edges.

Cluster of mushrooms with conical to convex light brown caps, some with a gentle central bump. Stems are slender, fibrous, and pale brown, with remnants of soil and moss at the base. Gills are closely spaced and pale brown beneath the largest cap.

A dark, smooth, elongated clavate structure extends from a larger mass. The surface appears even and unornamented, with a distinct attachment point visible. No additional external features are discernible at this magnification.

Irregular, flat, cream-colored patches with undulating, lobed edges. Surface densely covered in short, spiny projections, giving a rough, fibrous texture. Fruit bodies closely attached to wood, sometimes merging, with slightly reflexed margins.
Small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a distinctly triangular outline, yellowish-green color, and a dense covering of fine, granular or velvety texture. The margin is irregular and slightly undulate.
A small, nearly black, roughly spherical body with a slightly rough, irregular surface and a short, dark, beak-like projection on one side. Minor debris is present on the uneven surface.

A delicate, upright fruiting body with a slender, pale brown stem and a small, grayish-brown cap. The cap is slightly depressed in the center, matte or velvety in texture, with an even, slightly incurved margin.

Cup-shaped fruiting body with a rough, dark brown exterior and a smooth, creamy white inner surface. The margin is irregular and upturned, splitting into several lobes, giving a star-like appearance. Soil particles adhere to the inner surface.

Small mushrooms with slender, pale brown stems and convex to nearly flat, dark brown caps showing a velvety texture. One specimen displays widely spaced, attached gills in shades of brown. Cap margins are faintly striate. Scattered on sandy soil with moss and debris.

Close-up of a robust, off-white stem with fibrous texture and attached debris. Densely packed, decurrent gills radiate outward in a fan-like pattern, colored light brown to tan. The cap surface is not visible. Scale indicates a large fruiting body.

Tiny, bright white, circular to shallow cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly raised margins and central depressions, scattered singly across a dark, glossy stem. The apothecia contrast sharply with the substrate and have a smooth texture.

A thin, widespread mat of white to pale yellowish, cottony or woolly mycelium covers the wood surface, forming a soft, fibrous layer with diffuse edges. No erect fruiting bodies are present, only a continuous felt-like texture.

Small mushrooms with thin white stems and convex to slightly umbonate brown caps, featuring prominent white radial fibrils. Gills are closely spaced and pale, and the cap surface appears dry and fibrillose.

Densely packed clusters of tiny fungi with slender white stems and small, rounded to slightly flattened pale yellow caps. The caps appear moist and opaque, and the fruiting bodies form a spongy, carpet-like layer. Occasional droplets and fine hyphal threads are visible among the stems.
Numerous tiny, white to cream, rounded or button-like fruiting bodies with smooth, moist surfaces and short slender stalks, densely clustered on a dark, fibrous background.

A patchy, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, displaying a rusty to ochre-brown color with a granular to finely velvety texture and an irregular, diffuse margin blending into the substrate.

Minute, irregular whitish to translucent granules scattered across a greenish, uneven surface. The granules are angular to amorphous, lacking distinct margins or visible reproductive structures, and are distributed without a clear pattern.

Brownish, glossy surface dotted with numerous small, dark, rounded structures scattered irregularly. The surface appears moist and slightly textured, with the dark spots standing out distinctly against the lighter background.

Numerous small, irregular whitish to translucent granules are scattered across a greenish, matte surface with undulating, lobed edges. The granules vary in size and appear angular or blocky, contrasting with the smooth background.

Cluster of mushrooms with broadly convex to flat tan caps, slightly fibrillose surfaces, and irregular wavy margins. Stems are slender and pale, with attached soil at the base. Gills are closely spaced, pale beige to light brown, and visible beneath some caps.

Irregularly globose fruiting body with a thick, warty, yellowish-brown outer surface encrusted with soil. The cut section reveals a dense, dark marbled interior surrounded by a distinct pale layer, forming a somewhat triangular pattern.

Broad, fan-shaped caps with wavy, inrolled margins and smooth ochre to tan surfaces. Prominent, closely spaced gills run decurrently down short, off-center stems. Gills are pale cream to yellowish. Caps vary in size, with one specimen showing moss at the base.
Slender, white stipe supporting a small, pale convex cap with a moist surface and striate margin. Gills are free, closely spaced, and pale. The cap appears slightly translucent.

Numerous slender, upright, and contorted fruiting bodies with smooth, cylindrical, unbranched forms. They display a pale lilac to grayish-purple color, rounded tips, and emerge densely clustered among green moss, resembling delicate, finger-like projections.
Numerous tiny, round, yellow-orange fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces are scattered and loosely clustered on a dark, moist substrate with iridescent beetle fragments.

Broad, fan-shaped to trumpet-like caps with fluted, wavy margins; pale beige to light brown surfaces, some darker at the edges. Decurrent, closely spaced cream to pale tan gills run down slender, off-white, fibrous stems. Clustered arrangement, largest cap about 13–15 cm wide.

Numerous tiny, black, dot-like structures are evenly scattered across a dry, brown stem surface. The stem appears slightly rough, with a few small, pale, translucent protrusions visible among the embedded dark spots.

Irregular, rounded fruiting bodies with a smooth, moist ochre-brown surface, some partially coated in soil. A cut specimen reveals a granular, yellowish-brown to olive-brown marbled interior, lacking visible gills or pores. Texture appears firm and compact.

Large, fan-shaped caps with smooth, pale tan to light brown surfaces and wavy, inrolled margins. Prominent, closely spaced, creamy white to pale yellowish gills run down short, thick, off-white stems. Fruiting bodies overlap in a cluster.

Numerous tiny, bright yellow-orange, globose to club-shaped structures on short, slender stalks densely clustered atop a dark, granular, uneven substrate. The smooth fruiting bodies create a vivid contrast against the moist background.

Tiny, delicate, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with pale pinkish to whitish, translucent caps and slender, similarly pale stems. The smooth, fragile discs are scattered along a dead plant stem, appearing slightly moist.

Tiny, cup-shaped fruitbodies with white, fuzzy margins and smooth, pale cream interiors are scattered across a coarse brown surface. Some cups are fully open while others remain partially closed, showing a range of developmental stages.

Slender, light brown stems with small, convex to funnel-shaped caps. Caps are darker brown, smooth, and slightly undulating. Well-developed, decurrent gills underneath. Some green plant debris adheres to the dry, fibrous surface. Fruiting bodies are small and scattered.

Pale greenish-yellow, tightly appressed mat with deeply lobed, ruffled, and wrinkled thalli. Margins are irregular and incised, with a single cup-like apothecium visible near the center, creating a textured, bushy appearance.

Numerous small, smooth, translucent globose to subglobose fruiting bodies in pale cream to light orange hues, densely clustered and connected by fine white hyphae on a dark, moist background. Some appear slightly elongated or with short stalks, all with a gelatinous, moist texture.

Granular, uneven surface with a gradient from pale greenish-white to orange and brown. Numerous small, rounded, yellow-orange structures create a bubbly, textured appearance. Margins are irregular and the texture is rough and patchy.

Small mushrooms with slender, dark brown stems and rounded to conical, velvety brown caps. Caps are darker at the edges, lighter in the center. Pale beige gills radiate from the stem. Soil remnants cling to the base. Overall size is small.

Close-up of a spongy, white to cream surface with irregular, closely packed pores forming a honeycomb pattern. Adjacent is a dense, cottony, white mycelial mat with a soft, fuzzy texture. Small dark debris is scattered across the surface.

Broad, spreading patches with pale greenish-gray, rough, and granular surface forming concentric, radiating zones. The texture is dense and uneven, merging into irregular, contiguous areas tightly attached to the dark stone.

Cluster of mushrooms with smooth, shiny, pale tan to beige convex caps and robust white stems, some slightly bulbous at the base. Gills are pale lilac to whitish. Caps are unbroken with entire margins. Soil and moss are visible around the base.

Numerous tiny, white, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies scattered across a dark substrate, with fine white hyphal threads radiating from their bases. The fruiting bodies are smooth, clustered, and lack prominent stalks or differentiated margins.

Dense clusters of brown, irregularly branched cylindrical structures with a rough, powdery surface and whitish coating. The forms are closely packed, somewhat flattened, and display jagged, uneven margins with a crust-like appearance.

Small, dark brown to grayish-brown mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, ruffled caps and slender, matching stems. The cap surface appears velvety, and the pale gills are decurrent and visible on the upturned specimen.

Cream to off-white surface densely covered with irregular, angular to maze-like pores. The texture is rough and uneven, with scattered small flecks of debris. No cap, stem, or margin visible in this close-up view.

Cluster of mushrooms with pale, cream to light tan convex caps, some with wavy or split margins. Caps appear matte and slightly granular. Slender, smooth yellow stems and well-developed, decurrent white to pale cream gills are visible.
A fine, whitish to pale gray, powdery or fuzzy coating forms a thin, even layer on the surface, with a delicate, granular to cottony texture and no distinct margins or visible fruiting bodies.

Roughly round, irregular tuber with a pale brown to tan, warty surface marked by scattered darker spots. Cut section reveals a marbled brownish interior with lighter, vein-like patterns. Surface appears moist and partially covered by soil particles.
