Numerous tiny, angular to irregularly lobed whitish to pale yellowish discs with translucent, scalloped margins scattered across a matte greenish surface. The flat to slightly convex fruiting bodies appear granular and sharply outlined, often forming loose clusters.

Numerous tiny, dark, roughly spherical structures are scattered across a fibrous, brownish matrix. Fine, whitish threads are visible among the irregular, granular texture. The dark spheres are embedded and dispersed, lacking any distinct cap or stem.

Large, roughly spherical fruitbodies with thick, cracked, and scaly pale tan to light brown surfaces. The outer layer splits and peels back in places, exposing a paler interior. No visible stems or caps; texture is robust and rough with prominent fissures.

Close-up of yellowish to tan, glossy, moist tissue with a dense network of irregular, rounded to angular cavities. The margin is slightly darker, orange-brown, smooth, and continuous. The surface appears spongy and labyrinthine, with a shiny, hydrated texture.

Numerous small, globose to subglobose, translucent to whitish, gelatinous fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across the branch. The fruiting bodies have a smooth, moist, and shiny surface, appearing singly or in loose clusters, each only a few millimeters wide.

Tiny, shallow, pale whitish cups with conspicuously hairy, cottony margins. The fruitbodies are scattered in small groups, each with a delicate, crystalline fringe around the rim, standing out against the brown substrate.

White to cream, shelf-like fruiting bodies with wavy, undulating margins. The lower surface is densely covered in elongated, tooth-like spines, giving a fibrous, tough appearance. Fruiting bodies overlap in clusters on decaying wood.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, light brown caps featuring slightly darker centers and faint striations. Stems are slender, off-white to pale cream, and relatively long. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps.

Irregular, crust-like patches closely appressed to the surface, white to pale gray with some brownish areas. The surface appears smooth to slightly rough, showing cracking and peeling, with uneven, fragmented margins. Structures are very small and thin.

Slender, slightly curved stem in pale yellowish-brown, darkening at the base. Convex, smooth cap with a faintly wavy margin in light brown. Widely spaced, decurrent gills in pale beige extend partway down the stem.

Slender, brownish stems support convex to hemispherical caps with a smooth, pale tan center fading to darker brown margins. One fallen specimen reveals pale, well-spaced gills beneath the slightly incurved cap edge.

Small, solitary mushroom with a pale beige to tan, centrally depressed cap featuring distinct striations along the margin. The cap surface is smooth, with a subtle darker center. The slender stipe is whitish and unadorned.

Small, bright yellow, gelatinous fruiting bodies with irregular, lobed, and convoluted surfaces cluster and scatter along a woody surface. Their moist, jelly-like texture and undulate, uneven margins stand out against the darker background.
Small, bright yellow to orange, gelatinous fruiting bodies with irregular, lobed shapes and moist, translucent surfaces, clustered along a decaying branch.

Medium brown, convex to broadly convex caps with finely fibrillose texture and paler margins. Pale, closely spaced gills beneath. Slender, smooth, white to off-white stipes with slightly bulbous, soil-covered bases. No visible ring or veil remnants.

Bisected fruiting body with a figure-eight outline, displaying a yellowish-tan, marbled interior. The gleba has a dense, reticulate labyrinthine pattern, and the margin is smooth with a thin, slightly darker rim.

Slender, elongated yellowish-brown stems with slightly darker bases support convex to flattened, light brown caps showing cracks. Well-developed, decurrent dark gills radiate beneath the caps. The surface appears moist and fresh.

Minute, translucent to whitish, gelatinous fruiting body with a rounded shape, adorned with numerous dark purple, hair-like projections emerging from the upper surface. The moist, glistening texture contrasts with the striking dark structures.

Three small, upright fruiting bodies with slender brown stems and convex, velvety caps. The caps are pale grayish-brown on top, darkening toward the margin, and slightly depressed in the center. Margins are smooth and even, with no visible gills.

Two large, irregularly globose fruiting bodies cut open, revealing a thick, cracked tan outer layer and a dark brown to black, powdery interior. The peridium is rough and uneven, with a thick white to cream margin and no visible stem.

Numerous tiny, spherical fruiting bodies with a powdery surface cluster densely on thin, upright reddish stalks. The sporangia are brownish to grayish, forming compact groups across the decaying wood, with a granular texture and delicate appearance.

Large, irregular, roughly globose mass with a tough, thick, cracked outer surface. Earthy brown to yellowish coloration, rough and uneven texture with visible fissures. No distinct stem or cap; partially embedded in soil with patches of dirt adhering.

Numerous tiny, cream to white, cup-shaped bodies with smooth interiors and distinctly fringed, white, hair-like edges. The cups are scattered and clustered, each just a few millimeters wide, with a delicate, frosted appearance.

Small, conical to convex caps with light to medium brown color and darker centers. Cap surface is finely scaly and striate at the margin. Pale, closely spaced gills and slender, smooth, pale stems. No veil remnants or ring visible.

A single, small, pale, and translucent structure with a granular surface and irregular, lobed, star-like margin. Slightly raised above the greenish, textured background, it lacks visible reproductive bodies at this magnification.
Tiny, upright, white, hair-like stalks topped with globose to slightly elongated heads. The surface appears filamentous and cottony, with delicate, sparse groupings emerging from a dark background.

Small mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped, light to medium brown caps showing subtle radial striations and darker centers. Stems are slender, pale cream to light brown, and smooth. Gills are pale and attached, visible on some specimens. Caps have smooth, non-wavy margins.

Irregular, contiguous patches of pale greenish-gray lichen with a rough, granular, and uneven surface. The margins are diffuse and frilled, forming dense, spreading growth tightly pressed against the surface.

A small mushroom with a slender, slightly curved grayish-brown stipe and a dark, matte cap. The cap is convex with a subtle central depression, distinctly striate and scalloped at the margin, and finely textured.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat caps, central dark brown coloration, and paler, striate margins. Cap surface is smooth to slightly fibrillose. Densely packed, light brown gills and slender, fibrous stipes. No veil remnants or ring structures visible.

Minute, clustered fruiting bodies with off-white to light tan coloration and granular surfaces. Dark, tiny spots are scattered on the upper surfaces, giving a speckled appearance. The colonies are closely grouped, lacking distinct margins or prominent structures.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with slender, elongated stems and small, convex to slightly funnel-shaped caps. The caps are smooth and brownish-gray, with pale gills radiating underneath. The overall stature is diminutive, matching the fine scale of surrounding soil grains.

Large, fan- to trumpet-shaped fruiting bodies with pale cream to yellowish-brown, smooth caps and wavy, irregular margins. Prominent, densely packed, decurrent gills run down short, pale stipes. Some caps show darker brown zones. Largest specimen measures about 18 cm long.

Minute, whitish to pale, irregularly shaped patches with jagged, uneven margins. The structures are scattered, granular, and slightly translucent, forming discrete clusters on a rough, uneven surface.

Broad, cup-shaped fruiting body with an irregular, undulating margin. The upper surface is smooth, moist, and pale to medium brown with a slightly glossy sheen. Margin is thin and wavy, and the structure appears flattened and stemless.

Large, broadly convex to flat caps with a yellowish-orange, moist surface, often bearing debris. Cap margins are smooth and slightly inrolled on younger specimens. White, closely spaced gills and thick, white stems are visible, with soil clinging to the bases.

Small, whitish, granular to globose structures scattered across a greenish, rough lichen thallus with irregular, slightly lobed margins and some white, filamentous outgrowths at the edges. The pale fungal dots contrast with the darker background and are unevenly distributed.

Numerous tiny, dark, rounded dots are scattered irregularly across a smooth, pale tan surface with a prominent longitudinal groove, creating a speckled appearance. The dots are slightly raised and circular, standing out against the light background.

Large, irregularly globose fruiting body with a thick, leathery, yellowish-brown surface split open to reveal a hollow, darkened interior. The cracked, rough exterior curls outward, and the fungus appears partially buried in soil.
A dark, elongated, velvety patch closely appressed to the wood surface. The matte black growth has an irregular, diffuse margin and lacks any visible fruiting bodies or raised structures.

Sharply defined, dense dark central mass with lighter brownish, granular and filamentous margins. The center appears opaque, transitioning to a textured, possibly spore-laden periphery with fine details visible at the edges.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate caps, one pale brown and the other darker brown, both with striate margins. Prominent, widely spaced pale gills are visible beneath the upper cap. Stems are slender, cylindrical, and pale brown to translucent.
Numerous tiny, orange to pale orange, club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded heads and slender, translucent stalks densely clustered and emerging from a dark substrate.

Numerous tiny, white to pale cream, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with conspicuously fringed, hairy margins are scattered across a dark, rough surface. The cups are sessile, clustered loosely, and each measures less than a millimeter in diameter.

Several black, irregularly shaped patches with rough, granular surfaces are closely appressed to the substrate. The margins are uneven and indistinct, and the surface appears matte to slightly glossy. Scattered small white particles are present nearby.

Two tiny, shiny black, globose heads sit atop slender, pale yellow stalks on a brown stem. The fruiting bodies are well-separated, smooth, and lustrous, highlighting their delicate, minute structure against a blurred background.

Pale yellowish to off-white, irregular and lobed fruitbody with a moist, somewhat translucent surface and wavy, uneven margin. The texture appears brittle or fragile, nestled among green moss and plant debris.

Numerous tiny, pale cream to white, cup- to disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth to slightly wavy margins are scattered and loosely clustered on a brown, roughened stem. The apothecia appear sessile and minute, contrasting with the woody substrate.

Clustered mushrooms with medium to dark brown, slightly fibrous caps, convex to flattened in shape. Gills are brown and moderately close, stems are robust, cylindrical, and off-white to pale brown, some with soil at the base.

Patchy, irregular olive-green crust with a granular to warty surface. Scattered small, nearly black spots dot the dense, compact mat, which has uneven margins and closely hugs the pale, indistinct substrate.

Green foliage with whorled, lanceolate leaves and clusters of small, white, star-shaped flowers. A few scattered, tiny, dark spherical spots are visible on stems, but no distinct fungal structures are apparent.

Numerous tiny, white, disc-shaped to cushion-like fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces are scattered and occasionally clustered on a brown, fibrous stem. The fruiting bodies are minute, rounded, and slightly flattened, standing out against the textured substrate.

Two globose to urn-shaped fruiting bodies with vivid yellow-orange bases and dark brown, rough outer surfaces, attached laterally and oppositely to a dark stem. The surface is dry and granular, with short, robust stalks and visible yellowish residue on the substrate.
Numerous tiny, cream to pale beige, disc-shaped to slightly irregular fruiting bodies with a granular texture are scattered singly or in loose clusters along the surface of a dead stem.

Numerous small, nearly spherical black fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and distinct central openings, densely scattered and slightly clustered. The perithecia are matte to slightly shiny and partially embedded in a moist, fibrous substrate.

A thin, gelatinous, translucent to pale brownish film coats the wood surface, appearing moist and shiny. The layer is spread evenly without distinct margins or visible fruiting bodies, with small wood particles and debris scattered atop the slimy surface.

Delicate, slender, translucent stalks rise vertically, each topped with a compact, spherical cluster of golden-yellow, granular structures. The clusters have a fine, powdery texture, and the stalks are straight, unbranched, and scattered, emerging from a dark, irregular base. Structures are extremely small, just over 100 μm tall.
Whitish to pale, patchy crust with a granular to finely hairy surface, closely appressed and irregular in outline. The texture appears uneven, lacking any distinct cap, stem, or gills.

Tiny, shiny black, globose heads sit atop slender, upright pale yellow stalks. Each fruiting body is distinct and scattered, emerging from a moist, decomposing surface. The sporangia are smooth and glossy, with no visible network or reticulation.

Slender mushrooms with elongated, pale brown to grayish stems and small, conical to bell-shaped caps. Caps are grayish-brown with slightly paler, subtly uneven margins. Gills are pale, widely spaced, and radiate distinctly from the stem.

Delicate mushrooms with umbrella-shaped, pale brown to grayish-brown caps featuring grooved margins. White, broad, well-spaced gills are visible beneath the caps. Slender, translucent to pale brown stipes support the caps, creating a scattered, fragile cluster.

Dense clusters of minute, golden-orange to brownish-yellow spherical structures on a fine, translucent web of hyphae, forming a delicate, powdery mat. The fruiting bodies are fuzzy and irregularly distributed, with some areas showing denser groupings.

Pale yellow to off-white, fan-shaped fruiting body with irregular, lobed and undulating margins. Surface appears finely fibrillose and soft, partially embedded in soil with granules adhering. No visible gills or pores from this angle.

Tiny, yellowish-white discs and shallow cups scattered in clusters along the stem, some with irregular or lobed edges. Surfaces appear smooth to slightly granular, with fine white threads visible among the delicate fruiting bodies.

A thin, creamy white crust closely appressed to the surface, with a powdery or granular texture. The surface is irregular and patchy, showing fine linear cracks and a diffuse margin blending into the substrate. Scattered translucent crystalline granules are present nearby.
White to cream, irregular shelf-like clusters with soft, spongy, and uneven surfaces. Fruiting bodies have frilled, lacy margins and a waxy texture, overlapping along decaying wood.
Small, yellowish to orange, rounded pustules scattered across a green leaf surface. The pustules are slightly raised, moist, and granular, with an irregular distribution.

Close-up of a pale cream, off-white pore surface with a strongly reticulate, maze-like pattern. The pores are irregular, interconnected, and labyrinthine. The margin is thick and slightly undulate, with some brownish debris scattered on the surface.

Delicate mushrooms with slender, pale brown stems and smooth, conical to bell-shaped tan caps. One specimen stands upright, while the other lies flat, revealing closely spaced, light brown gills beneath the cap.

Dark, rough, nearly spherical to irregular fruiting bodies clustered along brown, desiccated conifer needles. The fruiting bodies are blackish to dark brown, with a textured surface, and emerge directly from the needle substrate.

Thin, irregular, pinkish crust forming a membranous, patchy layer with a reticulate pattern. Margins are diffuse, blending into adjacent greenish and yellowish lichen thalli. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Numerous tiny, rounded to slightly flattened, pale yellowish-white fruiting bodies with a soft, powdery or velvety texture are scattered in loose clusters. Margins are even and well-defined, with fine hyphal threads visible around them.

Smooth, moist, medium brown caps with a slightly flattened dome shape. Broad, decurrent, pale ochre to tan gills are visible beneath the cap. Cylindrical, pale to light brown stems with some soil and debris attached.

A large, loosely tangled mass of long, thread-like, intricately interwoven branches. The filaments are pale yellowish to straw-colored, fine, and flexible, forming an irregular, sprawling structure without visible reproductive bodies.

Numerous tiny, whitish, globular to irregularly shaped fruitbodies scattered across the surface. The fruitbodies are smooth, somewhat opaque to slightly translucent, and loosely grouped, with some isolated individuals visible.

Numerous tiny, cream to off-white, cup-shaped structures with smooth inner surfaces and slightly irregular margins are scattered in loose clusters across a dark brown background. Some cups are larger and more prominent, while smaller ones are dispersed around them.

Several minute, pale yellowish, disc-shaped fruitbodies with a delicate, almost translucent appearance are scattered sparsely across a fibrous background. The surfaces appear finely granular, and the fruitbodies are sessile with even, unfurrowed margins.

Shriveled, discolored corn kernels with a patchy, whitish, fibrous layer covering the surface. The fungal growth appears thin and cottony, concentrated along the rows and crevices between kernels, with some areas showing collapsed or desiccated kernels.

Two slender, yellow stalks each support a rounded, orange to reddish-brown cap with a distinct cracked, reticulated surface resembling a miniature brain. The fruiting bodies are spaced apart along a dead stem.
Numerous tiny, white to cream cup-shaped structures with smooth, slightly raised margins and central depressions are scattered and sometimes clustered on a brown, rough surface.

Leaves display numerous small, irregular, dark brown to blackish flat spots scattered across the surface. The spots are not raised or fuzzy and are distributed singly or in small groups. Leaf tissue otherwise appears smooth and healthy.
Pale, dried plant stem with numerous small, dark, elongated, slightly raised spots arranged in linear rows. The spots are narrow, oval to fusiform, and embedded in the smooth stem surface.

Small, delicate mushrooms with slender, pale stems and conical to bell-shaped light brown caps. The caps have smooth to faintly striate margins and a dry, matte surface. Gills are closely spaced and pale brown, visible beneath some caps.

Thin, irregular white patches closely adhere to the dark surface, forming a continuous, patchy crust. The texture appears granular to powdery, with uneven distribution and indistinct margins, giving a slightly fuzzy or powdery appearance.

Small, dark, nearly black rounded to irregular fruiting bodies scattered on a rough, granular, olive-green crust. The apothecia are embedded or slightly raised with a matte, uneven surface, contrasting against the greenish, uneven background.

Yellowish-green surface with numerous black, irregularly shaped spots, each with a pale center. Fine, white, hair-like threads crisscross the surface. The background shows a polygonal cell pattern and areas of brownish discoloration around the spots.

A thin, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, pale whitish to cream in color, with a finely granular or powdery texture and indistinct, blending margins. The surface is mostly uniform, with some denser, powdery patches visible.

Thin, effused crust with a pale whitish to cream color and finely granular, powdery surface. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the substrate, forming a continuous, patchy layer without distinct fruiting bodies.

Small, globose fruiting bodies with a wrinkled, reddish-brown surface sit atop slender, pale yellow stalks, spaced evenly along a dark brown, diagonal stem. The sporangia are vividly textured and orange to reddish in color.

White, shelf-like bracket with a semicircular, wavy margin. Upper surface dense, waxy to velvety, scattered with dark debris. Underside features fine, regular pores. Compact texture, consistently white throughout, laterally attached to wood.

Slender, elongated stems with pale brown to tan coloration support conical to bell-shaped caps. Caps are smooth, matte, and light brown, sometimes with faint radial striations. Gills are dark brown and closely spaced. Margins are mostly straight or slightly incurved.

Two slender, upright yellow-orange stalks each support a single, round, dark brown to black sporangium with a matte, slightly granular surface. The stalks are smooth, slightly curved, and emerge directly from the wood surface. Fine threadlike strands are visible nearby.

Two upright fruiting bodies with globose, orange-brown, warty heads atop short, yellowish-white stalks, each stalk broadening at the base. The heads have a rough, granular texture and are spaced apart on a fibrous surface.

Irregular, patchy brown areas with a granular to velvety surface, blending diffusely at the margins and intermingling with greenish material. The surface is finely textured and forms a crust-like, resupinate growth without visible fruiting bodies or distinct edges.

Irregular, crust-like patches with mottled olive-green, brown, and pale beige tones. Scattered small, dark rounded spots and translucent, gelatinous areas create a bumpy, granular, and slightly glossy surface with diffuse, blending margins.
Numerous tiny, white, disc- to oval-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces are scattered and clustered irregularly along a brown, decaying stem, standing out against the darker background.

Small, irregular dark brown to black spots with occasional pale centers are scattered across a smooth, glossy green leaf. The spots are flat and embedded in the tissue, with the leaf’s vein network clearly visible.

Minute, white, oval to nearly spherical fruiting bodies scattered on a dark background. The delicate structures appear translucent, with a smooth to faintly granular, gelatinous texture and subtle variations in white coloration.

Two slender, smooth yellow stalks each support a glossy, dark brown to black spherical head. The sporangia are distinctly separated, with a shiny surface and clear contrast between the stalk and the rounded top.

Highly magnified surface with a metallic, iridescent sheen in gray, brown, and black hues. The texture appears hard, reflective, and subtly undulating, with fine granular features and no distinct reproductive structures visible.
Slender, pale tan stem densely covered with numerous dark brown to black, oval to irregular, slightly raised spots scattered and clustered across the smooth surface.

A single, round sporocarp with a smooth, shiny brown surface marked by distinct polygonal, plate-like divisions. Firm and slightly reflective, it sits atop a slender, upright stem. The structure is solitary and sharply defined.

Two globose fruiting bodies with smooth, glossy surfaces; one dark brown with orange mottling atop a short yellow-orange stalk, the other below the twig, showing vivid concentric orange and brown bands. Both stalks are robust and pale yellow to orange.

Thin, irregular, crust-like patch with a whitish to cream surface, matte and slightly velvety in appearance. Scattered small brownish spots and denser granular clusters are visible, with uneven, patchy texture and indistinct margins.

A solitary, erect fungus with a slender, translucent yellow stalk topped by a smooth, globose, dark gray to black sporangium. The sporangium surface appears slightly glossy, sharply contrasting with the bright stalk.

Irregular, patchy growth with a dark brown to black upper zone, a white cottony middle band, and a grayish-blue lower area covered in dense, minutely granular or bubbly texture. The surface is flat and resupinate, with sharply defined color transitions.

Minute, cup-shaped fruiting bodies appear as pale cream to translucent white discs, clustered along a brown, fibrous plant stem. The surfaces are smooth to slightly granular, with even, non-fringed margins closely appressed to the substrate.

Thin, patchy pinkish to pale crust-like growth forms irregular, slightly granular patches scattered among green and yellow lichen. The surface is subtle, blending with the lichen, lacking prominent fruiting bodies or distinct margins, and follows the contours of the substrate.

Extensive crust-like layer with granular to powdery texture, pale blue-green to whitish coloration, mottled with darker patches and embedded debris. Cottony white tufts appear at the margins and among wood fragments. Surface is uneven and closely appressed, with indistinct, diffuse edges.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex brown caps, darker at the center and lighter toward the edges, dry and slightly scaly. Gills are closely spaced and pale brown. Cylindrical stems are fibrous and light brown, with white mycelial threads at the base.

Tiny, globose black sporangia perched atop slender, glossy yellow stalks. The smooth, spherical heads are scattered along the wood, sometimes appearing in pairs or small groups. Stalks are straight to slightly curved.

A thin, whitish, crust-like layer tightly adheres to the surface of herbaceous stems. The smooth, patchy texture has irregular margins and a subtle sheen, blending closely with the substrate and lacking any prominent fruiting bodies.

A thin, patchy, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, grayish to bluish-gray in color, with a granular to minutely warted texture, scattered small pits, and uneven, slightly roughened margins.
Leaves display minor brown spots and subtle discoloration, with one leaf turning yellow. No visible fungal fruiting bodies or distinct surface growths are present on the leaf surfaces.

Elongated green leaflets display scattered, irregular brown spots and lesions along the margins and surfaces. The lesions are flat, sharply contrasting with the smooth green tissue, and lack distinct fruiting bodies at this magnification.

Tiny, round, pale cream apothecia scattered on a fibrous surface, each with a distinct margin lined by fine, translucent, hair-like structures. The fruiting bodies appear matte and delicate, with a subtle, whitish coloration.

Tiny, dark, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies with long, slender, black necks protrude from the surface. The matte fruiting bodies are scattered and partially embedded, with necks straight to slightly curved, rising distinctly above the substrate.

Dense, felt-like mat of blue to blue-green mycelium with interspersed white areas, especially at the margins. The texture is matted and fibrous, forming a web-like network with diffuse, irregular edges blending into the substrate. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Clustered mushrooms with smooth, moist, light brown caps featuring darker centers and slightly incurved margins. Stems are slender, fibrous, white to light brown, with some showing veil remnants. Gills are closely spaced and pale brown, visible on upturned specimens.

Minute, nearly black, circular to slightly oval discs with smooth surfaces and distinct margins, scattered and loosely clustered on a fibrous, light-colored plant stem. The dark fruiting bodies contrast sharply with the substrate, lacking visible scaling or brick-like arrangement.

Thin, crust-like pinkish to pale reddish layer with a membranous, web-like texture and irregular, diffuse margins. Integrates closely with adjacent greenish and yellowish patches, lacking distinct fruiting bodies or caps.

Two tiny, globose fruiting bodies with dry, brown, cracked surfaces and yellowish-white stalks. Each stands separately, with granular yellow material at the base and some darkened patches on the upper surface.
Two tiny, globose fruiting bodies with brownish-gray, cracked, rough surfaces, each atop a slender white stalk emerging from a shared base. The sporocarps are dry and measure about 1 mm in diameter.

Dense, coral-like cluster with thick, irregularly branched lobes. Predominantly pale yellow with deeper yellow tones near the tips. Surface appears smooth to slightly fibrous, and the margins are uneven and irregularly split.

Minute fruiting body with a rounded, brown cap featuring prominent blackish patches and a rough, irregular surface. Supported by a slender, pale yellowish to off-white stalk, with a clear separation between cap and stalk.
Tiny, pale beige to tan cup-like structures with a granular, matte surface. The fruiting bodies are upright, scattered, and have rounded to slightly irregular shapes with even margins.

Dark brown to nearly black, globose to irregularly rounded structures with rough, cracked, and scaly surfaces, clustered on brown needle-like plant material. Margins are uneven and irregular, resembling small, weathered cones against a white background.
A solitary fruiting body with a bright red, globose, moist and slightly lobed head atop a slender, straight, yellow stalk with a granular texture, emerging from a brownish surface.
Tiny, white, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies less than a millimeter wide, some with a central depression or pore, scattered and loosely clustered on a dark, rough surface.

Irregular, contiguous patches forming a thin, crust-like layer with a brownish, matte, finely velvety or slightly fuzzy surface. No distinct cap, stem, pores, or gills are visible. The fruitbody adheres closely to the substrate and appears uniform in texture.

Irregular, lobed fruiting body with a moist, yellowish surface and undulating margin. The upper surface is coated with granular soil particles, giving it a rough texture. The fungus appears gelatinous and blends into the surrounding green moss.

Irregular, white to cream fruitbodies with a spongy, porous underside. The upper surface is uneven, fibrous, and embedded with woody debris. Pores are small, round, and densely packed. Edges appear broken or torn, exposing the internal spongy texture.

Small, delicate mushrooms with smooth, light brown to cream convex caps and thin, even margins. Gills are pale brown and closely spaced. Stems are slender, white, and fragile, lacking any ring or volva. Clustered together with varying sizes.

Minute, pale yellowish circular structures scattered on a granular, slightly rough surface with a subtle sheen. The fruiting bodies are tiny, closely appressed, and lack prominent stalks or distinct margins.

Elongated, dark brown structure with a shiny, reflective surface. Several small, rounded black spots are scattered along its length. The surface is slightly textured, with smooth margins and a narrow, linear form.

A thin, smooth, slightly glossy white film closely coats the surface of the herbaceous stem, lacking any distinct texture, margin, or visible fruiting bodies, and blending subtly with the stem’s natural coloration.

Small, black, rough-textured fruiting bodies with irregular, angular to elongated shapes are scattered and partially embedded in the bark surface, contrasting against pale filaments and greenish patches.

Small, clustered fruiting bodies with irregular, lobed, fan-shaped caps in pale yellow. Caps appear matte and slightly granular. Slender stems of varying lengths are attached to clumps of soil at the base.
Three tiny, stalked fruiting bodies with globose orange-red heads featuring a cracked, polygonal surface. The stalks are pale yellow, tapering at the base, and the heads appear dry and granular.
Small, scattered fruiting bodies with irregular, wavy, and ruffled margins. Off-white to pale yellowish in color, thin and fragile in texture, loosely grouped among moss and organic debris.

White to cream, shelf-like clusters with undulating, ruffled margins and a soft, waxy, uneven surface. Fruiting bodies overlap and adhere closely to the wood, forming irregular, confluent masses without visible pores or gills.

Granular, uneven surface with greenish-olive tones, scattered with numerous tiny, rounded, dark blackish discs. The discs are slightly raised and irregularly distributed, contrasting with rough, crusty patches and some translucent yellowish areas.

Numerous small, brown, circular to irregular spots scattered across green, narrow leaflets radiating from a central point. The spots sometimes merge, creating patchy discoloration, while the surrounding leaf tissue remains green. No visible pustules or raised structures are present.

Small, globose brown sporangia with a distinctly netted surface sit atop short yellow stalks, emerging from a dark slender stem. The base of each sporangium is surrounded by a membranous, yellowish, slightly translucent material.

Numerous tiny, pale cream disc-shaped fruiting bodies densely cover dark brown, shriveled catkins. The discs are smooth, flat to slightly convex, and lack visible stems, creating a granular texture against the contrasting background.

Numerous tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with a vivid turquoise to blue-green hue and smooth, rounded edges are scattered across dark wood. The cups are translucent and vary in size, with some clustered together. White, fuzzy mycelium is visible near the base.

A single, small fruiting body with a round, slightly convex, pale yellowish cap and a granular surface. The slender, pale, slightly curved stem attaches laterally to dark, cracked wood. The cap margin is smooth and even, with no visible gills.

Two mushrooms with pale brown, convex to slightly flattened caps, one showing a subtle darker center. Stems are slender, elongated, and dark brown with a fibrous look. The right specimen displays widely spaced, pale gills beneath the cap.
A dense mat of minute, upright, white to pale hair-like structures covers the surface, forming a fine, velvety layer with a delicate, uniform texture and even distribution across the substrate.

Numerous minute, white, hair-like structures emerge in dense, scattered clusters across the dark wood surface. The slender, upright filaments form irregular tufts, giving a delicate, thread-like appearance without distinct caps or stems.

Broadly convex to flat caps with smooth, moist brown to tan surfaces and subtle lilac tinges at the margins. Stipes are robust, lilac to violet near the apex, fading to whitish at the base. Gills are crowded, brownish to lilac. Some caps show slight undulation.

Dark reddish-brown to purplish caps with a matte, uneven surface. Stems are robust, white, and solid. Gills are closely spaced, off-white to pale cream. Internal flesh is firm and white, clearly visible in the cut sections.

Deep reddish leaf marked by numerous irregular, pale tan to whitish spots with darker, reddish-brown margins. Lesions vary in size and shape, some merging into larger necrotic patches, disrupting the leaf’s normal coloration.
A dense mat of slender, upright, white, club-shaped fruiting bodies covers the surface, creating a frosted, fuzzy appearance with uniform height and coloration across the area.
A delicate mushroom with a slender, pale brownish-yellow stem and a small, smooth, orange-brown cap. The cap is convex to nearly flat, with closely spaced, pale brown gills visible underneath.

Two mushrooms with bright orange, convex to slightly flattened caps featuring fine striations at the edges. Gills are white to pale cream and free from the slender, pale yellow stems, which show a yellowish tint near the base.

Tiny, pale yellow to off-white, cup-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, matte surfaces. Scattered singly or in small groups, each with a short, slender stalk supporting the delicate disc atop dark, wet wood.

Numerous small, round, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, pale cream to white upper surfaces and vivid blue-green, finely textured margins. The apothecia vary in size and are scattered or clustered against a dark background.

Clustered mushrooms with convex, brown, scaly caps featuring a darker central disc. Cap margins are incurved in younger specimens, expanding with age. White to cream, closely spaced gills and white stems with brownish discoloration and a visible ring. Dry, textured cap surface.

Circular to irregular greenish-yellow lesions with darker, well-defined margins scattered across the leaf surface. Some spots appear slightly sunken or water-soaked, with surrounding tissue showing chlorosis and necrosis. The leaf is smooth and moist with visible venation.
Numerous tiny, pale cream to whitish, cup-shaped bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces and thin, even margins, densely clustered and emerging from a dark, moist substrate.

Two green leaves with scalloped edges display scattered, irregular dark spots. The left leaf is smaller and curled with pronounced distortion, while the right leaf is larger, flatter, and more regularly shaped. Lesions are dark and diffuse, lacking visible lighter centers.

Small mushrooms with brown, circular caps; the left cap is slightly depressed with a darker center and fine radial striations. The gills are broad and attached, ranging from deep to pale brown. Stems are slender, with soil clinging to their surfaces.

Light brown cap with a distinctly darker center, smooth surface, and convex to flat shape. White, closely spaced gills attached to a long, slender, light brown stem with faint longitudinal striations. No ring or veil remnants visible.

Slender, upright stalks with pale greenish-gray, granular surfaces end in irregular, cup- or trumpet-shaped apices. The cups have uneven, split margins and a rough, powdery texture. The structures are delicate and scattered in small groups.

Numerous minute, translucent to whitish disc-shaped bodies scattered on dark wood, each with a delicate, glassy appearance. Some discs have slightly scalloped or irregular margins and smooth to faintly textured surfaces, closely attached and sessile, emphasizing their tiny, fragile form.

Dense clusters of small, black, rounded bodies with a matte, pebbly surface. Some fruiting bodies display tiny central depressions. The overall texture is granular and dry, forming an irregular, crust-like layer.

Dense clusters of minute, black, spherical structures with a rough, granular surface tightly packed among thin, brown, needle-like debris. The black fruiting bodies form irregular, contiguous patches, sharply contrasting with the lighter plant material.

Crustose thallus forming irregular, contiguous patches of vibrant green. Surface is granular and powdery with a mealy texture, tightly appressed, lacking visible margins, lobes, or fruiting bodies. Fine structure evident at small scale.

Broad, fleshy caps with smooth, moist, light brown surfaces and darker streaks. One specimen shows closely spaced, vivid purple gills beneath the cap. Stems are robust, pale with subtle purplish tones, and have soil debris at the base.

A single upright, hollow, cylindrical structure with a rough, granular surface and light greenish-blue color. The tube’s margin is irregular and slightly crenulate, featuring small, pebble-like protrusions along the edge and outer surface.

White cap with brownish scales, striate and slightly irregular margin. Gills are free, crowded, and white. Stem is white with yellowish-brown discoloration, brownish scales, a persistent ring, and some bruising.

Solitary mushroom with a tall, slender, reddish-brown, finely fibrillose stem. Cap is broadly convex, light brown, subtly textured, and slightly inrolled at the margin. Underside shows closely spaced, white, smooth gills.

Numerous tiny, upright, cup- to tube-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, whitish to translucent surfaces are scattered in loose clusters across a dark, rough plant stem. The fruiting bodies are cylindrical, slightly flared at the apex, and distinctly separate from the substrate.

Numerous tiny, translucent white to light gray disc-shaped fruiting bodies with finely hairy margins are scattered and clustered across the rough, dark brown wood surface. The delicate, cup-like structures are less than a millimeter wide and appear fragile against the fibrous background.

Small, pale, cup- to disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, translucent to whitish surfaces. Margins are even and unornamented, with a moist, slightly glossy appearance. Fruiting bodies are sessile or have very short, inconspicuous stalks, scattered on woody debris.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex caps, white to tan background, and dense reddish-brown scales. Cap margins are inrolled in young specimens, expanding with age. Stems are thick, pale, and feature a persistent membranous ring. Gills are white and free, with a dry, scaly cap surface.
Small fruiting body with a slender, dark stem and a shallowly convex, pale cream cap. The cap margin is thin and slightly wavy, with a smooth or minutely textured underside.

Solitary mushroom with a convex, tan-brown cap featuring a finely hairy margin. The cap surface appears minutely fibrillose, and the slender, cylindrical stem is dark brown with a fibrous texture. Gills are not visible from this angle.

A dense patch of fine, upright, white hair-like structures forms a fuzzy, powdery mat across a darkened surface. The filaments are closely packed, giving a clavate, filamentous texture with a diffuse margin blending into the background.

Smooth, glossy stem with scattered, irregular dark brown to black spots. Each spot has a well-defined margin and a central, darker area. The surface is even and lacks any visible fuzz or hair-like structures.

Slender mushrooms with pale, fibrous stems and smooth, conical to convex caps in a light grayish-white shade. The gills underneath are distinctly dark bluish-green to gray, contrasting with the lighter cap and stem.

Medium to dark brown caps with a dry, fibrous texture, some cracked or uplifted at the margin. Gills are closely spaced and brownish. Stems are sturdy, pale brown above, darker and soil-stained at the base.
Mushroom with a thick, white stem bearing soil at the base, pale yellow crowded gills, and a smooth cap margin showing pinkish to pale red tones with scattered white patches.

Sturdy mushroom with a thick stem showing lilac to pale violet tones, fading to whitish at the base. The broad, smooth cap is brownish to violet-brown, and the crowded gills are pale lilac, matching the upper stem. Cap margin is smooth and slightly inrolled.
Small, dark brown mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, granular caps. Undersides reveal pale grayish, crowded, wavy gills radiating from slender stems, some partially covered with soil.

Broad, nearly flat cap with rich orange-brown color and paler, smooth margin. Densely packed, deep orange-brown gills are fully exposed. Robust, cylindrical yellowish stem with soil clinging near the base.

A thin, creamy white, crust-like patch with a smooth to slightly uneven surface and granular areas. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the substrate, and the texture appears closely appressed and irregular.

Two robust mushrooms with convex, grayish-brown to tan caps, matte and dry, one cut to show pale, closely spaced gills. Thick, solid stipes are bulbous at the base, pale, and fibrous, with soil remnants attached.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, pale lilac to light purple caps showing subtle radial streaks and a moist sheen. Thick, white stems display some brownish and purplish discoloration. Gills beneath the caps are closely spaced and light purple.

Cluster of small mushrooms with light brown, dome-shaped to conical caps featuring striate margins. Slender, pale stems support the caps, revealing brownish gills underneath. The caps are smooth and the stems appear straight and delicate.
Clustered, round fruiting bodies with reddish-brown, slightly rough surfaces. Each has a gelatinous plug or star-shaped opening at the apex. Short, dark stalks are partly hidden by moss and soil.

Mushroom with a deep red, matte cap featuring irregular white patches and an uneven margin. White, crowded, brittle gills are visible, some damaged. The robust white stem shows surface abrasions and bite marks.

Numerous rounded, globose structures with textured, ornamented surfaces cluster along a reddish-brown matrix. The spores appear translucent to light brown under the microscope, with distinct surface ornamentation visible.

Dense, white, powdery or crystalline coating forms irregular patches on dark wood. The texture appears granular and fluffy, with small, rounded, translucent structures scattered across the surface, sharply contrasting with the substrate.

Broad, convex to slightly depressed cap with reddish-brown, pinkish, and ochre tones. Surface is smooth, matte, and dry, with scattered blemishes, soil patches, and minor white spots near the entire margin.

Yellow-green to ochre, lobed surface with a granular texture. Scattered, small, circular to oval, orange to yellowish discs are slightly raised and have distinct margins, irregularly grouped on the uneven thallus.

Thin, flat, crust-like surface with mottled greenish-olive tones, scattered tiny blackish dots, and a distinct cluster of bright yellow-orange granules on the right. The texture is uneven and granular with irregular, blending margins.

Leaf displays scattered, irregular circular to oval lesions with pale tan centers and darker greenish margins. Necrotic areas appear thin, papery, and perforated, with reddish-brown, yellow, and tan hues. Margins are distorted and venation is visible.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to broadly umbonate caps in rusty orange-brown, smooth and slightly fibrillose. Gills are densely packed and deep rusty brown. Stems are pale with rusty brown fibrils, thickened at the base, and show soil remnants.

Irregular, crust-like patch with a pale yellow to ochre color, granular and warty surface, and scattered small, rounded pustules. The margin is diffuse and uneven, blending into the substrate. Organic debris, including a brown leaf, is present on the surface.

A continuous, vibrant green, granular surface densely dotted with numerous small, rounded, blackish structures. The black structures are slightly roughened and evenly scattered, contrasting sharply against the compact, crust-like green background.

A slender, dark brown stem supports a shallowly convex, pale cream cap with a slightly wavy margin and faint brown speckling. The cap surface appears smooth, and the solitary fruiting body stands out against the dark background.

Mushroom with closely spaced, white to off-white gills radiating from a central, cylindrical, light brown stem. Cap margin is slightly wavy and pale brown, with a smooth surface. Some soil and a grass blade cling to the stem base.

Small mushrooms with delicate, convex to bell-shaped caps showing pronounced radial striations. Caps are pale orange to golden-brown, with long, slender, slightly translucent stems paler at the base. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps.

Irregular pale tan to white patches with a powdery, slightly fuzzy texture cover the leaf surface, appearing sunken and bordered by veins. The lighter areas contrast with the surrounding green and brown, with fine leaf hairs and scattered dark debris visible.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex caps, white to light brown with darker scaly centers, free crowded white gills, and cylindrical stems showing brownish bruising. Soil and mycelium cling to the stem bases. Some caps are split, revealing gill attachment.

A single upright, pale, granular stalk with a slightly flared, cup-like apex. The cup margin is irregular, lined with small dark granules, and features a prominent red dot. The texture is distinctly granular.

Upright, pale green, cylindrical stalks with rough, granular surfaces end in jagged, crown-like tips. Bright red, rounded structures cluster at the tops, contrasting sharply with the green stalks. The stalks are densely packed, forming a compact, visually striking group.

Numerous small, black, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies densely clustered, with matte to slightly rough surfaces. Many show a tiny central opening at the apex. The fruiting bodies are firm, carbonaceous, and often in direct contact or slightly separated.
Nearly spherical, dark reddish-brown fruiting body with a smooth, gelatinous surface and a distinctive star-shaped opening at the apex. No visible stem.

Large, broadly convex cap with a smooth, shiny golden-brown surface. The margin is even and slightly inrolled, with a few small patches of debris adhering to the cap. Only a small part of the stipe is visible.

Mushroom with a robust, white cylindrical stem and closely spaced, pale yellow gills. The cap margin is deep reddish-purple, smooth, and slightly undulating. The cap surface appears smooth, and the gills are even and unbroken.

Three mushrooms with pale cream, crowded gills and long, robust stems. Caps are light brown to grayish-brown, convex to nearly flat, with darker, slightly depressed centers and a subtle radial texture. Margins are smooth, and no veil remnants are visible.

Tiny, white, smooth, rounded to slightly cup-shaped discs scattered along dark, weathered wood. The fruiting bodies are closely attached to the surface, lacking visible stems, and are arranged singly rather than in tight clusters.

Mushrooms with brown, convex to flat caps featuring a darker central disc and paler, striate, irregularly split margins. The cap surface is dry and fibrous. Gills are white to pale cream and crowded. Stipe is long, slender, and brown with a darker base.

Leaf surface with numerous circular to irregular greenish-yellow lesions, some with darker margins and central necrosis. Lesions are scattered and coalesce in places, giving a water-soaked, translucent appearance against the reddish-brown leaf.

Convex cap with purplish to lilac tones, smooth and moist surface, featuring a prominent brownish patch. Faint radial fibrils are visible, and the margin is slightly incurved. The robust stem shares the cap’s purplish coloration.

Numerous tiny, pale yellow to off-white disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, thin margins cluster on dark decaying material. The surfaces are translucent to opaque, some with slight brownish spots, and most are less than a centimeter wide.

Small, vivid blue-green, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, translucent surfaces and well-defined margins, clustered on a dark substrate. The apothecia have a gem-like luster and striking coloration, standing out sharply against the blurred background.

Mushrooms with convex white to cream caps densely covered in brownish scales, dry and scaly surface, and slightly incurved margins. Stems are robust, pale brown, some with bulbous bases. Sectioned specimens reveal white, fleshy interiors and free, closely spaced gills.

Numerous small, circular, disc-like bodies with smooth, pale interiors and distinctive blue-green, finely textured margins. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped, sessile, and have a matte surface, creating a striking contrast against the dark background.

Two mushrooms with convex to irregularly flattened caps, reddish-brown to pale tan in color, featuring wavy, split margins. Gills are crowded, cream to yellowish, and attached to thick, white stems. Caps are dry and covered with soil and debris.

Small, dark, disk-like fruiting bodies with rough, granular surfaces and irregular, slightly raised margins scattered across a pale, intricately branched, greenish-gray lichen thallus with occasional cup-like structures.
Irregular, pale off-white to tan patch with a granular or powdery texture, scattered small dark specks, and a diffuse margin blending into the surrounding green leaf tissue.

Sturdy, stocky mushrooms with robust, bulbous stems thickly coated in soil. Caps are convex to slightly flattened, pale to medium brown, with a finely fibrous or velvety texture and smooth margins. Stems show a gradient from lighter brown near the cap to darker at the base.

Numerous small, black, roughly spherical to slightly irregular structures densely clustered together, forming a contiguous matte and dry mass. The surfaces appear non-glossy, with well-defined margins, interspersed with fragments of plant material.

Close-up of a cap with pale lilac to grayish tones, moist and slightly fibrous surface, featuring a subtle yellowish discoloration at the center. The gills beneath are dark, appearing brown to purplish-brown.

Broadly convex to wavy caps with grayish-brown to violet-brown tones and frilled margins. Stems are robust, lilac to violet, with soil remnants at the base. Gills are closely spaced, attached, and pale brown to lilac. Smooth surfaces and varied sizes are visible.

Stout mushrooms with convex, light brown caps mottled with darker patches. Caps appear dry and slightly scaly. Thick stems match the cap color, with soil clinging to the base. Gills are closely spaced, pale lilac to brownish. Sectioned specimen shows solid, brownish flesh.

A tiny, pale cream to white, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, delicate texture and thin, even margin. The hymenium faces upward, and the fungus stands out amid vibrant green moss on a dark, moist branch.

A solitary, dark reddish-brown, globose fruiting body with a finely granular, velvety surface. The cap is topped by a small, ornamented peristome. The short, robust stipe matches the cap in color and emerges from the leaf-littered ground.

White, powdery or granular patches form within irregular, yellowish, slightly sunken lesions on a green surface. The lesions have diffuse yellow halos and fine whitish deposits, with surrounding tissue remaining green and smooth.

A single, hollow, cylindrical structure with a rough, granular, and fuzzy white surface. The margin is irregular and slightly frayed, while the interior appears smooth and pale. The overall texture looks delicate and possibly brittle.
Upright, slender, pale greenish-white cylindrical structures with rough, granular surfaces and rounded or slightly club-shaped tops, standing singly or in small groups among leafy fragments and moss.

Tiny, white, cup-shaped fruitbodies with short, slender stalks and smooth to slightly granular surfaces, scattered and spaced apart on a brown, furry substrate. The delicate apothecia have even, non-lobed margins and a translucent appearance.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with translucent, frosted margins and smooth, pale brownish discs. The delicate, crystalline edges and slightly raised rims give a brittle appearance. The cups are closely grouped and irregularly scattered.

Mushroom with a long, curved, light brown stem darkening and thickening toward the swollen base. Cap is convex with a dark brown margin. White, widely spaced gills are visible underneath. Stem surface appears granular or slightly scaly.

Clustered mushrooms with broadly convex to flat caps, featuring concentric zones of darker brown scales on a lighter background and a prominent central disc. Gills are white to cream and free from the robust, white stipes.

Convex to slightly flattened brown caps with a subtle violet tinge, especially at the margins. Gills are pale lilac to grayish and closely spaced. The robust, cylindrical stipe is pale with violet hues and soil remnants at the base.

Three small mushrooms with convex, moist, glistening brown caps showing faint striations and white veil remnants at the margins. Stems are slender, pale, and slightly translucent, emerging among twigs and mossy debris.

Mature mushroom with a long, slender, brown fibrous stem, darker and textured near the base. The white cap reveals broad, thick, widely spaced gills radiating from the stem, with prominent, well-developed gill edges.

Dense clusters of elongated, dark, needle-like structures radiate outward with a rough, textured surface. Numerous small, white, granular deposits are scattered across the glossy, dark brown to black spikes, which overlap and project in various directions.

Dense, brown, fuzzy basal mass with several thin, elongated, hair-like structures extending upward. The structures are translucent and outlined in blue, diverging from a common base and highlighted against a white background.

Small, translucent pinkish-lilac discs with smooth, gelatinous surfaces and slightly irregular margins, scattered irregularly on a dark, moist substrate. Some discs have brownish debris on their surfaces and are partially embedded, with green mosses interspersed nearby.

Tiny, scattered, pale to reddish-brown, pin-shaped structures emerge directly from the slender stem. The fruiting bodies are minute, smooth, and club-like, blending subtly with the substrate and lacking any prominent caps or gills.
Pale, smooth stem-like surface densely dotted with numerous small, dark, angular to rounded raised spots scattered irregularly across the light background.

Two mushrooms with smooth brown caps, one convex and one hemispherical, white striate stems, and pale, closely spaced gills. Soil and organic debris cling to the stem bases. The larger specimen measures about 7 cm tall.

Small, irregularly lobed clusters with a soft, gelatinous texture. Pinkish to pale violet and somewhat translucent, with moist, smooth surfaces and undulating margins. Some areas appear slightly granular or frosted.

Three mushrooms with smooth, grayish-brown convex caps, pale cream to yellowish slender stems, and broad, well-spaced creamy white decurrent gills. The caps show a subtle gradient toward paler margins.

Upright, branched structures with a pale greenish-gray, granular to scaly surface, bearing several irregular, contorted brown discs at the tips. The texture appears brittle and the podetia are loosely clustered above a granular base.

Green, narrow leaves densely coated with a uniform, whitish, powdery or downy layer. The fine, fuzzy texture obscures much of the leaf surface, giving it a pale, frosted appearance. No distinct structures are visible, just an even, powdery covering.

Two well-defined, brown lesions with slightly raised, textured surfaces and subtle darker margins on a green leaf. The centers are lighter and show fine, superficial structures. Lesions are circular to angular and separated by healthy tissue.

Two small, oval to cylindrical mushrooms with light brown, vertically ridged caps fading to pale edges. The caps are smooth and moist. Stems are slender, white, and slightly powdery, with both fruiting bodies closely grouped.

Tiny, upright, club-shaped fruiting bodies with slender, translucent stalks and pale pinkish to salmon, notched heads. The heads have a granular or velvety texture and are sparsely scattered on a dark substrate.

White, crusty patch with a rough, granular texture and scattered tiny dark holes along the leaf edge, bordered by yellow and brown discolored zones with additional dark necrotic spots and yellow halos.

Elongated, oval to cylindrical cap with prominent deep vertical striations, light brown and slightly translucent with a darker apex. Cap margin is even and slightly incurved. Slender, white, smooth stem supports the cap centrally.

Dense, white mat with both cottony and granular textures, featuring fine, fibrous hyphae and compact, powdery patches. The growth is irregular and patchy, with diffuse margins blending into the substrate and partially covering a honeycomb-like structure beneath.

Irregular, thin patches closely appressed to the surface, whitish to pale gray in color, with a granular to slightly powdery texture. Margins are indistinct, blending into the dark background, and patches are scattered and variable in size and shape.

Slender, upright fruiting bodies with a pale pinkish to flesh-colored hue, smooth surfaces, and rounded to slightly tapered tips. They are elongated, cylindrical, and scattered in a parallel arrangement along the brown stem.

Irregular, crust-like patches tightly attached to the surface, white to cream in color, with a compact texture and a distinctly poroid, honeycomb-like surface. Margins are uneven but clearly defined, forming contiguous patches.

Two slender mushrooms with smooth, light brown convex caps featuring paler, striate margins. Stems are long, thin, and white with a fibrous look. The upturned specimen reveals crowded, dark brown gills beneath the cap.

Green cylindrical stem with a smooth surface, scattered irregular brown spots, and numerous sharp, conical white thorns. No visible fungal fruiting bodies or structures; brown spots may indicate areas of damage.

Broad, rounded lobes with scalloped, undulate margins; upper surface transitions from pale tan-brown at the tips to nearly black at the center, rough and granular with scattered small white specks. Matte to slightly shiny appearance.

Yellowish-brown leaf with leathery texture and jagged edge, displaying scattered small, circular to irregular brown spots with darker centers and faint halos. Prominent veins and serrated margin accentuate the pattern of lesions.

Minute, pin-like fruiting bodies with slender dark stalks topped by rounded, dark brown heads emerge from a pale greenish to yellowish, powdery crust. The upright structures are scattered densely across the uneven surface.

Slender white stem with a finely powdery texture supports an elongated, cream-colored cap. The cap is cylindrical to narrowly ellipsoid, smooth, slightly moist, and marked by prominent vertical striations. Subtle translucency is visible, and the stem is straight and uniform.

Small, delicate mushrooms with light brown, smooth, convex to conical caps featuring striate margins. Slender, pale stems are relatively long compared to the caps. Gills are closely spaced and attached, visible on an upturned specimen. Clustered among moss and plant debris.

Broad, smooth, moist brown caps with subtle darker centers; margins slightly inrolled on younger specimens. Crowded dark brown gills visible on upturned mushrooms. Cylindrical, pale stems with surface debris. Clustered among glistening, decaying leaves and woody fragments.

Small, crustose patch with a granular, yellowish-green to brownish-green surface. Several minute, slender, dark stalks topped with rounded, blackish heads emerge in a clustered arrangement from the thallus.

Small mushrooms with slender, elongated light brown stems and convex to slightly umbonate caps. Caps are light brown with a fibrous or scaly texture. Crowded gills beneath the caps are pale to medium brown. Sizes range from about 3 to 7 centimeters.

Dark brown, crust-like layer tightly adhering to wood, with a moist, slightly glossy surface. The margin is diffuse and blends into the substrate, showing an irregular, patchy distribution and a smooth to slightly uneven texture.

Greenish-gray, foliose thallus with irregular, overlapping lobes closely attached to the branch. Surface appears granular to slightly powdery, with some lobes showing upturned or scalloped edges. Texture is rough, covering a large portion of the bark.

A sharply defined, nearly circular pale lesion with a whitish to cream center densely speckled with tiny black dots. The margin is irregular and subtly brown, contrasting with the surrounding green tissue. The surface appears matte and dry.

Tiny, nearly circular disc with a slightly raised, dark greenish margin and a smooth, pale grayish interior. The margin is well-defined and the fruiting body is solitary and minute on the stem surface.

Irregular, contiguous white patches with a matte, crustose texture cover the surface, interspersed with numerous tiny dark dots. The underlying tissue appears brown and necrotic where exposed, and patch margins are diffuse and uneven.
Dense clusters of minute, pin-like fruiting bodies with slender dark stalks topped by small, rounded brown to blackish heads, emerging from a powdery, pale greenish-yellow, crusty surface.

Small, tightly clustered mushrooms with slender white stems and rounded to bell-shaped caps. Caps are pale cream to light tan, matte, and distinctly grooved with prominent longitudinal striations. Gills are pale and closely spaced. Surfaces appear finely textured, with no signs of inky dissolution.

Multiple round, blackish, slightly raised fruiting bodies with cracked surfaces are scattered irregularly across the light brown bark. The fruiting bodies vary in size and are embedded in the branch, which is covered in prominent thorns.

Leaves display a thin, patchy, white powdery coating on their upper surfaces, forming irregular, diffuse, whitish areas that overlay the green leaf color. The powdery appearance is most pronounced along the midrib and veins.

Small mushrooms with long, slender, pale stems and rounded to hemispherical caps in shades of light to grayish-brown. Caps are smooth, some with slightly darker margins. Soil and wood debris cling to the base of each stem, highlighting their delicate structure.

Delicate, thin mushrooms with pale tan to whitish, conical to bell-shaped caps. Caps are distinctly grooved and somewhat translucent, with finely lined margins. Long, slender, pale stems support the fragile caps. Fruiting bodies are sparsely scattered among grass and plant debris.
Irregular, black, crust-like patches with a rough, warty, and cracked surface scattered along the bark. Some patches are slightly raised, forming discrete colonies on the woody branches.

Cluster of medium-sized mushrooms with convex, brown caps densely covered in whitish, fibrous scales. Cap margins are irregular and inrolled. Gills are crowded and ochre to yellow-brown. Stems are slender, grayish-brown, and finely fibrous, with slightly bulbous bases.

Two small, angular to irregular lesions with pale tan to grayish, slightly sunken and powdery centers. Each is sharply bordered by a dark margin, encircled by a yellowish-green halo and reddish discoloration on the smooth leaf surface.

Dense cluster of upright, irregularly branched greenish-gray podetia with a scaly, granular texture. Small, dark brown rounded apothecia are visible at the podetia tips. The surface appears rough and uneven, forming a compact mat interspersed with moss.

Slender mushrooms with pale, grooved stems and conical to bell-shaped caps. Caps are tan to pale brown with pronounced radial striations, darker at the center, and have translucent, finely grooved margins. Young caps are ovoid and deeply striated.
Numerous tiny, whitish to translucent, irregularly round patches with a gelatinous, glassy texture are scattered and loosely clustered on the rough, dark brown bark surface.

Numerous tiny, globose structures with a metallic silvery sheen sit atop slender brown stalks. The sporangia display a finely granular, glittering surface, some with visible cracks or openings. Arranged in loose clusters, each structure stands distinctly apart, highlighting their delicate, crystalline appearance.

Slender mushrooms with elongated white stems and small, light brown caps. Caps are conical to convex with distinctly striated, frilled margins. Crowded, light brown gills are visible beneath the caps. The surface of the caps appears smooth and delicate.

Dense, pale greenish-gray granular crust with numerous minute, dark pin-like fruiting bodies. Each fruiting body has a slender stalk topped by a rounded, dark head, scattered irregularly across the powdery surface.

A thin, continuous crust of bright yellow to orange-yellow, forming dense, granular patches with indistinct margins. The surface appears finely roughened, with small, rounded to irregular areas blending into the stone.

Leaves display a dense, white, powdery coating forming irregular patches across the surface. The powdery layer is unevenly distributed, giving the leaves a dull, matte appearance. Some leaves show minor holes and slight edge damage.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to flattened, light brown caps densely covered in coarse, fibrous scales. Cap margins are uneven. Cylindrical, fibrous stems are light brown, with granular material near the base. Gills are pale to light brown and crowded.

Small, delicate mushrooms with slender, pale stems and medium brown, convex to bell-shaped caps featuring pronounced striations along the margins. The closely spaced, lighter brown gills are visible beneath the caps. The surface of the caps appears smooth.

Small mushrooms with slender, pale whitish stems and light brown, convex to conical caps. Caps have prominent radial grooves, giving a pleated look. Gills underneath are closely spaced and pale brown. Surface of caps appears smooth.

Two mushrooms with smooth, convex light brown caps and slightly paler margins. Stems are white, sturdy, and coated with soil at the base. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps. The cap surface appears moist, with a small chip on the larger specimen.

Irregular, pale to white necrotic patches with sharply defined, dark brown to black margins cover the leaf. The affected areas appear dry, papery, and cracked, bordered by a narrow band of discolored tissue against healthy green leaf.

Small, thin, irregularly rounded translucent to whitish patches scattered across the bark surface. The patches appear smooth, moist, and gelatinous or membranous, closely appressed and lacking any significant thickness or raised structure.

Oval, pale lesion with a sharply defined dark margin on a leaf. The center is dotted with tiny black specks and features a small hole. The lesion appears slightly sunken compared to the surrounding yellowish-brown, hairy leaf surface.
Irregular, pale grayish lesion with a slightly raised, rough, and granular surface, surrounded by a darker, well-defined margin contrasting with the surrounding leaf tissue.

Cluster of small to medium mushrooms with smooth, moist, medium brown convex to bell-shaped caps. Cap margins are distinctly striate. Stems are slender, translucent to pale beige, and relatively long compared to the caps.

Two slender mushrooms with elongated, pale, fibrous stems and medium brown, conical to bell-shaped caps. The caps have paler, striate margins and smooth surfaces. Fruiting bodies emerge directly from the soil.

Leaf with extensive silvery-white, papery discoloration along the margins, scattered dark brown to black spots of varying size, and yellowing around the lesions. The surface is smooth, with pronounced central vein and severe damage at the tip and edges.
A thin, flat, greenish crust-like patch with a matte, finely textured surface and irregular, diffuse margins, closely adhering to the dark, moist background. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Dense, flat mat with a white base interspersed with brown and reddish-brown patches. Surface covered in numerous small, circular to oval pores, giving a spongy, granular appearance. Irregular margins and no distinct fruiting bodies or stalks.

Dense, irregular patch of nearly black, fuzzy growth tightly appressed to the surface, covered with numerous minute, bead-like granules. The colony appears bumpy and amorphous, with subtle brownish tones at the edges.

Broad, rounded lobes with a blue-green to gray-green leathery surface, scattered white spots, and wart-like outgrowths. A patch of vivid green material is present on one lobe. Margins are slightly undulate and the thallus appears closely attached.

Small mushroom with a brown, conical to convex cap densely covered in coarse, upturned scales, giving a shaggy appearance. The margin is irregular. The slender, slightly curved stem is coated with soil particles. No gills are visible from this angle.

A thin, flat, brown crust tightly appressed to the wood, with a finely granular or powdery texture and scattered minute white specks. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the substrate, and the growth is irregular and patchy.

Leaf with irregular, necrotic brown margins and a patchwork of light green tissue marked by numerous small, dark brown spots. Surface appears slightly wrinkled with prominent veins and visible cracking along the edges.

Small, black, rounded fruiting bodies scattered irregularly on a coarse, fibrous, golden-brown surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised with a matte to subtly glistening appearance, distinct from the textured background.
Dense clusters of tiny, nearly spherical, black to very dark brown fruiting bodies with a matte, minutely roughened surface, tightly grouped in irregular patches across a rough brown background.

Thin, patchy crust with a granular to slightly woolly texture, displaying grayish tones interspersed with brown and orange-brown areas. The surface is uneven, forming small, rounded patches tightly adhering to the substrate.
A crustose, granular greenish layer covers the bark, dotted with numerous minute, upright, dark pin-like stalks topped with rounded heads, scattered evenly across the rough surface.

Numerous slender, cylindrical fruiting bodies with smooth, pale cream to light pinkish surfaces. They stand upright or curve gently, unbranched with rounded tips, and are scattered or loosely grouped on a dark, moist background.
Circular cap with a dark brown, pronounced central disc, surrounded by a paler, radially fibrillose and velvety margin. Surface is matte and textured, with a mostly flat to slightly incurved edge.

Close-up of a mushroom's underside showing numerous thin, white, smooth gills radiating from a central stem. The cap margin is slightly wavy with a brownish tint, and the stem is slender, uniformly dark brown.

A solitary, nearly black, circular lesion with a rough, warty surface stands out against the smooth green stem. The margin is irregular yet well-defined, contrasting with the surrounding sharp, pale thorns.

White to off-white, crust-like growth with a granular texture, scattered with numerous small black dot-like structures. The surface is patchy with irregular margins and areas where the underlying substrate is exposed.

Broad, overlapping blue-green lobes with a leathery texture and scattered white spots. Lower surface densely covered in granular, powdery structures. Margins are undulate and irregular, with a layered, ascending arrangement.

Upright, branched structures with a rough, granular surface densely covered in small, pebble-like outgrowths. Predominantly grayish-green to brown, with some darker tips and irregular, bushy, compact branching.

Slender, upright greenish stalks with a granular texture, each topped by a small, rounded dark brown disc. The base shows overlapping, leafy green to pale brown scales, forming a dense, clustered arrangement.

Several tiny, slender, white, club-shaped fruiting bodies emerge upright and scattered along a thin, brown plant stem. The fruiting bodies are smooth, unbranched, and spike-like, lacking any visible cap or stem differentiation.

Tiny, dark brown to nearly black disc- to cup-shaped fruitbodies with slightly raised, well-defined margins and central depressions, matte surface, and smooth texture, scattered singly across the substrate.

Dense, irregular black crust composed of numerous minute, bead-like structures tightly clustered on pale, peeling bark, creating a rough, granular texture that sharply contrasts with the underlying wood.

Columnar, robust lichen with a dense, rough upper surface covered in granular, cauliflower-like soredia. The lower portion displays broad, flat, pale green lobes with undulate, irregular margins and a slightly glossy texture. The structure is tightly packed and distinctly three-dimensional.

A thin, pale grayish-white, crust-like layer covers the rough, weathered wood surface. The fungal growth appears matte, patchy, and uniform in color, with no visible fruiting bodies or distinct margins.

Circular to angular, tan to brown sunken lesions with dark, well-defined borders and faint yellowish halos scattered across a mottled green and brown leaf surface. Lesion centers appear matte and dry, with irregular distribution.

Upright, branched structures with a granular to scaly pale green surface, topped by small brown cup-like tips. The rough, uneven texture and clustered growth emerge from a mat of leafy squamules, creating a distinctly shrubby appearance.

A tiny, dome-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, gelatinous, and glistening surface. Its color is pinkish to violet, slightly translucent, and the margin is rounded and even. No distinct stipe is visible.
A thin, extensive, grayish-white layer with a cottony, fuzzy texture and finely granular to filamentous surface, loosely attached and forming irregular margins across the wood.
A single, circular to slightly irregular brown lesion with a granular, powdery surface and a faint diffuse margin, slightly sunken compared to the surrounding healthy green leaf tissue.
Minute, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with whitish, powdery surfaces and jagged, irregular upper edges, each perched on a slender, slightly branched stalk attached to decaying wood.

Slender, upright, club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, unbranched, cylindrical forms. They are pale to light brown and emerge directly from a moist, reflective substrate, spaced irregularly along its surface.
Pale woody branch with a rough surface, densely covered in sharp thorns. Scattered across the bark are multiple black, circular to irregular patches that contrast sharply with the lighter background.

Granular, crustose surface with greenish and yellowish patches. Scattered minute, erect, dark brown to blackish pin-like fruiting bodies on slender stalks, each topped with a rounded head. The thallus appears uneven, powdery, and textured.

Numerous tiny, black, punctate dots scattered irregularly across a smooth, pale stem surface. The dots are slightly raised or sunken, sharply contrasting with the light background. No large fruiting bodies or visible mycelium present.

Cluster of contorted, upright, pale greenish-grey branched structures with a granular surface. Brown, rounded to irregularly lobed apothecia are present at the tips, contrasting with the rough, uneven texture of the podetia.

Delicate mushrooms with slender, translucent stems and small, light brown to tan, umbrella-shaped caps. The caps are circular with grooved margins, slightly conical to convex, and spaced apart on a damp, leafy surface.

Numerous upright, slender, pale green stalks with granular texture, each topped by a smooth, rounded brown disc. Dense cluster emerges from a mat of small, leafy, yellowish-green squamules at the base.

Slender, elongated white stems support conical to bell-shaped, light brown caps with pronounced radial striations. Caps appear thin and translucent, with straight to slightly wavy margins. Gills are crowded, pale, and free from the stem, darkening with age. Delicate, fragile texture is evident.
Slender, elongated green stems with finely divided, feathery leaves; no visible surface growth, discoloration, or fungal structures apparent on the plant material.
