Delicate mushrooms with conical to bell-shaped, light to medium brown caps featuring striate margins. Slender, elongated white stems support crowded, attached gills beneath the smooth caps. The overall texture is smooth and the fruiting bodies are scattered.

Clusters of small, shiny, nearly black, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies partially embedded in rough, decaying, dark brown material. Some fruiting bodies display tiny apical openings. The surface appears lustrous and moist.

Dense clusters of small, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies with a granular, finely tomentose surface. The orange-brown coloration and velvety, powdery texture are prominent, with individual structures closely packed and margins indistinct due to the dense covering of fine hairs.

Dense cluster of upright, slender, dark hair-like stalks topped with tiny, rounded droplets and small spherical tips. The stalks glisten with moisture, creating a delicate, filamentous texture among green mossy foliage.
Two mushrooms with long, slender, light brown stems; one shows crowded pale tan gills, the other a moist, shiny, dark brown cap with a slightly wavy edge and smooth, sticky surface.

Dense, continuous crust composed of tightly packed, small, rounded orange-brown granules, creating a granular to velvety texture. Color varies subtly in lighter and darker patches, with no distinct margin or visible reproductive structures.

A cluster of pale, cream to off-white, slender finger-like projections radiates chaotically from a central mass. The projections are smooth, waxy, and irregular in length and orientation, lacking a distinct stem or cap.

Small, scattered mushrooms with convex to plane, medium to dark brown caps, some with pale margins and white powdery patches. Caps are striate, occasionally centrally depressed. Slender brown stems support the caps, and pale, decurrent gills are visible on an upturned specimen.

A compact cluster of small, rounded to irregular, cushion-like bodies with a granular to velvety brownish-gray surface. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped, attached directly to the substrate, and lack visible stalks or prominent margins.

Elongated, brownish, linear streaks split the green leaf surface, forming raised, crust-like lines with a granular texture. The margins of these streaks are irregular and slightly elevated, running parallel to the leaf veins.

Numerous small, black, cushion-shaped fruiting bodies with a velvety to fuzzy texture are densely clustered and irregularly scattered across the brown, textured wood surface. The margins of the fruiting bodies are indistinct, blending into the substrate.
Creamy white, finger-like cylindrical projections radiate outward from a central mass, appearing robust, smooth, slightly translucent, and somewhat curved, densely clustered on the host body.

Tiny, spherical to slightly irregular fruiting bodies with a light orange to yellowish hue and a granular, somewhat translucent surface. Scattered loosely, their margins blend subtly into the substrate, lacking sharp definition.
A dense mat of tightly packed, elongated, downward-pointing spines in pale tan and beige tones, creating a distinctly textured, shaggy surface with irregular, fused margins.

Dense, irregular patches forming a crust-like layer with grayish to whitish coloration. Surface appears granular to powdery, with some velvety areas. Margins are diffuse and blend into the substrate, lacking distinct fruiting bodies or caps.

Mushroom with a long, slender, rooting stipe covered in soil, a tan to ochre convex cap with a slightly depressed center and moist, translucent margin, and closely spaced pale gills attached to the stipe.

Dense, brown, powdery coating forming elongated, linear streaks along the leaf veins. The granular, loose texture appears in parallel lines, with coloration ranging from light to medium brown, restricted to the upper leaf surface.

Numerous small, black, shiny, elongated fruiting bodies with slit-like openings are tightly clustered and partially embedded in decaying wood, their glossy surfaces contrasting with the rough, fibrous substrate.

A thin, white, crust-like layer tightly adheres to the wood, with a finely granular to slightly roughened surface. The margin is diffuse and blends gradually into the substrate, showing a cracked or patchy appearance in places.
Small, rounded to slightly flattened reddish-brown fruiting bodies with distinctly fringed, spiky margins and granular, crystalline surfaces, clustered closely together.

Small mushrooms with thin, elongated, slightly curved pale stems and convex to nearly flat brown caps. Caps are smooth with faint striations near the margin. Gills are crowded and grayish-brown, visible on upturned specimens.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened pale yellow to ochre caps, some showing minor cracking and adhering debris. Gills are white to pale cream and closely spaced. Stems are robust, pale, and have white cottony bases with soil remnants.

Slender, translucent, thread-like stalks rise vertically from the substrate, each topped with a small, glossy, yellowish spherical head. The stalks are sparsely scattered and stand separately, contrasting against the darker, fibrous material below.

Small, dark, nearly circular fruiting bodies with granular surfaces and distinctly fringed or toothed margins, scattered across decaying leaf litter. Several bright yellow-orange, cup-shaped structures are also present nearby.

A single, elongated, dark cylindrical stalk rises vertically from a compact, irregular base with fine, radiating filaments. The stalk is smooth and uniformly pigmented, with no visible sporangium at the tip. The background is plain and white, highlighting the fungus’s structure.

Pale, cream-colored oval body with numerous thick, blunt, finger-like projections radiating outward. Surface appears smooth to slightly waxy, and the appendages are evenly spaced around the central structure.

Dark, roughened surface with numerous small, black, rounded to slightly elongated embedded structures. The texture is coarse and uneven, with visible cracks and irregular distribution of the black fruiting bodies across the area.

Convex to broadly convex caps with smooth, ochre to pale yellow-brown surfaces and paler margins. Sturdy, cylindrical stipes with pale coloring and visible surface fibrils. Exposed, closely spaced gills are pale to light brownish. Fruiting bodies in various stages of development.
Thin, brittle fragment with a tan to ochre, cracked, granular surface. The broken edge reveals a dark interior with patches of white, powdery material. Irregularly shaped and papery in consistency.

A dense, upright cluster of long, slender, black hair-like filaments forms a tangled, wiry mass. Tiny rounded droplets cling to the filaments, and small, rounded tips are visible at their ends, creating a chaotic, dark tuft above the green moss.

Thin, crust-like layer tightly attached to the surface, with a granular, uneven texture. The coloration is mostly grayish, interspersed with darker and lighter patches, and the surface appears slightly glistening. The margin is irregular and blends into the background.

Numerous small, rounded to slightly flattened, bright orange fruiting bodies with smooth to minutely textured surfaces, clustered together. Margins are entire and not lobed, and the vivid orange color stands out against the granular background.

Numerous tiny, rounded fruiting bodies with pale to tan exteriors and darker centers, some split open to reveal internal spore masses. Surfaces appear smooth to slightly granular, with well-defined margins and clustered arrangement.

Pale yellow to tan upper surface with a porous, granular texture, sharply contrasting with a dark, almost black lower layer. The surface appears spongy and uneven, with scattered dark patches and irregular margins.

Elongated, dark brown to rusty-brown powdery streaks and irregular aggregations run parallel along the green leaf surface, forming granular, linear deposits with diffuse margins closely following the leaf veins.

Slender, elongated pale stems with fragile appearance support conical to bell-shaped brown caps, some finely striate at the edges. Gills are grayish-brown and closely spaced, visible on horizontally positioned fruiting bodies.

Medium to dark brown, conical to convex caps with a slightly fibrillose texture. Caps are smooth and dry, with incurved margins on younger specimens. Gills are closely spaced and pale beige. Stems are slender, elongated, and pale, with soil clinging at the base.

Patchy, uneven surface with mottled green, yellow, and brown areas. Scattered minute, dark dot-like structures are dispersed across the substrate, with a granular texture and irregular coloration. Some exposed woody fragments are visible among the diffuse fungal growth.

Three mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, smooth ochre to yellow-brown caps, moderately spaced brownish-ochre gills, and pale cylindrical stems showing ochre staining. The caps appear moist and the stems have remnants of soil and moss at their bases.

Light green leaf with numerous irregular, dark brown to black necrotic spots and patches. Lesions are scattered, some merging into larger discolored, sunken areas with indistinct, uneven margins. Affected tissue appears dry and slightly depressed compared to surrounding healthy areas.

Long, slender, translucent stalks rise vertically, each topped with a small, dark, spherical head. The stalks are delicate, hair-like, and pale, with smooth surfaces and widely spaced, upright arrangement.
Numerous tiny, spherical, reddish-brown structures scattered across a moist, glistening pale surface. The spheres are slightly translucent, smooth, and shiny, standing out against the wet background.

Elongated, thread-like brown streaks run parallel along the green leaf veins, splitting the tissue and exposing narrow, embedded spore masses. The margins of the affected areas are sharply defined, following the leaf’s natural contours.

A continuous, thin white crust with a bumpy, granular surface and densely packed, small rounded protrusions. Scattered brownish patches are visible, and the margin blends gradually into the underlying material without a sharp edge.

Convex to slightly depressed caps with smooth, dry, yellow to ochre surfaces and subtle velvety texture. Crowded yellowish to ochre-brown gills are visible on one specimen. Stems are pale yellowish and slender. No veil remnants present.

A central mass with numerous elongated, slender, pale tan projections radiating outward. The projections are wiry, smooth, and irregularly spaced, giving a sparse, spiky appearance. The overall structure is held up for a detailed close-up view.

Green, elongated, linear leaves and a branched, spike-like flower head are visible. Surfaces appear smooth and healthy, with no visible discoloration, fungal growths, or distinctive structures present on the plant.

Small, round, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, well-defined margins and a waxy, translucent yellowish to pale green surface. Scattered and grouped, the apothecia have a smooth texture and lack visible ornamentation.

Irregular, compact black mass with scattered white patches and a dry, crust-like, brittle texture. Margins are uneven, and the surface appears granular or powdery in places. Small scale, held between fingertips.

Elongated, linear, slightly raised grayish to dark brown streaks run parallel to the veins on the smooth green leaf surface. Lesions are subtle and confined to the leaf tissue, with no visible fruiting bodies or spore masses.
Small, delicate cup with a flat, yellowish disc. The center is densely speckled with minute dark dots, and the margin is finely granular or minutely hairy, forming a well-defined edge.

Small, vivid yellow fruiting body with a conical to cup-shaped form and finely granular surface. The margin is even and slightly translucent. Several similarly colored, clustered fruiting bodies are visible in the background.

Dark brown to reddish-brown, matte, and finely granular surface with irregular shallow depressions and scattered small pale inclusions. The texture appears velvety, spreading flatly with no distinct edge or prominent structures visible.

Numerous long, slender, translucent hair-like stalks rise from dark, fibrous pellets, each topped with a tiny, dark, spherical head. The delicate, scattered filaments create a wispy, irregular appearance against the coarse substrate.

Irregular, thin, patchy crust with a granular to finely nodular surface. Cream to pale yellow granules are scattered within a whitish to grayish, diffuse matrix, closely appressed and blending into the dark wood.

Irregular, cushion-like patches with dull ochre to brown coloring, compact and crustose texture, some surfaces cracked or weathered. Margins are diffuse, blending into the rough, decaying wood. Fruiting bodies are scattered and not interconnected.

A dense tangle of upright, slender, dark filaments covered in glistening water droplets, with scattered small, yellowish spherical structures. The glossy, brush-like mat intermingles with bright green moss, highlighting the intricate, moist, filamentous texture.

Numerous minute, round to slightly oval, orange-reddish granules densely clustered on a dark, irregular surface. The fruiting bodies have a fine, granular texture and are distributed in small groups, creating a striking contrast against the substrate.

A cluster of minute, reddish-brown, spherical to slightly irregular fruiting bodies with moist, glistening surfaces. The structures are densely packed, with indistinct margins and a compact arrangement. No stalks or differentiated tissues are visible.
Three small, spherical, golden-brown structures with glossy, slightly translucent surfaces and a granular, sparkling texture. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped on a pale, fuzzy background.

Convex to slightly flattened caps with light brown tones and darker centers, dry and finely fibrillose surface. Pale, closely spaced gills underneath. White, robust stems with soil clinging to the base. One mushroom lies cap-up, others upright.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, medium to pale brown caps showing darker centers and smooth, inrolled margins. Stems are robust, off-white to tan with fibrous texture and brownish bases. Gills are closely spaced, pale brown, and attached to the upper stem.
Crust-like, reddish-brown surface with a polygonal, cracked texture. Slightly bumpy with scattered small pits and a single dark patch. The margin is irregular and blends into the substrate.
Smooth, moist, yellowish-brown convex caps with minor blemishes; densely packed brown gills; white to pale cream, cylindrical, smooth stems. Some caps show slight cracking or irregular edges.

Smooth, light brown to tan cap with subtle darker spots and a small, slightly depressed brown area at the apex. Cap is conical to bell-shaped with a rounded top and even margin. Pale, slender stipe visible; no gills shown.

Thin, crust-like patch with mottled grayish and pale tones, irregular white flecks, and uneven, patchy surface. The margins are diffuse and blend gradually into the decayed wood, with no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Long, slender pale ochre to tan stems with adhering soil, supporting ochre to tan, smooth, somewhat flattened caps. Brownish, closely spaced gills are visible on upturned specimens. Fruiting bodies are scattered among leaf litter, with straight, elongated stems and smooth to slightly uneven cap surfaces.

Clustered, irregularly shaped fruiting bodies with a blackish to very dark brown color and rough, cushion-like surfaces. The margins are indistinct, blending into the substrate, and the texture appears granular and slightly cracked.

Tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with pale yellow-green coloration and finely granular surfaces, featuring dark speckles inside. Smaller, bright orange cups are also present, all scattered and clustered on a background of decaying leaves.

Thick, robust stem with a bulbous, soil-encrusted base. Cap is brownish with lighter patches. Sectioned specimen reveals pale lilac to purple flesh throughout, with smooth stem surface and uniform internal coloration.

A dense tuft of upright, slender, blackish-gray, hair-like filaments rising from a central base, each tipped with tiny rounded heads. The cluster forms a striking, vertical, brush-like structure contrasting sharply with the surrounding green moss and grass.

Numerous tiny, upright, white tufts with a cottony, hair-like texture are scattered across a smooth brown surface. Each cluster appears soft and filamentous, forming discrete, rounded to slightly elongated shapes, loosely grouped but not densely packed.

Thin, fan-shaped fruiting bodies with wavy, lobed margins and a white to off-white coloration, growing in small, loose clusters. Surfaces appear smooth to slightly uneven, with overlapping caps and no visible stipe.

Minute, upright tufts composed of fine, white to pale filaments intricately interwoven into a netted, mesh-like surface. Each structure is cylindrical to ovoid, airy, and delicately spaced apart, with visible gaps between the filaments.

Irregular, diffuse patch of yellowish to brownish-green discoloration with a granular, powdery texture. Numerous minute, pale to whitish spots are scattered across the sunken lesion, blending indistinctly into the surrounding healthy green tissue.

Clusters of dark, nearly black, irregular fruiting bodies with rough, bumpy surfaces are embedded in elongated fissures. Some are surrounded by exposed brownish tissue, and the fruiting bodies appear granular and grouped within open cavities.

Numerous small, round to irregular blackish structures with a granular, glittery surface and slightly raised, well-defined margins are scattered across a rough, mineral-rich background. The fungal bodies display a reflective, metallic sheen.

Leaf surface shows multiple dark brown to black circular spots with diffuse margins, some encircled by yellowish halos and purplish discoloration. Spots vary in size, are irregularly scattered, and the surrounding leaf tissue appears chlorotic and necrotic.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, pale tan caps covered in fine scales. Cap margins are striate and slightly uplifted. Gills are white to cream, free from the slender, pale, fibrous stipes. Both cap and gill surfaces are visible in the cluster.

Clusters of tiny, spherical to pear-shaped fruiting bodies with finely netted, powdery light brown surfaces, each perched on slender dark stalks. The sporangia are closely grouped, displaying a delicate, reticulate texture.

Cluster of vibrant green, round to kidney-shaped leaves with serrated edges and a slightly wrinkled surface. Leaves overlap densely and appear healthy, with no visible discoloration, lesions, or fungal growth.
Broadly convex cap with a reddish-brown center fading to beige at the margin, finely fibrillose surface, and a slender, pale, fibrous stem with dark flecks and a slightly bulbous base.

Scattered minute, blackish, nearly spherical to slightly irregular bumps dot a fibrous, reddish-brown and tan surface. The structures are matte, partially embedded, and irregularly distributed, with no visible spore masses or mycelium.

Small, compact, tangled masses with densely branched, wiry, filamentous thalli. The color is predominantly blackish-brown with a rough, somewhat glossy surface. Clusters are irregular, tufted, and finely divided at the margins, lacking visible reproductive structures.

Tiny, round, white fruiting bodies with a distinctly fuzzy, cottony appearance. Each sphere is covered in fine, radiating hair-like filaments, giving a delicate, dandelion-seed-like texture against a dark background.

Leaves display numerous small, dark, circular to irregular spots scattered across their surfaces, contrasting with the green background. The spots are distinct and evenly distributed, giving a speckled appearance to the foliage.

Dense clusters of small, rounded, dark brown to nearly black granules are scattered across a yellowish to brownish-orange translucent background, forming subtle linear and radiating patterns with a granular texture.

Small, cup- to shell-shaped fruit bodies with dark grayish-brown, velvety upper surfaces and paler margins. Undersides show radiating, gray to dark gray gills with a frosted appearance. No visible stipe; attached laterally to the branch.

Small, irregular, tufted or cottony growths with a whitish to pale hue and darker, brownish centers. The surface is filamentous, tangled, and fuzzy, with delicate, hair-like textures and indistinct, irregular margins.

Small, clustered fruiting bodies with convex to bell-shaped caps, pale tan to light brown, densely covered in fine, darker granules. Caps have smooth, rounded margins. Stems are short, slender, and pale with a fibrous look. No prominent gills visible.

A dark, linear, powdery mass runs along a split grass stem, sharply contrasting with the pale, fibrous plant tissue. The infected area is elongated, granular, and sooty, with an abrupt margin against healthy tissue.

Delicate mushroom with a slender, smooth white stem and a cap showing closely spaced, light brown to tan gills radiating outward. The gills are free to narrowly attached, and the cap margin is even and smooth.

Circular, crust-like patch tightly attached to stone, pale grayish-green in color with a granular, cracked surface of closely packed, rounded to angular areoles. The margin is irregular yet distinct against the darker background.

Fine, powdery, whitish to pale greenish growth forming diffuse, irregular patches across the surface, blending with the underlying green and interspersed with visible leaf veins. The texture appears granular and slightly glistening, with no distinct margins or prominent structures.

Clusters of small, erect, dark brown to black, elongated fruiting bodies with rough, striate surfaces. White, cottony or powdery mycelium is visible at the bases and scattered across the substrate. The fruiting bodies are minute and irregularly grouped.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with thin, translucent white stems and small, pale, bell-shaped caps. The caps are faintly striated, and the mushrooms are scattered in loose groups across rough, fissured bark.

Clustered mushrooms with shiny, brown, convex to bell-shaped caps featuring white, powdery or fibrillose margins. Pale, closely spaced gills and slender stems also display white, powdery remnants. Caps appear moist and reflective.

Small, fragile mushroom with a slender white stem and a pale cap featuring prominent black radial grooves. The cap margin is strongly curled upwards, exposing dark, closely spaced gills beneath. The cap surface appears wrinkled and striate.

Small mushroom with a convex, light brown cap featuring a finely fibrous texture and a slightly darker center. The slender, pale stem is slightly curved and bears some soil particles. No gills are visible from this angle.

Minute, stalked fruiting bodies with globose to pear-shaped heads, each supported by a slender, dark stalk. The sporangia have a brownish, net-like, reticulate surface texture and are less than a few millimeters tall.

Two small, dark brown, ovoid bodies densely covered in long, white, hair-like filaments radiating outward, giving a rough, shaggy appearance. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped on a pale, slightly textured surface.

Two tiny, white mushrooms with slender, short stems and smooth, ovoid caps. The caps are slightly granular and off-white, with some adhering debris. Each fruiting body stands alone, emerging from a mat of decaying plant material.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, light brown caps featuring a darker central disc and striate, translucent margins. Stems are long, slender, and pale with a fibrous texture. Gills are pale to light brown and attached.

Dense clusters of tiny, upright, whitish to pale gray tufts with a fuzzy, filamentous appearance. Each structure is granular or powdery, closely spaced yet distinct, lacking clear cap or stalk differentiation, and forming irregular margins across the surface.

Delicate, thread-like stalks rise vertically from a dark surface, each topped with a small, fuzzy, grayish-brown to white tuft. The stalks are slender, smooth, and either straight or gently curved, with powdery or tufted apical heads spaced apart.

Broad, grayish-brown caps with irregular white patches and slightly fibrous texture. Cap margins are undulating and irregular, with one cap overlapping the other. A portion of the white stipe is visible beneath the caps.

Irregular, lobed caps ranging from pale cream to reddish-brown, with finely tomentose surfaces and wavy margins. Undersides display prominent spines. Slender, fragile stipes elevate the caps above moss and debris.

Several thin, white to off-white, fan-shaped fruiting bodies with wavy, irregular margins and smooth to slightly wrinkled surfaces are scattered on a mossy tree stump. The fruiting bodies are small, delicate, and appear resupinate to effused-reflexed.

Small, bell-shaped to convex caps with pronounced gray striations and scattered brownish granules, supported by slender, translucent white stems. Exposed gills are dark and radially arranged, with caps showing various stages from closed to expanded.

Dense mat of tightly packed, conical to spiky protrusions with a granular, crystalline texture. Color transitions from white at the tips to grayish at the base, giving a soft, velvety, cotton-like appearance. Growth is irregular and patchy, conforming to the surface contours.

A diffuse, brownish patch with a granular, powdery texture covers the leaf surface. Numerous tiny, whitish specks are scattered across the lesion, and fine, elongated leaf hairs are visible throughout the area.

Numerous tiny, white, fuzzy tufts with a delicate, feathery appearance are scattered irregularly. Each tuft forms a loose, upright cluster with soft, cottony texture and wispy, diffuse margins blending into the brown surface.
White, fan-shaped fruiting body with wavy, irregular, and lobed margins. Surface appears dry, slightly rough, and creamy to light brown. The fungus stands out against a mossy background.

Convex to hemispherical caps, medium brown and densely covered with white, fibrous scales, giving a shaggy, textured appearance. Margins are even and slightly incurved. Three fruiting bodies are closely grouped, with stipes mostly hidden by the substrate.

Slender, elongated stipe supporting a small, irregularly rounded cap with undulating margins and a textured surface. The underside of the cap features fine, downward-pointing spines. Overall appearance is delicate and fibrous.

Broad, convex to flattened caps with shiny, viscid light brown surfaces and darker moist centers, often covered in plant debris. Margins are smooth and slightly incurved. Gills are closely spaced, pale tan, and attached to off-white cylindrical stipes with brownish bases.

Small, rounded, orange to yellowish-orange textured structures scattered on a dark, leathery surface with an undulate, irregular margin. The fruiting bodies are globose and distinct against the darker background.

Irregular lesion on a green, hairy leaf, displaying brown, reddish-brown, and yellowish tones with a granular texture and slightly raised, uneven edges. Fine pale structures are visible at the lesion’s periphery, blending into the leaf’s dense trichomes.

A small, dense cluster with a brownish-pink hue, appearing compact and granular with a powdery, tufted surface. The fruiting mass is tightly aggregated and stands out against the rough wood background.

Two tiny, hemispherical to subglobose caps, pale cream to light tan, densely speckled with fine dark brown granules. Smooth outlines with even margins, stems mostly hidden by the fibrous, organic substrate. No gills or splitting visible at this stage.

Leaf with irregular, brownish necrotic spots and patchy discoloration. The brown areas appear dry and papery, contrasting with the remaining green tissue. No visible fruiting bodies. A finger provides scale for the small, affected leaf.

Clustered mushrooms with broadly convex to irregularly flat, wavy caps. Surfaces are light brown to grayish-brown with irregular white patches and smooth to slightly fibrous texture. Caps overlap densely, some with minor holes or abrasions.

Clusters of small, dark brown to nearly black, elongated structures with pointed tips, surrounded by fine, white, cottony tufts of mycelium on a rough, granular brown surface. The fungal bodies appear slightly fuzzy, with mycelial patches scattered around them.
Two tiny fruiting bodies: one with a slender, translucent stem and a pale, pleated cap; the other oval and pale, both delicate and fragile, emerging from moist, decaying plant material.

Numerous white, pendulous, icicle-like projections hang closely together, forming a dense mat. The structures are soft, somewhat translucent, with irregular, pointed margins and a smooth to slightly uneven surface, standing out against a dark background.

Pale, rough stone surface scattered with numerous tiny, black, rounded dots. The black structures are irregularly distributed, and the overall texture is granular and crust-like, blending with beige to grayish tones.

A tiny mushroom with a slender, translucent white stem and a small, pale brown cap featuring pronounced radial grooves and a slightly upturned, pleated margin. The cap surface appears moist and delicate.

Small, delicate cap with prominent radial grooves and a distinctly pleated, scalloped margin. Cream to pale tan color with fine brownish speckles across the surface. Slender, pale stipe partially visible.

Small mushroom with a brown, convex, smooth cap and slightly uneven margin. Underside shows dark, closely spaced gills. The slender, white stem is slightly curved and fibrous. Height is about 23–24 millimeters.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with smooth, pale to light tan convex or bell-shaped caps and thin, fragile stems. The caps appear slightly translucent and are scattered in small clusters across rough, moist bark.

Irregular, lobed white fruiting body with a thin, even margin and a soft, porous texture. The upper surface is densely covered in fine, regular pores, giving a spongy appearance. Some soil and organic debris are attached at the base.

Extensive, pale gray to off-white, powdery and granular growths form irregular, dense patches with uneven, diffuse margins on the soil and around plant bases. The texture appears crustose and compact, lacking visible cottony or filamentous structures.

Delicate cluster of mushrooms with slender, pale grayish-white stems and flat, pleated caps. The caps are white with subtle beige centers and pronounced radial striations, giving a finely textured, fragile appearance.

Numerous slender, dark, hair-like stalks rise from a brown, fibrous surface, each topped with a tiny, rounded black head. The stalks vary in height and are scattered irregularly, creating a delicate, miniature forest appearance.

Two ovoid, white, cottony structures with a fluffy, granular surface and small brown protrusions. The surface appears densely covered in fine, powdery material, giving a soft, woolly look. Margins are irregular yet distinct, and the fruiting bodies are closely grouped.

Delicate mushrooms with very long, slender, translucent white stems and small, pale grayish caps. The caps are convex to nearly flat, distinctly striate, thin, and fragile, with finely lined, slightly translucent margins. Fruiting bodies are scattered and vary in size.

Tiny, spherical fruiting bodies with metallic green, gold, and purple iridescence sit atop slender, dark stalks. The sporangia are finely textured and reflective, scattered loosely and measuring about 1 mm tall.

A single, slender dark brown stalk supports a pear-shaped sporangium with a delicate, translucent, net-like upper surface. The lacy peridium features numerous nodal thickenings, creating an intricate, reticulate pattern. The overall structure is minute and finely detailed.

A dense cluster of tiny, nearly spherical bodies about 1 mm wide, pale grayish-white with cracked, segmenting surfaces. Subtle iridescent sheen and fine, net-like threads emerge from the ruptured fruiting bodies, giving a crystalline, delicate appearance.
Small, spherical to subglobose fruiting bodies with a distinctly granular, warty surface and medium to dark brown coloration, closely attached to the substrate. No visible cap or stem structures.
The branch surface is greenish to dark, covered with numerous small, black, irregularly shaped bumps scattered along its length, giving it a rough, uneven texture.

Two tiny, delicate mushrooms with smooth, pale convex to bell-shaped caps and slender, light stems emerge closely together from a deep crevice in rough, furrowed bark. Their fragile appearance contrasts with the coarse, textured background.

Dark brown to blackish, linear to slightly curved swollen streaks run along the length of the grass stem, splitting and distorting it. The surface of these streaks is rough and irregular, with indistinct margins contrasting against the pale, dried grass.

Delicate, slender white stems rise from the substrate, each topped with a tiny, pale, umbrella-shaped cap. The caps are smooth, striate, and convex to nearly flat, some showing slight inky edges. Fruiting bodies are scattered and emerge at various angles.

Numerous minute, dark, round to oval fruiting bodies with rough, granular surfaces are scattered irregularly across a pale, mottled background. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised and have well-defined margins, contrasting with the granular, uneven surface beneath.

Cluster of small, dark brown to nearly black structures densely packed along a thin branch, with a rough, bumpy surface and numerous minute, raised, wart-like projections. The elongated mass appears irregular and textured.

A delicate, slender white stem supports a small, pale, bell-shaped cap with pronounced radial striations and a scalloped margin. Several immature, ovoid primordia cluster along the moist, decaying plant stem.

Small, spherical fruiting bodies with a metallic, silvery-gray sheen sit atop slender, dark stalks. The smooth, reflective spheres are closely clustered, with delicate, straight stalks highlighted against a blurred background.

Irregular, dark gray to brown lesions with a mottled appearance on a light green leaf. Several small, dark, circular structures are visible within the lesions, contrasting with the surrounding healthy tissue.

Numerous small, upright, globose fruiting bodies with a metallic silvery sheen, each elevated on slender dark stalks. The smooth, reflective sporangia are densely clustered, creating a striking, gregarious appearance across the substrate.

Clustered mushrooms with medium brown, dry caps bearing a fine whitish, hairy coating and paler margins. Two fruiting bodies show closely spaced, pale gills and slender, pale stems, some with adhering soil and debris. The caps have a frosted, fibrous appearance.

Slender, erect, hair-like stalks topped with compact, elongated, pale beige heads. The heads have a distinctly fuzzy, powdery texture and a brush-like appearance, standing singly or in small scattered groups against a dark background.

Cluster of slender mushrooms with elongated, white fibrous stems and grayish-brown, shaggy caps. Cap margins are striate and inrolled. Crowded, pale gills are visible beneath the caps. Fruiting bodies appear delicate and slightly curved.

Dense, coral-like clusters with numerous upright, slender, intricately branched projections. Vibrant yellowish-orange coloration, smooth to slightly granular surface. Branch margins are irregular and somewhat flattened, with blunt to slightly pointed tips. Clusters vary in size, forming prominent central and smaller groupings.

Clustered mushrooms with brown, granular, frosted caps and whitish margins. Stems are slender and coated with fine granules. One cap is upturned, showing crowded, pale gills. Numerous small, button-like immature fruitbodies surround the mature ones.

A compact, dome-shaped mass with a rough, granular, powdery white surface. The structure appears dense and hemispherical, closely pressed to the base of a plant stem, with no visible stalk or distinct reproductive structures.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with thin, translucent white stems and grayish, pleated caps. The cap margins are deeply grooved and scalloped, with a slightly inrolled edge. The gills are visible from below, and the overall texture appears smooth and fragile.

Numerous small, rounded orange structures are scattered across a matte, green, granular surface. The orange spots are slightly raised and evenly distributed, standing out against the textured background.

Delicate, slender white stems support tiny, pale, bell-shaped caps with pronounced radial striations. The caps are smooth and translucent, and the fruiting bodies appear fragile, thin, and loosely scattered across the fibrous substrate.

Two mushrooms with broad, glutinous, light brown caps—one showing a moist, shiny surface with debris and a wavy margin, the other displaying closely spaced brown gills and a cylindrical, off-white stem with brownish discoloration.

Dense, coral-like clusters with upright, intricately branched arms. The base is white, fading into vibrant yellow-orange tips. Branches are smooth, somewhat flattened, and end in rounded, irregular tips. Multiple fruiting bodies are closely packed together.

Irregularly rounded, translucent to pale off-white structure with a granular, faintly striated texture. The margin is diffuse and blends into the background, with a slightly uneven surface and no visible hair-like projections.

Dense, overlapping cluster of semicircular to irregular fan-shaped caps, white to cream in color with a velvety to slightly rough texture, faint concentric zones, and wavy, lobed margins. Thin fruiting bodies with some debris on the surface.

Fan-shaped, sessile fruiting bodies with wavy, irregular margins. Surfaces are dry, white to off-white, and slightly fibrous, with some brownish areas at the base. Largest specimen measures about 7 cm across. No visible stems.

Dense, intricate network of fine, thread-like stalks radiating from a central point, each ending in a small, rounded, dark sporangium. The sporangia form a delicate, lacy, web-like spherical cluster with primarily dark brown to black coloration.

Two small, delicate mushrooms with slender, translucent stems and pale, conical caps. The caps display fine radial striations and are covered in minute, granular scales, giving a subtly textured appearance. The margins are even and smooth.

Irregular, pale whitish patches cover the green leaf surface, appearing as diffuse, powdery or slightly felted spots with indistinct margins blending into the healthy tissue. No prominent structures are visible.

Leaf surface shows numerous small, round to irregular black spots with faint yellowish halos, scattered randomly. The spots are well-defined and dark, contrasting against the pale, slightly wilted and discolored leaf tissue.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped, pale grayish-white caps featuring fibrous, shaggy surfaces and subtle radial striations. Slender, white stems show a faintly powdery texture, with white mycelium visible at the base.

A compact cluster of small, pinkish-orange fruiting bodies with a granular, powdery texture. The structures are tightly grouped, cylindrical to oblong, and appear slightly fuzzy, emerging directly from decaying wood.

Clustered mushrooms with convex, medium to dark brown caps densely coated in a whitish, woolly layer, especially at the margins. Stems are short, robust, and similarly shaggy, with fruiting bodies at various developmental stages.

Green, elongated fruits with ruptured areas exposing dark brown to black, powdery and granular masses. The fungal growth distorts and discolors the fruit, with sori breaking through the smooth, glossy surface.

Numerous upright, slender stalks with shallow, cup-shaped tops. The cups are pale green to greenish-grey, with granular surfaces and irregular, frilled margins. Some cups show a faint pinkish hue inside. The group forms a dense cluster among mosses and small plants.

Small, round to irregular black fruiting bodies scattered densely across a green, rough-textured surface, with a few translucent to white granular bodies also present. The dark, slightly raised spots contrast sharply with the lighter background.

Dense, crustose mat with irregular, lumpy surface. Bright yellow and orange dominate, interspersed with brown, white, and greenish patches. Numerous small, rounded, powdery or granular outgrowths cover the uneven, granular surface.

Chain-like clusters of dark brown to nearly black, bean-shaped sporocarps with a matte, slightly roughened surface, forming an irregular, sinuous line along the wood. The fruiting bodies are closely connected and have a firm, leathery appearance.

Small, dark brown, oval to round raised pustules scattered irregularly across smooth green leaves, some surrounded by faint yellowish halos. The spots are well-defined and slightly elevated above the leaf surface.

Cluster of green, lobed thalli with crisp, irregular margins and scattered black specks. Several bright red, globose structures stand out on the right, contrasting with mossy elements and a dark, textured background.

Leaf surface covered with numerous small, rounded, blister-like swellings that are light green and slightly translucent, contrasting with the darker green healthy tissue. The swellings are smooth, irregularly distributed, and concentrated near the edges, with no visible external structures.

Pale, granular surface densely dotted with numerous small, black, rounded to angular spots. The black structures are slightly raised and irregularly scattered, contrasting against a yellowish to pale green background.
Small, yellowish, globose fruiting bodies with a powdery surface, each perched on short, slender stalks and clustered loosely on dark, decaying wood.

Numerous minute, round to irregular, cap-like fruiting bodies scattered densely on a pale, fibrous surface. The fruiting bodies are brown to tan, with a fuzzy or velvety texture, some showing slightly raised margins and central depressions.

Delicate, slender white stems topped with small, smooth, translucent caps form a tight cluster. The caps are rounded to slightly conical, resembling tiny umbrellas, and the overall appearance is graceful and fragile.

Numerous minute, circular to irregular brown-tan discs with distinct margins and a velvety or granular texture, scattered or loosely clustered on a pale, fibrous background. The cup-like fruiting bodies contrast with the substrate and are densely arranged in some areas.

Fine, powdery whitish coating covers the leaf surface, with numerous tiny, dark, dot-like structures scattered across the area, especially along the veins. The texture appears delicate and superficial.

Upright, slender stalks expand into shallow, cup-shaped tops with rough, granular pale green surfaces. Cup margins are irregular and adorned with small brownish dots. Stalks cluster together, showing a powdery texture throughout.

Irregular patches of white, powdery growth scattered across the green leaf surface, forming diffuse, slightly raised areas with a fine, powdery texture. The fungal colonies are most concentrated along the central and lateral veins, contrasting with the smooth leaf.
Two slender, dark stalks each support a rounded, dark green to black head with a densely granular, pebble-like texture and a slightly glossy surface, resembling miniature trees or lollipops.

Numerous slender, elongated, and branched pale brown structures radiate outward in a tangled cluster, interwoven with fine, fibrous mycelial threads. Small, rounded yellowish bodies are scattered among the dense, bushy fungal growth.

Numerous tiny, pale brown to tan, globose fruiting bodies with a powdery surface are borne on slender, dark, hair-like stalks. The sporangia are scattered and loosely grouped among greenish and brownish plant debris, appearing uniform in size.

Clusters of raised, irregular brown pustules rupture through the green surface, forming crusty, dark brown patches with lighter, slightly swollen margins, arranged in a scattered, linear pattern along the plant organ.

Three bell-shaped caps with pronounced radial striations, pale grayish to off-white with a tan center. The smooth caps show small holes or damage. Slender, pale stems support the caps above dark soil and leaf litter.

Minute, dark, spherical to ovoid heads sit atop slender, translucent stalks, scattered densely across the surface. The heads are darkly pigmented, while the stalks are pale, giving a granular, punctate appearance with a slightly glistening texture.

Minute, white to off-white, globose fruiting bodies with a granular surface, scattered and emerging from a dark, moist background. No visible stipes or filaments; the structures appear compact and slightly irregular in shape.

Slender, pale, threadlike filaments emerge irregularly from a brown, shiny exoskeleton. The fungal growths appear delicate and matte, contrasting with the glossy surface of the host remains. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.
Numerous tiny, white, round to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered and somewhat clustered along a dark, moist-looking stem. The surfaces appear smooth and soft with entire, unlobed margins.
Dense layer of minute, rounded yellow to orange granules covers the surface, creating a granular, powdery texture with scattered darker brown patches and a slightly moist, glistening appearance.

A localized, irregular brown patch with a granular, slightly glistening texture blends into the surrounding green leaf. The lesion is flat and lacks distinct fruiting bodies, with the brown color concentrated at the center.

Convex to slightly flattened brown caps with a matte, dry surface. Stems are robust, cream to pale yellowish with brownish stains and soil at the base. Gills are densely spaced, attached, and pale lilac to pinkish. Cap margins are smooth and uncurled.

Irregular, crust-like patch tightly attached to stone, composed of small, angular to rounded areoles in bright yellow to yellow-orange. Scattered darker orange disk-like structures are visible across the surface. The margin is diffuse, blending into the stone.

A cluster of thin, brownish, clavate and filamentous outgrowths with a matte, textured surface, irregularly arranged and interspersed with fragments of exoskeleton and mycelial debris. The scene is intricate and visually complex.

Tiny, delicate fruiting body with a smooth, dome-shaped white cap and slightly scalloped margin. The slender, translucent stem appears fragile and smooth, supporting the solitary cap among dried plant stems.

Numerous small, rounded to irregular, flat disc-like bodies with brownish centers and paler, slightly raised margins are scattered and clustered on a textured, fibrous surface. The apothecia appear granular and closely grouped, some merging at the edges.

Dense patches of yellow-orange lichenous material covered with scattered, irregular tan to brownish fuzzy or granular outgrowths. The surface is uneven, matte, and powdery, with diffuse margins blending into the substrate. Rounded and lobed structures are visible throughout.
Dense canopy of large, palmate green leaves with some minor brownish spots; no visible fungal growth or powdery patches apparent on the leaf surfaces.

The leaf displays irregular, blister-like swellings and mild undulations, with subtle discoloration and mottling. The surface is green and slightly glossy, with clearly visible veins and a wavy margin. No sharply defined spots or necrotic lesions are present.

A dark green leaf with serrated edges, displaying irregular white, powdery patches mainly on the left side. Some brownish spots are present, and the powdery coating appears fine and superficial, lacking visible fruiting bodies.

Upright, slender, pale green stalks with small, cup-shaped tops. The surface is granular or powdery, and the cup margins are slightly irregular. Multiple stalks emerge densely from a common base with dark organic matter.

Small, rounded to irregular black fruiting bodies scattered across pale green to yellowish-green, lobed surfaces with slightly undulate, scalloped margins. The surface appears granular, and the black dots contrast strongly with the lighter background. Lichen lobes overlap densely, with some white areas at the edges.

Thick, shelf-like brackets with a cracked, dark greenish-black upper surface and broad, pale yellow to off-white, undulating margins. The texture appears hard and woody, with overlapping tiers along the wood.

Tiny, delicate fruiting bodies with slender, elongated stems and small, dome-shaped caps. Both stems and caps are covered in fine, whitish tomentum, giving a frosted, powdery appearance. Caps are pale, matte, and evenly margined, with a soft, velvety texture.

Palmate leaves display a conspicuous grayish-white, powdery coating on their upper surfaces. The powdery layer is fine, diffuse, and uniform, variably covering large portions of the leaf blades and giving a frosted appearance.

Numerous small, disc-shaped to irregular, grayish-olive to pale greenish fruiting bodies with a smooth, slightly gelatinous and translucent surface are scattered and clustered along a dark, moist stem. The apothecia are sessile with even, non-raised margins.

Small mushrooms with pale, slender stems and caps that are initially rounded and densely textured, becoming convex to nearly flat with pronounced radial grooves. The cap surface is smooth and almost translucent, with a delicate, whitish to tan coloration.

Delicate mushroom with a slender, pale, translucent stem and a conical, light brown to grayish cap. The cap features prominent vertical striations and an irregular hole on one side, with a smooth surface and slightly uneven margin.

Leaflets display a dense, powdery, silvery-white coating that obscures the green surface, creating a frosted appearance. The coating is uniform and superficial, with some leaf edges showing browning and slight curling.

Small, irregularly shaped brownish to reddish-brown clusters with a granular, slightly fuzzy texture, scattered as minute patches on a pale, featureless background. No visible stalks or differentiated fruiting bodies are present.

Irregular yellowish lesions and diffuse chlorosis appear along the veins and margins of the leaf, forming coalescing patches. The leaf surface remains smooth with no visible fruiting bodies or external growths.

Thick, hoof-shaped fruiting bodies with a rough, cracked brown upper surface and layered zones. The pore surface is finely pored, yellowish-brown, and velvety, with an undulating margin. Robust, perennial structure and sessile attachment are evident.

Upright, pale green to grey-green cup-shaped structures with irregular, sometimes jagged margins. Surfaces appear matte and slightly rough. Cups vary in size, some with minor splits or uneven rims, scattered singly or in small clusters among moss and small plants.

Dense clusters of small, round, yellowish-orange spheres embedded in a moist, glistening, spongy matrix. Fine, filamentous threads weave between the closely packed, slightly translucent fruiting bodies, creating a bubbly, compact appearance.

Clusters of green, swollen, and irregularly shaped fruits with smooth surfaces and tinges of red and purple, some showing tip discoloration. The abnormal fruits are grouped along the upper stems, giving a bumpy, distorted appearance.

Slender, upright, pale green stalks with a granular, powdery surface. Some stalks flare at the tips into shallow, irregular cups with crenulate margins. Clustered closely together, emerging from a base with visible debris.

Mushrooms with convex to flat, pale tan to light brown caps, some showing faint lilac or pinkish hues and a slightly scaly surface. Gills are closely spaced and pale, attached to sturdy, cylindrical stipes with bulbous bases, often covered in soil and debris.

Delicate, tiny mushrooms with slender, elongated white stems and small, rounded, slightly translucent caps. The caps are convex to nearly flat with smooth margins, and the stems are straight and thin, supporting the caps at an angle.

A tiny, fragile fungus with a slender, translucent white stem and a small, bell-shaped cap. The cap displays pronounced striations along the margin, and widely spaced gills are visible underneath. The stem appears smooth and minutely pruinose.

Small, white, smooth, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies less than 1 cm wide, scattered in tight clusters among moss, dead leaves, and twigs. No visible stipe or cap margin; surface appears even and unornamented.

Dense, dark fungal mass covered with numerous small yellow spherical structures. Multiple elongated, wiry, tan to light brown outgrowths emerge, some curved or twisted. Fine web-like material is interspersed among the robust fungal projections, creating a textured appearance.

Tiny, white to pale gray, round to slightly irregular discs with smooth surfaces and scalloped or uneven margins, scattered and sometimes clustered directly on the substrate. Fruiting bodies are minute, sessile, and somewhat translucent.

Small, round, disc-like fruiting bodies scattered irregularly on a dark, moist, glossy stem. The discs are pale to dark, slightly raised, with smooth, well-defined margins, contrasting against the slimy surface.

Delicate mushrooms with thin, whitish to translucent stems and caps that start conical, becoming flat with age. Caps are pale brown with darker centers and pronounced radial striations, often wavy or upturned at the edges.

Small, dark brown, raised pustules are scattered along the smooth, pale green leaf surface. Irregularly shaped holes and thinning tissue surround the pustules, with uneven margins indicating localized damage.

Brownish, matted, and filamentous fungal growth envelops a spider host, forming irregular, tangled hyphal masses with fine, hair-like projections and denser clumps. The surface appears uneven and slightly glossy in some areas.

Three upright, pale green, cup-shaped structures with granular surfaces. The cup margins are distinctly lined with small, brownish dots. The slender, tapering stalks support shallow, open cups, highlighting the detailed texture and rim features.

Dense, intricate network of fine, white filamentous hyphae forming a cottony mat, interspersed with numerous small, yellow to orange, globose or granular structures. The surface appears uneven, with irregular color zoning and a powdery texture.

Cluster of mushrooms with broadly convex to flat, pale tan to light brown caps, some showing subtle lilac hues and scattered debris. Stems are sturdy, pale to brownish with lilac tones, and gills are pale lilac, closely spaced, and attached to the stem.
Three large, dry leaves with curled, irregular margins and yellow to brown coloration, scattered black spots, and holes. No visible white, powdery, or fuzzy growth is present on the leaf surfaces.

Bright yellow to yellow-orange crust forming irregular, patchy mats with a granular texture. Densely packed, small, rounded, slightly raised apothecia cover the surface, creating a distinctly textured and clustered appearance. Margins are diffuse and blend into the underlying rock.

Large, irregular, hoof-shaped fruiting body projecting from the trunk. Surface is velvety to finely tomentose with brown coloration and darker, glossier patches. Margin is thick and rounded, with a small hole visible on the left side. Substantial and robust appearance.

A cluster of pale, slender, thread-like filaments emerges from a dark, glossy mass, with fibrous, matte surfaces and off-white to pale brown coloration. The intricate threads extend outward, entwined with remnants of organic material.

Several trees with dense green canopies; the central trees show a subtle pale or grayish cast on their leaves, suggesting a fine, powdery surface. No distinct fungal structures are visible at this distance.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with translucent white, bell-shaped caps and faintly striated margins. The slender, elongated stems are finely pruinose, accentuating the fragile appearance of the fruiting bodies against the dark substrate.

Single mushroom with a medium brown, smooth convex cap, slightly darker at the margin. Gills beneath are closely spaced and brownish. The slender, light brown stem shows longitudinal streaks and has soil and leaf debris at the base.

Dense clusters of slender, upright stalks with shallow, pale green cup-shaped tops. The surface appears granular and slightly rough, with finely scalloped cup margins. Stalks vary in height, forming a delicate, carpet-like mat among mosses and brown plant debris.

Numerous tiny, shiny, nearly black globose fruiting bodies on slender, erect stalks emerge from rough, decomposing woody material. The sporocarps are smooth and spaced apart, with a scattered arrangement across the substrate.

Medium-sized mushrooms with pale lilac to tan, smooth caps showing brownish and whitish patches. Caps are convex to nearly flat. Stems are thick, white, and fibrous, with some soil at the base. Gills are closely spaced and pale. One specimen is sectioned, revealing a solid white interior.

Three pale yellow to ochre mushrooms with smooth, rounded caps and elongated, bulbous-based stems. The central specimen is cut lengthwise, exposing white internal tissue and partial gill structure. Surfaces appear dry with some soil remnants at the base.

Small, scattered, irregularly rounded to slightly flattened fruitbodies with a pale yellowish to olive, moist, gelatinous, and smooth surface, embedded on a dark decaying stem. The fruitbodies appear glistening and lack a distinct margin.

Pale greenish to yellowish surface densely covered with numerous small, black, rounded, slightly raised spots. The granular, uneven texture highlights the sharp contrast between the dark fruiting bodies and the lighter background.

Convex to slightly flattened caps with moist, smooth, light brown to grayish-brown surfaces and distinctly striate margins. Slender, white, fibrous stems with slightly bulbous bases. Gills are pale, crowded, and free from the stem.
A dense mat of fine, fuzzy hyphae covered with numerous small, rounded yellow to orange structures, creating a granular, powdery surface with subtle brownish and greenish tones throughout.

Broad, flattened caps in ochre to rusty brown with irregular patches and debris; wavy, uplifted margins. Robust, yellowish stems with fibrous texture, covered in soil. Prominent, closely spaced yellowish gills extend from stem to cap margin.
Green, elongated, clustered fruit pods are visible among dense green foliage. No distinct fungal fruiting bodies or spore masses are apparent on the pods or surrounding plant structures.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, dark brown interiors and finely textured, pale to whitish outer surfaces. Margins are rounded and slightly rolled, with several cups clustered closely together on the soil.

Small, dark brown, irregularly shaped, powdery pustules scattered along a bright green leaf. The pustules are raised and sharply defined, contrasting with the smooth leaf surface. A fine white hair crosses one pustule.

Tiny, spherical fruiting bodies with a fuzzy, yellow surface resembling miniature pom-poms, each perched on a slender, short stalk. The fruiting bodies are loosely clustered and finely filamentous, standing out against the dark background.

A single, tiny, whitish, roughly circular fruiting body with a granular, dotted surface and slightly uneven margin. The texture appears rough, and the structure stands out against a dark, blurred background.

Numerous tiny, brown, spherical fruiting bodies with finely textured surfaces stand upright on slender stalks, closely grouped on a greenish, mossy substrate. The sporangia are scattered to gregarious, with a subtle granular appearance.

Numerous tiny, dark disc-shaped fruiting bodies with distinct pale, crisp margins scattered across the stem. The discs are slightly raised, smooth, and sessile, varying in size and often appearing in loose clusters.

Two small, bell-shaped mushrooms with pale tan, finely textured caps featuring vertical striations and a velvety surface. The slender, whitish stems are short, and one cap is slightly collapsed, revealing its inner surface.

Minute, upright structure with a golden, funnel-shaped base and a dense, bushy plume of orange-yellow, coiled threads. The slender, dark stalk tapers to a small, irregular base. The entire structure is about 1 mm tall.

Numerous small, dark, spherical bodies with delicate, translucent, radiating filamentous appendages create a starburst effect against a smooth yellow background. The fruiting bodies are irregularly grouped, each surrounded by fine, spiky filaments.

Cluster of upright, greenish stalks with a granular, powdery surface, each topped by smooth, vivid red, rounded discs. The stalks emerge densely from a common base, with the red apothecia sharply contrasting against the green.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, slightly raised pustules are scattered irregularly across a smooth, green stem with yellowish discoloration around the spots. The pustules break through the epidermal layer, forming distinct, embedded dots.

Dense clusters of small, yellowish to brownish, globose structures embedded in a loose, whitish to pale yellow, fuzzy mycelial mat. The rounded bodies are smooth, moist, and slightly glistening, with indistinct margins blending into the surrounding hyphae.

A partially opened green fruit pod reveals a dark brown to black, powdery and granular mass with a rough, uneven, matte surface filling the interior, sharply contrasting with the smooth green outer tissue.

Numerous small, upright, pale green to yellowish-green cup-shaped structures with granular surfaces form a dense, carpet-like mat. The slender, cylindrical stalks taper toward the base, and the cups have even, slightly flared margins.

Pale, filamentous fungal growths form irregular, branched, and granular masses emerging from a spider’s body. The fungus appears light tan to brown, with delicate, fibrous, and matted textures contrasting against the darker exoskeleton.

Pale, moist, fleshy interior with irregular pinkish and brownish patches. Some soil debris adheres to the cut surface. The tissue appears fibrous, and the stipe extends from the center with attached organic remnants.
Slender, translucent white stems support small, smooth, glassy caps with thin, delicate margins. The mushrooms are tightly clustered, appearing ethereal and fragile against a lush green background.

Thick, cushion-like bracket with a convex upper surface, brownish-orange at the top fading to lighter brown and grayish-brown below. Surface densely covered in minute pores, with rounded margins and small outgrowths scattered across the robust, finely textured body.

Thin, irregular, crust-like layer with a grayish to whitish color, granular to slightly warty texture, and diffuse, patchy margins blending into the substrate. Scattered brownish debris and soil particles rest on the uneven surface.

Mushrooms with smooth, moist, pale peach to light brown convex caps. One specimen shows closely spaced, pale, decurrent gills and a cylindrical, pale stipe with soil adhering near the top. Another has a rounded, unopened cap.

A small, irregular pale lesion with whitish to purplish discoloration and a slightly raised, blistered texture. The center shows a darkened, ruptured area, contrasting with the surrounding matte, green, slightly hairy leaf surface.

Small, bluish-gray, disc-like fruitbodies with smooth, waxy surfaces and irregular, undulating margins. Some show central notches or depressions, and a few have slightly lobed edges. Arranged in a loose vertical cluster on a dark brown stem.

Compact, mound-like cluster of minute, rounded, grainy structures in white to light brown hues. The surface appears granular and crystalline, with a rough, uneven texture and some fine, thread-like elements visible.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to flat, yellowish-brown caps bearing darker streaks and soil patches. Cap margins are slightly uplifted and split. Gills are pale, closely spaced, and attached to thick, white stems with bulbous, soil-covered bases. Caps appear dry and somewhat fibrillose.

Thin, crust-like layer tightly pressed against the wood, pale beige to off-white in color, with a matted, fibrous texture and slightly fuzzy, irregular edges. No distinct fruiting bodies or margins are visible.

Dense cluster of small, nearly spherical bodies with muted gray to brownish tones, each featuring a distinct apical pore. Surfaces appear minutely roughened and granular, lacking any obvious fuzziness or external structures.

White, crust-like layer tightly adhering to the surface, with a dry, granular to nodular texture. Small, rounded aggregations and irregular patches are scattered throughout, interspersed with cracks and crevices.

Irregular, patchy pale orange to white growths scattered along a dark, rough branch. The patches are powdery to granular, slightly raised, and crust-like, standing out against the bark's coarse texture.

Extensive, irregular pale grayish-brown patches tightly adhere to the wood, displaying a granular to powdery texture with slightly uneven, cracked areas. The diffuse margin blends into the substrate, and the surface lacks distinct fruiting bodies or velvety texture.

Crust-like, irregular patch enveloping plant stems with a rough, scaly surface. Predominantly brown with grayish and tan areas, blending into surrounding debris. Closely adherent, lacking distinct cap or stalk, and displaying a dry, fibrous texture.

Crustose, granular to warty surface with yellow-green to yellowish tones. Numerous small, rounded, bright yellow to orange discs are scattered and clustered, some with slightly raised margins. Texture is rough and uneven, tightly compacted on the substrate fragment.

Slender, light brown substrate with fine longitudinal striations, bearing several distinct, shiny black oval to elongated fruiting bodies. These fruiting bodies are embedded or slightly raised, smooth, and have well-defined margins, distributed along the length.

Numerous black, irregular, slightly raised stromatic structures cluster in a linear arrangement along the edge of exposed, darkened wood, contrasting with the rough, pale bark. The fruiting bodies appear rough-textured and embedded in the wood.

Two small mushrooms with slender, white, slightly fibrous stems and white caps that are convex to nearly flat. The caps show subtle translucency at the edges. Gills are white, broad, and moderately spaced, radiating from the stem.

A single, roughly circular thallus with a dark gray to nearly black, matte surface. Irregularly lobed and undulating margins, several perforations, and a lighter gray edge. Central area has an attached stone fragment.

Numerous small, white, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies cluster densely on a dark, moist surface. The structures appear granular or powdery, with a delicate, slightly translucent quality and a fine, glistening texture. No distinct stalks or margins are visible.

Small, delicate mushrooms with pale, smooth, slightly convex caps and matte texture. One fruiting body shows broad, widely spaced white gills radiating from a slender white stipe. The overall appearance is clean and unornamented.

Large mushroom with a convex, brown cap covered in paler streaks and scales. The margin is inrolled and irregular. The thick, robust stem is brown with lighter patches and a slightly bulbous base. Both cap and stem have a dry, fibrous texture.

Irregularly shaped thallus with a rough, leathery texture, gray to brown coloration, reticulate cracked surface, uneven lobed margins, and several visible perforations. Edges appear slightly curled, and the specimen is isolated against a dark background.
Pale gray to whitish crust tightly appressed to the surface, with a rough, granular, and cracked texture. Scattered rounded, pale discs are visible across the uneven, irregularly margined thallus.

Minute, translucent to pale, irregularly shaped apothecia scattered across a green leafy surface. The apothecia are smooth, gelatinous, and blend subtly with the substrate, lacking prominent margins or visible reproductive structures.

Numerous tiny, cup-shaped structures with smooth, well-defined margins and a slightly translucent, pale gray to olive hue. The fruiting bodies are tightly clustered in some areas, sparsely scattered in others, and have a smooth, gelatinous surface.

Pale peach to pinkish caps with moist, slightly sticky surfaces and wavy margins. One cap is convex to slightly depressed with soil debris. Broad, well-spaced, decurrent gills and a thick, white, solid stipe covered in soil at the base.

Deformed, swollen plant tissues with yellow-green discoloration and brown necrotic areas. Irregular blackish, powdery spore masses break through the surface, surrounded by thickened, gall-like growths and distorted leaves.
Numerous black, irregularly shaped, slightly raised fruiting bodies with a rough texture are arranged in a linear pattern along the border of cracked, light bark and exposed reddish-brown wood.

Irregular, lumpy fruiting body with a dark, nearly black upper surface and rusty brown margins. The texture is rough and uneven, with some greenish patches and bracket-like lateral attachment to the wood.

Tiny, white, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with flat to slightly concave discs, densely covered in long, thin, radiating hair-like setae. The surface appears fuzzy and delicate, with the setae giving a distinctly velvety texture. Fruiting bodies are scattered and very small.

Tiny, round, bright yellow to yellow-orange discs scattered irregularly across a granular yellow-green surface, tightly pressed against rough, fissured bark. The discs are mostly under 1 mm wide, with smooth edges and slightly convex to flat tops.

Two slender mushrooms with elongated, pale grayish-brown, slightly translucent stems and conical to bell-shaped caps. The caps are smooth to faintly striate, light grayish-brown, with pale, moderately spaced gills visible beneath.

Clusters of swollen, irregular galls with green bases and prominent purplish to violet discoloration appear along stems and leaf veins. The affected tissue is thickened and distorted, with smooth to slightly roughened surfaces and irregular margins.

Elongated, black, linear fruiting bodies embedded within pale, cylindrical structures. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised, smooth, and glossy, with well-defined narrow margins, arranged parallel and scattered along the length.

Numerous tiny, dark disc-shaped to irregularly angular fruitbodies with wavy or lobed margins and pale interiors, closely attached and scattered in small clusters on a fibrous surface. The apothecia are smooth and minute, typical of microfungi.
Broad, brownish-red cap with lighter patches near the edge, yellow pores underneath, and a long, pale cream stem showing brownish discoloration at both base and cap attachment.

Tiny, translucent to grayish disc-shaped bodies with smooth, glassy surfaces and finely fringed margins, scattered irregularly across a dried, fibrous plant stem. Some discs are clustered while others are isolated.

Thin, crust-like growth spreading irregularly over decayed wood, with a whitish to grayish, patchy and uneven surface. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the surrounding wood. No distinct pores or structures are visible.

Convex to slightly flattened caps in pale yellowish-brown with irregular darker streaks and soil patches. Margins are uneven. Stems are robust, white, fibrous, and brownish at the base. Crowded, pale gills are visible on upturned fruiting bodies.

Crustose lichen with a yellow-green, granular to areolate surface, scattered with flat to slightly convex, bright orange, round apothecia. Some apothecia are grouped, others solitary. White lacy patches and dark, rimmed circular fruiting bodies are also present.

Broad, convex to flat caps with a dry, velvety medium to dark brown surface and paler yellowish margins. Yellow, finely porous undersides and cylindrical, pale yellow to ochre stems with brownish streaks. One cap shows a lighter central patch.
A thin, crust-like layer closely appressed to the surface, pale off-white to light beige, with a finely granular, powdery texture and a diffuse, irregular margin blending into the substrate.

Irregular yellow to orange crust tightly attached to rough bark, with dense clusters of small, disc-shaped, vivid orange apothecia, some with paler margins. Surface appears granular and rough, forming patchy, confluent areas across the bark.

Delicate, small mushroom viewed from below, showing pale, widely spaced, ruffled gills radiating from a central point. The cap margin is translucent with a subtle pinkish hue, and the visible stem is slender and pale. The texture appears soft and fragile.

Crustose lichen with a granular, uneven grey-green surface, closely appressed to the substrate. Scattered small, bright yellow, circular apothecia are immersed to slightly raised, each with a distinct margin, irregularly distributed across the thallus.

Two slender, upright, white fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces rise from a pale substrate. Each has a narrow stem and a slightly swollen, club-shaped apex. The taller and shorter structures are spaced apart, with even, unornamented surfaces.

Thin, crust-like layer spreading irregularly with pale brown to grayish-lilac coloration. The margin is lighter and slightly fibrous, while the surface appears smooth to finely granular with diffuse, patchy edges.
Tiny, smooth, white club-shaped fruiting bodies are scattered and upright along a dried stem. Each structure is unbranched and directly attached, standing out against the dark background.

Tiny, white, cup-like fruiting bodies with a central depression, each surrounded by a fringe of long, delicate, translucent hairs, giving a feathery appearance. The fruiting bodies are scattered and spaced apart on the surface.

Numerous small, black, spherical fruiting bodies with a smooth, matte surface densely clustered across a fibrous, brown substrate. The spheres are glabrous and lack visible ornamentation, forming tight groups on the uneven surface.

Numerous tiny, round, bluish-gray discs with smooth, slightly convex to flat surfaces are scattered irregularly across a brown plant stem. The fruiting bodies have well-defined, even margins and vary in size, some clustered and some solitary.

Patch of yellowish to pale orange, cracked crust with scattered, vivid orange, rounded apothecia slightly raised above the surface. The apothecia are distinct and sharply contrast with the paler thallus and dark, textured background.

Two mushrooms with convex, light brown to tan smooth caps, densely packed light brown gills, and slender white fibrous stems. Soil and moss cling to the bases. Each fruiting body measures about 7–8 cm long, shown next to a ruler for scale.

A continuous, crust-like layer with a granular, powdery texture in yellow-green hues. The surface is uneven and finely roughened, closely following bark contours and fissures, with diffuse margins blending into the substrate.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, pale to medium brown caps displaying pronounced radial striations and a moist sheen. Caps have thin, wavy margins and smooth surfaces. Slender, pale brown stems support the caps above grass and soil. Gills are not visible from this angle.

Scattered, circular fruiting bodies ranging from pale yellow to yellow-orange, with the largest appearing smooth and matte, while smaller ones are granular. Margins are entire and well-defined, and surfaces are compact without visible stalks.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, light brown to yellowish caps and a smooth to subtly velvety surface. Undersides display prominent, honeycomb-like pores. Stipes are robust, cylindrical, pale yellow to brownish with reddish streaks and subtle longitudinal markings.

Numerous small, bright yellow to yellow-orange, circular discs are scattered across a rough, fissured surface. The discs are slightly raised, smooth, and matte, appearing in discrete patches rather than forming a continuous layer.

Cluster of small mushrooms with pale brown to tan, conical to convex caps showing pronounced radial striations. Caps are smooth and striate at the margins, with long, thin, pale stems and pale gills visible beneath some caps.

Small, funnel-shaped fruiting body with a whitish, slightly translucent cap and scalloped margin. Decurrent gills run down a slender, whitish stem. The cap surface is delicate and faintly striate, giving a fragile appearance.

Tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a distinctly cottony, fluffy surface. Caps are slightly convex to irregular, supported by slender white stems, and scattered loosely among fine plant debris. Both cap and stem are uniformly white and minutely hairy.

Pale brown to tan convex caps with wavy, striate margins; slender, elongated white stems. Gills are pale and attached beneath the cap. Surface appears smooth to slightly fibrous, with caps at different stages of expansion.

Irregular, dark blackish patches with a cracked, crust-like surface. The texture appears matte to slightly shiny, with some rounded, slightly raised areas. The margin is distinct against the surrounding substrate.

Irregular, patchy crust tightly attached to the surface, light brown to tan with a granular, warty texture. Margins are diffuse and blend into the substrate, lacking any distinct cap or stem. Surface is uneven with small, raised granules.

Pale greenish-gray, crust-like surface tightly adheres to bark, with a rough, granular texture. Scattered small, round, pale discs are visible across the uneven thallus. Margins are irregular and blend into the substrate.

Two medium-sized mushrooms, one showing a smooth, moist, pale brown cap with a wavy edge, the other displaying broad, widely spaced, pale pinkish gills and a robust, white, slightly fibrous stem with soil at the base.

Irregular, dark brown to black dry lesions on the leaf surface, angular and following veins, with yellowish margins and slightly sunken compared to the surrounding green tissue. Lesions coalesce, causing significant discoloration and breakdown.

Dense, irregular patches of minute, orange-yellow granular pustules cluster along the prominent veins of a green leaf. The pustules are slightly raised and form discrete, textured groups that contrast with the smooth leaf surface. Inset shows oval, single-celled spores with dark outlines.

Irregularly shaped, vibrant yellow patches with granular, slightly rough surfaces and uneven, somewhat lobed margins. Some thalli display darker reddish-brown areas. The patches are scattered and closely associated but remain distinct from each other.

Crust-like, resupinate growth tightly adheres to the surface, displaying rough, uneven texture with irregular margins. The coloration blends grayish, yellowish, and brownish tones in patchy, extensive areas. No distinct cap or stem is visible.
