Two small mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped, medium brown caps featuring darker centers and striate margins. Smooth, moist surfaces and slender, pale brown stems. Well-developed gills are visible beneath the cap edges.

Clusters of small, black, irregularly shaped and lumpy growths scattered along tree bark, often aligned with cracks. The rough, uneven surface of the fungal bodies contrasts sharply with the smooth, pale bark.
Bracket-shaped fruiting body with a brown, rough, velvety upper surface and irregular margin. Some grayish or bluish patches are present. The underside shows a dense, maze-like pore structure.

Numerous small, bright yellow-orange, round disc-like fruiting bodies densely clustered on rough, fissured bark. The surface is smooth to slightly granular, with a yellowish, granular crust visible between the apothecia.
Pale cream to off-white cap with brownish streaks and scattered dark debris. The surface appears dry, slightly fibrous, and uneven at the margin with faint brownish discoloration.

Convex to irregular caps with a smooth, moist surface, showing a gradient from darker brown centers to paler, uneven margins. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps. Cylindrical, pale stems with some debris at the base.

Two mushrooms with ochre to yellowish-brown, dry, smooth to slightly fibrillose caps; one cap convex, the other flattened with scattered debris. Gills are closely spaced and pale to light brown. Stems are robust, white, with rusty-brown fibrillose zones near the base and adhering soil.

Numerous tiny, bluish-gray, disc-shaped structures with smooth surfaces and slightly raised margins are scattered irregularly along a dead stem. The discs are translucent, sessile, and vary in size from less than a millimeter to a few millimeters in diameter.

Two roughly spherical fruiting bodies with thick, brittle, brown outer surfaces covered in fine granules. One is cut open, revealing a solid, dark, powdery interior. The peridium shows irregular cracking and flaking.

Brown, convex to slightly flattened caps with velvety texture, some showing yellowish margins and patchy surface damage. Thick, pale to yellowish stems with surface markings. Cut specimen reveals white flesh and small, angular yellow pores beneath the cap.

Numerous tiny, bright yellow to orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered and clustered across rough, deeply fissured gray bark. The discs stand out sharply against the bark, with no visible thallus or distinct margins.
A single, slender, erect fruiting body with a smooth to faintly granular surface, white to cream in color, cylindrical and slightly tapering at the base where it attaches to the plant stem.
Minute, dark brown to black fruiting bodies with slender, upright stalks topped by rounded, granular-textured heads. The structures are sparsely scattered and emerge vertically from the substrate.

Clusters of small, round to slightly irregular, bright orange discs with a matte to velvety surface, tightly grouped on rough bark. Some discs show a faintly raised margin, standing out vividly against the textured background.

A dense, crust-like patch with a finely granular, powdery surface. The color is beige to off-white, and the margin is uneven. The layer appears compact and closely adherent to the substrate, lacking any cottony or woolly texture.

Numerous tiny, round, bluish-gray discs with smooth, matte surfaces and even margins are scattered irregularly along a vertical plant stem. The fruiting bodies are sessile and only a few millimeters wide, some clustered and others isolated.

A thin, crust-like layer tightly adheres to the surface, off-white to pale grayish in color, with a distinctly granular to finely warty texture and irregular, diffuse margins. A small brown leaf fragment rests atop the mat.
Tiny, pale grayish to translucent white discs with smooth, slightly glossy surfaces. The delicate, gelatinous fruiting bodies are sessile, evenly margined, and loosely scattered on a dark woody stem.

Minute, pale to translucent, disc-like or cushion-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across a green leafy surface. The apothecia are smooth, moist, and lack stalks, with entire, non-lobed margins and an embedded appearance.

Crustose surface with yellowish-green, granular texture. Numerous small, rounded, slightly sunken apothecia with yellow to orange discs and raised margins. Dense clustering and scattered reddish pigmented patches are visible.

Crustose patch with a granular, yellowish thallus tightly appressed to the surface. Numerous vivid orange, rounded to angular discs cluster centrally, each with a slightly raised margin. The surface is uneven and merges gradually into the background.

Brown convex to slightly flattened caps, some with patchy yellow areas where the surface is damaged. Yellow pores are visible beneath the caps. Stipes are thick, cylindrical to curved, pale to brownish, with a textured surface. Both whole and sectioned fruiting bodies are shown.
A dense cluster of small, nearly spherical bodies with a grayish-brown, velvety surface. Each structure has a distinct central dark spot, giving a textured, pitted appearance across the mass.

Three mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate caps, dark brown at the center fading to yellowish-brown at the edges. Gills are widely spaced and yellowish. Cylindrical stipes are yellowish with brownish discoloration and soil debris at the base.

Dense, continuous mat of pale beige to light tan fungal tissue with a granular, velvety surface. The margin is irregular, and yellowish mycelial threads extend from the edges onto the dark background. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Crustose thallus with a rough, granular, pale greenish-gray surface. Scattered round apothecia have slightly raised, textured margins and lighter, whitish discs, contrasting with the uneven background.

Pale tan to light brown convex caps with smooth margins, white broad widely spaced gills, and slender white smooth stipes. Fruiting bodies vary in size, with a slightly fibrous texture on the stems. No rings or veils are visible.

Delicate, slender mushrooms with elongated white stems and small, smooth, moist caps. The caps are convex to hemispherical, slightly translucent, and pale. White, well-spaced gills are visible beneath one cap. The overall texture appears fragile and almost glassy.

Two small, delicate mushrooms with conical to bell-shaped, smooth caps showing pronounced radial striations. The caps are light brown to grayish, and the slender, cylindrical stipes are pale and match the cap color. Margins are even and not wavy.
Black, crust-like patch tightly embedded in bark crevice, with a rough, cracked surface and several small, rounded pits scattered across its surface.

Pale, elongated needle with parallel brown stripes, scattered tiny black dots, and two prominent, dark, oval fruiting bodies with raised margins and a central slit, slightly protruding from the surface.

A tiny, dark structure with sharply defined, elongated hair-like projections radiating from a compact central point. The surface appears somewhat granular, and the spiky setae are distinctly visible against the blurred background.

Broad, flat fruiting body with irregular, jagged white margin and a chalky texture. Central area is densely matted and fibrous, displaying a mix of brown, reddish-brown, and white tones. Surface appears dry and thin.

Dense, shaggy mat of rusty brown hyphae with lighter, whitish tips on long, jagged fibers. The texture is fuzzy and irregular, with short, straight fibers blending into longer, uneven projections along the margin.

Leaves display a powdery, whitish-gray coating forming diffuse patches on the upper surfaces. The fungal growth appears as a superficial, dusty layer, most prominent on older or damaged areas, without visible fruiting bodies.

Smooth, glossy, pinkish-brown caps with a wet, reflective surface. The caps are convex and slightly irregular, with entire margins. Fruiting bodies are clustered together, and stems are mostly obscured by moss and grass.

A small, dark, rounded fruiting body with a smooth, slightly glossy surface and a somewhat flattened dome shape. It appears solitary, with regular, well-defined margins, sharply contrasting against the lighter, mottled background.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, light brown to grayish-brown caps featuring a subtle central depression and slightly darker center. Caps are smooth with faint radial fibrils. Gills are pale and closely spaced. Stipe is slender, pale, and smooth with a slight basal thickening.

Microscopic cross-section showing a compact, layered structure with a light brown upper zone, a distinct reddish-brown middle band, and a dark brown to blackish base. The tissue appears dense with clear color stratification and fine vertical texture.

Numerous dark, elongated, rough-textured structures protrude from decaying wood, partially embedded and scattered. Pale, filamentous mycelium weaves across the surface, contrasting with the blackish fruiting bodies and the lighter, fibrous wood matrix.

A small, irregularly rounded patch with muted purple coloration and a translucent, gelatinous, moist surface. The margins are indistinct, blending into the fibrous substrate. The texture is smooth and slightly glossy, with no visible reproductive structures.

Three small, fan-shaped fungi with frilled, undulating margins and dry, fibrous light to medium brown caps. The gills are crowded and pale brown, clearly visible beneath the caps. Short, fibrous stems are present, and the overall appearance is delicate and fragile.

Elongated, cylindrical fruiting body with a vivid yellow, smooth surface. The apex is slightly bulbous and darker brown, while the stipe tapers gently toward the base. Some soil and debris adhere to the moist surface.

A patchy, crust-like layer tightly attached to the surface, densely covered with short, white to off-white spines. The margin is irregular and lobed, and the overall texture is distinctly hydnoid with pale, creamy tones.

Numerous tiny, bright reddish-orange cup- to disc-shaped fruitbodies with undulate or lobed margins, smooth to minutely granular surfaces, and closely attached in a loose, irregular line across a dark, decaying surface.

Large, convex cap with pinkish-red surface and irregular pale yellow patches where the skin is missing. Cap margin is slightly inrolled and dry. Thick, robust yellow stem with brownish discoloration near the base. Yellow pore surface with small, tightly packed pores.

Small, loose clusters of mushrooms with off-white to pale tan, irregularly lobed caps. Caps are dry, slightly textured, and mottled with brownish patches and soil. Slender, pale stems support closely spaced, pale gills beneath the caps.

Three mushrooms with convex to wavy reddish-brown caps, paler striate margins, slender stems showing reddish to pale tones, and broad, closely spaced white to cream gills. Some stems have darkened bases with attached debris. A ruler provides scale.

A tiny, disc-like fruiting body with an irregular, amorphous outline. It is translucent, pinkish-orange, and has a smooth, slightly granular or gelatinous texture. The margin is uneven and the fungus is directly attached to the surface.
Elongated, pointed green stems with reddish tips, scattered with small, round, brownish-orange raised spots. Fine white hairs cover the surface, and the spots are irregularly distributed.

Numerous tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, yellowish to pale brown surfaces and slightly translucent appearance, scattered in loose clusters. Some discs appear more opaque or dusted with fine, whitish threads, and margins are rounded to slightly irregular.
Single fruiting body with a smooth, dome-shaped, light to medium brown cap showing a slightly glossy surface. The slender stem is light yellow and subtly textured or bumpy. Background is blurred.

Numerous small, black, elongated to oval, slightly raised fruiting bodies are scattered irregularly across a slender, pale, dried stem, giving it a speckled appearance. The fruiting bodies appear embedded in the stem's surface.

Broadly convex to slightly depressed caps in greenish-gray to bluish-green shades, with moist, sticky surfaces bearing leaf and soil fragments. Cap margins are wavy, irregular, and notched. White, closely spaced gills and smooth, cylindrical white stipes are visible.

White, closely spaced gills radiate from a thick, cylindrical white stem. The cap surface is not visible. Small invertebrates are present on the gills, and the fungus lies among green grass and plants.
Close-up of the underside showing densely packed, radially arranged, light brown gills attached to a smooth, similarly colored stem. The gill edges are even and regular, with no visible cap margin.

Tiny, dark brown to black, upright cylindrical to slightly club-shaped fruiting bodies sparsely scattered along a pale, woody stem. The structures are smooth and project perpendicularly from the surface.

Dense, irregular patch of bright yellow-green thallus with a granular to minutely lobed texture. The colony is rounded, with small, tightly packed, convex to flattened structures and uneven, blending margins. Surface appears matte and slightly rough.

Two pale grayish to off-white caps with darker central spots and irregular patchy discoloration. The surface appears finely fibrous and slightly roughened, with uneven, wavy margins and a subtle central depression. Only the cap tops are visible.

Tiny, dark brown to nearly black, upright cylindrical bodies sparsely emerge from the surface of a pale, ribbed plant stem. The fruiting bodies are minute, firm, and rough-textured, standing singly and distinctly against the light background.

Numerous tiny, slender, black, cylindrical fruiting bodies stand erect and scattered in a linear pattern along the length of a pale, dried plant stem. The fruiting bodies are smooth and project distinctly above the surface.

Numerous small, round to slightly oval, cream to pale yellow fruiting bodies with smooth, opaque surfaces. They appear soft, slightly gelatinous, and are irregularly scattered, with some closely clustered and others isolated.

Irregular, contiguous patches of bright yellow, crustose growth tightly adhere to the stone. The surface is granular to finely areolate, with diffuse, uneven margins blending into the background. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible; the texture is densely powdery and granular.

Minute, globose to subglobose yellow-ochre sporangia with rough, granular surfaces, supported by short dark stalks. Some sporangia show ruptured, irregular margins and a powdery, flaking appearance, exposing the inner spore mass. Fruiting bodies are scattered and spaced apart.

Small, cup-shaped structures with thin, fragile yellow walls. Interiors display a striking, net-like pattern of yellow filaments radiating from a dark central mass. Margins are irregular and delicate, with overall yellow to brown coloration.

Crustose, granular greenish-yellow surface with scattered small, round, pinkish to light brown discs featuring smooth, slightly raised centers and paler margins. The thallus is uneven, with whitish and darker green patches, and the apothecia contrast distinctly against the textured background.

Numerous small, black, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies densely cover a coarse, granular, light brown surface. The fruiting bodies are closely packed, matte to slightly rough in texture, and stand out sharply against the lighter background.
Numerous tiny, translucent to whitish, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded margins and a gelatinous, glassy texture are scattered irregularly across the dark, textured wood surface.

Minute, pale to off-white, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with granular or powdery surfaces and rounded, slightly irregular margins, clustered closely together among greenish and brownish particulate matter.

Broad, nearly flat caps with smooth grayish to olive-gray surfaces, darker centers, and scattered white patches. White, closely spaced gills and robust, short white stems are visible. Margins are mostly even with slight irregularities.
A pale pink flower with smooth petals and slightly irregular edges. The center shows a faintly darkened or powdery area, but no prominent fuzzy or vividly colored growth is visible.

Numerous small, pale, rounded discs scattered across a rough, greenish surface. The discs are off-white to light beige, mostly flat to slightly convex, with smooth surfaces and subtle margins. Sizes vary, with some larger, more prominent discs among smaller ones.

Slender, elongated fruiting bodies with a pronounced curved, hook-like shape. Smooth surface, light brown to tan with a distinct darker brown stripe along the upper side. Pointed tips, even margins, and delicate, somewhat translucent edges. Arising in small, scattered groups.

A dense, irregular patch of bright yellow, granular to minutely lobed surface tightly attached to stone, forming a rough, textured colony. The yellow area stands out amid surrounding white, crustose patches with circular structures.

Cluster of mushrooms with slender, fibrous stems and smooth, moist caps. Caps are pale brown with a darker, wet-looking center fading to a lighter margin. Gills underneath are pale and closely spaced.

Numerous tiny, white, cup-shaped discs densely scattered across a dark, moist decaying leaf, creating a speckled pattern. The fruiting bodies are minute, stemless, and lack visible gills, standing out against the dark background.

Upright, ear- or tongue-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, matte ochre to light brown surfaces. Bases are white and slightly fuzzy, often with attached debris. Margins are irregular and not sharply defined. Fungi appear in small groups.
Small, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, waxy surfaces and slightly irregular, lobed margins. Scattered in loose groups among dense green moss on dark, cracked wood.

A dense cluster of minute, smooth, glossy, vivid orange spherical to slightly ovoid fruiting bodies, lacking visible stalks and directly attached to a dark, moist substrate among green moss and plant debris.

Small, irregular white patches scattered on the surface, appearing thin, flat, and powdery with diffuse, uneven margins. The colonies are closely appressed to the substrate and lack visible tufts or distinct structures.

A widespread, powdery, whitish-gray coating covers the leaf surface, following the contours of the veins. The growth is even and diffuse, giving the leaf a dusty or frosted appearance without distinct patches or visible fruiting bodies.

Mushrooms with smooth, convex to slightly flattened brown caps and slender, pale stems streaked with brown. The gills underneath are well-developed, brown, and radiate outward from the stem. Caps vary in size, with both larger and smaller specimens present.

Flat, disc-like fruiting bodies with smooth, cream to pale beige surfaces and a subtle moist sheen. Outlines are circular to slightly irregular, with even margins and scattered small debris. Fruiting bodies are closely grouped, varying in size.

Numerous tiny, white, smooth, hemispherical to slightly flattened fruitbodies scattered across weathered wood, some nestled among green moss. The fruitbodies are stalkless, varying in size from minute dots to a few millimeters wide, and appear in loose clusters and singly.

Broad, nearly flat cap with pale grayish to off-white coloration and a darker, mottled center. The margin is irregular, jagged, and broken, exposing white flesh. Surface appears matte with scattered small black specks.

Small mushrooms with convex to flat, shaggy light brown caps featuring darker centers and frayed margins. Gills are pale, closely spaced, and free, while the stems are long, slender, ochre to brownish, and fibrous.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, pale beige to tan caps featuring a subtle central bump. Caps are smooth with faint radial striations at the margin. Gills are closely spaced and light brown. Stems are slender, off-white, and slightly brownish at the base.

Small, white, disc-like fruitbodies with smooth, somewhat translucent surfaces. Margins are irregular, lobed, or folded, and the texture appears smooth and gelatinous. Fruitbodies vary in size and shape, clustered together among green moss.

Delicate mushrooms with convex, pale tan to translucent caps showing moist, striate surfaces. White, broad, widely spaced gills are visible beneath. Stems are slender, whitish, and slightly fibrous, giving a fragile, glassy appearance.
A solitary mushroom with a smooth, pale beige to off-white conical cap featuring two small brown spots. The cap margin is even, and the slender, straight stipe is light grayish-brown and smooth.

Bright yellow to orange, worm-like, sinuous strands tightly intertwined and scattered across the dark wood. The structures are smooth and glossy with variable thickness, some areas appearing powdery or granular, and the margins are irregular and interconnected.

Cluster of three mushrooms with convex, olive to grayish-brown caps, smooth and matte, some with inrolled margins. Stipes are thick, white to pale cream, with soil clinging at the base. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps.

Two shiny, dark brown beetles with oval bodies, prominent eyes, long segmented antennae, and thin yellowish-brown legs. Their smooth, glossy elytra show subtle longitudinal striations. No visible fungal structures are apparent on the beetles at this magnification.

Solitary, upright cup-shaped fruiting body with a pronounced split along one side. Outer surface is matte, velvety, and light brown; inner surface is smooth and slightly paler. Margin is irregular and undulating, giving an ear-like appearance.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, pale cream to light brown caps featuring a slightly darker center. Caps have smooth surfaces and thin margins. White, closely spaced gills are visible underneath. Slender, elongated stems darken toward the base, growing in a tight cluster.

Numerous tiny, translucent to whitish, cup-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across a dark surface. The delicate apothecia have a smooth, almost crystalline appearance and are grouped loosely or scattered individually.

Pale, off-white to light tan caps with smooth, slightly conical to rounded shapes, some showing a subtle umbo. Slender white stems with soil at the base. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream, and free to slightly adnexed.

Irregular, rounded patches with dense greenish centers and white, fuzzy margins. Colonies are closely grouped, slightly raised, and have a soft, cottony texture with color fading from green in the center to white at the edges.

Medium-sized mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, matte brown caps, some showing shallow radial cracks. Gills are closely spaced and dark brown. Cylindrical stems match the cap color and appear smooth. Mushrooms are scattered among moss and grass.

Bright orange, smooth, tubular strands form an intricate, reticulate network with rounded to angular mesh openings, creating a contiguous, lace-like mat with irregular margins that follows the contours of the surface.

Dense clusters of small, bright orange, cushion-shaped to discoid bodies with a moist, smooth surface. The fruiting bodies are tightly packed, irregularly lobed, and scattered across a dark, charred substrate.
Thin, patchy white crust closely adheres to the branch, forming irregular, smooth to slightly granular areas with indistinct margins blending into the wood. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Compact, irregular white aggregations with a crystalline, granular texture. The clusters appear rough and sparkling, composed of tightly packed minute elements. Margins are diffuse and irregular, lacking any distinct cap or stalk, and are scattered across a dark background.

Two small, irregularly shaped brown structures with a granular, clumpy surface. The right specimen has a rough, nodular exterior with fine threads, while the left is sectioned, showing a pale, compact interior.

A dense, powdery to cottony white-gray layer forms a fuzzy, finely filamentous mat on the leaf surface, with patchy distribution and diffuse margins blending into the green tissue. Underlying areas show browning and discoloration.

Numerous small, pale beige to light brown, disc-like fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces and thin, even margins, densely clustered and closely attached in varying sizes along a decaying branch.
A green leaf surface densely coated with a white, powdery, and fuzzy layer, giving it a velvety texture and obscuring much of the leaf’s natural color and detail.

Pale mushroom with a convex to nearly flat cap, slightly wavy margin, and subtle brownish center. The elongated white stem shows brownish discoloration and a soil-encrusted base. Densely crowded, off-white gills are attached to the upper stem. Cap and stem appear smooth.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, light brown to tan caps, some showing pale patches and irregular edges. Smooth surfaces are marked by debris and minor damage. Gills are pale to medium brown and moderately crowded. Stems are robust, cylindrical, and white, often with soil at the base.

Numerous tiny, translucent to pale gray cup-shaped fruiting bodies densely clustered on wood. The delicate, glassy discs have thin, even margins and smooth surfaces, with some appearing slightly undulate or irregular. Sizes vary but all are very small, creating a fragile, intricate texture.

White to grayish-white, powdery and cottony patches form a thin, fuzzy coating on the leaf surface. The fungal growth is diffuse, with irregular spots and indistinct margins blending into the healthy tissue. The texture appears soft and filamentous.

Clusters of thin, delicate, cup- to ear-shaped fruitbodies with irregular, upturned margins. Surfaces are light brown to tan, with smooth interiors and slightly velvety exteriors. Sizes vary, with some upright and others reclined, all displaying pale brown hues.

Small, white, crystalline or granular clusters tightly grouped on a dark brown surface. Each patch consists of numerous minute, spherical structures forming irregular, frost-like growths with diffuse margins that blend into the substrate.

A dense carpet of minute, round, white to pale grayish discs, each a few millimeters wide, closely packed and evenly scattered across a dark surface. The smooth, well-defined margins create a fine, granular texture with striking contrast.

Clusters of small, rounded, vibrant orange structures densely packed on dark, charred material. The surface appears bubbly and granular, with irregular, lobed shapes merging into indistinct patches. No visible stems; fruiting bodies are sessile and closely coalesced.

Clumped, irregular mass of several rounded to subglobose bodies, off-white to pale tan in color, with rough, granular surfaces and some darker soil encrustations. Fragmentation is visible, and the structures are closely aggregated.

Small to medium mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, smooth, moist light brown caps featuring darker centers. Stems are slender, pale to yellowish-brown, and fibrous. Gills are closely spaced, pale brown, and visible beneath the caps. Cap margins are smooth and slightly incurved in younger specimens.

Medium brown cap with a darker center and paler, striate margin; dry, fibrous surface. Pale brown, closely spaced gills beneath. Slender, cylindrical stem coated in sand, with the base embedded in sandy soil.

Dense, powdery white mycelial growth forms irregular, coalescing patches on the green leaf surface, creating a mottled, pale appearance. The texture is soft and fuzzy, closely following the contours of the leaf veins and margins.

Two mushrooms with smooth, rich brown caps—one convex with a darker center, the other showing closely spaced brown gills and a slender, pale yellowish-brown stem. Cap margins are even, and surfaces appear slightly fibrillose.

Two slender mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, pale tan caps and well-spaced, straight gills in a uniform light brown shade. Stems are pale, cylindrical, faintly fibrous, and slightly curved. Surface appears dry and matte.

Elongated, ear-shaped fruiting bodies with a distinct split along one side, light brown to ochre in color, finely textured outer surface, and irregular, undulating margins. Pale whitish bases emerge from woody debris.
Bright orange, glossy, net-like lattice of interconnected ridges forming an irregular honeycomb pattern, raised distinctly above the substrate and covering a patch of decaying wood.

Two slender, upright, black, club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, subtly textured surfaces and rounded tips. The matte to slightly shiny exterior and unbranched, finger-like form stand out against the blurred green and yellow background.

Upright, ear-shaped fruiting bodies with thin, wavy, and irregularly frilled margins. Surfaces are smooth and slightly glossy inside, matte outside. Light tan to ochre in color, clustered and delicate, emerging from forest floor debris.

Three small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat caps, each displaying a pronounced brown central disc and paler, cream to light tan margins. The cap surfaces appear dry and slightly fibrous. Stipes and gills are obscured by the top-down view and surrounding grass.

Clustered mushrooms with broadly convex to nearly flat, light brown caps showing subtle zonation and wavy, irregular margins. Caps are dry and slightly fibrous. Densely packed, pale to medium brown gills and off-white cylindrical stems with brownish bases.

Tightly packed, radially arranged gills in light to medium brown, with a velvety matte texture. The gills are attached to a pale, slightly fibrous central stipe. A small fragment of debris rests on one gill.

Two small, irregular, subglobose to lobed fruitbodies with dark brown to nearly black, wrinkled, brain-like surfaces and rough, uneven texture. No distinct cap, stem, or gills are visible; the bodies appear truffle-like and rest side-by-side.

Pale beige to cream, thin, smooth caps with slightly translucent edges and subtle lobing. Slender, tapering stems of similar color support the caps, arranged in scattered to clustered groups on dark organic material.
Pale cream to off-white cap with a fibrous texture and a distinctive central hole. The cap margin is irregular and slightly fringed. The thick, white stipe is relatively short compared to the cap.

White, crust-like layer tightly covering the surface, featuring a rough, matte texture with numerous vertical and horizontal cracks and fissures. Some darker patches are visible where the crust is thicker or broken.
Numerous tiny, white to cream, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and distinct central depressions are scattered densely and in small clusters across a dark, moist leaf surface.

Solitary, upright, ear-shaped fruitbody with a split, wavy margin. Outer surface is tan and finely velvety; inner surface is smooth, moist, and lighter in color. The base is whitish, and the structure appears thin and delicate.

Small, irregular whitish to grayish patches with darkened edges scattered along a reddish-brown, wrinkled surface. The patches have rough, uneven textures and indistinct margins, appearing slightly raised from the substrate.
A solitary, elongated, black fruiting body with a smooth, matte surface and a slightly curved, club-like shape. The structure tapers toward the base and has unornamented, entire margins.

Cluster of small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, white to light brown caps showing distinct striations and a finely fibrous texture. Thin, elongated stems darken toward the base. White gills are visible beneath the caps.

Irregularly shaped, clumpy tan to light brown nodules with a granular, dusty surface. Some pieces show lobed contours, one has a rootlet attached, and another reveals a compact, solid cross-section. Each measures about 1–1.5 cm in diameter.

Dense, white, powdery to filamentous mat covering a green surface, forming a continuous, fuzzy layer with fine, hair-like threads radiating outward. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the underlying tissue.

A single mushroom with a medium brown, conical to bell-shaped cap showing a scaly texture and uneven margin. The slender stem is pale but mostly coated with sand, obscuring its surface. Gills are not visible.
Broad, nearly flat cap with a slightly uplifted margin, covered in fine pale tan to ochre fibrils. The dry, fibrous surface sits atop a long, slender, pale stem with subtle darkening near the base.

Pale yellowish to off-white caps with brownish patches, wavy and lobed margins, and dry, slightly fibrous surfaces. White to cream, closely spaced gills and robust, short white stems with soil at the base. Largest cap about 3 cm wide.

Thin, grayish-white crust forming irregular, patchy layers on a woody branch. Surface appears rough and uneven, with diffuse margins blending into the substrate and some areas showing darker or greenish discoloration.

Numerous tiny, white, cup-shaped structures with smooth, glassy surfaces and thin, delicate margins are scattered in loose clusters across dark, decaying wood. The fruiting bodies are circular to slightly oval, appearing somewhat translucent and directly attached to the substrate.

Upright, ear-shaped fruitbodies with deep splits and irregular, wavy margins. Surfaces are matte, velvety, and warm yellowish-brown to golden-brown, with slightly paler interiors. Most are clustered, with one solitary specimen, all emerging from a mossy background.

Tiny, white, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with delicate, finely hairy margins are scattered closely together on a dark, moist surface. The apothecia appear smooth, somewhat translucent, and slightly reflective.

Two mushrooms with medium to dark brown, smooth convex caps and slightly inrolled margins. Undersides show closely spaced, brown gills. Stems are long, slender, yellowish-tan, and fibrous, tapering toward the base. No veil remnants visible.

Two mushrooms with convex, pale tan to light brown smooth caps and closely spaced gills. Stems are long, slender, slightly curved, and fibrous, with some soil attached at the base. No spots or scales are visible on the caps.

A single mushroom with a robust, slightly curved white stipe, a smooth, moist olive-brown convex cap with inrolled margin, and closely spaced white gills attached to the stipe. Some brownish soil clings to the stipe base.
A minute, dark, slender, and elongated structure with a smooth surface, firmly attached to the shiny, brown, striated exoskeleton of an insect. No visible ornamentation or reproductive structures.
A slender, elongated, nearly black fruiting body with a matte, dry surface. It is slightly curved, tapering at both ends, and has a somewhat irregular, twisted appearance.
A fine, powdery whitish-gray coating evenly covers the leaf surface, accentuating the network of veins beneath with a granular texture and diffuse appearance.

Two upright mushrooms with pale, conical to bell-shaped caps featuring a dry, fibrillose surface and uneven margins. Slender, light brown stipes display faint whitish veil remnants. Gills are not visible.

A dense scattering of minute, round to slightly irregular, white to pale grayish dots covers the dark wood surface, creating a fine, granular or powdery appearance with patchy, clustered distribution.
Minute, rounded ochre to tan fruiting bodies scattered on a plant stem, some partially covered by a whitish, cottony mat. Surfaces appear dry to powdery, with smooth margins and no visible stalks.

Small, pale cream to off-white, disc-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, slightly depressed centers and even margins. The thin, flat discs are sessile and scattered loosely across dark, decaying wood, contrasting with patches of green moss.

The leaf surface is densely coated with fine, dark, powdery granules, creating a mottled gray appearance. The fungal growth follows the leaf’s veins, accentuating the network of lines and giving the leaf a speckled, dusted look.
Tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a fine, fuzzy surface are scattered across a dark, rough background. The discs are minute, sessile, and have even, well-defined margins.

Clusters of soft, cream to pale yellow, funnel-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, moist surfaces and thin, even margins. Short to moderately elongated stipes taper toward the base, giving a delicate, cup-like appearance.

Small, irregularly shaped, rough and granular structures with a coating of soil particles. Colors range from light brown to tan with some darker patches. Forms vary from roughly spherical to lobed and nodular, all compact in size.

Ear-shaped, vertically oriented fruitbodies with irregular, split margins. Surfaces are smooth to faintly textured, yellowish to ochre-brown, with the inner side slightly paler than the outer. Thin flesh and scattered grouping among forest debris.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to flattened, light brown caps featuring frilled, irregular margins and occasional splits. Stems are slender, pale with brownish speckling, and slightly fibrous. Gills are exposed, fan-like, and light brown, radiating from the stem.

Close-up of a cap with muted grayish-green to grayish-brown color, slightly velvety matte texture, shallow indentations, and a smooth, gently curved margin. Small organic debris is present on the surface.

Convex to slightly umbonate caps with tan to light brown, fibrous surfaces. Densely packed, pale to light brown gills are visible beneath. Cylindrical, pale stems show soil remnants at the base. One cap lies on its side, exposing the gill structure.

Numerous thin, white, shelf-like fruiting bodies with wavy, irregular margins overlap in dense clusters. The upper surfaces are smooth and bright, while the undersides show a fine, poroid or toothed texture. The texture appears soft and slightly fibrous.

Cluster of mushrooms with medium brown, smooth, convex caps showing subtle radial striations and slightly wavy margins. Slender brown stems emerge from a base with attached soil and moss. Largest cap about 3 centimeters wide.
A fine, powdery, whitish to pale gray coating forms a diffuse, slightly fuzzy layer across the leaf surface, with leaf veins clearly outlined beneath and no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Upright, ear-shaped cups with undulating, irregular margins. Yellowish-brown, finely textured, and slightly velvety surface. Inner surfaces are brighter with scattered small black specks. Fruiting bodies are clustered and somewhat folded.

Small mushrooms with slender, pale cream to light brown stems, some darkened at the base. Caps are rounded, smooth, and off-white with brownish marks. Gills are closely spaced and white. Stems appear thin and wiry.

Convex to slightly expanded cap with a light brown, fibrous surface and faint radial striations. Margin is somewhat inrolled. Gills are closely spaced and white. Stipe is robust, white, and finely fibrous, with some soil at the base.

Broad, nearly flat cap with light brown, finely fibrous surface and a subtly darker center. Slender, slightly curved brown stem with whitish mycelium at the base, attached to soil and moss. Gills not visible.

Small, black, glossy, globose to irregular structures closely grouped and embedded in a rough, brown, fissured substrate. The surfaces reflect light, and no distinct necks or spore masses are visible at this magnification.

Numerous tiny, brown, disc- to cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly darker rims and lighter brown centers, closely grouped in a linear row on a slender twig. The margins are well-defined and slightly raised, with no visible stems.

Mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened light brown to tan caps, smooth surfaces, slender off-white to pale brown stems, and closely spaced brownish gills. Some stems have brown streaks and soil at the base. Sizes range up to about 5 cm tall.

Numerous small, round to slightly irregular yellowish-orange fruiting bodies with a fine granular surface, often clustered or confluent. Margins are mostly smooth but can appear lobed or irregular, standing out vividly against the dark brown background.

White, cottony mat with several small, translucent to yellowish-brown, finger-like projections emerging from the surface. The texture is soft and filamentous, with irregularly spaced structures and intricate surface details.

Small, dark, circular to oval pustules scattered across a pale yellowish-brown leaf, each slightly raised with a powdery or granular surface. The pustules are well-defined and do not merge, standing out against the discolored leaf tissue.

Solitary mushroom with a slightly curved, smooth white stem and a light brown, partially open cap. The cap margin is slightly undulating, and the underside reveals closely spaced, pale brown gills. Soil and organic debris cling to the base.

Clustered mushrooms with broadly convex to nearly flat, rich brown caps featuring paler, striate, and finely fibrillose margins. Gills are lighter brown and moderately spaced. Slender, pale to brownish, slightly curved stipes. Caps vary from convex to expanded.

Tiny, stalked, globose fruiting bodies with a metallic or iridescent sheen, brownish to gray in color. The surface appears slightly rough and granular. Slender, dark stalks elevate the sporocarps above the mossy substrate, with scattered arrangement.
Green, round leaves display scattered, pale, angular spots and marginal discoloration. No visible fungal fruiting bodies or growth structures are apparent at this scale.

Round, central spore sacs with a distinct apical pore sit atop star-like rays that have peeled back into pointed segments. The rays range from light to dark brown and have a dry, rough texture. Margins of the rays are irregular and sometimes cracked.
A circular, pale lesion with a faintly defined margin and subtle central discoloration appears on a smooth green surface, blending into the surrounding tissue.

Cluster of mushrooms with smooth, light brown convex to flattened caps, some showing surface debris and minor damage. Stems are thick and white, with inrolled cap margins on younger specimens. Cut specimens reveal white flesh and pale brown gills.

Irregular, club-shaped fruiting bodies with rough, granular surfaces. Upper portions are grayish-white, transitioning to dark, almost black bases. Tips are pointed or slightly lobed, and the bodies emerge singly or in small clusters from the litter.

Small, pale beige to light tan mushrooms with delicate, striate, and slightly wavy caps. Caps are convex to slightly depressed at the center. Slender, whitish stems support the clustered fruiting bodies. Fine white mycelial threads are visible on the wood surface.

Cluster of tiny, pale yellowish to olive, globose to slightly flattened fruiting bodies with granular surfaces, some on slender stalks, nestled among spiky green moss leaves. The delicate structures stand out against the contrasting moss background.

Pale tan to light brown caps with depressed centers and distinctly grooved, fluted margins. Cap surfaces are uneven, with patches of soil and debris. Thick white stems, one showing a dark bluish-black stain. Cream-colored, closely spaced gills beneath the caps.

Dark, narrow, elongated streaks and lines slightly raised above the surface, with a matte, striate texture. The coloration is predominantly dark brown to blackish, blending subtly into the background with a rough, uneven appearance.

Pale green, flattened, strap-like lobes form irregular tufts with curled, uneven margins. The lobes are loosely attached, spreading outward in small clusters, and have a smooth to slightly wrinkled texture against the stone surface.
A dense layer of minute, bright yellow to yellow-green granules tightly covering the surface, forming a finely granular, uneven texture with the underlying substrate visible in some areas.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with light blue, convex to flat caps featuring darker blue centers and pronounced radial striations. Caps appear moist and slightly translucent. Thin, white, smooth stems support the caps, forming a loose cluster along the wood.
Light brown, smooth convex caps with robust, pale stems. One mushroom is cut lengthwise, revealing white, fleshy interior and brown gills. The surface appears moist and the cap margins are smooth.

A small, elongated slit-like fruiting body embedded in bark, with a rough brown surface, dark granular interior, and surrounded by fine, thread-like hyphae. The margins of the opening are uneven and slightly raised, giving a coarse texture.

Pale green to yellow-green crust forming a continuous, tightly-adhering layer with a cracked, areolate texture and granular to powdery surface. Irregular margins blend into the background, with some darker patches interspersed.

Elongated, upright fruiting bodies with a rough, powdery gray to dark brown surface and irregular, finger-like shapes. Several display a prominent, swollen white base. Clustered together, they emerge from the forest floor litter.

Broadly funnel-shaped caps with irregular, undulating margins and a rough, scaly brown surface. Undersides densely covered in elongated, downward-pointing spines. Stems are dark brown, fibrous, and irregular, with moss and debris attached at the base.

Close-up of a mushroom's underside showing densely packed, smooth-edged gills in light orange to tan hues. The slender stem, centrally attached, matches the gill color. Mosses and lichens are visible around the base.

A single mushroom with a matte, finely textured cap that is pale beige to light brown, featuring a distinctly darker grayish-brown center. The cap is flat with a gentle central depression and slightly undulate margin. The slender, pale stem is partially visible.

Green trifoliate leaves densely covered with numerous small, circular, yellowish-orange pustules. The pustules are slightly raised, scattered, and sometimes clustered, standing out against the otherwise healthy leaf surface. Some leaf tips show withering.

Irregular, darkened lesion with diffuse margins and a faint yellowish halo on the leaf. The central area is slightly sunken and matte, featuring scattered small white spots. The surrounding leaf tissue remains smooth and green.
Convex cap with yellowish to ochre-brown tones, covered in soil patches. Margin slightly inrolled. Pale, closely spaced gills beneath. Robust, off-white, fibrous stem with soil adhering to the base.

Slender, white stem with a fibrous texture supports a small, light brown cap that is convex with a slightly depressed center and thin, incurved margin. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the cap.

Small mushrooms with pale, off-white to light tan caps featuring a slightly fuzzy or granular surface. The cap margin is incurved. Stems are slender, pale, and slightly curved with a fibrous look. Gills are pale and moderately spaced.
Leaves display a conspicuous white, powdery coating on their upper surfaces, forming a fine, evenly distributed mycelial layer that gives the foliage a dull, matte appearance.

Small, dark, conical fruiting bodies with a glossy, mucilaginous surface. Each structure is erect, uneven, and slightly granular, emerging distinctly from a fibrous, brownish substrate. The moist sheen highlights their scattered arrangement.

Small, globose to subglobose pale tan spore cases with a central opening, each atop a slender, fibrous stalk. Some spore cases are dusted with soil, and the stalks appear striate and elongated. The overall texture is smooth, with scattered arrangement among moss and sand.

Numerous small, black, elongated to irregularly shaped, slightly raised structures densely scattered along a pale, dried stem. The fungal bodies are rough and granular, arranged in linear groups following the contours of the plant tissue, sharply contrasting with the lighter background.

Elongated, flat, black patches with rough, cracked surfaces and irregular margins, closely adhering in a linear arrangement. The matte, crust-like bodies are thin and somewhat fused, embedded in the decaying wood.

Numerous small, circular, yellowish-orange pustules densely clustered on the green leaf surface, especially along veins. The pustules are slightly raised with a granular texture, surrounded by yellowed areas and some necrotic spots and holes.

Flat, circular cap with a slightly depressed center, pale cream to light tan with a pinkish center. The margin is distinctly striate, giving a ribbed, lacy appearance. Surface appears smooth and somewhat translucent at the edges.

A patch of minute, densely clustered white powdery spots forms along a leaf vein, creating a distinct area with a grayish-brown tinge beneath the fine, evenly distributed pustules. Margins are diffuse and the rest of the leaf surface is smooth.

Numerous leaves display yellowish to brownish irregular spots and lesions, with some areas showing necrosis, discoloration, and curling or distortion, especially along veins and margins. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

A small, rounded structure densely covered in white, cottony or powdery material, with a prominent dark patch on the upper surface. The margins are irregular and blend into the surroundings, giving a diffuse appearance.
Two small, rounded structures; the left is compact and brown with a granular, crusty surface and dark specks, while the right is paler, loosely fibrous, and irregular, both with scattered dark spots.

Medium-sized mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, smooth tan-brown caps, some with darker centers. Gills are densely packed and tan to brown. Stems are robust, white to light brown, often with soil at the base. Some caps show age or insect damage.

Numerous tiny, black, round to oval dots scattered irregularly across a translucent, veined leaf surface. The dots are minute and embedded in the tissue, with the leaf showing some discoloration and decay.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with thin, translucent white caps showing pronounced radial grooves. Caps are slightly convex to flat, with widely spaced, translucent gills and slender, semi-translucent white stems. Some caps have small dark flecks and a smooth, moist appearance.

Smooth, moist-looking cap with a gentle gradient from a darker ochre-brown center to a paler, cream-colored margin. Broadly convex to nearly flat with a subtle central depression. Margin appears even.

Single fruiting body with a convex, smooth, light orange cap and a slender, off-white to pale cream stipe tapering toward the base. The base is surrounded by dense moss rhizoids and substrate debris. Gills are not visible.

Mushrooms with smooth, moist, light brown convex caps and closely spaced pale gills. Stems are thick, white to light brown, and covered in soil. Cap margins are even, and the fruiting bodies cluster among leaves.

Irregular brown lesions with diffuse, pale halos scattered across the leaf blade. Some spots merge into larger patches. Lighter, slightly raised areas are visible, and lesion margins blend gradually into the surrounding tissue.

Mushroom with a smooth, convex light brown cap and a robust, pale stem featuring prominent brownish, scaly or fibrillose markings toward the base. The cap margin is even but partially damaged, and the gills are mostly obscured.
Dark, linear, crust-like patches with a rough, irregular texture cover the weathered, rectangular wood fragment. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible to the naked eye.

Clustered mushrooms with broadly convex to flat, light brown caps featuring darker centers and wavy, uneven margins. Cap surfaces are smooth with scattered debris. Gills are closely spaced and pale brown. Stipes are robust, cylindrical, and pale, with soil clinging to the bases.

Two mushrooms with tan to light brown, smooth caps featuring distinctly striate margins. One shows closely spaced white gills and a robust white stem with a blue-green bruise and soiled base. Both are nestled among green grass and clover.
Elongated, slightly raised brown to dark brown lesions with irregular margins and rough texture, interspersed with white and yellowish-orange patches, aligned along the veins of a green leaf.

A single elongated leaf with smooth surface, displaying numerous small, scattered, yellow-orange, powdery pustules along the veins. The leaf shows green and yellowing areas with faint brown streaks, and the pustules are slightly raised and granular.

Two fungi with round, off-white spore sacs atop long, pale, fibrous stalks. The surface of the sacs is slightly rough, one displaying a small apical opening. Stalks are partially coated with sand and soil.
Small, stalked, globose fruiting bodies with a whitish to pale gray, powdery or crystalline surface, each well separated and attached to a woody branch by slender, dark stalks.

Cluster of mushrooms with light to medium brown, convex to nearly flat caps showing subtle fibrillose texture. Stems are white to pale cream with fine fibrils, some tinged yellowish near the base. Gills are crowded and pale brown to tan beneath the largest cap.

Elongated, narrow, black fruitbodies with smooth, slightly shiny surfaces. They are linear, slightly raised, and closely appressed to the substrate, with well-defined margins and a flattened appearance.

Small, dark brown to nearly black rounded structures with rough, granular surfaces. Each has a distinct central opening at the top. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped and partially embedded in a pale, fibrous background.

Small, globose fruiting bodies with smooth, metallic golden-brown to bronze surfaces, each perched atop slender, translucent stalks. The heads display a subtle iridescent sheen and are scattered among fine, moss-like material.

Light brown, smooth cap with a slightly inrolled margin. Gills are closely spaced and brownish. The sturdy white stem has brownish tinges near the base and remnants of a web-like veil around the upper part. The base is slightly bulbous with soil debris.

Numerous small, black, elongated structures are arranged in irregular, somewhat parallel rows along the length of a pale, dried plant stem. The slightly raised bodies create a speckled, linear pattern contrasting with the lighter stem surface.

Broad, flattened cap with pronounced radial striations along the wavy, irregular margin. The cap is brown with a darker center, dry and slightly cracked. Off-white, crowded gills are visible; the stem is obscured by the angle.

Dense, crust-like layer of numerous small, rounded, yellowish to light brown fruiting bodies tightly clustered together. The surface is granular and slightly rough, with a dotted or pitted appearance and irregular margins blending into the background.

Numerous tiny, irregularly shaped brown fruiting bodies with a granular, rough texture are scattered across the surface. Some display shallow cup or disc-like forms with slightly raised, matte margins.
A single green, heart-shaped leaf with a smooth, slightly glossy surface and prominent veins. Minor edge damage is visible, but no distinct fungal growth, discoloration, or fuzzy patches are present.

Close-up of a mushroom showing densely packed, broad, pale cream to off-white gills radiating from a slender brownish stipe. Another stem nearby is mostly white with brownish debris. The cap margin is smooth, and the overall structure is delicate.

Dark, nearly black patches with lighter brownish-gray mottling cover the rough, uneven surface. Small, scattered, dark granular or slightly raised structures are visible along the irregular margin, distributed in non-uniform patches.

Small, delicate mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate pale bluish-gray caps, closely spaced pale gray to white gills, and slender, smooth, pale grayish stems. The fruiting bodies appear somewhat translucent and moist, clustered together on decaying wood.

Pale greenish to yellow-green crust with a cracked, areolate surface and rough, granular texture. Numerous small, rounded discs with pale, slightly raised edges are scattered across the tightly appressed, irregular patch.

Small, upright fruiting bodies with pale gray, globose heads and slender, rough-textured stipes. The heads have a dry, powdery surface, and one shows a small apical opening. The stipes appear granular or sand-encrusted, with one lying prostrate in the foreground.

Underside of a mushroom with closely spaced, ochre to light brown gills radiating from a slightly curved, pale to light brown smooth stem. Some soil adheres to the stem base. Cap surface is not visible.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened pale tan to yellowish-brown caps, darker centers, and subtle scaly texture. Stems are robust, off-white with brownish stains and soil at the base. Gills are densely spaced and brownish.

Broadly convex ochre to yellow-brown cap with a smooth surface and inrolled margin, robust pale stipe with surface fibrils, and closely spaced pale gills visible in sectioned fruitbodies. Flesh is pale, and soil debris adheres to cap and base.

Light brown, flat caps with wavy, irregular margins and a subtle darker central zone. Cap surface is smooth and slightly translucent-striate near the edge. Slender, pale stems with fibrous texture; closely spaced, pale brownish gills beneath.

A patch of bright yellow, finely granular to powdery crust forms an irregular, tightly appressed colony on a rough surface. The vivid yellow coloration is uniform, with no visible lobes or fruiting bodies at this magnification.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, rounded fruiting bodies with central pores are scattered across a pale, fibrous, and granular surface. The fruiting bodies are embedded or slightly raised, with rough, uneven surfaces and a scattered distribution.

Numerous small, bright yellow-green, granular patches form irregular, compact aggregations with a finely textured, powdery surface. The patches are closely appressed, with some cracked or slightly lobate margins, scattered across a rough, brownish background.

Three mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, smooth yellow-brown caps and robust, pale cream to yellowish stems. Gills are closely spaced and pale cream. Bases show remnants of soil and mycelium.

Cluster of mushrooms with smooth, moist, medium to dark brown convex caps, paler minutely fibrillose margins, closely spaced light brown gills, and long, slender, fibrous stems with faint striations and soil at the base.

Green surface densely covered with numerous small, irregularly distributed pale whitish spots and occasional darker flecks, giving an uneven, slightly rough texture. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible at this magnification.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, yellowish to ochre-brown caps, moist and slightly sticky surfaces, and inrolled, uneven margins. Gills are pale cream to yellowish and closely spaced. Stems are thick, cylindrical, yellowish-buff with brownish discoloration near the base.

Broadly convex cap with a pronounced, darker central umbo. The surface is smooth, moist, and reddish-brown to ochre, with a striate, slightly inrolled margin. Slender, cylindrical stipe matches the cap in color.
A light brown, fibrous pellet with an uneven surface, scattered with numerous small, black, rounded dots embedded irregularly and slightly protruding from the matrix.

Irregular, wavy caps with lobed, uneven margins; centers are dark brown and mottled, fading to pale, almost whitish edges. Underside shows dense, pale spines. Surface appears fibrous to scaly, especially at the center.

Four small, round to oval fruiting bodies with a reddish-brown to orange hue and finely granular, matte surfaces. Margins are even and well-defined, and the bodies are closely grouped in a square-like arrangement.

Pale green to grayish-green tufts with branched, flattened, strap-like lobes radiate outward. Lobes have irregular, finely divided margins, creating a delicate, bushy appearance. Some areas show slight brownish tinges. Surface appears smooth to slightly granular.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened tan to ochre caps, smooth and slightly moist surfaces, and subtle darker centers. Gills are closely spaced, pale grayish-brown, and adnate to slightly sinuate. Stems are slender, off-white to pale tan, fibrous, and variably discolored.

Single small mushroom with a pale beige, smooth cap and slightly incurved margin. Underside shows closely spaced, pale gills. Slender, off-white stem with some substrate and moss remnants at the base.

Small, irregularly shaped, dark gray to black fruiting bodies scattered across a green, slightly hairy leaf surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised, variable in shape—some nearly circular, others elongated or curved—and closely appressed to the leaf.

Solitary mushroom with a convex, pale yellow-ochre cap showing darker discoloration and marginal splits. The cap surface appears slightly fibrillose. The robust, cylindrical stem is pale with brownish streaks and soil clinging to the base.

Dense clusters of minute, white, fuzzy tufts form a powdery, velvety patch with irregular margins, sharply contrasting against the green surface beneath. The closely packed structures create a granular, cottony texture across the affected area.

Numerous small, round, yellowish to brownish raised pustules scattered across green trifoliate leaves, some surrounded by pale or necrotic halos. The pustules disrupt the leaf surface, causing visible damage and discoloration.
A small mushroom viewed from below, showing well-spaced, pale lilac to whitish gills radiating from a slender, slightly curved, velvety lilac-purple stem. The cap surface is not visible.

Slender, upright, club-shaped structures with thin, dark stalks and rounded, pale to whitish, granular-topped heads. The fruiting bodies are sparsely scattered and well separated, each with a slightly expanded apex.

Green leaves with a slightly hairy surface and entire margins, displaying scattered small, irregular brown spots and pale yellowish lesions. Some leaves show irregular holes. No distinct fungal structures are visible.

Small, spherical fruiting bodies with a metallic bronze to gold sheen, borne on slender stalks among green moss. Some translucent, globular structures are also present, possibly representing different developmental stages. Surfaces appear smooth and the fruiting bodies are loosely grouped or solitary.

Leaves display numerous pale, circular to irregular spots, some with faint yellow halos and central brownish areas. Lesions are flat to subtly raised, scattered, and vary in size, with no clear margin or fuzzy texture.

Leaf displays scattered, irregular pale yellow to light greenish spots with diffuse brownish centers and margins. Affected areas are slightly sunken, surrounded by healthy green tissue. The leaf surface is fuzzy with fine trichomes. Spots vary in size, some merging together.

A solitary mushroom with a slender, pale cream stipe and a smooth, convex cap. The underside reveals closely spaced, decurrent gills that are pale and run partway down the stem. The margin of the cap is thin and even.

A small, circular to slightly irregular brown disc with a smooth, moist, and glossy surface. The margin is entire but subtly uneven, and the fruiting body is sessile, directly attached to the substrate.

Leaves display numerous small, round to irregular dark brown or blackish spots scattered across pale green to yellowish surfaces. Margins are scalloped, and the leaf texture appears slightly wilted with lesions distributed throughout.
Thin, irregular, grayish to dark brown crust closely attached to the wood, with a rough, uneven surface and indistinct margin. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible.

Tiny, upright fruiting bodies with slender brown stalks and pale, cup-shaped tops. Each cup is capped with a granular, white powdery material, and the sides appear smooth to slightly roughened. The cups are loosely clustered and mostly even-margined, with occasional slight splits.

Small mushrooms with ochre to tan, dry, fibrous caps showing fine radial fibrils and striate margins. Caps range from convex to nearly flat, some with a central bump. Slender, pale stems are soil-covered at the base. Gills beneath caps are closely spaced and well-developed.

Rounded, olive-brown fruiting bodies with finely granular to minutely spiny surfaces. The texture appears rough, and the surface ornamentation is darker than the background tissue. No visible stipe or openings; fruiting bodies are closely clustered.

Several minute, rounded fruiting bodies with a granular, roughened surface. They are closely grouped, grayish to off-white in color, and display a slightly moist, reflective appearance under magnification.
A small, low, oval fruiting body with a matte, granular to velvety surface. The color is grayish to dark brown, and the margin is indistinct, blending smoothly into the surrounding granular matrix.

Slender, dark, hair-like stalks each support a single, round, powdery head with a delicate, fuzzy texture. The sporangia are dark brown to black, appearing fragile and finely detailed against the woody surface.

Tiny, dark, upright structures with antler-like branching emerge from the surface. The texture appears rough and granular, and the color ranges from blackish to dark brown. The fruitbodies are scattered, solitary, or in small groups, and are very small in size.
Extensive irregular patches of tiny, black, dot-like fruiting bodies densely scattered and embedded in rough, weathered wood, forming granular, darkened zones against a lighter background.

Dense, pale, cottony mycelial mats with numerous minute, slender, dark brown to black erect structures emerging. The surface is web-like and filamentous, with small, scattered, stalked fruiting bodies and no distinct caps visible.

A long, cylindrical structure with a pointed tip, showing a gradient from dark to light brown. The surface is dotted with small white spots and sparsely covered with fine, black, hair-like projections, giving a smooth yet slightly bristled appearance.
A slender, dark brown stick with a rough, textured surface and a small lateral protrusion. The surface is uneven and slightly ridged, with minor discoloration and no clearly visible fruiting bodies.

Light brown caps with darker spots and a slightly uneven, fibrillose surface. Margins are irregular and inrolled. Stems are pale cream, with soil at the base. Gills are closely spaced and pale, visible on upturned and sectioned specimens.

Small, black, rounded to flask-shaped structures are scattered and slightly raised above the pale, fibrous wood surface. The fruiting bodies have a hard, compact appearance and are partially embedded in the substrate.

Numerous tiny, rounded black structures scattered irregularly across reddish-stained wood, with a matte to slightly rough texture. Some pale, cottony patches are present nearby, contrasting with the dark fruiting bodies.

A single, delicate mushroom with a long, slender, translucent white stem and a small, brown cap. The cap is convex with distinctly grooved margins and slightly curled edges. The overall appearance is fragile and graceful.

Convex to slightly flattened ochre to yellow-brown caps with darker centers and subtle fibrillose texture. Irregular, wavy margins, pale brown gills, and slender, pale stems with fibrous surfaces and soil at the base. Leaf debris adheres to some caps.

Pale gray to greenish-gray foliose thallus with irregularly branched, lobulate margins. Central area is granular and sorediate, with a slightly powdery texture. Lobes radiate outward, tightly appressed, showing a mottled, uneven surface.

A single, delicate mushroom with a thin, translucent pale stem and a small, conical to bell-shaped cap. The cap margin is smooth and slightly incurved, with faintly visible gills beneath. The overall structure appears fragile and semi-translucent.

Uneven, dark brown to blackish surface dotted with numerous small, pale yellow to cream granules. Scattered, slightly raised, rounded to irregular reddish-brown bodies and fine, filamentous strands are visible across the textured surface.
Tiny, dark brown, globose sporangia with finely textured surfaces, each perched atop a slender, translucent stalk. The sporangia are arranged singly but closely together on the wood surface.

A single, slender, upright cylindrical structure with a smooth to slightly granular surface. The color is yellowish, more intense toward the top and paler at the base, tapering slightly to a rounded tip. No cap or gills are visible.

Numerous tiny, cup-shaped structures about 1 mm wide, with thin, fragile margins and white, powdery or crystalline interiors. Some cups are partially broken, exposing granular spore masses, and all contrast sharply against the brown background.

Small, dark brown to black, globose bodies with elongated, glossy, tapering necks emerge from a dense, white, cottony mat. The necks are smooth and shiny, contrasting with the fuzzy, filamentous mycelial covering.

Numerous small, black, round to slightly oval fruiting bodies with rough, granular surfaces are scattered and sometimes clustered on the woody substrate, partially immersed and blending into the bark. The fruiting bodies appear matte to slightly shiny, contrasting with the lighter, fibrous wood.

A single mushroom with a convex, brown cap fading to a paler, striate margin. The cap is dry and finely fibrous. Gills are closely spaced and pale, and the long, slender stem is white with soil clinging to its base.

Leaves display scattered, irregular dark brown to black spots with surrounding yellow and red discoloration. The spots are circular to angular, sometimes merging, and concentrated along veins and margins. Leaf colors range from green to yellow to brown, with matte surfaces and flat lesions.

Mushrooms with smooth, convex to slightly flattened brown caps, medium brown gills, and slender, pale stems showing brownish or pinkish discoloration and fibrous texture. Some fruiting bodies are upright while others are tilted or lying on their sides.

Thin, spreading white to cream patches with a spongy, finely pored surface and irregular, slightly fibrillose margins blending into the substrate. The patches are contiguous and form a crust-like appearance.

Numerous tiny, round, pale gray to off-white sporangia with cracked, powdery surfaces sit atop slender, orange-brown stalks. The fruiting bodies are scattered and evenly spaced, some emerging from holes in the substrate.

Tiny, cup-shaped structures with finely granular brown exteriors, each topped with a dense, intricate mass of white filaments. The cups are supported by short reddish-brown stalks and grouped closely together, with sharply defined margins.

Thin, spreading white to cream patch with a densely textured surface of fine, maze-like pores and short ridges. The margin is irregular and lobed, with a soft, slightly cottony appearance and no visible stem or cap.
Three slender, translucent to whitish, thread-like stalks with smooth, shiny surfaces and subtle club-shaped swellings at their tips emerge delicately from a small piece of plant debris.

An elongated, unbranched, club-shaped fruiting body with a yellowish-brown color, smooth to slightly rough surface, white patches near the base, and a gradual tapering toward the tip, emerging upright among decaying leaves.

Several black, irregularly rounded to flattened patches are embedded in the woody surface, appearing as discrete, dark, slightly raised spots with a roughened texture scattered across the light brown, fibrous substrate.

Tiny, spherical fruiting bodies about 1 mm wide, pale cream to whitish, each topped with a dense, cottony, white tuft. The bases are distinctly darker brown and each structure stands on a short, slender stalk, forming scattered, clustered groups.
Numerous small, dark, nearly spherical bodies densely clustered, each surrounded by prominent, stiff, dark hair-like bristles radiating outward, creating a bristly texture on the woody surface.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to flattened, yellow to yellow-brown caps showing greenish tints and a moist, sticky surface. Cap margins are irregular and wavy. White to pale cream, crowded gills and robust, pale stipes with soil at the base.

Dense mat of small, overlapping, greenish to brownish foliose lobes with rounded to irregular, slightly crenulate margins. Surface appears slightly glossy and three-dimensional, with no visible reproductive structures. Lobes are compact and only a few millimeters across, creating an intricate, cohesive texture.

Irregular, flat patches with a grayish-white to pale greenish hue, featuring small, rounded, overlapping lobes and a slightly granular surface. Margins are uneven and indistinct, scattered in discrete clusters on rough bark.
Slender, light brown conifer needles scattered on green moss, each needle marked by parallel rows of small, elongated black spots forming narrow, slightly raised lines along their length.

Two mushrooms with convex to conical, light to medium brown caps, finely fibrillose and striate at the margins, partially covered in soil. Pale brown, closely spaced gills are visible beneath, and slender, smooth stipes match the cap color.

Dense clusters of tiny, circular fruiting bodies with dark, glossy centers and prominent white, fuzzy margins, creating a speckled pattern on a dark, granular surface. The white rims are finely filamentous, giving a soft, hairy appearance around each disc.

Small, delicate mushroom viewed from below, showing pale, translucent, well-spaced gills radiating in a star-like pattern. The thin, slightly undulate cap margin has a faintly frosted texture. The slender stipe is pale and enters centrally.

Small, rounded fruiting bodies densely coated in pale, woolly mycelium, each topped with a slender, dark, erect neck. The clustered structures display a fibrous, matted surface with beige to light brown coloration and contrasting dark necks.

Whitish to pale gray, rough crust with scattered small black rounded structures. The black fruiting bodies are slightly immersed to sessile, with a granular or powdery surface, distributed irregularly across the uneven thallus.

Green, deeply lobed leaves display numerous small, irregular white spots scattered across the surface, creating a distinct contrast with the healthy green tissue. The leaf margins are smooth, and no other fungal structures are visible.

Irregular brown lesions and diffuse necrotic patches on a green leaf surface, with affected areas blending into healthy tissue. No distinct fruiting bodies or visible mycelium are apparent at this magnification.

A thin, white to off-white, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, with a papery, membranous texture. The patch is irregular and diffuse, showing slightly scaly or cracked areas and scattered small debris. Margins are uneven and indistinct.

Crustose thallus with a cracked, areolate, grayish-white surface. Scattered small, black, rounded apothecia are slightly raised and rough-textured. The surface appears dry, uneven, and granular, with irregular margins and distinct fissures.

Numerous tiny, white, cap-like fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces, each perched on a slender, short stalk. Densely clustered, they create a finely granular texture against the dark, rough background.

Elongated, smooth-edged green leaves on a slender stem, with some leaves showing faint yellowish or pale patches. No visible fungal structures or sporulation; leaf surfaces appear smooth and undistorted.

Dense mat of small, overlapping, irregularly lobed segments with a yellow-green to olive hue and slightly glossy, undulate surfaces. Lobes are closely packed, forming a leafy texture with occasional darkened spots.

Numerous small, dark, nearly spherical bodies with rough surfaces, each surrounded by prominent, stiff, hair-like bristles. The fruiting bodies are densely clustered and stand out against a lighter brown background.

Tiny, dark, erect structures with rounded blackish bases and slender black stalks, some topped with small white, pearl-like tips. The surface appears smooth to slightly rough, and the fruiting bodies are sparsely scattered.

A single mushroom with a convex, ruffled light brown cap and prominent gills underneath. The slender, elongated stem is light brown with darker patches and some soil debris, lying horizontally on a weathered wooden surface.

Multiple circular lesions with pale yellow to whitish halos and dark brown to blackish centers are scattered across the leaf surface. The spots have distinct margins and appear slightly sunken compared to the surrounding healthy tissue.

A resupinate, crust-like layer with pale cream to light yellow color, finely porous surface, and minutely textured appearance. The margin is thin, slightly undulating, and even, with small, densely packed pores and a smooth to finely granular texture.

Three mushrooms with convex, pale yellow to greenish-yellow caps, smooth and moist surfaces, and wavy margins. White, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps. Stipes are robust, pale, and darkened with soil at the base.

Yellowish-brown needle segments with several black, elongated, lens-shaped fruiting bodies embedded in the surface. The fruiting bodies are shiny, slightly raised, and arranged in a linear pattern along the needle.

Small, upright, urn-shaped structures with slender stalks, each topped by a granular white covering. Many have open apices revealing dark spore masses inside. The surface appears powdery or crystalline, and the sporocarps are scattered across the woody substrate.

Granular, pale greenish to whitish surface forming irregular patches with indistinct margins. Densely covered with minute, powdery structures, giving a rough, crustose texture. Some brownish areas are interspersed, and no distinct lobes or fruiting bodies are visible.

Numerous small, irregular pale to light brown spots scattered across the green leaf surface, some slightly sunken with faint central darkening. Lesions are diffuse, vary in size, and follow the leaf veins without forming distinct fruiting bodies.

Dense mat of small, intricately lobed, greenish-olive to brownish thallus with rough, uneven texture. Lobes are closely packed, with undulate and crenulate margins, forming a tightly appressed, contiguous patch.

Small, sessile, disc-shaped fruiting body with a brownish-yellow, finely granular upper surface. The margin is pale and slightly fuzzy, while the lower surface is also pale. The fungus appears solitary and directly attached to the substrate.

A tiny, delicate mushroom with a pale, conical to bell-shaped cap showing faint striations and a smooth surface. The margin is even, and the slender, elongated stem is similarly pale. No gills are visible from this angle.

Delicate mushroom with a slender, translucent pale stem and a small, smooth, cream-colored cap. Gills are broad, widely spaced, and creamy white, free from the stem. The overall structure appears fragile and glassy.

Numerous tiny, black, rounded dots densely scattered and slightly embedded on a rough, cracked, light to dark brown woody surface, creating a dotted appearance with uneven texture and darkened patches.
