Numerous tiny, white, fuzzy patches and tufts are scattered irregularly across the green leaf surface, forming delicate, cottony clusters. Some areas show denser aggregations, while the underlying leaf remains green and intact.
Tiny, white, cup- to disc-shaped fruiting bodies with conspicuously hairy, fuzzy margins. The surface appears soft and delicate, and each structure is sessile and closely grouped.
Pale greenish to whitish patch with a granular, finely lobed surface. Irregularly shaped colony with small, overlapping lobes and a powdery, matte texture. Margins are uneven and slightly lobulate.

Pale pinkish-tan cap with a velvety texture and inrolled margin, closely spaced cream to pale yellow gills, and a solid, fibrous off-white stem. The cut surface reveals dense, fibrous flesh. Some soil clings to the base.

Pale gray to whitish patchy thallus with a granular to lobulate surface, small irregular lobes, rough uneven texture, and slightly raised, irregular margins. The lichen appears tightly appressed and covers much of the visible area.

Cluster of globose to pear-shaped fruiting bodies with a dry, muted brownish-tan surface covered in fine, granular to warty texture. Rounded margins and no visible openings, closely grouped among leaf litter and soil.

Whitish, cracked, and granular surface with scattered black, rounded, slightly raised apothecia. The apothecia contrast sharply against the pale, rough, and uneven background, some appearing slightly immersed within the crust.

Pale whitish to light gray, flat, leaf-like structure with irregularly lobed, somewhat scalloped margins. Surface appears smooth to slightly granular, closely pressed to the background, with radiating lobes and no visible reproductive structures.

Dark brown, rough, and crusty surface tightly adhering to wood, with irregular bumps and wart-like protrusions. Lighter patches and subtle greenish or whitish areas are scattered across the uneven, hard texture.

Black, irregular, crust-like patches embedded in or slightly raised above the brown bark surface, with a rough, compact, and almost carbonaceous texture. The patches are scattered and lack distinct margins.

A thin, gray, crust-like layer tightly covering the stone, dotted with numerous tiny, black, rounded to irregular specks. The surface appears rough, granular, and uneven, with no visible margins or lobes. The black spots are scattered and slightly raised or immersed.

Small, cup-shaped structures with thin, fragile white margins and interiors dotted with orange-yellow granules. Some cups display a powdery, crystalline white mass, while others have fragmented edges revealing granular inner surfaces. The overall texture appears delicate and brittle.

A single, centrally positioned mushroom cap with pale beige to light yellowish color, faint radial striations, and a slightly uneven surface. The margin is smooth and regular, with no visible gills or stem from this top-down view.

Cluster of round, smooth to slightly roughened fruiting bodies, pale cream to light brown in color. One specimen shows a darker, purplish-brown apex with a ruptured opening exposing the spore mass. Surfaces appear dry and somewhat powdery.

Robust mushrooms with thick, white stems covered in soil and debris. Caps are convex to slightly flattened, pale beige to cream, with some brownish patches and inrolled margins. Gills are closely spaced, pale to light tan, and attached to the stem.

Thin, white, crust-like layer with a smooth to finely granular surface, scattered small brownish spots, and several clear water droplets. The margin is diffuse and irregular, blending into the decaying leaves.

Dense mat of thin, irregularly lobed, leaf-like structures with finely incised, lacy margins. Predominantly pale green to olive-green, some areas grayish. Surface smooth to slightly wrinkled, overlapping and closely appressed.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, pale yellowish to cream caps, one showing a woolly margin. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to light yellow, and decurrent onto robust, similarly colored stipes. Some soil and debris adhere to the surfaces.
A green, three-lobed leaf with a central, dark brown, irregularly edged lesion and smaller brown spots near the lobe tips. The affected areas appear dry and discolored compared to the healthy tissue.

A single, delicate structure with a slender, black, hair-like stalk topped by a globose, brown sporangium. The sporangium has a rough, granular, and slightly fuzzy surface. The entire fruiting body is about 1 mm tall.

Convex to irregular caps with pale yellow to greenish-yellow tones and brownish patches, smooth inrolled margins, white crowded gills, and robust yellowish stems with soil at the base. Surface of stems appears smooth.

Tiny, pale yellow to cream cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded margins cluster on a dark, moist surface. The cups are smooth, somewhat translucent, and very small, accentuating their delicate appearance against the contrasting background.

Irregular, dark gray to black crustose patches scattered across a reddish-brown surface, with a rough, uneven texture. Small granular or slightly raised areas are present, along with powdery deposits and a prominent central crack. The growth appears mottled and blends into the background.

Dense mat of small, rounded to irregular lobes with glossy olive-green to yellow-green coloration. Surface is smooth with granular outgrowths, and margins are undulate and slightly crenulate. No visible fruiting bodies.

Multiple circular to irregular spots with dark brown centers and distinct yellowish halos are scattered across the moist green leaf. The lesions appear slightly sunken and well-defined, with raised margins and a random distribution.

A single, small, dome-shaped fruiting body with a finely granular, glistening surface. The color is pale tan to yellowish-brown, with a smooth, slightly raised margin and a compact, sessile structure.

Delicate, upright fruiting bodies with slender, brownish stems and smooth, white, club-shaped heads. The structures are sparsely distributed and emerge individually, appearing very small against the substrate.

A single mushroom with a medium brown, convex to bell-shaped cap featuring a granular surface and darker soil patches. The slender, cylindrical stipe is pale cream to off-white, emerging cleanly from moist soil. Gills are not visible.

Pale yellowish, convex cap with a slightly inrolled, woolly margin. Closely spaced, decurrent cream gills and a robust, cylindrical stem matching the cap’s color. Some soil and debris adhere to the surface. A smaller, rounder specimen is nearby.

Dense, circular patch with dark olive-green to brownish color, lobate and irregular wrinkled margins. Surface appears uneven, granular, and slightly velvety, standing out with its compact, matte texture against lighter surrounding lichens.

Two mushrooms with convex, dark reddish-brown, matte caps bearing scattered pale patches. A cut specimen reveals closely spaced, moderately broad, cream to pale yellow gills and a solid, off-white cylindrical stipe with slight brownish discoloration at the base.

Several small, pale, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, whitish to cream surfaces and thin, delicate texture are scattered among decaying leaves. The cups are sessile, lack visible stems, and have even, unornamented margins.

Cluster of medium to small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, dry, finely hairy brown caps. Stems are slender, pale to light brown, and slightly fibrous. Gills are closely spaced, pale to light brown, and attached to the stem. Caps have even margins.

Two small, irregularly rounded bodies with a rough, mottled brown exterior; one is cut open, showing a dense, uniform, brownish interior. The surface appears thin and fragile, with some soil particles adhering.

Mature fruiting body with a reddish-brown, smooth, slightly convex cap and even margin. Gills are closely spaced, white to cream, and clearly visible. The robust, cylindrical stipe is white, smooth, and firm.
Multiple upright, branched, coral-like fruiting bodies in pale yellowish to white, with a powdery surface, emerge from a reddish-brown insect pupa partially covered in a white fungal mat.

Dense cluster of irregular, branched structures with curled, contorted margins. Surfaces appear granular, illuminated in vivid purple, green, and white hues, creating a striking, intricate pattern. The growths are small and closely packed, with no clear reproductive bodies visible.

Patchy, crust-like growth tightly attached to the surface, with a rough, uneven, and dry texture. Brown with lighter and darker mottling, featuring scattered black-bordered, angular to irregular embedded fruiting bodies. Some greenish areas are present.

Pine needles display reddish-brown bands and irregular necrotic lesions, with some needles showing tip dieback. The coloration ranges from green to brown, and the smooth-textured needles are loosely scattered and overlapping.

Green leaf surface marked by scattered, irregular brown spots of varying size with diffuse, mottled margins. Spots are distributed across the matte, slightly granular leaf, intersected by a prominent central vein.

Globose to subglobose fruiting body with a dry, rough, brown surface densely covered in small, wart-like projections. A lighter patch is visible near the top, and the base has remnants of adhering debris. Margins are rounded and compact.

A small, dark, irregularly shaped fruiting body with a rough, wrinkled surface and uneven margins, emerging from fibrous material. The structure is compact, somewhat globose, and solitary, with nearby greenish and translucent elements.

Convex cap with deep reddish-brown color, peeling cuticle exposing pinkish-white flesh beneath. Cap margin is irregular and damaged. Robust white stem and closely spaced white gills. Some debris present on the cap surface.
Slender, elongated pale stipe supporting a small, bell-shaped cap with a brownish apex fading to a translucent margin. Cap surface is smooth, moist, and marked by prominent radial striations.
Long, slender pine needles in clusters, with several displaying a transition from healthy green to reddish-brown discoloration and drying, while others remain green and flexible.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to flattened, light brown, finely scaly caps and irregular, wavy margins. Gills are medium brown and moderately spaced. Stems are cylindrical, pale, and show soil at the base.

Broad, gray to pale gray thallus with a leathery, undulating surface. Margins are lobed and wavy, featuring small holes and indentations. The thallus is closely appressed with a slightly raised central area.

Convex to broadly convex caps in pale to medium brown with smooth to finely fibrillose surfaces. Stipes are long, slender, white to pale cream, often with brownish stains and soil at the base. Gills are moderately crowded, pale ochre to light brown, with faint veil remnants on the stipes.

Numerous tiny, translucent whitish to pale gray discs with conspicuously fuzzy, ciliate margins are scattered and loosely clustered on a dark, moist surface. The apothecia are circular to slightly oval, with smooth, glassy surfaces and delicate, hair-like edges.

Numerous tiny, vivid reddish-brown to orange, disc-shaped fruitbodies scattered across dark soil. The discs are mostly circular, closely appressed, and display minutely granular or hairy margins. Sizes vary slightly, with some forming small clusters among soil particles and roots.

Slender, yellowish stalk slightly curved, ending in a dense, white, cottony mass. Base attached to a lumpy, off-white and reddish-brown mass with a smooth stalk and distinctly fluffy, irregular spore-bearing tip.

Cluster of upright, irregularly branched structures with pale to light brownish, flattened, and contorted lobes. Margins are uneven and lobed, with a granular, dusty surface and some powdery coating. Soil and sand grains are attached at the base.

Small, delicate fruiting body with a long, slender, light brown stem and a tiny cap featuring a ruffled, frilled margin. The cap is dry and opaque, with visible gills underneath. The specimen measures only a few centimeters in length.

Elongated, parallel, needle-like structures in pale tan to light brown, each showing faint reddish or orange bands or lesions. Surfaces appear smooth and uniform in width, with subtle discolorations and no prominent fruiting bodies.

Slender, upright, white fruiting bodies with a fine, fuzzy texture. Cylindrical and elongated, some with small lateral branches, giving a tree-like or antlered appearance. Surface appears powdery or granular, and the fruiting bodies are scattered but arise from the same area.

Irregular, subglobose to lobed fruiting bodies with a warty, leathery dark brown to yellowish-brown surface. Some are cut open, showing a pale yellowish to off-white, marbled and firm interior. Partially embedded in soil and surrounded by organic debris.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, dark reddish-brown caps featuring scattered white spots and smooth, slightly incurved margins. Thick, robust, white stems with a smooth texture. Gills are not visible.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, light to medium brown, fuzzy-textured caps featuring a central umbo. Stems are slender, off-white to pale brown, and slightly fibrous. Gills beneath the caps are closely spaced and pale brown. Caps have irregular, indistinct margins.

Crustose, reddish-brown to rusty brown surface with rough, granular texture. Scattered, slightly raised pustules and numerous tiny black dots create a speckled appearance. Margins are irregular and the surface appears compact and brittle.

Solitary mushroom with a convex, smooth brown cap showing a missing section at the margin, exposing white flesh. The stipe is thick, cylindrical, and bright white with a smooth surface. Gills are not visible.

Cluster of small mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate brown, finely fibrous caps, lighter margins, crowded pale to medium brown gills, and slender, curved, fibrous stems. Soil clings to the stem bases, and the caps display a subtle fuzzy texture.

Convex to slightly flattened caps with a fuzzy, fibrous surface; light brown with darker centers. Cap margins are irregular. Stems are pale cream with brownish tints, and gills are closely spaced and pale. Soil and leaf debris adhere to the bases.

Slender, upright, white to pale cream fruiting bodies with a slightly rough or powdery surface. Cylindrical and unbranched, tapering gently toward the apex, scattered among decaying leaves and twigs on the forest floor.

Two pale, oval, fibrous masses with coarse surfaces, each bearing several small, dark, rounded to irregular bumps on top. The dark fruiting bodies stand out against the light, plant-debris-covered background.

Numerous tiny, white, cup-shaped structures with slightly raised, well-defined margins are densely scattered across a dark, rough surface, creating a granular, delicate appearance. Each cup is less than a millimeter wide and appears translucent to opaque.

Several upright, slender, cylindrical fruiting bodies coated with sand, each with a distinctly black tip. The lower portions are pale and granular from sand, emerging from a bulbous, irregular central mass.

Dense cluster of irregularly lobed, curled squamules with a grayish to brownish hue. Surface appears dry and rough, with overlapping scales forming a compact mat. Scattered brown, rounded apothecia are visible among the squamules. Some areas show a reddish tint.
Small, vivid orange disc-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, slightly moist surface. The margin is densely fringed with fine, dark, hair-like structures, giving a velvety appearance.

Small, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with vivid orange-red, smooth, moist-looking surfaces. Margins are slightly darkened and appear fringed with fine hairs. Each disc is attached to clumps of plant debris, and a ruler shows their small size.

A small, dark, irregularly lobed fruiting body with a compact, rounded shape. The surface is matte and slightly textured, showing subtle purplish hues. A central depression contains a clear droplet, and no stipe is visible.

Dense cluster of oval to cylindrical caps, white to pale gray, covered in coarse, upturned scales. Caps vary from round and small to elongated and mature, forming a compact, tightly packed group with short, mostly hidden stems.

Two mushrooms with smooth, convex reddish-brown caps and slightly paler margins. Stipes are thick, cylindrical, and white. Gills are closely spaced, cream to pale yellow, and attached to the stipe. Surfaces appear smooth and unblemished.

A single, erect fruiting body with a dark brown to blackish, rough and knobby cap, tapering into a coarse, uneven stalk. The surface is dry and irregular, with a solitary arrangement against fibrous substrate fragments.

Numerous small, orange-brown, slightly raised pustules scattered irregularly across a smooth, light green leaf surface. The pustules are dry, granular, and mostly located between visible leaf veins, with diffuse margins and variable sizes.

Subglobose, truffle-like fruiting bodies with a rough, brown, warty exterior. The cut surface reveals a dense, pale brown to tan interior with a marbled, labyrinthine pattern. No distinct cap or stem is visible.
Numerous tiny, circular, slightly raised fruiting bodies with translucent yellowish centers and distinct reddish-brown, glistening margins, closely grouped on a yellowish-brown woody surface.

A small, bright orange, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, moist surface and slightly irregular margin, sitting flat and sessile on dark, decaying wood. The vivid orange sharply contrasts with the rough, brown substrate.

Dense clusters of small, rounded, pebble-like bodies with a dark, almost blackish-brown, matte surface. The texture is granular to slightly rough, and the fruiting bodies are closely packed, forming irregular, contiguous patches.

Slender, elongated fruiting bodies with pale to off-white, conical to bell-shaped caps. Cap margins are smooth, and the gills beneath are closely spaced and pale. Stipes are thin, pale, and slightly curved, with soil clinging to the base.
Small, roughly spherical bodies with a brown, patchy, and slightly rough exterior. The cut surface reveals a dense, solid, marbled brown interior with a labyrinthine pattern and even margin.
A single mushroom viewed from below, displaying white, closely spaced gills and a thick, smooth, cylindrical white stipe with some soil debris attached. The cap surface and margin are not visible.
Dark, nearly black crust forming a rough, uneven patch on the soil. The surface is granular with lumpy protrusions and irregular margins, tightly adhering to the substrate.

A thin, continuous, white to pale cream crust covers the surface, appearing smooth to slightly uneven with fine cracking and scattered embedded debris. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the background without distinct fruiting bodies.

A thin, crust-like layer forms a continuous, whitish to pale cream coating with a finely granular, frosted texture. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the surface, and the growth appears patchy and irregular without distinct edges or visible fruitbodies.

Minute, nearly black, spherical bodies scattered on wood, each adorned with stiff, radiating hair-like setae, giving a spiny appearance. The dark fruiting bodies contrast sharply with the lighter, fibrous substrate.

Dense cluster of elongated, white mushrooms with shaggy, scaly cylindrical to ovoid caps. Caps are mostly closed, pale, and slightly yellowed, with inrolled or splitting margins and soil adhering to surfaces.

Clustered mushrooms with conical to bell-shaped, pale off-white caps featuring a shaggy, fibrous texture. Some caps show splitting or damage at the edges. Stems are short and white, with fruiting bodies in various stages from rounded to elongated.

Tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with slightly irregular edges are scattered in loose groups. They appear translucent to opaque and are connected by fine, white mycelial threads across a dark, woody surface.

A small, roughly spherical fruiting body with a mottled brown surface, patches of lighter color, and a slightly rough, uneven texture. The margin is rounded and the surface appears dry, with no visible gills or pores.

Scattered, round lesions with dark brown to black margins and pale tan centers, some showing faint concentric rings. Spots are well-defined, slightly sunken, and vary in size, with a few merging at the leaf edge.

Dense cluster of slender, elongated stems topped with small caps in various stages of black, inky collapse. Many caps are dissolving, with irregular, moist, and tattered edges, and remnants of lighter color on some caps.

Scattered brown lesions with irregular, angular margins and dark borders surround pale, sunken centers on a green leaf. The lesions are sharply demarcated from healthy tissue, with some yellowing near the edges. No visible fungal structures are present.

Densely packed, ovoid caps with a cracked, patchy surface showing a mosaic of pale tan, gray, and brown. The dry, scaly texture reveals lighter tissue beneath the cracks. Stems and gills are mostly obscured by the tight clustering.

Cluster of mushrooms with brown, finely hairy caps, some convex and others nearly flat with darker centers. Gills are closely spaced and pale to light brown. Stems are slender, white to pale brown, and several bases retain soil. Size ranges from about 2 to 8 centimeters.
Solitary mushroom with a deep reddish-brown, smooth convex cap and paler striate margin. White, closely spaced gills beneath the cap and a robust, cylindrical, smooth white stipe.

Dense cluster of upright, branched structures with rough, granular surfaces. Color ranges from pale brown to grayish with whitish, powdery areas. Margins are irregular and sometimes lobed, and the overall appearance is compact with closely grouped branches.

Slender, elongated fruiting bodies with smooth, white to pale yellow surfaces emerge from a central mass. The cylindrical structures are thin, slightly curved, and radiate outward, displaying a delicate, fibrous texture with even, unornamented margins.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, smooth, dark reddish-brown caps and even margins. The gills are closely spaced, white to cream, and the robust, cylindrical stipes are solid white, slightly tapering toward the base.

Slender, elongated, club-shaped fruiting bodies emerge in a clustered arrangement from soil. They are pale yellowish to white, unbranched, tapering, and have a slightly rough or powdery surface. No distinct cap or gills are visible.

Numerous minute, rounded, dark brown to nearly black bumps scattered across a woody surface. The structures are slightly raised, embedded, and have a somewhat glossy appearance, arranged in a loose, irregular pattern.

Dark brown to black, slender, wiry fruiting bodies with a twisted, contorted form emerge in small groups from pale, fibrous pellets. Surfaces appear rough and textured, contrasting with the light substrate.

A white, slightly curved stem with a bulbous base, partially covered in soil and dark speckles. Fine, root-like strands and clumps of dark organic matter surround the base. No cap or gills are visible in the image.

Clustered mushrooms with convex, light brown to tan caps, smooth to finely fibrillose surfaces, and slightly inrolled margins. Gills are brownish and well-developed. Stipes are robust, cylindrical, pale to light brown, and slightly fibrous, emerging from beneath dense fallen leaves.

Patch of rough, cracked, cushion-like tissue in orange, reddish, and brown tones. Surface divided into polygonal sections, each with a small dark dot. Texture appears dry, granular, and slightly scaly, with irregular, indistinct margins.

Numerous tiny, rounded, dark brown to nearly black bumps are scattered irregularly across a fibrous, woody surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised, compact, and have a matte to subtly glistening appearance.
Two small, rounded fruiting bodies; one has a smooth, matte brown surface, while the other is more textured and mottled. Both are compact, lacking visible stalks or external structures.

Numerous tiny, dark reddish to brownish, rounded structures are scattered across the wood surface. These hemispherical to subglobose bodies are smooth to slightly roughened and appear embedded or slightly raised, contrasting with the lighter wood.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to flattened, light brown caps featuring darker, velvety centers and uneven margins. Slender, pale stems emerge from the soil, some covered with dirt. Gills are not visible from above.
Dense cluster of pale grayish-brown, ovoid to bell-shaped caps with granular or scaly surfaces. Some caps show splitting at the margins. Slender, white stipes emerge in tight groups among wood chips.

Light to medium brown caps with smooth to slightly fibrous surfaces, convex to plane in shape. Gills are closely spaced and brown. Stems are slender, elongated, and strongly curved, with a fibrous texture and pale brown internal flesh.

Dark, irregularly shaped fruiting bodies clustered together, each with a dense, warty, and lobed surface. The texture appears dry and granular, with rounded protrusions and no visible stalks or distinct margins.

Small mushrooms with convex to plane, dry, finely tomentose brown caps. Gills are crowded and pale to medium brown. Stems are short, sturdy, and fibrous, with soil at the base. Cap margins are even to slightly undulate.

Green, slightly hairy stems densely covered with numerous small, round to irregular, dark brown to black, slightly raised spots. The spots are well-defined, rough-textured, and vary slightly in size, standing out against the green plant tissue.

Numerous tiny, rounded, reddish-brown bumps with a granular texture are scattered irregularly across a fibrous, striated woody surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised and blend into the substrate, forming small clusters.

Small mushroom with a conical, pale cream cap featuring a pronounced central umbo and faint radial fibers. The underside shows moderately crowded, pale gills attached to a slender, matching stem with a fibrous surface. No ring or veil remnants are visible.

Numerous tiny, reddish-orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly glossy surfaces are scattered across dark, moist soil. The discs are mostly under a centimeter wide, grouped loosely or singly, with even, non-fringed margins.

Pine branch with clusters of long, slender needles, some showing brown discoloration and drying. Needles are arranged in bundles, with a mix of healthy green and reddish-brown, dying foliage. No visible fruiting bodies or fungal structures present.

Numerous tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, circular outlines and a slightly translucent look are scattered across dark woody debris. Fine, whitish mycelial threads weave among the delicate discs, creating a subtle, filamentous texture.

Irregular, dark brown lesion with diffuse margins blends into lighter green leaf tissue. The affected area is matte and slightly textured, lacking glossiness or visible spore masses. The lesion appears embedded within the leaf surface.

Four slender mushrooms with smooth, moist, light brown convex to slightly flattened caps. Stems are elongated, pale cream to light brown, with some soil at the base. Gills are closely spaced and pale brown. No veil remnants are visible. Tallest specimen is about 3 cm.

Scattered, irregular brown spots with diffuse margins appear across the green leaf surface, varying in size and shape, with some lesions aligned along the veins. No visible fruiting bodies or mycelium are present.

Sectioned fruiting body showing tightly packed, moderately broad, pale cream to yellowish gills. The cut surface reveals firm, brittle, white to pale internal flesh. The cap margin is slightly curved, and the gills are clearly attached to the context.

Rough, crust-like surface with brownish-orange to reddish-brown coloration, densely dotted with small black spots. Central fissures ooze glossy, black exudates. The texture is uneven, with slightly raised and cracked areas, lacking distinct fruiting bodies or stalks.

Numerous tiny, white, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces and irregular margins are scattered closely together on a rough, brown substrate. The cups are sessile and delicate, varying slightly in size but all very small.

Irregular, dark brown to grayish sunken lesions with pale yellow margins scattered across the leaf. Lesions are angular, with central necrosis and fine whitish particulate material visible on the surface. Surrounding tissue shows some yellowing.

Three mushrooms with smooth, moist, medium brown convex caps. One specimen is upturned, showing pale, closely spaced gills and a pale, slightly fibrillose stem that gently tapers toward the base. Cap margins are even and not striate.
Irregularly rounded, dark brown fruiting bodies with a thick, warty, and scaly exterior. The cut specimen reveals a solid, pale cream to whitish marbled interior, lacking visible gills or pores.
Numerous small, dark brown to black rounded pustules densely scattered along the veins and surfaces of narrow green leaves and stems, creating a rough, irregularly clustered appearance.

Pale, whitish to light gray surface densely scattered with small brownish spots and irregular greenish patches. The texture appears smooth and flat, with no prominent ridges or margins visible in this close-up view.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to flat caps, featuring a darker, felt-like center and paler, fibrous margins. Caps are dry and subtly scaly. Gills are pale to light brown and closely spaced. Stems are slender, cylindrical, and tan, matching the cap edges.

A single, small, rounded sporocarp with a brownish-orange upper surface and a darker, nearly black lower region. The surface appears granular and uneven, with lighter patches and a smooth margin. No stalk is visible.

Small, subglobose to irregular fruiting bodies with thick, white to off-white surfaces, heavily encrusted with soil and debris. Some show cracked or open tops, and all lack visible stems or caps, appearing compact and partially embedded in the ground.

Numerous tiny, smooth, brownish, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies scattered loosely across a moist, granular substrate with plant debris and crystalline particles. Some sporocarps are partially embedded, while others are more exposed.

Leaves display numerous tiny, dark, raised spots scattered across surfaces and veins, with yellowing, browning, curling, and wilted edges. The dark pustules are prominent and concentrated along leaf margins and veins.
Small, round to slightly oval fruiting bodies with a cinnamon to brownish hue and a velvety or granular surface, scattered and sessile with smooth, unraised margins.

Two mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, pale tan caps featuring a slightly darker center. The cap surface is smooth and dry. Gills are free, closely spaced, and pale. Stems are slender, cylindrical, whitish, and slightly fibrous. No ring or veil remnants visible.

Elongated, oval, black fungal structures attached to green stems, with rough, fibrous surfaces and scattered pale, hair-like remnants. The sori are integrated with the plant tissue, standing out sharply against the green background.

Extremely slender, pale, and fragile stems support small, dark, convex to flat caps with smooth or faintly striate margins. The caps appear almost black, contrasting sharply with the translucent stems. No veil remnants or rings are visible.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened light brown caps, smooth to subtly fibrillose surfaces, and densely packed rich brown gills. Stems are pale with brownish streaks and soil remnants, some showing basal mycelium. Pocket knife provides scale.

Longitudinal section reveals a pale to light brown cap with brown, closely spaced gills attached to a fibrous, pale stipe. The interior shows brown discoloration and damage, with visible internal texture and gill attachment.

A green, pinnately divided leaf covered with a conspicuous, powdery white coating that gives the surface a slightly fuzzy appearance. The white layer is diffuse and even, with no visible fruiting bodies or distinct fungal structures.
A hemispherical, brownish to grayish fruiting body with a firm, slightly rough surface densely dotted with minute black pores, giving it a finely speckled appearance.

Semicircular, compact fruiting body with a densely textured, granular black surface. The upper side is covered in dark, coiled or curly elements, with numerous tiny black curls scattered above, creating a strikingly rough and matte appearance.

A slender, translucent stem supports a small, delicate cap with pronounced radiating grooves. The cap is pale white, pleated, and thin, with a fragile, slightly wavy margin. The overall appearance is dainty and solitary.
Small, rounded to slightly elongated yellow-orange fruiting bodies with a fine, powdery or granular surface, scattered and somewhat clustered on a fibrous, organic substrate.
A contiguous mass of dark brown to blackish, irregularly lobed fruiting bodies with a rough, convoluted, brain-like surface, tightly fused and arranged in a linear pattern along decaying wood.

Numerous small, round to oval fruiting bodies with a pale cream to light brown, granular or powdery surface, densely clustered and sometimes fused, covering a dark brown background. Margins are even and surfaces appear dry and finely textured.

Mushrooms with smooth, brownish-purple convex caps, pale closely spaced gills, and stout, off-white stems. One specimen is split, showing brittle, creamy flesh. Caps have even, non-striate margins and some surface debris. Gills are attached and pale yellow.

A delicate, slender stem supports a small, pale grayish cap with pronounced radial pleats and a papery texture. The cap is centrally depressed and slightly damaged, with a fragile, finely grooved margin.

Slender, pale stem supporting an ovoid to conical cap densely covered with rough, wart-like granules. The cap is off-white to grayish, with a powdery texture and no visible splitting at the margin. Fine mycelial threads are present nearby.

Small, scattered, orange-brown powdery pustules with a granular texture are visible on the lower leaf surface and stem. Infected leaves show irregular brown necrotic patches and marginal withering, with some chlorosis and wilted areas.

Irregular clusters of brown, powdery spore masses scattered across a vibrant green leaf, interspersed with numerous white, hair-like trichomes. The spore deposits appear granular and loosely attached, forming distinct patches.

Scattered, dark brown, irregularly shaped, slightly raised pustules appear on the green, slightly hairy leaf surface. The spots are grouped but not merging, with diffuse margins disrupting the smooth leaf texture.

Small mushrooms with slender, pale stems and conical to bell-shaped, light brown caps featuring prominent striations along the margins. The gills are dark and closely spaced, visible on upturned specimens. Clustered among woody debris and leaves.

Elongated, black, rough-textured masses with a fibrous or fuzzy surface, varying from fusiform to cylindrical shapes, attached along green stems with finely divided leaves. Sori appear solitary or in small groups, displaying irregular contours.

A single, round brown sporocarp densely coated in fine yellowish granules, suspended among translucent, ribbon-like, twisted threads. The surface appears slightly rough, with delicate, pale filaments radiating outward.

Numerous small, round, bright orange disks with slightly scalloped edges are scattered among green moss. The smooth, vivid fruiting bodies form loose clusters and contrast sharply with the surrounding foliage and soil.

Swollen, distorted stems and leaf axils display prominent pinkish-red galls with a powdery surface, contrasting sharply against the surrounding healthy green foliage. The affected areas appear irregular and waxy, lacking visible fruiting bodies.

A single, semi-circular fruiting body with pronounced concentric zoned bands in shades of gray-black. The surface is rough, hard, and woody, with an irregular, jagged margin and a robust, compact appearance.

Two close-set fruiting bodies: the left is brown, oval, rough and granular with a short stalk; the right is smaller, darker brown, nearly spherical, and smoother. Both have scattered white particulate debris on their surfaces.

Dark, irregular patch with a cracked, reticulate texture and slightly raised surface on the green leaf. The lesion has a diffuse margin blending into the leaf, with small yellowish-brown spots scattered nearby.

Broad, nearly flat caps with distinct concentric zones of light brown and tan, featuring a scaly texture. Margins are even, and gills are closely spaced, pale cream, and decurrent. Stipe is cylindrical, pale, and smooth.

A compact cluster of small, round, light brown sporangia with a granular, powdery surface, closely grouped on a smooth woody surface. The fruiting bodies are globose and lack visible stalks, forming an irregular arrangement.

Roughly spherical, off-white to light brown fruiting bodies with cracked, warty surfaces and central openings. Surfaces appear dry, brittle, and irregularly fissured, with some darker brown patches. No visible stems; clustered among grass and soil debris.

Numerous small, rounded to slightly flattened yellowish to pale orange dots are scattered across the surface of a brown, woody cone. The dots are discrete, slightly raised, and have smooth margins, standing out against the darker background.

Small, dark brown to black, rounded spots scattered irregularly across a light green leaf surface. The spots are slightly raised, varying in size, and some are surrounded by faint pale or yellowish halos.

A cluster of small, round, beige to light brown fruiting bodies with a granular, powdery surface. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped, sessile, and have indistinct margins blending into the moist brown surface.

Broad, flat caps with a light brown color and distinctly darker, granular centers. The dry surface shows subtle radial fibrils and faintly striate, uneven margins with minor splits. Pale, slender stems support the caps upright.

Slender mushroom with a pale, elongated stem and a cap that is dark brown to nearly black at the margin, with a paler, wrinkled, and textured center. The cap edge appears inky and rough, with a somewhat uneven surface.

Small, round fruiting bodies with a yellowish-brown to ochre hue and smooth to slightly granular surfaces, scattered individually across fibrous and mineral-rich debris. The sporocarps are discrete and measure less than 1 mm in diameter.

Broadly convex to flat yellowish-brown caps with irregular white patches, smooth to slightly sticky surfaces, robust pale to yellowish stipes with veil remnants at the base, and closely spaced pale gills. Some caps are dirt-speckled and margins are entire.

Cluster of mushrooms with brown, dry, finely textured caps showing paler, fibrillose margins and subtle color zoning. Gills are crowded and pale brown, stipes are robust and white to pale brown, with soil clinging to the base.

Elongated, oval-shaped black growths with rough, uneven surfaces and slightly frayed margins, attached directly to green plant stems. Fine filamentous material is visible on the surface, creating a pronounced contrast with the host plant.

Medium-sized mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, medium brown caps showing subtle paler margins and a slightly fibrous surface. Gills are densely packed, broad, and pale brown. Cylindrical, fibrous stipes are encrusted with soil and slightly thickened at the base.

Convex to slightly depressed caps with a central indentation, ochre to tan and covered in rough, scaly texture. Margins are inrolled in younger specimens. Gills are pale, closely spaced, and decurrent. Stipes are robust, cylindrical, and similar in color to the caps.
Rounded, dark brown to black fruiting body with a leathery, textured surface densely dotted with small white granules. The margin is smooth and the structure appears firm and compact.

Two hemispherical, nearly discoid fruiting bodies with alternating dark and pale concentric bands, rough matte surface, and hard, woody texture. The outer margin is dark, rounded, and slightly irregular, with the bodies closely attached side by side.

Hemispherical to cushion-shaped fruitbodies with medium brown, slightly granular matte surfaces and smooth, rounded margins. The fruitbodies are large, well-separated, and rest on weathered wood, with no visible reproductive openings.
Tiny, pale yellow to cream, smooth, disc-shaped fruitbodies with a waxy appearance, scattered and emerging from crevices in a reddish-brown, scaly background. Margins are entire and not fringed.
A fine, powdery white coating covers the surface of a deeply lobed, serrated green leaf, giving it a slightly fuzzy and dusty appearance without visible fruiting bodies.

Clustered mushrooms with smooth, convex to slightly flattened medium brown caps, subtle darker margins, and matte surfaces. Gills are closely spaced, pale brown to tan. Cylindrical stems are off-white to pale brown with darker streaks and soil at the base.

Irregularly lobed, cushion-like masses with a convoluted, brain-like surface. The texture appears rough and matte, colored dark grayish-brown. Multiple lobes are densely merged, forming a firm, compact cluster attached to wood.

Small, round, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with vivid orange, smooth, matte surfaces, scattered among dense, spiky green structures. One fruiting body is pale white, possibly a color variant. The apothecia are sessile, with even, well-defined margins and no visible stalks.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, smooth, moist-looking caps in medium to light brown, darker at the center. Cap margins are wavy and irregular, with one cap showing damage. Stems are robust, pale brown to off-white, and gills are closely spaced and brownish.

A single, dark brown ovoid body with a glossy, slightly wrinkled surface, adorned with several translucent to off-white crystalline deposits. Supported by a short brownish stalk, the sporocarp stands out against a moist, granular background.

Two slender mushrooms with smooth, pale stems showing subtle brownish granulation near the base. The gills are off-white to cream, closely spaced, and free from the stem. Cap margins are even and not ruffled, with the caps only partially visible from below.

Broad, depressed cap with dark brown to reddish-brown surface, irregular pale patches, and weathered areas. Cap margin is wavy and uneven. White to cream, closely spaced gills extend to a stout, cylindrical white stipe. Surface shows debris and damage.

Solitary mushroom with a convex to slightly flattened cap, dark brown at the center fading to lighter brown at the edges. The cap margin is distinctly white, frilled, and fibrous. The surface appears finely granular or velvety. Pale, slender stem partially visible.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, circular to irregular spots scattered across the green leaf surface, some slightly sunken and contrasting with the healthy tissue. The lower leaf shows fewer, less pronounced spots. Leaves are broad with serrated edges and prominent veins.

Two pale, smooth-capped mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened shapes; the larger cap has a scalloped margin. Slender white stems support free, closely spaced, pale gills. Both fruiting bodies rest on decaying wood.

Two mushrooms with broadly convex to nearly flat caps, showing a gradient from dark brown centers to pale beige margins. Cap surfaces are finely granular, especially at the center. Stems are slender, straight, and white with a smooth texture.
A dense, white, powdery coating covers much of the green leaf surface, forming a continuous, finely granular to cottony mat with diffuse margins blending into the leaf tissue.

A single, rounded, dark brown sporocarp with a smooth, subtly textured, glossy surface. A small, pale crystalline structure is attached near the base. The margins are even, and the structure is solitary without a visible stalk.

Clusters of mushrooms with broadly convex to flat, light to medium brown caps, some with darker, slightly scaly centers. Stems are thick, white to off-white, often soiled, and gills are closely spaced and brown. Cap margins appear wavy and irregular.

Irregular, pale brown to tan lesion with a matte, slightly roughened surface and scattered minute dark specks. The margin between the discolored area and adjacent green tissue is diffuse and uneven, with no prominent fruiting bodies visible.

Numerous small, bright orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and well-defined margins are scattered singly or in loose groups, contrasting sharply against the green and brown background.
Irregularly shaped brown to tan necrotic spots with yellowish halos and multiple holes where leaf tissue has deteriorated, creating a patchy, damaged appearance.

Two medium to dark brown, globose to subglobose structures with smooth, shiny, slightly leathery surfaces. Pale encrustations and debris adhere to their rounded margins. The compact, globular forms emerge directly from a moist, granular substrate.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, smooth ochre-brown caps. Slender, pale brown stipes. Gills are densely packed and rusty brown. Some specimens are cut to show internal structure. Red Swiss Army knife provides scale.

A tiny, solitary fruiting body with a globose to convex cap densely covered in white, woolly or granular texture. The short, white, fibrous stem supports the cap above the dark, moist substrate. No gills are visible.

Dark, elongated, cylindrical mass with a rough, granular surface tightly attached to a green stem. Surrounded by brown, peeling plant tissue and fibrous material at the edges, with irregular, ragged margins.

Elongated green leaves display numerous small, irregularly scattered dark brown to black spots, giving a speckled appearance. The spots are flat and not visibly raised or powdery, with mild to moderate coverage on affected leaves.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, pale beige caps featuring a subtle fibrous texture. The caps have even margins and are supported by slender, smooth, off-white stems. Gills are visible beneath the caps, and both fruiting bodies grow closely together from a woody surface.

Numerous small, round, pale yellow structures scattered across a dark brown, woody surface. The yellow bodies are discrete, sessile, and matte, varying slightly in size but generally uniform and clustered.

Delicate, semicircular cap with smooth, pale off-white to light pinkish surface. Crowded, free gills are pale pinkish. Slender, centrally attached stem is light brown to tan. Cap margin is irregular, not scalloped.

Two robust mushrooms with convex, soil-encrusted caps obscured by debris. Stems are thick and tan, supporting well-developed, closely spaced brown gills. Cap margins are even and slightly inrolled, with a dry, textured appearance.

Two small, white, ovoid to ellipsoid caps with a granular, powdery surface stand on slender, cylindrical stems. The caps are smooth and entire, with no visible gills, and the fruiting bodies are at different stages of development.

Leaves display irregular dark patches and pale, powdery areas along the margins and surfaces. Some regions show subtle whitish coating, while others exhibit browning and necrosis, especially near the edges and tips.

Small mushrooms with smooth, moist, light to medium brown convex caps, some with cracked or uneven edges. Stems are slender, white to off-white, with soil at the base. Gills are closely spaced and pale brownish. Shown singly and in clusters.

Irregular, lobed, brain-like masses with a dry, cracked, granular surface. Light to medium brown coloration. Clustered fruiting bodies with rounded, bulbous protrusions and convoluted margins emerging from the surface.
No visible fungal growth or powdery patches are present on the green, serrated leaves and stems in this image.

Small, rounded to irregular yellow-orange sporangia with a powdery, granular surface, appearing slightly fuzzy. Scattered among fibrous debris, with nearby translucent, globular structures. Arrangement is irregular and the fruiting bodies are minute.

Cluster of small mushrooms with smooth, moist, light to medium brown conical caps showing pronounced radial striations. Slender, pale stems support the caps, and one upturned specimen reveals closely spaced, dark brown to purplish gills beneath.

Smooth, narrow green leaves with entire margins surround clusters of pink, unopened flower buds along the upright stem. No visible fungal structures or discoloration are present on the plant surfaces.

Convex to slightly depressed caps with a light brown, velvety surface and inrolled margins. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to yellow, and attached to cylindrical, pale stipes. Caps appear dry and finely hairy.

Numerous small, round, brownish-reddish spheres with a metallic sheen and finely granular surface, densely clustered together. The sporangia are smooth, well-defined, and closely packed, creating a sparkling appearance against the dark background.

Large, irregularly rounded mass with a lumpy, convoluted surface. Dark brown to blackish-brown coloration, hard crust-like texture, and deep grooves and folds. Margins are uneven and not sharply defined.

A single, rounded brown fruiting body with a central depression and smooth surface is encircled by thin, wavy, yellow-orange, fan-shaped structures with paler, slightly fuzzy margins, creating a striking contrast in color and form.

Dense clusters of tiny, off-white to pale cream, disc-shaped fruitbodies with finely granular surfaces, scattered and often merging into irregular patches across a dark background. Margins are mostly even but sometimes slightly irregular, forming a patchy, extensive covering.

Broadly fan-shaped, semicircular cap with a velvety white to cream surface and a distinct brownish-orange central spot. The margin is irregular, and the fruiting body is attached laterally. No gills or stipe are visible.

Numerous tiny, round to oval, disc-like fruitbodies with a pinkish-brown to cinnamon hue, matte and finely textured, clustered closely in a line along decaying wood. Margins are slightly raised and the fruitbodies are sessile, each just a few millimeters wide.

Clustered, rounded to irregularly lobed bodies with a bumpy surface; mature areas are dark black and shiny, while younger regions are pale grayish-brown. Pale, crust-like outgrowths surround the main masses, creating a dense, contiguous appearance.

Dark, irregularly shaped mass with a glossy surface, surrounded by scattered brown and black particulate debris on a smooth, pale background. No distinct fruiting bodies or structures are visible in this magnified close-up.

Tan to light brown convex caps with a matte, slightly fibrillose surface and paler margins. Crowded dark brown gills are visible on an upturned specimen. Slender, pale brown stems with fibrous texture; some mushrooms are sectioned, showing a solid, pale interior.

Two globose, smooth fruiting bodies with a glossy, moist surface—one dark brown to nearly black, the other golden-brown. Both are slightly elevated on short stalks, with some granular debris adhering to their surfaces.

Several tiny, vivid orange, smooth cup-shaped bodies with even, well-defined margins are scattered among green moss and small plants. Their moist surfaces and bright color sharply contrast with the surrounding foliage, and their diminutive size is evident next to the moss leaves.

Yellowish-orange caps densely covered in fine, hair-like structures, giving a fuzzy texture. Gills are pale cream to light yellow, closely spaced, and attached to robust white stipes. Some soil debris adheres to the surfaces. Prominent trichomes fringe the cap and gill edges.

Irregular patches of fine, powdery whitish-gray coating cover the upper surface of the green, pinnately lobed leaf, giving it a mottled and slightly dulled appearance. The fungal growth is unevenly distributed along the leaf blade and veins.

Convex to slightly sunken caps with reddish-brown surfaces and scattered white patches. Cap margins are faintly striate. White, closely spaced gills and robust, white stipes, some with soil adhering. Mushrooms show a firm, smooth texture.

Small, black, roughly circular to irregular fruiting bodies scattered singly or in loose groups on a pale, fibrous plant stem. The fruiting bodies are partially embedded, matte to slightly shiny, and vary slightly in size.

Thin, patchy, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, pale grayish to light brown with a finely granular or powdery texture. Scattered, tiny, dark, minutely raised spots are visible. Margin is diffuse and irregular, with some fibrous threads nearby.

Granular, crustose surface with scattered, small, rounded brownish to reddish-brown structures. Fine white hair-like filaments extend from some fruiting bodies. The texture is rough and uneven, with yellow-greenish tinges and indistinct margins blending into the substrate.

Two mushrooms with smooth, convex brown caps and fibrous, elongated stems. The upper specimen is larger, showing ochre gills and longitudinal striations on the stem. Both have soil and mycelial remnants at the base, with entire cap margins and no visible veil remnants.

Dense cluster of nearly black, irregular masses embedded within elongated, pendant fruiting structures. The dark fungal bodies are surrounded by persistent, papery, light brown bracts, giving a rough, textured appearance. The sori appear granular and powdery along the axis.

Cluster of mushrooms with smooth, glutinous brown convex caps and robust yellowish stems. The pore surface beneath the caps is bright yellow and sponge-like. Caps have smooth, slightly incurved margins. Largest specimen measures about 6 centimeters.

Dense, contiguous patches of dark, nearly black granular thallus form a rough, pebbly crust. The surface is uneven, with small, rounded, irregularly clustered lobes creating a bumpy texture across the stone.

A minute, pale, cushion-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, moist surface, surrounded by a tangle of fine, translucent, hair-like structures. The fungus appears solitary and extremely small against a background of organic debris.
Dark, irregularly shaped, nodular masses with a rough, granular surface. The thalli are compact, bumpy, and blackish to dark brown, forming textured aggregations among coarse mineral grains.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to hemispherical, brownish to reddish-brown caps, some slightly scaly. Stems are white and slender, with dark brown gills visible on an upturned specimen. Some caps show damage or partial consumption.

Granular, crustose surface with mottled grayish-brown coloration, scattered small orange-brown to yellowish granules, and moss-like tufts. Texture is rough, compact, and uneven, with irregular margins and a dense, clustered appearance.

Small mushroom with closely spaced, pale tan gills and a slender, smooth white stem. The cap margin is even, and the cap appears convex to flat. Some soil adheres to the stem base. No veil remnants or ornamentation are visible.
Dark, nearly black clumps with uneven, lobed edges densely covered in small, pale to grayish rounded granules, creating a beaded texture across irregular patches on the stone surface.

Small, round to slightly irregular, pale cream discs with smooth, slightly raised margins are scattered along a dry, straw-colored stem. The fruiting bodies are flat-topped and sessile, appearing as discrete spots on the fibrous surface.

Delicate mushroom with a slender, smooth pale brown stem and a conical, grayish cap featuring prominent radial grooves. The white, widely spaced gills are clearly visible beneath the cap, giving a fragile and graceful appearance.

Numerous minute, brown, globose to oval sporangia with slender dark stalks, some with a fuzzy or powdery surface, are scattered and loosely grouped along decaying wood. Delicate reticulate surface patterns are visible on some sporangia. Scale bar shows their very small size.

Two mushrooms with sticky, convex chestnut-brown caps, yellow pore surfaces underneath, and thick stems showing yellow tops with brownish streaks and remnants of a partial veil. Cap diameter about 2 cm, height up to 6 cm.

Small to medium mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, dry, brownish to reddish-brown caps, pale to medium brown free gills, and cylindrical white to pale cream stems bearing a partial veil ring. Some soil clings to the base.

A small, delicate mushroom with a conical to bell-shaped, off-white to pale gray cap featuring a matte, slightly fibrous surface. The slender, straight stem is pale gray and matches the cap. The margin of the cap is even and not striate.
A single, erect fruiting body with a slender, shiny black stalk topped by an oval, brown, fuzzy sporangium with a filamentous surface, emerging from woody substrate.

Clustered mushrooms with irregularly convex to wavy caps, pale grayish to light brown with darker mottling and soil. Uneven, undulate cap margins. Prominent, decurrent, closely spaced pale to grayish gills. Slender, curved stems, white to pale brown, with soil and wood debris attached.

A minute, pale yellowish to cream, disc-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, flat to slightly convex surface. Lacks visible stipe or marginal structures. Surrounded by fine, hair-like plant trichomes, the fungus appears solitary and inconspicuous.

Granular, dark brown to blackish mass with a powdery, irregular, and somewhat velvety texture embedded within a split, dry, straw-colored plant stem. The fungal material appears dense and clumped, lacking distinct fruiting bodies.

Clustered mushrooms with slender, elongated white stems and smooth, conical to bell-shaped tan caps. Some caps have wavy or upturned margins. Gills underneath are medium to dark brown and moderately spaced. Soil and debris cling to the stem bases.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, moist reddish-brown caps featuring a darker center. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the cap, and the smooth cylindrical stipes are pale to light brown. Caps appear shiny and slightly sticky.

Bright orange, semicircular to fan-shaped fruiting bodies with a velvety texture and deeply pitted, honeycomb-like undersurface featuring numerous angular pores. Margins are even and slightly lobed, and the fungi are arranged in small, scattered groups.

Clustered mushrooms with slender, pale, fibrous stipes and smooth, conical to bell-shaped caps in light brown to ochre hues. Margins of caps are slightly darker and irregular, with rich brown, closely spaced gills visible underneath.

Clustered mushrooms with irregular, wavy caps in pale brown to gray, slightly scaly. Gills are prominent, closely spaced, and range from pale to dark gray. Slender, pale stems often have soil or debris attached at the base.

Delicate mushroom with a slender, pale stem and a conical to bell-shaped, smooth cap that is pale yellowish-tan with a slightly darker, striate margin. Gills are closely spaced, pale tan, and free to narrowly attached.

A close-up of a leaf surface densely covered with small, dark brown to nearly black, rounded and slightly raised spots, giving the area a textured, mottled appearance. The leaf tissue appears discolored around the spots.

A small mushroom with a smooth, light brown convex cap and a slender, off-white fibrous stem. The cap margin is even, and the base of the stem appears slightly bulbous where it emerges from the substrate.

Numerous tiny, pale yellow to tan, shallow cup-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across a rough, granular surface. The cups are closely clustered, with indistinct margins blending into the substrate, giving an overall uneven, earthy appearance.

Pale gray to bluish-gray, leafy thallus with rounded, overlapping lobes. Surface is uneven and rough, covered in numerous granular to wart-like structures. Margins are irregular and slightly crenulate, with a tightly appressed appearance.

Irregular, overlapping caps with scalloped, wavy margins. Light yellow to yellow-brown coloration, paler uplifted edges, and a dry, slightly uneven surface. Some caps show scattered debris and a smooth to slightly velvety texture.

Thin, whitish to pale crust-like layer tightly covering the stem surface, with a granular or powdery texture and no distinct edges or raised structures. The coating appears patchy and follows the contours of the substrate.

Pale beige to light tan cap with a slightly fibrillose surface and gentle central depression. The margin blends subtly with the cap. Whitish, slender stem with a slightly bulbous base, partially covered in soil. Gills are not visible.

Small, vivid yellow-orange semicircular fruiting bodies with smooth upper surfaces and undersides marked by a prominent honeycomb-like pored texture, arranged in scattered clusters along a decaying log.

A single mushroom with a broadly convex, grayish-brown cap featuring a slightly darker center and paler, finely fibrous margin. Subtle radial striations are visible on the silky surface. The stem and gills are mostly hidden by surrounding dead leaves.

Numerous tiny, round to slightly irregular discs with dark gray, matte surfaces and distinctly fuzzy, minutely hairy margins. The fruiting bodies are scattered and sometimes clustered, showing a granular or velvety texture.

Rounded, bulbous fruiting body with a dense covering of fine, granular to spiny ornamentation. The surface is off-white to pale tan, distinctly rough and granular, lacking smooth or shiny areas. No visible margin, base, or ostiole in this close-up view.

Broad, convex cap with reddish-brown to pinkish-brown tones and subtle darker mottling at the center. Surface appears velvety and finely fibrillose, with a smooth, slightly inrolled margin. No gills or stipe visible from this angle.

Broadly depressed to funnel-shaped caps with smooth, rich reddish-orange surfaces. Cap margins are inrolled in younger specimens, more uplifted in mature ones. Decurrent, closely spaced pale orange gills and matching cylindrical stems, some with soil at the base.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate, light to medium brown caps showing a fibrous texture. Gills are crowded and pale beige, stems slender, pale, and slightly bulbous at the base. Cap margins appear paler than the center.

Irregular, flat to slightly raised black patches with rough texture and uneven margins scattered across a discolored trifoliate leaf. The fungal growth appears embedded in the leaf tissue, lacking any distinct stem or separate structures.

Clustered mushrooms with white to grayish, smooth caps, some with wavy or lobed edges. Caps are speckled with soil. Gills are crowded, pale, and attached, visible on upturned specimens. Stipes are short, robust, and soil-stained. Texture appears moist and fragile.

Clusters of small, gelatinous fruiting bodies with a moist, glistening surface; some are bright orange while others are translucent white. The shapes are irregular, merging into the substrate with indistinct margins and a soft, jelly-like texture.

Medium-sized mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, matte orange-brown caps and entire margins. Stems are cylindrical and pale orange-buff, matching the cap. Gills are decurrent, closely spaced, and pale cream to light orange. No visible latex exudation.

Two mushrooms with slender, pale beige stems and medium brown, dry, slightly scaly caps. One shows densely packed, pale tan to light brown gills with a slightly serrated edge. Soil clings to the base of the stems.

A tiny, pale, cushion-shaped structure with a smooth to slightly textured surface, attached singly to a brown woody stem. The fungus appears whitish or grayish and is minute, with no visible reproductive features at this magnification.

Small mushrooms with grayish to brownish, convex to plane caps and crowded, attached gills. Stems are short, sturdy, and often curved, with soil and wood debris clinging to the base. Caps show some uplifted or wavy margins, and fruiting bodies are loosely clustered.

Round to oval fruiting bodies with pale tan, finely textured surfaces. Cut specimens reveal a white to yellowish interior that darkens to olive-brown as it matures. No distinct stem is visible; bases are slightly narrowed.

Small, pale cream to yellowish-white cup-shaped bodies with smooth interiors and conspicuous margins adorned with dense, glassy, yellowish beaded or crystalline structures, forming loose clusters on the substrate.

Small clusters of mushrooms with smooth, dark brown, broadly convex to flat caps and pale, crowded gills. Stems are fibrous, slightly curved, and pale brown, with soil attached at the base. No ring or veil remnants are visible.

Small, bright orange fruiting bodies with semicircular to fan-shaped caps and porous surfaces, densely clustered along the underside of a decaying branch. Short, lateral stems attach each cap to the wood. The caps appear smooth to slightly velvety.

Broadly convex to nearly flat light brown caps with slightly darker centers and smooth, matte surfaces. Gills are moderately close and pale brown to ochre. Cylindrical, pale, fibrous stipes with soil at the base. Caps have entire, non-striate margins.

Two clustered mushrooms with convex, wavy grayish-tan caps showing subtle darker zones at the margins. Densely packed, decurrent, off-white to pale gray gills. Short, robust, off-white stems covered in soil and organic debris, with a smooth to slightly fibrous texture.

A compact, earthstar-shaped fungus with several smooth, pointed rays spreading outward. At the center sits a grayish-brown, globose spore sac featuring a finely textured surface and a distinct apical opening at the top.

A tiny, solitary, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, brownish-tan surface and a distinctly darker, slightly raised margin. The texture is even and unbroken, and fine white mycelial threads and small white granules are visible nearby.
Small, black, irregularly rounded to subglobose fruiting bodies with a rough, granular surface are scattered and slightly raised from the dry, layered bark substrate.

Numerous black, circular to irregular spots with yellowish halos scattered across the green leaf, some merging into larger brown, necrotic patches. Affected areas appear slightly sunken compared to the surrounding healthy tissue.

Globose to subglobose fruiting bodies with finely granular, pale tan to off-white surfaces. Some show a central apical opening or rupture. Texture appears dry and powdery, with one specimen displaying a narrowed sterile base.

Irregular, dark patches tightly attached to the stone, with a blackish, granular to minutely tufted surface. Numerous tiny, rounded dark structures cluster densely, giving a rough, velvety or finely filamentous appearance. Patch margins are diffuse and blend into the background.

Elongated green leaf with several irregular, brown lesions featuring darker margins along the central axis. Some lesions merge into larger necrotic patches, disrupting the smooth surface and parallel venation. No visible fruiting bodies.

Small, delicate mushroom with a convex to bell-shaped, off-white cap showing a subtle brownish center. The cap surface is smooth and finely textured. The slender stem is brownish and slightly fibrous or pruinose.

Dense, compact mat of small, black, irregularly branched, finger-like segments with a granular, rough texture. The surface appears pebbly and uneven, interspersed with tiny mineral grains and subtle brownish hues.

Crustose to squamulose thallus with a predominantly gray, uneven, and granular surface. Numerous small, rounded, yellowish-brown to ochre structures are scattered across the tightly appressed, rough-textured thallus, giving it a compact, granular appearance.

Medium to dark brown convex caps with smooth, matte surfaces. Densely packed rusty brown gills beneath. Cylindrical stems are pale brown to ochre with darker streaks and white mycelial remnants at the base. Scattered among fallen leaves and grass.

Narrow green leaf with several irregular, diffuse-edged lesions showing yellow-orange halos and central red patches. Small, black, raised dots are clustered within the lesions, contrasting sharply with the surrounding healthy tissue.

Two small, cup-shaped fruitbodies with pale to light brown discs and distinctly darker, reddish-brown, slightly raised margins. The surface appears dry and finely textured, with the larger apothecium oval and the smaller one circular.

Several tiny, whitish, hemispherical to subglobose fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces are scattered and embedded in a fine, web-like mycelial network. Each fruiting body is directly attached to the substrate and lacks a visible stipe.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to flattened, brownish to purplish caps, some with fibrous or scaly texture. Stems are robust and white, with brownish stains and adhering debris. Dense clusters of dark, granular masses nestled among tightly packed, dry, papery brown bracts. The rough, irregular texture and pronounced color contrast highlight the dark fungal deposits against the lighter bract surfaces.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, pale to medium brown caps and dry, fibrous surfaces. Stems are sturdy and off-white, showing brownish discoloration near the base. One cap is upturned, displaying closely spaced, pale brown gills.

Medium-sized mushroom with a convex, light brown cap showing darker spots and a smooth to slightly fibrillose surface. The margin is slightly incurved. The robust stem is white to pale brown with a bulbous, soil-covered base and some pinkish discoloration. Gills are closely spaced and pale brown.

Three mushrooms with convex, reddish-brown to purplish-brown, dry, slightly fibrillose caps. Stems are white to pale yellowish, with substrate debris clinging to the base. Pale gills are visible, free from the stipe. One cap shows a missing section along the margin.

Clustered mushrooms with pale to off-white, flat to slightly depressed caps, some with grayish tones and soil debris. Prominent, crowded, decurrent gills run down slender, white stems. Margins are wavy, and both mature and immature specimens are visible.

Numerous small, smooth, pink spherical bodies densely clustered along the crevices and surface of decaying wood. The spheres are uniform in size and color, with a delicate, fragile appearance and smooth margins. No stalks or supporting structures are visible.

Densely packed, thin, cream to light tan gills with slightly wavy, uneven margins. The surface appears smooth and moist, with small specks of soil or debris scattered across the intricate lamellar structure.
Numerous tiny, dark, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded margins and slightly depressed centers are scattered irregularly along a slender, brown, fibrous substrate.

Small, bright yellow-orange, semicircular fruiting bodies with a deeply pitted, honeycomb-like surface. The caps are fan-shaped, dry, and slightly velvety, with numerous angular to hexagonal pores dominating the surface. Margins are even and slightly undulate, and the fungi grow in clusters.

Clustered, overlapping mushrooms with grayish-tan, wrinkled, irregular caps and wavy, lobed margins. Short, pale stems support closely spaced, pale to grayish gills. Fruiting bodies display a somewhat fan-like but irregular arrangement among decaying woody debris.

Delicate white cap with a smooth margin and prominent, widely spaced gills. The cap is convex and slightly translucent, supported by a long, thin, pale stem. The overall appearance is fragile and slender.
Numerous tiny, rounded, yellow-orange globose bodies with a granular texture are scattered irregularly across a dark, moist, shiny patch on a rough, pale surface.

Green leaf with scattered, irregular dark spots, each encircled by a yellowish-brown halo. Small whitish structures are visible at the centers of the spots. Some lesions merge into larger patches, while the leaf surface remains smooth.

Medium to dark brown cap with a paler, whitish margin and finely fibrillose surface. Cap margin is uneven and striate. Slender, pale beige stem with faint longitudinal striations and soil clinging to the base.

A sharply triangular, thin, and membranous fruitbody with a translucent light brown surface, subtle darker brown margin, fine striations, and a delicate, whitish edge. The texture appears fragile and slightly undulating.

Broadly convex to nearly flat cap, pale cream to light brown with a distinctly darker center. The margin is irregular, slightly wavy, and shows minor cracking. Surface appears matte and somewhat fibrous.

Small, delicate mushroom with a pale tan, smooth, conical to bell-shaped cap and slightly darker margin. The slender, cylindrical stem is light brown and matches the cap. Gills are not visible from this angle. The surface appears smooth and thin-fleshed.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, smooth light to medium brown caps and subtly darker centers. Gills are broad, closely spaced, and brown, attached to sturdy off-white stems with some brownish discoloration. Cap margins are even and uncurled, and surfaces appear dry and matte.

Clusters of small, bright orange, semicircular fruiting bodies with a deeply pitted, honeycomb-like surface. The caps are fan-shaped, attached laterally, and lack visible stems, standing out vividly against the dark substrate.

Elongated green grass leaf displaying several irregular brown lesions with darker centers and lighter margins. The affected spots appear dry and necrotic, scattered along the smooth-edged blade. No visible fruiting bodies or fluffy growths are present.

Numerous small, round to oval discs with dark gray to black centers and slightly lighter, minutely fringed margins. The fruiting bodies are flat, matte to finely velvety, and closely clustered, with some variation in size and shape.

Three small mushrooms with slender, white, slightly fibrous stems and smooth, pale caps ranging from hemispherical to nearly flat. Gills are free, crowded, and pale cream to light pinkish. No ring or volva is visible; cap margins are even.

Clustered mushrooms with off-white to pale grayish, flat to slightly depressed caps, some with wavy margins. Crowded, decurrent gills radiate from the attachment point. Slender, cylindrical stems are off-white and often soiled. Caps appear smooth to slightly fibrous, with both mature and immature specimens visible.

A small, young fruiting body with a short, stout white stem and a cap densely covered in shaggy, white, hair-like structures. The cap margin is irregular and fringed, giving a distinctly textured, feathery appearance.
A glass slide displays a central, dark, irregularly shaped deposit with scattered black specks radiating outward, forming a diffuse spore mass. No visible fruiting bodies or substrate are present.

Pale yellowish to tan caps with fibrous or slightly scaly surfaces, mostly convex to plane, some with uplifted margins. Crowded pale brown gills are visible on upturned specimens. Stems are elongated, slender, and smooth, all surrounded by dead leaves.

Numerous tiny, dark, circular to shallowly cup-shaped fruiting bodies are scattered across a pale, fibrous stem, some appearing slightly sunken or with a central depression. The fruiting bodies are minute and evenly distributed.

Pale, creamy to off-white fungus with a thick, slightly fuzzy stipe covered in fine hair-like structures. The base of the cap flares outward in a subtle funnel shape, with a fibrous surface texture visible under high magnification.

Mushroom with a smooth, pale brown to tan convex cap showing faint radial striations near the margin. White, closely spaced gills are free from the robust, off-white stem, which has faint tan fibrils and a bulbous base with white volva remnants.
Numerous small, brownish to rust-colored, slightly raised pustules are scattered irregularly along the surfaces of slender green leaves.

Small, brown, rounded to slightly domed fruiting bodies with a granular, minutely roughened surface, scattered across a greenish, granular background. No distinct margin or edge is visible; surface appears matte rather than shiny.

Small mushrooms with hemispherical to convex, moist dark brown caps, some with striate margins and covered in organic debris. Slender, light brown stems also bear substrate remnants. Dark brown, closely spaced gills are visible on a few specimens. Fruiting bodies vary from rounded to slightly flattened.

Tiny, rounded to irregular pale greenish patches with a granular or velvety surface, scattered and blending indistinctly into the background. The structures are minute and delicate, with no visible reproductive features at this magnification.

Dark, irregularly rounded necrotic spot with a cracked, papery texture and slightly raised margin on a pale green leaf. The lesion is dark brown to black with lighter brown areas toward the center and diffuse but well-defined edges.
Clusters of hard, irregularly rounded, dark brown to nearly black growths with cracked, uneven, woody surfaces tightly attached to the side of a branch.

Roughly spherical mass with a convoluted, velvety surface. Predominantly greenish-gray, featuring powdery areas and scattered yellowish or brownish patches. Irregular margins blend into surrounding organic debris.

Broadly convex, yellowish to orange-brown cap with rusty orange discoloration and scattered soil. Thick, robust stipe with orange-brown streaks, tapering toward a bulbous, soil-encrusted base. Smooth cap and fibrous-streaked stipe. No gills visible from this angle.

Dark, irregularly shaped crusts with rough, cracked surfaces and a mottled pattern of black, grayish-white, and brown. The surface shows a distinct reticulate or tessellated texture, with patches merging at the edges and tightly pressed against the background.

Long, slender white stem with soil clinging to the base. Cap is elongated, cylindrical to bell-shaped, pale grayish-white, distinctly striate, and splitting at the margin. Surface appears smooth to slightly fibrous.

Numerous tiny, dark, nearly black fruiting bodies scattered across a light brown stem. The fruiting bodies are irregularly shaped, slightly flattened, and closely appressed to the plant tissue, with matte to slightly rough surfaces.

Mushroom with a convex, slimy, glistening light brown cap featuring darker zones and scalloped, irregular margins. The off-white to pale cream stem is slightly curved and shows some brownish discoloration. Cap surface appears smooth and viscid.

Tiny, grayish-brown, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with slightly paler margins, appearing in small, scattered clusters. The discs are shallow, flattened, and smooth, directly attached to the decaying wood without visible stalks.
