Two mushrooms with convex, pale tan to light brown caps and smooth, moist surfaces. White to cream, widely spaced decurrent gills are visible beneath. Slender, slightly curved stipes are pale off-white to light tan, with a smooth texture and subtle translucency at the cap margins.

The fruit is covered in a dense, fuzzy greenish-gray mold with a powdery texture. Some orange skin is still visible beneath the mat of mold. The surface appears wrinkled and shrunken, with a granular, continuous coating.

Small, irregular white patches with a granular, powdery surface closely appressed to the substrate. Margins are diffuse and not sharply defined. The thin, crust-like fruiting bodies lack any visible pores or gills and are scattered in an uneven arrangement.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, glossy light brown caps featuring darker centers and inrolled margins. White, broad, widely spaced gills are visible beneath, attached to sturdy, cylindrical stems that are white and soiled near the base.

Clustered mushrooms with broad, yellowish caps bearing dark patches and smooth, moist surfaces. Stems are thick, white, and often soil-stained at the base. Gills are pale to light lilac and closely spaced, with some caps showing slightly inrolled margins.

A thin, crust-like layer with a white to grayish-white, powdery or granular surface. The margin is diffuse, blending into the substrate, with scattered darker granules and some greenish patches across the uneven surface.
A single mushroom with a smooth, rounded light brown cap that subtly darkens toward the edge. The thick, pale stipe has faint surface ornamentation and a slightly bulbous base. Gills are not visible.

Tall, slender stem with a delicate, bell-shaped pale cap. The cap features prominent vertical striations from apex to margin, giving it a grooved, almost translucent appearance. Margin is even and the overall structure appears fragile.

Numerous tiny, dark brown to nearly black filamentous tufts composed of fine, radiating, hair-like structures. The tufts are scattered, discrete, and bristly, giving a fuzzy texture across the surface. Each cluster appears erect or slightly spreading, with a consistent dark pigmentation.

Numerous tiny, dark, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with shallow open discs and thin, slightly raised margins are scattered irregularly across a smooth, pale brown cylindrical surface. Some cups are solitary while others form small clusters.

Numerous tiny, dark, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered and clustered along a light brown stem. The discs are flat to slightly convex with a rough, granular surface and regular margins, each much smaller than the width of the stem.
Leaf surface covered with a thin, white, powdery coating and scattered small dark specks. The powdery layer is patchy but widespread, with visible discoloration and slight damage to the leaf tissue.

Heart-shaped leaf with extensive browning and blackening along the edges, irregular necrotic patches, mottled green and brown surface, and curled, desiccated margins. The texture appears dry and brittle, with discoloration most pronounced at the periphery.

Slender mushrooms with elongated beige stems and conical to bell-shaped, light to medium brown caps showing faint striations. Dark brown, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps. Small droplets of moisture are present on the caps and stems.

Numerous small, oval to elongated black spots are scattered irregularly along a smooth, light brown stem. The black structures are slightly raised and sharply defined, standing out against the stem’s surface.

Patchy, crust-like growth with granular yellowish-green surface. Densely scattered, small, round to oval orange apothecia stand out, some with slightly raised edges, tightly adhering to a rough, dark background.

A thin, continuous, crust-like layer with a finely granular, powdery surface. The color ranges from white to pale gray, with a diffuse, patchy margin that blends gradually into the substrate. No distinct structures are visible.
Elongated, black, club-shaped fruiting bodies with a shiny, moist surface and distinct wrinkled grooves. Margins are irregular, and the upright structures are closely grouped together.
Thin, flat, crust-like patch with a pale whitish to grayish color, finely granular to slightly velvety surface, and irregular, diffuse margins blending into the substrate.

Numerous tiny, flat, disc-shaped fruitbodies densely cover the decaying stems. The discs are grayish to bluish-gray, smooth, circular, and flush with the surface, each with a distinct margin, creating a speckled appearance.

Tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with pale yellowish, slightly raised margins and darker brown centers. The apothecia are circular to irregular, smooth, moist, and clustered in small groups, each less than a few millimeters wide.

Numerous tiny, dark disc- to cup-shaped structures with smooth, slightly raised rims and central depressions scattered irregularly across a pale, fibrous surface. The fruiting bodies are blackish to dark brown and minute, sometimes appearing in small clusters.
Small, white, cup-shaped structures are scattered along the lower margin of a smooth, brown, rounded fruit. The apothecia are minute and grouped, contrasting with the darker surface of the fruit.

A tiny, delicate fruiting body with a pale, almost translucent fan-shaped cap. The cap edge is distinctly wavy and finely scalloped. A short, central stipe supports the smooth, thin cap, and the overall structure appears fragile against the dark background.
Thin, crust-like growth tightly attached to the surface, pale whitish to cream, with a smooth to slightly granular texture and scattered small bumps. The margin is irregular, lobed, and membranous.

Small mushrooms with hemispherical to convex, moist brown caps covered in debris, featuring a darker central disc. Gills are dark brown and crowded. Stems are slender, pale to mid-brown, and also bear substrate remnants. Caps measure about 1.5–2 cm wide.

A circular, tightly attached patch with a pale whitish-gray, cracked, mosaic-like surface. The thallus is composed of small, angular segments, with scattered small dark rounded spots and irregular but distinct margins.
Leaves and stems are coated with a whitish, powdery layer. The affected areas appear slightly curled and discolored, with dense, patchy white growth following the contours of the plant surfaces.

Irregular, pale gray to white crusty patches tightly adhere to the rough stone, forming scattered, somewhat circular to diffuse areas with granular to powdery surfaces and indistinct, blending margins.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped, smooth, moist caps in light brown to tan hues. Caps show subtle radial striations and slightly translucent margins. Slender, elongated, pale brown stems appear fibrous and somewhat translucent. Fruiting bodies grow tightly together.

Crustose surface of tightly packed, angular, white to light gray patches outlined by thin dark lines. Each polygonal areole features small, dark dot-like structures, giving a cracked, mosaic appearance with a dry, rough texture.

Whitish, irregular patches with a granular to powdery surface, closely adhering to the substrate. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the surroundings. No cap or stem is visible, and the texture appears fine and crust-like.

Bright yellow to yellow-orange, crustose surface with a cracked, areolate pattern. Scattered rounded orange discs are visible among granular, rough-textured patches, separated by dark fissures and forming a contiguous patch.

Numerous tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with dark grayish to brownish centers and distinct pale margins are scattered and clustered irregularly across the decaying wood surface. The apothecia are minute, sessile, and lack visible stalks or gills.

Several tiny, rounded white fruiting bodies cluster together on a smooth surface, each with a slightly granular texture and smooth margins, standing out distinctly against a vivid purple-lit background.

Broad, irregular cap with a yellowish-orange surface, scattered brownish spots, and patches of adhering soil. The margin is wavy and uneven, with some areas showing a deeper orange hue. Surface appears smooth with visible dirt and organic debris.

Tightly packed, grayish-white crust with numerous small, angular areoles forming a cracked, mosaic-like pattern. Surface appears rough and scaly, with well-defined margins and scattered minute dark spots within some areoles.

Numerous small, bright yellow-orange, powdery pustules are scattered in clusters along the veins and margins of a green, hairy leaf. The pustules are slightly raised, irregularly shaped, and have a granular texture, standing out vividly against the leaf surface.

Sectioned fruiting body displaying sharply defined, regular concentric rings in alternating dark brown and silvery-grayish tones. Texture appears hard, woody, and brittle, with a cracked surface and an irregular, rough outer margin. Rings radiate from a central point.

Small, delicate mushroom with a slender, pale, fibrous stem. The cap margin is light brown to tan and striate, contrasting with the dark brown, closely spaced gills radiating from the stem attachment.

Irregular, contiguous white patches with a granular to powdery surface and diffuse, poorly defined margins. The fruiting body is closely appressed and crust-like, lacking any raised or bracket structures.

Upright, club-shaped fruiting bodies with a glossy black surface and smooth, rounded or irregular tips. Some are straight while others curve or lean, clustered together and emerging from the forest floor.

Whitish to pale gray, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, with a granular, uneven, and somewhat fibrous texture. The margin is irregular and diffuse, blending gradually into the substrate.
Loose, irregular patches of minute, white to grayish, crystalline or powdery granules form a thin, fuzzy layer. The texture appears granular and dust-like, with no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Irregular, crusty white to pale gray patch with a cracked, areolate surface. Numerous small, dark gray to blackish rounded discs are scattered across the center. Margins are uneven, blending into the substrate, with rough, granular texture.

Irregular, black to dark brown patches with rough, scaly, and slightly raised texture scattered across a green leaf. The spots have uneven margins that blend into the surrounding healthy tissue, creating a sharp contrast.

A tightly adherent, pale gray to whitish crust with a rough, cracked surface. Composed of numerous small, irregularly polygonal areoles separated by narrow fissures, forming a patchwork of angular segments. Surface appears granular to slightly warty, with well-defined areole margins.

Pale gray, crust-like patch with a rough, granular surface. The thallus is cracked into small, polygonal areoles separated by dark fissures, giving a mosaic appearance. Scattered minute, dark, rounded apothecia dot the areoles. The margin is irregular and blends into the substrate.
Small, rounded, yellow-orange pustules scattered across the leaf surface, slightly raised and granular, grouped irregularly along the veins and standing out against the green, hairy leaf background.

Numerous dark, nearly black, globose to irregularly rounded bodies are scattered along the pale, smooth trunk. The surfaces appear matte and slightly rough, with sizes ranging from small spheres to lumpy forms, attached directly to the bark.

Irregular, knobby mass with a lumpy, matte surface, colored brown to nearly black. Firmly attached to the side of a pale, peeling branch, the fungus appears robust and rough, with no distinct reproductive structures visible.

Numerous small mushrooms with round to convex, smooth, moist caps in light brown to tan shades, some showing darker vertical striations. Thin, elongated light brown stems support the caps, all densely clustered atop a fibrous substrate with scattered green moss.

Small, densely clustered mushrooms with smooth, convex to bell-shaped pale tan caps and slender, light brown stems. Some caps show subtle translucency at the margin. Dark, closely spaced gills are visible beneath several caps. Fruiting bodies emerge tightly from a compact substrate.

Small, rounded, orange-yellow fruiting bodies with a granular texture are scattered among greenish, moist material. Some smaller, smooth, brown structures are also present, interspersed with moss-like fragments.

Small, clustered mushrooms with smooth, light to medium brown convex caps, some showing darker centers and faint striations. One specimen displays closely spaced, medium brown gills beneath a pale, slender, slightly curved stem.
Tiny, circular fruiting bodies with conspicuous white, slightly raised, hairy margins and brown to olive-brown centers, scattered in small groups across the textured bark surface.

Dense, crust-like layer with a granular to powdery surface, predominantly white to grayish-white. The texture appears finely crystalline and minutely tufted, forming an uneven, patchy, continuous coating without distinct margins or visible fruiting bodies.

Numerous tiny, rounded to irregular, light orange fruiting bodies with a granular texture densely clustered in patchy, carpet-like groups across a greenish-brown surface. The fruiting bodies are sessile and directly attached, lacking visible stalks or gills.

Numerous small, scattered yellowish-orange powdery pustules cover the green leaf surface, often aligning along veins and sometimes merging into larger patches. The pustules are slightly raised, giving the leaf a mottled, rough texture with prominent venation.

Dense, continuous mat of pale greenish to grayish-green mold with a fuzzy, cotton-like, powdery texture. Surface forms irregular, slightly raised, velvety patches with diffuse, gradually blending margins and no sharply defined edge.

Minute, pale cream to whitish, cup-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, thin, translucent margins. The delicate, membranous apothecia are scattered and sessile, appearing slightly raised and granular against the dark substrate. No stalks or prominent structures are visible.

Delicate, fan-shaped creamy-white cap with undulating, wavy and subtly lobed margins. The surface is slightly velvety, showing faint radial striations and gentle translucency at the edges. No stipe or gills are visible from this angle.

Small, elongated, brownish pustules are aligned in a linear pattern along narrow green leaf blades. The pustules are slightly raised, dry, and powdery, disrupting the otherwise smooth surface of the leaves.

Numerous tiny, pale cream to whitish, disc-shaped structures are scattered irregularly across a dark, segmented, woody surface. The discs are minute, smooth, slightly translucent, and glossy, standing out against the textured brown background.

Clusters of small, blackish, raised, and irregularly shaped structures with a rough, granular texture scattered across a brown, veined leaf surface. The fruiting bodies are grouped along the leaf veins, contrasting sharply with the reddish-brown background.
Numerous tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies scattered and clustered on wood, dark brown to grayish with conspicuous pale or whitish margins, smooth texture, and rounded to slightly irregular outlines.

Tiny, upright fruiting bodies with slender, translucent stalks topped by small, rounded, pale yellow heads. The heads appear granular or powdery, and the structures are scattered and spaced apart on a dark substrate.

Small, delicate fruiting bodies with pale beige, thin, papery cups. Margins are distinctly wavy and irregularly lobed, giving a crisped appearance. Surfaces are smooth, and the fungi are scattered closely together among green plants on dark soil.

A single, irregularly rounded, hemispherical body with a dark brown to grayish-brown, rough, and slightly cracked surface. The texture appears hard and woody, with a compact form and no visible gills or pores.

Moist, glistening surface dotted with numerous minute, dark, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies scattered across a greenish-yellow background. Some fruiting bodies are partially immersed, and the texture appears wet and uneven with no prominent margins.

Small mushrooms with smooth, moist, light brown dome-shaped caps showing faint radial striations near the margin. Caps are convex to hemispherical with slightly translucent edges. Slender, pale to light brown stems are relatively long and fibrous.
Small, delicate fruiting body with a pale beige, cup- to fan-shaped cap featuring a wavy margin. The cap is smooth and slightly translucent. A slender stem tapers toward a base with attached soil.

Minute, irregularly shaped whitish to bluish patches scattered on a dark, uneven surface. The lighter areas appear granular or powdery, with a striking glow under intense blue or ultraviolet lighting.
Numerous tiny, dark brown to black, rounded to slightly irregular glossy fruiting bodies densely scattered across a light brown to greenish stem, creating a speckled appearance.
Elongated, brown, slightly raised lesions scattered along the green leaf surface. The lesions are linear to oval, rough-textured, and distinctly contrast with the healthy tissue.

Clustered mushrooms with broad, orange, dry caps featuring ruffled, irregular edges. Stems are thick and white, contrasting with the caps. Undersides display dense, white, tooth-like spines instead of gills.
Tiny, dark brown, tree-like structures with slender, irregularly branched filaments emerge from the surface, forming scattered, bushy clusters with a delicate, fuzzy texture.

Two slender mushrooms with pale, almost whitish stems and conical to bell-shaped caps. The caps are grayish-white with a darker brownish center, pronounced radial striations, and a fibrous, slightly shaggy texture. Margins are delicate and slightly inrolled.

Pale gray, tightly adherent crust with a dry, rough surface cracked into small, angular areoles forming a distinct mosaic pattern. Margins are irregular and closely pressed to the stone, with fine fissures separating the areoles.

Small, circular, yellowish-orange pustules scattered across a green, velvety leaf surface. The pustules are well-defined, slightly raised, and evenly distributed, contrasting with the fine texture of the leaf.
Textured brownish-tan surface with numerous small, rounded, slightly raised dots scattered across it. The surface appears glossy and uneven, with subtle color gradations and fine, radiating lines.

Crustose thallus with numerous minute, rounded to irregular, brownish to reddish-brown fruiting bodies embedded in a greenish, granular, uneven surface. The structures are scattered and partially immersed, giving a rough, irregular texture with variable greenish to brownish coloration.

Numerous small, glossy black, rounded dots are scattered irregularly across a smooth, pale straw-colored stem with faint longitudinal striations. The black dots are slightly raised and contrast sharply with the lighter background.

Small, black, star-shaped fruiting bodies with radiate, spiky margins scattered across a smooth, glossy surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised and contrast sharply with the lighter background.

A single, irregularly shaped thallus with dark gray to nearly black color, rough warty surface, and undulating lobed margins. The leathery texture is punctuated by small holes and a matte, granular appearance. No visible reproductive structures.

A continuous, pale greenish to whitish crust with a distinctly powdery, granular surface. The thallus forms irregular patches with a loose, mealy texture, lacking visible lobes or defined margins. No reproductive structures are present.

Minute, globose to subglobose dark brown body with a rough, irregular surface. A slender, upright stalk emerges from the top, lighter brown to reddish-brown and smooth. The margins are rounded, and the overall form is compact and solitary.

Densely clustered mushrooms with broadly convex to nearly flat, smooth grayish-brown caps. Cap margins are slightly inrolled on younger specimens. Crowded grayish to brownish gills are visible on upturned fruitbodies. Stipes are robust and pale, often with adhering soil and debris.

Mushrooms with convex, light brown caps covered in fine scales, pale pinkish-brown free gills, and sturdy white stems featuring a prominent ring. One specimen is cut to show the internal structure, revealing a solid stem and closely spaced gills.

Numerous tiny, pale grayish to off-white, disc-like structures scattered irregularly along the bark. The discs are flat, closely attached, and have a slightly granular texture with indistinct margins.

Numerous small, irregularly shaped, pale tan to light brown fruiting bodies with wavy, uneven margins cluster together. They appear soft, possibly gelatinous, and are closely grouped, sometimes overlapping, on a mossy surface.

Slender, upright pale stems display numerous small, black, oval to slightly elongated raised spots scattered irregularly along the surface. The fruiting bodies are embedded in the stem, appearing as discrete black dots.

Two mushrooms with dark brown, moist caps—one hemispherical and smooth, the other conical with striate margins. Stipes are slender; one is dark, the other pale with bluish-gray tones and soil at the base.

Small, dark, nearly circular to irregular spots with sharply defined black margins and paler, slightly translucent centers, some showing a central depression or pore, scattered on a smooth, pale surface.

Small to medium mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, chestnut-brown caps covered in fine scales. Pale, free gills contrast with the darker cap. Slender, cylindrical stems show brownish, fibrillose markings and soil-attached bases.

Slender mushrooms with pale yellow to light tan, smooth convex caps, some with adhering debris. Gills are closely spaced and pale, attached to whitish cylindrical stems showing faint brownish streaks and soil remnants at the base.
Small, glossy black rounded structures scattered irregularly across a smooth, moist reddish-brown surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised and stand out against the substrate.

Four tiny, white fruiting bodies with smooth, convex caps and slender, translucent stems. The caps have slightly uneven edges and a delicate, fragile appearance. The fungi are scattered along a brown substrate, with a soft texture highlighted against a dark background.
Numerous small, pale orange to peach disc- or cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, moist surfaces and wavy, lobed margins cluster densely and often overlap on a mossy branch.

Slender, elongated mushroom with a long, white, cylindrical stem and a small, smooth, convex white cap. The cap margin is even and uncurled. The fruiting body appears delicate, with some soil and debris adhering to the stem.

Extensive, thin, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, pale grayish to off-white, with a rough, minutely tuberculate to spiny texture. The margin is irregular and blends into the substrate, forming a continuous, patchy covering.

Numerous minute, dark, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered across a pale, fibrous, cracked surface. The fruiting bodies are embedded or slightly raised, contrasting sharply with the lighter substrate and distributed singly or in small clusters.

Fern fronds display irregular, pale yellow to brown patches and necrotic, slightly sunken areas along veins and margins. Lesions are scattered and sometimes coalesce into larger, discolored patches, contrasting with the healthy green leaflets. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Small, delicate mushroom with a smooth, pale tan to light brown convex cap and a slender, elongated, nearly white stem. Soil clings to the base. The margin of the cap is slightly inrolled. Gills are not visible from this angle.

Clusters of round, pale apothecia with slightly raised whitish margins and tan to light brown, granular central discs on a cracked, rough, and patchy surface. The thallus appears pale and areolate, with visible fissures throughout.

Tiny, bright orange to ochre, cup-shaped discs with smooth surfaces and slightly paler margins, scattered in a loose group along a dark, weathered stick. The apothecia are flat, sessile, and only a few millimeters wide.

Small, rounded fruiting bodies with a soft, velvety, peach to light orange surface. Some have translucent, whitish lobes. The surface appears minutely granular or fuzzy, and the bodies are tightly clustered.

Pale, irregular crust with a rough, granular texture, scattered with minute, dark brown to blackish rounded fruiting bodies embedded in the surface. The margin is indistinct, blending into the surrounding green plant material.

Three mushrooms with broadly convex to nearly flat, light brown caps featuring a darker central disc. Caps are dry and finely fibrillose. Stems are slender, elongated, mostly white with brownish bases, and slightly fibrous. Gills are pale brown to tan and closely spaced.

Numerous small, round, golden-yellow to orange pustules scattered across the underside of a green leaf, mainly along veins and interveinal areas, causing localized discoloration and slight chlorosis. Pustules are slightly raised and distinct, disrupting the otherwise smooth leaf texture.

Conical to bell-shaped cap with a dry, slightly fibrous light brown surface. Cylindrical, pale beige stem with fibrous texture. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to yellowish, and attached. Cap margin is even; overall stature is slender.

Two robust mushrooms with hemispherical to convex caps, brown in color and covered in distinct scales or fibrils. The right cap is split, revealing white interior flesh. The younger cap shows an inrolled margin. Stems are mostly hidden by soil and vegetation.
Mushroom with a convex, smooth yellowish cap and gently curled margin. Crowded, light brown gills radiate from a solid, pale tan stem with soil at the base. No ring or veil remnants visible.

Two mushrooms with convex brown caps, darker at the center and finely textured. The margin is subtly striate. Stems are long, slender, and blue-gray, turning white at the base with soil attached. Gills are crowded, pale cream, and free to slightly adnexed.

Numerous small, round to slightly lobed brownish fruiting bodies with a granular to finely fuzzy surface, some showing a whitish mycelial fringe at the base. Margins appear irregular or slightly lobed, scattered gregariously across the wood.

Pale, nearly colorless microscopic field with several thin, elongated, hyaline structures scattered across a uniform light background. No prominent or textured structures are visible; faint linear elements are present with a darker peripheral area.

Small, clustered mushrooms with smooth, pale cream to white convex caps and even margins. Slender, cylindrical stems match the cap color and have a fibrous texture. Gills are closely spaced and white, visible on the upturned specimen. No ring or volva present.

Extensive, crust-like patch with a granular to powdery surface. Pale grayish-green coloration, uneven texture, and small, irregularly shaped, closely packed granules. Margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the substrate, with no visible lobes or reproductive structures.

Cluster of mushrooms with conical to convex brown caps, striate margins, and smooth surfaces. Stems are long, slender, and pale, with crowded, pale gills visible beneath some caps. The caps lack distinct spots or rings.

Caps are pale yellow to yellow-buff, convex to nearly flat with a slightly depressed center and moist, smooth surface. Margins are smooth and slightly incurved in young specimens. Stipes are robust, white to pale yellowish, with white, stringy mycelium at the base. Gills are pale, closely spaced, and attached.

Three pale, smooth mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened caps and even margins. The caps are cream to white, with slender, cylindrical stems matching the cap color. Surfaces appear moist and smooth, with no visible gills from this angle.
Broadly convex cap with an irregular, undulating margin. Surface shows a gradient from yellowish edges to a darker brown center, with a smooth to slightly fibrillose texture. No gills visible.

Small mushrooms with brown, scaly to granular caps, some caps crumpled or with missing pieces. Slender, light brown stems. Caps measure about 1.5 to 2 cm across. No gills visible from this angle. Displayed on a white background with a ruler for scale.

Numerous well-defined, black, rounded to slightly elongated raised spots scattered irregularly across a pale tan, striated stem. The fruiting bodies vary in size, with some smaller black dots interspersed among larger, prominent ones. The stem surface shows fine longitudinal lines.

Irregular, patchy colonies with a pale greenish-yellow hue form a tightly appressed, powdery and finely granular surface. The thallus lacks lobes, appearing as merged, leprose patches directly on the reddish-brown stone.

Pale, irregularly shaped discolorations and small, diffuse brownish spots scattered across the leaf surface. Affected areas are slightly sunken, blending into the surrounding tissue, with no prominent fruiting bodies or raised structures visible.
Minute, round, black fruiting body with several fine, radiating, hair-like appendages at its base. The surface appears slightly fuzzy, set against a brown, textured background.

Two mushrooms with robust, white, fibrous stems and brown, granular to scaly caps. One cap is hemispherical, the other shows dark, crowded gills beneath. Cap margins are even, and the surface texture is distinctly granular.

Small, delicate mushrooms with convex to slightly irregular, pale cream to white caps and faintly scalloped margins. Stems are slender, cylindrical, and match the cap color. The surface appears smooth, and the caps are proportionally wider than the stems.

Delicate mushrooms with pale to light brown, striate caps, some with a central depression. Caps range from convex to flattened. Slender, white stems with soil clinging to the base. Dark gills visible on mature specimens.

Small, dark, cup-shaped structures with a central slit, clustered irregularly along the stem. Margins appear fringed or hairy, and the surface is slightly rough. Fruiting bodies are scattered to gregarious.

Small mushrooms with smooth, white, convex to slightly flattened caps and slender white stems. Caps show minor blemishes and even margins. Bases are covered with soil and green moss fragments. Size comparison with a coin highlights their petite stature.

Two mushrooms with robust white stems, one showing densely packed pinkish-brown free gills, the other displaying a brown, scaly, fibrillose cap. The cap margin is inrolled on the younger specimen, and remnants of a partial veil are visible near the stem base.

Pale gray to whitish, smooth crust with numerous tiny, black, rounded dots scattered across the surface, forming a continuous, patchy layer. The black dots are slightly raised, giving a speckled appearance. Occasional greenish patches are present.

Small, rounded cap with a smooth, light brown to tan surface showing subtle darker streaks. The margin is even and slightly incurved. Slender, light brown stem is partially hidden by dense green vegetation.

Clustered mushrooms with convex, light brown to tan caps showing faint striations and darker centers. Gills are densely packed, broad, and pale cream, attached to slender, smooth, white stems. Some caps and stems are covered with soil and organic debris.

Irregular, thin, pale gray to grayish-white patches form a powdery, granular crust on the stone. The surface is matte, with diffuse, uneven margins and a delicate, film-like appearance blending into the substrate.

Broad, fan-shaped caps with smooth, moist brown to grayish-brown surfaces and wavy, irregular margins. Prominent, creamy white, decurrent gills are visible on upturned specimens. The mushrooms vary in size and are loosely clustered.
Conical to bell-shaped cap with pale yellowish-brown, dry, fibrillose surface. Even, slightly incurved margin. Long, slender, pale yellowish to light brown fibrous stipe. Gills not visible.

A continuous, powdery pale greenish-gray crust covers large areas of the rock, forming broad, irregular patches with finely granular texture and diffuse, blending margins. No distinct structures are visible.

Four mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, smooth light brown to yellowish caps, slender white stems, and pale, closely spaced gills. Some stems have soil at the base. A matchstick shows their moderate size. Cap margins are smooth and unstriate.

Cluster of mushrooms with dark brown to nearly black convex caps, paler striate margins, and slender, dark gray to blackish stems. Pale, widely spaced gills are visible on upturned specimens. Caps appear smooth, with both mature and young fruiting bodies present.

A single, dark, roughly spherical structure with a jagged, uneven margin is sharply silhouetted at the center of a bright, circular microscope field. The object appears opaque and solid, lacking visible internal features or ornamentation.

Small, shallow, orange to reddish cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth inner surfaces and slightly paler, well-defined margins, scattered and attached directly to woody twigs. The exterior appears matte to slightly velvety.

Cluster of delicate mushrooms with convex to sub-hemispherical, white to off-white caps featuring a matte, slightly velvety surface. Stems are slender, cylindrical, and pale, matching the cap color. Margins are smooth and even, with no visible gills or central depression.

Two fan-shaped mushrooms, one showing a rich brown, wavy, and lobed cap with fine radial striations and a moist, velvety surface; the other displays pale, closely spaced, decurrent gills beneath a similarly shaped cap. Each cap measures about 5 cm wide.

Dense cluster of small mushrooms with olive-green to yellowish-brown, slimy, translucent caps. Caps are rounded and irregular, some flattened. Gills are closely spaced and yellowish-brown, with slender yellowish stipes. Fruiting bodies appear moist and tightly packed.

A single, slender, elongated structure with a white, minutely fibrous surface. The upper portion is slightly swollen and densely white, while the lower part is more translucent and subtly hairy. Fine surface ornamentation is visible throughout.

Irregular, lumpy brown fruiting bodies with rough, warty surfaces. Some are cut open, showing a marbled, veined interior. Color ranges from medium to dark brown with reddish-brown tones. Sizes vary, with both larger and smaller specimens present.

Numerous tiny, rounded, reddish-brown bumps scattered across a rugged, grayish-brown surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised, some with faint central depressions, and irregularly clustered within bark crevices and ridges.

Numerous small, rounded, blackish spots are scattered along a smooth, pale cylindrical stem. Each spot is slightly raised and surrounded by a faintly discolored halo, appearing as discrete fruiting bodies embedded in the surface.

Small, tightly clustered mushrooms with smooth, convex to hemispherical pale cream caps and slender, elongated white stems. Some fruiting bodies are toppled, exposing closely spaced, pale grayish to light brown gills beneath the caps.

Small, densely clustered, cup-shaped bodies with grayish-black coloration and a conspicuous fringe of fine, whitish hairs. Each has a distinct, slit-like opening at the top, and the surface appears velvety to hairy.

Cluster of pale grayish-white mushrooms with smooth, slightly convex to flat caps, closely spaced decurrent white gills, and slender, fibrous white stems. Some caps have adhering debris and the stems show slight curvature.

Pale gray to grayish-brown, roughened surface with numerous small, rounded disk-like structures. These have slightly raised, pale margins and central disks matching or slightly darker than the background. The surface is cracked in places, with dense groupings of the disks creating a granular texture.

Small mushroom with a light brown, convex cap and crowded, pale beige gills. The slender, elongated stem is white to pale and has soil clinging to its base. The cap margin is smooth, and the overall appearance is delicate and wiry.

Small mushrooms with convex to conical, light to reddish-brown caps covered in fine granules or scales. Gills are free, white to pale brown. Slender stems are white to pale brown, some with soil clinging to the base. Both cap and gill surfaces are visible.

Four slender mushrooms with vivid orange-red, flat to slightly convex caps displaying pronounced radial striations. Stems are long, pale orange to tan, slightly curved, and end in bulbous bases with soil attached. Pale, closely spaced gills extend partway down the upper stem.

Small, pale cream to off-white mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped smooth caps, free and well-spaced pale gills, and long, slender, fibrous stems. The fruiting bodies appear delicate and wiry, clustered among grass.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened chestnut-brown caps, some showing subtle scaly texture. Gills are free, closely spaced, and cream to pale yellow. Stems are slender, pale, and soil-encrusted at the base, with no prominent ring visible.

Clustered mushrooms with deep brown, smooth, broadly convex to flat caps and wavy, irregular margins. Undersides reveal closely spaced, white to pale cream gills that run down short, lateral stems. Some caps and gills have soil and debris attached.

Thin, elongated, cylindrical structure with a light brown to tan surface densely covered in small, black, dot-like points. The texture is smooth except for these raised black dots, and the margins are even and unbranched.
Tan to light brown surface densely covered with small, dark brown to blackish dots. The texture appears rough, granular, and slightly velvety, with an irregular, uneven contour.

Two mushrooms cut lengthwise reveal thick, solid, pale stems and convex, medium brown caps. The gills are closely spaced and brownish, with a firm, fleshy texture. Soil clings to the stem bases, and the cap surface appears smooth to slightly fibrous.

Pale greenish to whitish, finely granular to powdery patches coalesce into an uneven, mealy crust. Margins are irregular and somewhat lobate, blending with tufts of dark green to brown moss for contrast.

Small, black, disc-like fruiting bodies with shiny, radially striate surfaces and well-defined, slightly raised margins. The texture appears rough and structured, and the discs are scattered on a pale, smooth stem.

Small mushrooms with convex to flattened caps, light brown to orange-brown, densely covered in darker scaly patches. Cap margins are irregular and slightly uplifted. Gills are pale cream, free, and closely spaced. Slender, curved stems are orange-brown with darker zones and soil at the base.
Numerous tiny, black, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with slightly raised, well-defined margins and minutely fringed edges are scattered and clustered across the decaying plant stem surface.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to flat, light brown caps featuring darker centers and faint radial striations. Stems are slender, white, and fibrous, often soiled. Gills are pale, closely spaced, and attached to the stem. Some caps show slightly wavy edges.

Upright, solitary fruiting body with a slender, translucent stalk fading from reddish-brown at the base to pale near the top. The head is distinctly club-shaped, white, and frosted with fine granules. A dark, globose base anchors the stalk.

Numerous tiny, rounded, reddish-brown fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly raised on rough, fissured bark. The fruiting bodies have a smooth, glossy surface and are embedded in the bark, forming small, distinct clusters against the textured background.

Solitary mushroom with a smooth, conical to bell-shaped yellowish-brown cap and an even, slightly incurved margin. The tall, slender white stem is fibrous and lacks a ring or volva. No gills are visible from this angle.

Slender, elongated white stems support pale brown to tan convex or bell-shaped caps, some with a subtle central disc and faint radial striations. Gills are closely spaced and pale. Caps appear smooth to slightly fibrous, with fruiting bodies at various stages of development.
Small, delicate mushroom with a smooth, convex white cap showing faint striations at the margin. Supported by a slender, elongated white stem, emerging from dark soil among decaying leaves and twigs.

Thin, brittle, and irregularly circular thallus with a dark gray to black color. The surface is rough, granular to warty, with small holes and protrusions. Margins are uneven, lobed, and curled, giving a lumpy, undulating appearance.

Irregular, powdery patches of pale greenish to bluish-gray cover the bark, forming finely granular, diffuse crusts that follow the cracks and contours. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible; the surface appears granular and somewhat crustose.

Tiny, white, cup-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, rounded caps and short, pale stalks are clustered along a slender brown twig. The caps appear delicate, waxy, and slightly translucent, with even, unornamented margins.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened brown caps, featuring a scaly or fibrous texture. Gills are crowded, cream to light brown, and stems are slender, cylindrical, and light brown with soil remnants at the base. Cap margins are uneven and slightly split.

Broad, fan-shaped caps with smooth, dark brown surfaces and wavy margins. The underside reveals closely spaced, white to pale cream gills running down a short lateral stem. Texture appears moist and pliant.

Small mushroom with a convex to slightly bell-shaped brown cap featuring a striate margin, slender elongated white stipe, and crowded dark gills visible from below. The fruiting body lies at an angle among twigs and leaf litter.
Rounded, tuber-like bodies with a dark brown, smooth exterior. One is cut open, revealing a striking marbled black and white interior. No visible stipe or cap; surface is uniform and unscaled.

Patch of light green to grayish-green, scaly thallus with small, rounded, closely clustered lobes. Numerous globular, wart-like structures dot the upper surface. Lobes have irregular, slightly upturned margins, forming a compact, low mat.

Minute, cup-shaped fruiting body with a pale, whitish disc and a slightly darker, irregular brownish margin. The slender stem is dark brown to nearly black, tapering toward the base. Cap surface appears finely textured or granular.

Numerous small, white, powdery spots are scattered across the upper surface of the green, serrated leaf. Some spots merge into larger patches, giving a superficial, dusty appearance without visible discoloration or necrosis.

Aphid host covered in a dense, buff to pale tan, powdery coating. The surface appears granular and matte, obscuring body details. Appendages are splayed and rigid, with no visible thread-like structures or fruiting bodies.

Numerous small, greenish to brownish cup-shaped structures with granular, slightly roughened surfaces. Margins are irregular and dusted with fine granules. The base forms a patchy, crusty mat in pale green, yellow, and brown hues, interspersed among mosses.

Dense clusters of small, cup-shaped structures with upturned, irregular margins. The upper surfaces are granular and rough, brownish to grayish, with scattered pale granules inside the cups. The texture is coarse and the coloration is muted.

Catkins display pronounced yellowish swellings and irregular, thickened, twisted segments with patchy yellow-green discoloration, indicating abnormal growths on the reproductive organs. No distinct fungal structures are visible.
Aphid bodies clustered on a green stem, enveloped in a yellow, powdery, granular coating that retains the insects’ shape and appendages.

Dense mat of green to yellow-green, patchy squamulose thallus with numerous upright, funnel-shaped cups. Cup margins are speckled with small, red-tipped dots. Podetia surfaces appear granular, and the cups vary in size, forming clustered, irregular groups.

A small insect is covered in a dense, pale tan to light brown powdery fungal growth, giving its body a fuzzy, granular texture. The insect’s legs and antennae protrude visibly from the enveloping fungal mass.

Aphid bodies are swollen and mummified, coated in a yellowish-beige, powdery layer. The fungal growth envelops the insects, sometimes with fine hyphal outgrowths, giving a granular texture. Aphid legs and antennae are splayed, and the coating is most prominent on their dorsal surfaces.

Small, reddish-brown, coral-like fruiting body with compact, irregularly branched arms. The surface appears smooth and moist, with blunt, rounded branch tips. Surrounded by sand, dead grass, and ice crystals.

Numerous small, slender, helmet-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, pale ochre to tan surfaces emerge upright among pine needles and leaf litter. Their apices are pointed or gently curved, blending subtly into the thin stalks. The arrangement is scattered and irregular.

Tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with thin, pale brown to grayish-brown stems and shallow, disc-like caps. The caps have slightly inrolled, darkened margins and a subtle velvety texture, standing side by side on dark wood.

Numerous small, flat, disc-like structures with light brown to tan, slightly fuzzy surfaces and irregular, crenulate margins. These discs emerge from a patchy, greenish to whitish crusty mat scattered across the soil.

A close-up of a leaf surface showing subtle yellowish and brownish discoloration, with a faint, powdery patch near the center. The leaf’s veins are clearly visible, and the surface appears slightly textured.

A tiny, delicate cup-shaped structure with a slender stalk. The cup has a dark, granular outer surface and a smooth, lighter inner disc, with a slightly irregular margin. The overall appearance is fragile and minute.

A single, tiny, disc-shaped fruiting body with a smooth to slightly granular surface and uniform light brown to tan color. The margin is entire and regular, standing out against a dark, blurred background.

A single, delicate fruiting body with a slender, translucent stem that darkens at the base, topped by a small, smooth, white, oval to club-shaped head. The surface appears slightly granular and the structure is minute and fragile.

Two mushrooms with smooth, reddish-brown convex caps and slender, fibrous beige stems. One is cut lengthwise, showing a white to off-white interior and closely spaced pale gills. Soil debris clings to the stem bases.

Sharply defined rectangular brown lesion with a dark margin on green leaf tissue. The patch is flat, slightly granular, and contains scattered minute dark specks. The boundary between the necrotic area and healthy tissue is distinct and well-marked.

Four mushrooms with convex to broadly convex, rich brown caps—darker and moist at the center, paler and striate at the margins. Gills are pale brown and moderately spaced. Slender, slightly curved stems are pale tan to light brown, with smooth surfaces and soil remnants at the base.

Pale gray, leathery, leaf-like surface with uneven texture and scattered small, dark, rounded granules. Lobed margins are undulating, slightly upturned, and darker at the edges. Yellowish granules dot the surface, with overlapping, fissured lobes visible.

Elongated, pendulous catkins display yellowish, swollen, and deformed areas with a fuzzy texture, standing out against slender, leafless branches. The abnormal swellings are prominent on the otherwise greenish and grayish catkins.

Numerous small, upright fruiting bodies with pale orange to ochre, smooth, rounded to conical caps atop slender, dark brown to blackish wiry stems. Closely clustered, emerging from a dense layer of pine needles and woody debris, with delicate and uniform appearance.

Slender, upright, club-shaped fruitbodies with a smooth, even surface and pale yellow to cream coloration. Tips are rounded to slightly pointed. The fruitbodies are unbranched or sparsely branched and scattered in small groups among grass and leaf litter.

Cluster of upright, slender stalks with distinctly flattened, cup-shaped tops. Surfaces are granular and rough, colored greenish-gray to brown, with irregular, crenulate cup margins. The base is crustose and granular, blending into the substrate. Arrangement is dense and compact.

Green leaves with serrated edges display irregular, diffuse white powdery patches and coatings, especially on the upper surfaces. The white areas are unevenly distributed, forming a thin, powdery layer without visible fruiting bodies or significant leaf deformation.

Dense, coral-like cluster with upright, flattened, thick branches. Light pinkish-beige color, smooth surface, and irregularly notched, rounded tips. Compact formation with smaller clusters adjacent to the main body.

Compact, coral-like cluster with numerous upright, intricately branched arms. Branches are smooth, light pink to peach, with blunt, flattened tips and a slightly translucent appearance. Small sand grains adhere to the surface. Branches emerge from a short, thick base.

Slender, upright, unbranched fruitbodies with smooth surfaces and rounded tips, displaying a gradient from creamy white to pale yellow. Cylindrical and club-like, they emerge scattered among leaf litter and twigs.
Slender, upright, club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, waxy surfaces and blunt, rounded tips. They are pale yellow to orange and scattered in loose groups among green mosses and low plants.

Elongated green catkins with densely packed floral elements, featuring conspicuous, irregularly shaped, smooth yellow swellings emerging directly from the catkin surface and contrasting sharply with the surrounding tissue.

Leaves display numerous brown, irregular spots with yellowish halos. Lesions vary in size, some merging into larger necrotic patches. Surrounding tissue appears chlorotic, and leaf surfaces look slightly wilted and desiccated.

A tiny, delicate fungus with a slender, slightly curved stalk supporting an irregular, grayish-brown apical body. The surface appears matte and granular, with uneven margins and a solitary, lateral attachment to the substrate.

Bright yellow, irregular, blister-like swellings scattered along elongated, fuzzy catkins. The smooth, waxy fungal outgrowths distort the catkin’s shape, standing out against the hairy surface. Swellings vary in size and are clustered in some areas.

Green leaves with serrated edges display scattered, irregular white powdery patches on the upper surfaces. The powdery areas contrast with the healthy green tissue, and some leaf edges show minor damage and small holes.

White, powdery patches form irregular, coalescing spots across the green leaf surface, with some areas showing brown, necrotic margins. The fungal growth appears as a superficial, powdery layer, giving the leaf a mottled appearance.

Tiny, pale brown to tan caps with pronounced pleats sit atop long, slender, dark wiry stems. The delicate fruiting bodies are sparsely scattered and well-separated, each emerging individually from the surface of a decaying leaf.

Pale gray to gray-green foliose thallus with a rough, uneven surface. Scattered small black raised granules dot the surface. A central orange patch is present, and the margins are irregular and lobed with slight yellowish tinges.
Convex caps with rich orange color and dry, slightly fibrous texture. Slender brownish stems with some basal mycelium. The cut specimen shows a white, fleshy interior.

Delicate, small fruiting body with a thin, brownish, somewhat translucent cap. The cap has a darker central region, lighter scalloped margins, and a smooth surface. The stipe is partially visible and out of focus.

Coral-like clusters with upright, antler-shaped branches in pale cream to off-white tones. Branches are smooth, blunt-tipped, and slightly flattened, emerging densely from a short, thick base. The texture appears delicate and brittle.
Dense, powdery white coating covers large portions of the green leaf surfaces, especially along veins and margins. The growth appears soft, patchy, and extensive, with no visible fruiting bodies.

Aphids display a yellowish, powdery or fuzzy coating enveloping their bodies, giving them a swollen, mummified appearance. The pale yellow to tan fungal layer sometimes obscures the aphids’ natural features, creating a diffuse, granular texture.

Overlapping, irregularly lobed patches with pale gray to whitish, mostly smooth surfaces and some granular areas. Broad lobes have crenate to incised margins, forming a dense, closely appressed mat over the substrate.

Bright yellow, swollen, irregularly shaped outgrowths cluster along elongated green catkins with tightly packed scales. The catkins are attached to a reddish-brown stem, contrasting with the surrounding exposed soil and organic debris.

Pale gray to whitish, irregularly lobed thallus with a rough, uneven surface. Rounded to slightly crenulate margins. Numerous small, dark, rounded structures scattered across the surface. Granular texture in places, with dense, overlapping lobes.

A thin, patchy, whitish cobweb-like coating overlays the rough, dark brown surface of the branch. The fungal growth appears as a subtle, powdery layer without distinct fruiting bodies, blending into the bark's texture.

Pale gray to whitish, leaf-like thallus with irregular, lobed margins. Surface is uneven, granular, and rough, featuring numerous small, dark, rounded structures scattered across the undulating, overlapping lobes.

Compact, coral-like cluster with intricately branched, upright arms. Branches are pale pink to light tan, smooth, and waxy, ending in blunt, irregularly forked tips. The overall form is bushy and emerges from a central base.

Tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with pale gray upper surfaces and slightly darker, well-defined margins. Each disc sits atop a slender, dark stalk, scattered along a brown woody stem. The apothecia appear smooth and delicate, with a clear contrast between the disc and the margin.
Small, irregularly shaped, pale whitish to grayish patches with lobed margins and a slightly granular surface, scattered across rough, fissured bark and interspersed with greenish moss.

Greenish-gray, crusty surface with numerous small, rounded, whitish to cream nodules tightly clustered and unevenly distributed, creating a bumpy, irregular texture. Margins are indistinct and blend into the background, with no visible lobes or prominent fruiting bodies.

Bright yellow, finger-like projections emerge from dense, spiky green catkins on a brown stem. The yellow growths contrast sharply with the catkin’s scale-like texture, creating a striking visual effect. Young, glossy leaves are also present nearby.

Pale gray-green surface with a granular, uneven texture. Scattered across are numerous small, dark, rounded structures. The surface shows cracks, fissures, and irregular, undulating margins, highlighting intricate detail.

Irregular patches of white, powdery growth scattered across a green leaf surface, forming diffuse, granular or cottony areas without distinct margins. The fungal colonies are unevenly distributed, with some denser and some sparser regions, giving a mottled, powder-dusted appearance.

Small to medium mushrooms with smooth, light brown caps, some deeply depressed in the center. Stems are slender and pale, with closely spaced, pale to light brown gills visible beneath several caps. The surface appears slightly moist.
Bright yellow, irregularly shaped, swollen outgrowths scattered along the fuzzy green catkin, appearing smooth and waxy, with a curved and lobed form that contrasts sharply against the host tissue.

Numerous upright, greenish to brownish cup-shaped structures with granular rims rise from a patchy, crustose base. The cups vary in size and display a rough, granular texture, contrasting with the irregular, green and yellowish thallus below.

Two delicate mushrooms with slender white stems; one has a dark, striate, inky cap with dissolving edges, while the other displays a gray, ovoid cap with a fibrous surface. Both caps appear thin and fragile.

Tiny, delicate fruiting bodies with slender, slightly curved, finely textured stipes supporting smooth, pale beige to light tan caps. The caps are rounded to conical, and the stipes are covered in fine, short hairs, giving a subtly roughened appearance.

Convex to slightly flattened orange-brown caps with a dry, subtly fibrillose surface. Gills are closely spaced, yellowish to rusty brown, and attached. Slender, elongated stems match the cap color and appear fibrous. Both caps and gills are clearly visible.

Tightly adherent, crustose surface with small, rounded to polygonal areoles separated by dark cracks. Light brown to tan coloration, with a rough, granular texture and numerous minute, pebble-like structures scattered across the thallus.

Numerous tiny, translucent to pale cream discs with smooth, slightly glossy surfaces and regular circular margins, scattered loosely across a dark brown background with some black patches. The delicate fruiting bodies vary slightly in size and appear thin-walled.

Leaves display numerous angular to irregular brown spots, each surrounded by yellow halos. Some lesions have merged, causing partial browning and curling at the edges. The leaf surfaces appear rough and wrinkled, with prominent veins and areas of desiccation.

Low, crustose to squamulose mat with irregular, overlapping, pale green to whitish lobes. Surface appears rough and granular, with a single cup-shaped podetium featuring a granular margin and slightly roughened texture. Interspersed with soil bits and surrounded by mosses.

Tan to light brown mushrooms with smooth, matte, centrally depressed caps and slightly incurved margins. Slender, pale stems show faint striations. Gills are crowded, pale cream to light brown, and slightly decurrent. Fruiting bodies appear clustered.

Minute, cup-shaped fruiting body with a pale, off-white to light gray disc and slightly wavy, irregular margin. The surface appears matte and finely textured. A slender, pale brownish stem attaches laterally to the substrate.

Elongated, cylindrical catkins densely packed with small, vibrant yellow, scale-like structures. The surface appears smooth with a slight fuzziness, and the catkins cluster at branch nodes. No visible fungal fruiting bodies or discoloration are present.

Small aphids are enveloped in a yellowish, powdery, fuzzy coating that swells their bodies. The aphids’ legs and antennae protrude from the dense fungal covering, creating a distinct contrast between the smooth plant surface and the textured fungal mass.
Small, oval aphids display a pale yellowish-brown, fuzzy coating with a powdery texture, appearing slightly swollen and rigid on a smooth green stem.

Five slender mushrooms with smooth, convex to conical light brown caps, slightly darker at the center. Stems are long, pale tan to white, some with soil and moss at the base. Gills are closely spaced, pale tan, and clearly visible beneath the caps.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, dry, finely textured light to medium brown caps. Stems are slender, curved, and light brown with darker streaks. Gills are densely packed, attached, and yellowish-brown. Some soil clings to the base of one stem.
Slender, delicate fruiting bodies with thin, pale to light brown stems and small, smooth, conical to hood-shaped caps in cream to ochre hues, scattered upright among forest floor debris.

Slender, upright fruiting bodies with thin brownish stems and small, smooth, pale cream to light tan, helmet-shaped caps. The fungi are delicate and scattered, each with a rounded cap and smooth texture.

A pale, translucent insect with smooth, glossy texture and visible appendages. Subtle, delicate thread-like features and a slight sheen are present on the body, with no prominent dense growths or reproductive structures.

Irregular, powdery white patches scattered across green, serrated leaves. The fungal growth appears diffuse and granular, forming coalescing spots mainly on the upper leaf surfaces, with colonies merging into larger areas in some places.

Patchy, irregular mass with a predominantly white surface and a faint yellowish-green center. Texture appears soft, cottony to foam-like, with diffuse, wispy margins blending into the background. Flat and closely appressed, lacking distinct fruiting bodies.

Light brown to tan caps with wavy, lobed, or frilled margins; some caps are centrally depressed, others convex. Gills are densely packed, pale to light brown, and attached. Slender, light-colored stems with remnants of substrate at the base. Specimens show varied developmental stages.

A tiny, pale tan fruiting body with a short, slender stem and a shallow, cup-shaped cap. The cap surface is matte and dry, with an even, slightly incurved margin. The fungus appears solitary on the dry plant stem.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, light brown, finely textured caps. Caps are dry, slightly fibrous, and have smooth, even margins. Slender, cylindrical stems are paler near the base. Gills are not visible.

Elongated, oval, light brown structure with a granular, slightly fuzzy surface. Fine, translucent, hair-like projections extend outward, and the surface is covered in delicate, filamentous material, giving a velvety appearance.

Small, bright yellow, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly glossy surfaces and irregular, wavy margins. The discs are sessile and lie flat against the dark, fibrous substrate, closely grouped together.

Numerous tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, even margins are scattered along thin, brown, decaying stems. The delicate, circular discs appear slightly translucent to opaque and cluster loosely, standing out against the dark background.

Irregular, overlapping patches with pale gray to bluish-gray coloration, smooth to slightly granular surface, and undulate, lobed margins. The thalli are closely appressed, forming a matte, contiguous mat without visible fruiting bodies.

Broad, pale bluish-gray to grayish-white patches with irregular, lobed margins and a slightly undulating, mostly smooth surface. Thalli are tightly appressed, overlapping in places, and show a faintly granular texture in some areas.

Dense, cottony mat with a yellowish-white hue, composed of fine, filamentous structures. The surface appears soft and velvety, forming a uniform, fuzzy layer without distinct fruiting bodies or visible reproductive structures.

Pale gray to bluish-gray, thin foliose patches with irregular, rounded to lobed margins. Surface appears matte, slightly wrinkled, and uneven, forming dense, scattered, overlapping clusters closely appressed to the bark.

Convex to slightly flattened medium brown caps with a darker center, dry and finely textured. Yellowish, closely spaced gills beneath. Stems are pale with brownish streaks, fibrous and striate, with soil remnants at the base. No ring or veil remnants visible.

Dense cluster of upright, cup-shaped structures with flared, irregular margins. Podetia are pale greenish-gray to brown, with a rough, powdery surface and a compact, scaly base. Margins of the cups appear uneven and slightly frayed.
Slender, elongated, unbranched fruitbodies with a smooth, waxy surface and pale yellowish-white color. Slightly curved with blunt to tapered tips, lacking visible gills or ornamentation.

Small, cup-shaped structures with flat, shallow, brownish to pale greenish discs. Margins are irregular and granular, with a roughened surface. Forms low, scattered patches among mosses and debris, displaying a granular texture.

Small, compact, coral-like clusters with densely branched, upright, antler-like tips. Fruiting bodies are pale tan to light brown with a faint pinkish hue, smooth surface, and blunt, rounded branch ends. Slightly moist appearance, nestled among sand and plant debris.
A single, delicate fruiting body with a slender, yellowish-brown, slightly translucent stem and a small, smooth, oval to club-shaped yellow cap.

Slender mushrooms with pale brown to tan, smooth caps, some slightly depressed at the center. Gills are crowded, pale grayish to light brown, and attached to fibrous, cylindrical stems. Caps reach about 3 cm in diameter, with even, non-striate margins.

Small mushrooms with light brown, centrally depressed caps up to 3 cm wide, smooth and slightly moist surfaces, and faintly striate margins. Gills are pale and moderately close. Stems are slender, fibrous, and pale brown, with some bases showing soil and moss remnants.

Broad, rounded lobes with scalloped, undulate margins; upper surface pale brown to tan, mottled and densely covered in dark, granular or isidiate structures. Margins are paler, slightly upturned, and some lobes appear faintly translucent.

Small, delicate fruiting body with a thin, translucent stem and a pale brownish, moist cap. The cap is somewhat translucent, with pronounced radial grooves and an irregular, lobed margin. Subtle color variation is present, and the surface appears slightly glossy.

Small, densely clustered fruiting body with intricately branched, frilly, coral-like structure. Branches are thin, somewhat flattened, reddish-brown, and slightly translucent with irregular, jagged margins. Surface appears smooth to slightly glossy.

Translucent, gelatinous mass with a whitish to pale hue, irregular and compact in shape. Surface appears moist, shiny, and lobed, with a distinctly jelly-like texture. Margins are uneven, blending into adjacent dark material.

Irregular, crust-like patch tightly appressed to the surface, with a granular to slightly woolly texture. Colors range from pale white to cream and light brown, with a diffuse margin blending into the surroundings. Scattered green moss tufts intermingle with the fungal growth.

Large, irregular necrotic lesion with a brownish, papery center and sharply defined dark border on green leaf. Margins are uneven, with rough, brittle texture and visible leaf veins. Several smaller brown spots are scattered nearby.
Small, bright yellow, gelatinous fruiting bodies with a smooth, moist, and translucent surface. They appear globose to slightly irregular and are scattered in clusters along the branch.

Cluster of mushrooms with broad, flattened caps in ochre, tan, and brownish tones, featuring darker patches and subtle zonation. Caps are finely fibrillose, margins even. Gills are pale grayish-brown and moderately crowded. Stipes are robust, cylindrical, and whitish to pale yellowish.

Needles display irregular reddish-brown discoloration and patchy necrosis, with some tips appearing dry and desiccated. Affected areas are unevenly distributed along the branch, with no visible fruiting bodies or external fungal structures.

Small mushrooms with convex brown caps featuring a paler whitish center and faint striations. Stems are slender, white, and fibrous, with slightly bulbous bases. Gills underneath are crowded and pale to brownish.

Small, bright yellow-orange, gelatinous fruit bodies with smooth, moist, somewhat translucent surfaces. The ear- or cup-shaped fungi have irregular, wavy margins and cluster in small groups along the wood.

A dense layer of minute, reddish to reddish-orange dot-like structures scattered across a fibrous, moist brown surface. The tiny rounded fruiting bodies glisten and contrast sharply with the darker background, forming an irregular but dense aggregation.

Tiny, stalked fruiting bodies with slender dark stems topped by spherical, reddish-brown heads. The heads have a distinct scaly texture formed by polygonal plates, giving a delicate, patterned appearance.

Delicate mushrooms with conical to bell-shaped, light brown to grayish-brown caps, some with striate or ruffled margins. Smooth, slender white stems and closely spaced pale gills are visible. Caps appear moist, with some debris adhering. Mushrooms measure around 15–16 cm tall.

Leaflets display numerous small, circular to irregular brown spots with yellowish halos scattered across the green surface. Some leaf margins show minor necrosis and discoloration. The leaf texture is smooth with visible veins and no prominent pustules.

Douglas-fir needles display irregular patches of reddish-brown discoloration, especially at the tips and along the length. The fine, needle-like foliage shows scattered browning, with some branches more affected than others. No visible fruiting bodies are present.

Slender, elongated white stems support pale tan to light brownish-grey, smooth, convex to bell-shaped caps with thin, striate margins. Crowded, pale brown gills are visible beneath the delicate, fragile caps. Cluster includes both mature and young fruiting bodies.

Irregular, contiguous patches with a black to very dark brown color. The surface is rough, warty, and uneven, forming a crust-like layer with indistinct, irregular margins scattered across the substrate.

A bulbous fruit with a section removed, exposing a dense, black, granular and crusty fungal mass with a rough, irregular surface and scattered white fragments. The surrounding tissue appears dry and papery.

Faint, patchy whitish areas form a thin, powdery film on the leaf surface, interspersed with scattered dark spots. The fungal growth is subtle, irregularly distributed, and lacks prominent margins or dense colonies.

Numerous tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a slightly stalked base are scattered along the veins and surface of a decaying brown leaf. The discs are smooth and translucent, appearing singly and in small groups.

A dark, nearly black, crust-like layer spreading irregularly with a rough, granular surface covered in small, raised bumps. The margin is diffuse, blending into the substrate, and the growth lies flat against the surface.

Irregular, gelatinous masses with translucent to whitish centers and shiny, wet surfaces. Distinctly dark, almost black, convoluted margins sharply border the paler, jelly-like tissue. Growth is closely appressed and lacks a visible stalk or cap.

Two mushrooms with slender, smooth, pale stems and tan to ochre-brown caps. The caps display irregular, slightly wavy margins and closely spaced, ochre-brown gills radiating from the stem. No veil remnants or ring are visible.

Delicate mushrooms with thin, convex to nearly flat pale tan caps, some with undulating margins. Crowded, pale gills are visible beneath, attached to slender, off-white stems. The fruiting bodies appear fragile and are shown in various stages of development.

A small, fragile mushroom with a pale brown, smooth, moist convex cap and a thin, delicate stipe. The cap margin is even, and the overall appearance is dainty, standing solitary among dried grass stems.

Irregular, lumpy, dark brown to nearly black compact mounds with a granular, rough texture. The margins are diffuse, blending into the wood, and the patches are scattered and discrete rather than forming a continuous crust.

Delicate, slender mushrooms with pale, smooth stems and conical to bell-shaped, light brown caps. Caps have finely textured, subtly hairy surfaces and distinctly striate margins. Densely packed, pale ochre to brownish gills are visible beneath.

A dense mat of fine, hair-like filaments forms a delicate, wispy layer. The structures are white to light gray, closely packed, and radiate outward, creating a frosted, lace-like appearance across the surface.
A dry, yellowish-brown leaf with a fine, pale, powdery coating covering much of its surface, giving it a dusty or frosted appearance. The leaf is slightly curled with prominent veins.

Reddish cap with pale patches, smooth surface, and brittle, crowded cream to pale yellow gills. Stipe is robust, white with pinkish-red tinges, and slightly bulbous at the base. Sectioned specimen reveals the fragile, crumbly texture of the gills and flesh.
Pale gray to white, bumpy crust with scattered, rounded black discs slightly sunken or flush with the surface. The patchy growth blends into the stone, and the texture is distinctly verrucose.
Two elongated, brown, slightly raised lesions with smooth surfaces and well-defined margins are embedded parallel to each other on a green leaf, contrasting with the leaf’s striped texture.

A small, solitary mushroom with a slender, fibrous pale stem and a smooth, slightly incurved cap margin. The underside reveals closely spaced, pale grayish to off-white gills. The fruiting body lies among grass and moss.

Thin, crust-like layer tightly covering the wood, white to light gray in color, with a rough, granular texture from dense minute raised granules. Some areas appear slightly fuzzy, and the margin blends indistinctly into the substrate.

Numerous tiny, white to cream, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded edges are scattered and loosely clustered along a dark, decaying surface. The delicate, translucent discs stand out against the blurred background, highlighting their minute size and fine structure.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened pale to medium brown caps, some whitish patches, and moist, uneven surfaces. Cap margins are slightly inrolled. Cylindrical stems are pale brown to yellowish with bulbous bases, showing white mycelial remnants and adhering soil.

Numerous small, irregularly clustered, brownish to reddish-brown pustules dot the green stem, appearing slightly raised and disrupting the surface. Fine, white, hair-like structures are visible along the stem, contrasting with the dark background.
Numerous tiny, dark brown to black spherical bodies scattered across a greenish-yellow surface, interwoven with fine, translucent filaments forming a delicate web-like layer.

Tiny, upright fruiting bodies with slender dark stalks topped by globose, reddish-brown heads. The heads have a shiny, distinctly net-like surface texture and are loosely clustered, each standing separately and delicately above the substrate.

Needles display irregular, elongated reddish-brown lesions running lengthwise, contrasting with the otherwise green, flattened foliage. No visible fruiting bodies; discoloration is the main feature on the needle surfaces.

Solitary mushroom with a pale grayish, convex cap showing a slightly darker center. The margin is smooth, and pale gills are moderately spaced beneath. The slender, cylindrical stipe is dark and smooth, appearing relatively long compared to the cap.

Numerous tiny, bright red, globose to slightly ovoid structures with smooth, glossy surfaces are densely clustered within the fibrous, brown, layered substrate. The red bodies vary slightly in size and are less than a millimeter in diameter.

Tiny, brown, cup- to urn-shaped fruiting bodies with delicate, net-like surfaces sit atop slender, dark stalks. The sporangia are scattered and display a porous, reticulate texture, with some grouped and others solitary across the surface.

Delicate mushroom with a slender, elongated white stem and a small cap showing a pale, striate, slightly translucent margin. Prominent, closely spaced pale gills are visible from below, highlighting the fine structure and fragile appearance.
Small, spherical, yellowish to ochre fruiting bodies with smooth, matte surfaces, each elevated on a short, dark stalk and arranged in a scattered line along decaying leaf litter.
Tiny, round, orange to tan cup-like fruiting bodies with smooth, moist surfaces are scattered among vibrant green moss and leafy liverworts on a clump of soil.

Convex to nearly flat caps with pale grayish-brown color and darker center, fibrous surface with organic debris. Gills are warm brown, closely spaced, and free from the slender, smooth white stems with slightly bulbous bases.
A dense layer of tiny, rounded to slightly elongated reddish-brown structures closely packed together, giving a textured and subtly glistening appearance across the surface.

Dense, white, cottony mat with a soft, velvety texture, forming irregular, loosely interwoven patches. The surface appears uneven and fibrous, with darker granular material scattered throughout. No visible fruiting bodies or distinct structures are present.

Numerous small, smooth, shiny, dark brown to black spherical bodies scattered across a greenish, granular surface, embedded in a fine, whitish mat of mycelium. The fruiting bodies vary slightly in size and are irregularly distributed.

Slender mushrooms with elongated, pale stems and small, smooth, conical to bell-shaped light brown caps. Gills are closely spaced and pale brown, visible on upturned specimens. The overall appearance is delicate and fragile, with scattered and slightly clustered growth.

Delicate mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened brownish-tan caps, moist and faintly grooved, thin margins, pale gills, and slender short stems. Fruiting bodies are scattered among dried stems and grass.

Leaf surface covered with a fine, powdery, patchy coating of numerous tiny dark specks, distributed diffusely and following the leaf veins. The affected area has an irregular margin and a matte, slightly roughened texture.

Whitish, powdery coating forming irregular, diffuse patches on the upper surfaces of elongated green leaves, with some darker specks visible. The fungal growth appears as a thin, superficial layer, leaving the leaf tissue slightly discolored but mostly green.
Small, bright yellow-orange, disc- to spatula-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, gelatinous, moist surfaces and slightly wavy margins, scattered in loose groups directly attached to the wood.

A tightly adhering, crust-like layer with a white to off-white color, densely covered in small, granular, rice-like structures. The surface appears compact and textured, with a diffuse margin blending gradually into the substrate.

Tiny, white to pale cream, disc-shaped to slightly cup-like fruiting bodies with smooth, even margins, scattered and clustered along a dark, decaying branch. The surface appears smooth and somewhat translucent, each apothecium only a few millimeters wide.
Small, bright yellow to orange, gelatinous fruiting bodies with wrinkled, undulating surfaces and irregular, lobed margins. They appear cup- to disc-shaped and cluster on a piece of weathered wood.

Large, glossy red cap with a moist, sticky surface and irregular edges, showing some splitting and soil debris. White to cream, closely spaced gills are visible, along with a robust, fibrous white stem bearing dirt at the base.

Green leaves with irregular, sharply defined brown lesions along the margins and tips. Affected areas appear dry and necrotic, with some curling and distortion of the leaf edges. Leaf surfaces are slightly rough with prominent veins.

Green leaves display a thin, continuous white powdery coating on their upper surfaces. The powdery layer varies in density, with some areas more heavily covered, while leaf margins remain intact and underlying tissue appears slightly discolored.
Dense, irregularly lobed blackish fungal mass with a granular, uneven surface and scattered pale patches. The margins are rough and the structure appears compact and bumpy.
Light brown to golden-brown caps with a fibrillose, scaly texture and striate, uneven margins. Long, slender, pale stems with soil at the base. Crowded, pale gills visible beneath the caps.
