Numerous tiny, pale cream to whitish, disc-shaped fruitbodies are scattered in small groups along the length of slender twigs. The fruitbodies are minute, sessile, and lack visible stalks, appearing directly attached to the wood.

A compact, crust-like layer with a smooth to granular white upper zone sharply transitioning to a black, warty, nodular region below. The black nodules are irregularly grouped and raised, with a well-defined, uneven margin between the two zones.

Irregular, patchy discoloration on the leaf with scattered, fine, hair-like filaments emerging from the surface. Some areas show denser clusters of these filaments, and the leaf veins are clearly visible, adding texture contrast.

The leaf displays irregular pale blotches and extensive discoloration, with areas of tissue loss. Its surface is dry and brown, marked by a central vein and pronounced lobes, lacking visible fruiting bodies.
Single mushroom with a slender, pale stem and widely spaced, pale gray gills. The cap margin is smooth and small relative to the stem, viewed from below among green grass.

Numerous tiny, dark brown to black spherical structures are scattered irregularly across a light tan, slightly hairy leaf surface. A prominent horizontal vein runs through the center, with the dark spheres contrasting against the textured background.

Slender mushrooms with off-white to pale cream stems, smooth convex to bell-shaped caps in grayish-brown to tan hues, and pale, moderately spaced gills. Some caps show margin splitting, and soil clings to the stem bases. Sectioned specimens reveal delicate internal structure.

Crustose thallus with a grayish-white, cracked, areolate surface. Irregular polygonal patches are interspersed with numerous small, black, rounded apothecia, giving a speckled look. Surface is rough, uneven, and tightly appressed, with slightly raised, fissured areole margins.
Light brown, translucent cap with a wet, slimy surface and striate, delicate margin. The stem is long, slender, and white, while the gills beneath the cap are pale and closely spaced.

Close-up of a mushroom’s underside showing broad, moderately spaced, pale gray gills radiating from a central stem. The gills have a slightly wavy, irregular edge, and the cap margin appears undulate and finely textured. The stem is pale and fibrous.
Small, irregularly shaped, dark brown to nearly black mass with a granular, matte surface. The structure is compact, lumpy, and has indistinct margins blending into the substrate.

Thin, crust-like layer with a granular, frosted surface. Predominantly grayish-beige with scattered brown mottling, covered in fine, glistening granules. Margin indistinct, blending into the background. Texture appears finely roughened and powdery.

Small, delicate mushrooms with conical to bell-shaped, light brown caps showing faint grooves at the margin. Caps appear smooth and moist. Stems are slender, pale, and fibrous, proportionally long compared to the caps.

Delicate mushrooms with thin, convex to slightly flattened caps, smooth and moist, colored light brown to grayish with paler, almost whitish edges. Slender, pale stems support the caps above a dense mat of dried plant stems.

Small, bright yellow, gelatinous discs and cups with irregular, undulating margins cluster along a brown stick. The fruiting bodies appear moist and somewhat translucent, standing out vividly against the wood.

Green leaves display scattered, irregular dark brown to black necrotic spots with sharply defined margins. Some lesions show central cracking and tissue breakdown, occasionally associated with small holes or tears. The unaffected leaf areas remain green and healthy in appearance.

Minute, dark, nearly black structures embedded in a pale surface; one features a distinct, upright, elongated beak-like projection. The surface appears slightly rough, and the fruiting bodies are scattered and not clustered.

Two mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped, shaggy brown caps and uneven margins. Gills are closely spaced and attached to slender, fibrous, light brown stems. Both stems have clumps of soil at the base.

A diffuse, irregular patch of fine white powdery growth coats the upper surface of a green leaf, standing out against the healthy surrounding foliage. The texture appears soft and powdery, with no visible fruiting bodies or significant leaf distortion.

Green leaves display numerous small, round to irregular dark brown spots, some with yellowish halos, scattered across the surface. Inset shows a single, thick-walled, oval to teardrop-shaped spore with a granular interior at high magnification.

Numerous small, circular to slightly elongated reddish-brown pustules are scattered across the green leaf surface, appearing slightly raised and disrupting the smooth texture. The rust-colored spots are irregularly distributed and clearly demarcate the infected area.

Slender, elongated pale stems with small, smooth, conical to bell-shaped light brown caps. Undersides reveal closely spaced, pale tan to light brown gills. Fruiting bodies appear delicate and minimally ornamented.

Slender mushrooms with elongated, fibrous grayish-brown stems and convex to bell-shaped caps. Caps are pale gray to light brown with a finely fibrous surface. Gills are pale gray to pinkish-gray, crowded, and clearly visible on the upturned specimen.

Clustered mushrooms with convex, coppery-brown, moist caps and paler, wavy margins. Gills are pale cream to yellowish and moderately spaced. Stipes are thick, pale, and display rusty-brown zones with a fibrillose texture, especially near the base.

Irregular, spreading patches with a dark brown to nearly black, crust-like surface. The texture is rough and warty, dotted with tiny, pore-like structures. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the surrounding bark.
A single small mushroom with a smooth, pale brownish cap that is convex to nearly flat, and a slender, straight, pale stem. The cap margin is even, and no gills are visible from this angle.

Thin, irregular, crust-like patches with pale yellowish to off-white coloration, appearing granular and powdery. The fungus closely adheres to woody debris and pine needles, lacking distinct fruiting bodies or defined margins.

Green, oval leaflets are densely covered with fine, brownish speckles, creating a mottled, dusty appearance. The speckles are scattered across the leaf surfaces, forming slightly roughened patches that are more concentrated in some areas.

A single, bright yellow-orange, gelatinous fruiting body with a lobed, undulating margin and moist, translucent, slightly wrinkled surface. The texture appears soft and jelly-like, with some whitish fibrous debris on top.

A single mushroom with a convex, grayish-brown cap showing a subtle fibrillose texture and slightly inrolled margin. The slender, grayish-brown stem has faint vertical striations and a slightly bulbous base. Gills are not visible.

Mushroom with a convex to slightly depressed pink cap, paler uneven margin, smooth surface with soil particles, closely spaced white gills, and a thick cylindrical stipe with brownish streaks and surface debris. Approximately 2 centimeters tall.

Light brown, fibrous caps with a silky or hairy texture, some with a central umbo. Gills are densely packed and pale cream to tan. Slender, white to off-white stems show brownish discoloration and soil at the base.

Slender white stems support smooth, moist, pale brown to tan caps that are convex to slightly bell-shaped. Gills are light brown and visible on upturned specimens. Caps have even, non-striate margins. Mushrooms are scattered on dried plant material.

Small, bright yellow to orange, gelatinous discs with glossy, moist surfaces cluster along a dark brown branch. The fruiting bodies are disc-shaped to slightly cup-like, with irregular, rounded margins and a vivid, eye-catching coloration.

Small, delicate mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, light to medium brown caps showing pronounced radial striations. Cap margins are paler. Stems are long, slender, and off-white. Gills are grayish and closely spaced. Fruiting bodies are scattered and not clustered.

Thick, crust-like fragments with a rough, cracked green upper surface, interspersed with blackish and pale patches. The underside and cross-sections reveal a white to cream, finely poroid layer and pale, fibrous interior. Margins are irregular and undulating.

Small, bright yellow-orange, gelatinous discs with irregular, lobed shapes and scalloped, undulating margins. Surfaces are smooth, moist, and translucent at the edges, clustered directly on the wood without visible stems.

Small, bright orange to yellow, gelatinous discs and cushions cluster directly on twigs. The fruit bodies are smooth, moist, translucent, and jelly-like, lacking distinct stems or caps, and are scattered to gregarious along the wood.

Dense, dark, nearly black felt-like mat tightly covering the wood surface, with a granular, uneven texture and sharply defined margin. No visible fruiting bodies or distinct structures at this magnification.

Irregular, whitish to cream patches tightly attached to decaying wood, with smooth to slightly uneven surfaces and wavy, indistinct margins. Some areas show darker patches from debris. No distinct cap or stipe, forming spreading, effused growths.

Minute, dark, globose fruiting body with a rough, granular surface and a short wiry stalk. A small, glistening droplet sits atop the textured sphere, which is attached directly to woody debris. No cap, gills, or pores are visible.
Several small, slender, black, cylindrical fruiting bodies stand upright and sparsely spaced on a woody surface, each with a matte to slightly roughened texture.

White to cream, crust-like growth tightly attached to wood, with a porous lower surface and jagged, fibrous upper margin. The texture appears soft and fibrous, and the pores are small and evenly distributed across the surface.

Numerous tiny, black, slender, and slightly curved cylindrical structures emerge vertically from a rough brown surface. The glossy fruiting bodies are scattered irregularly and spaced apart, each standing upright and distinct against the textured background.
Oval fruit with a mottled brown and gray surface, scattered with numerous small, black, rough-textured, slightly raised specks, giving a speckled appearance. The fruit appears partially decomposed.

Highly branched, tree-like structures with slender, contorted branches in pale greenish-yellow to brownish hues. Surface is uneven and granular, featuring small wart-like projections. Branch tips are irregular, pointed, and finger-like, forming a dense, intricate cluster.

Numerous tiny, bright orange, smooth, club-shaped fruiting bodies with rounded tips emerge from a moist, organic-rich surface among decaying leaves and twigs. The slender clubs vary in height, are cylindrical to slightly swollen at the tip, and are scattered or loosely clustered.

Numerous tiny, whitish to translucent, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies with a smooth, slightly granular surface are scattered across a dark substrate. Fine, delicate hyphal threads are visible among the minute, sessile apothecia, which lack a distinct margin or stipe.

Pale tan fruit surface densely covered with numerous small, dark, raised pustules. The pustules are irregularly distributed, varying slightly in size, giving a rough, textured appearance with patches of discoloration and decay.

A thin, crust-like layer tightly adheres to the wood, dark brown to nearly black, with a rough, uneven surface. Small, rounded depressions are scattered along the irregular margin, blending subtly into the surrounding tissue.

Medium to dark brown, conical to bell-shaped caps with fibrous, striate surfaces and scalloped margins. Slender, pale grayish stems appear fibrous. Pale brown to grayish, crowded gills are visible beneath the caps. Mushrooms vary in orientation, showing both cap and gill surfaces.

Bright orange-yellow, undulating surface with scattered small, dark, rounded structures and several cup-like discs. The texture appears irregular and slightly rough, with minute embedded bodies dotting the thallus.

Delicate, white mushrooms with long, slender, translucent stems and small, convex caps. The caps have a central depression and radiating gills visible from below. The overall appearance is smooth, fragile, and minute, with a graceful, almost threadlike stature.
Dense clusters of small, irregular, nodular structures with a pale greenish-gray color and scattered dark spots, forming a compact, granular surface interwoven among tangled lichen strands.

Numerous small, upright, unbranched, bright orange club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces are scattered closely together among dried grass and plant debris. Each fruiting body is cylindrical and lacks a distinct cap or stem, forming a striking contrast against the ground.

Dense cluster of pale yellowish-green, irregularly contorted branches with a rough, granular, warty surface. Numerous small dark specks cover the uneven, jagged branch margins, giving a miniature coral-like appearance.
Rounded fruiting body with a smooth, shiny, wet surface. Light brown center fades to a darker, almost black margin. Numerous small, black, raised specks are scattered across the glabrous surface.

Irregularly shaped, pale cream to light tan caps with wavy or lobed margins. Thick, white stems show some brownish or yellowish discoloration near the cap. Caps appear dry and slightly velvety, with fruiting bodies scattered on moss and leaf litter.

Clustered mushrooms with convex, pale yellow to light brown caps, some with wavy margins and a dry, matte surface. Stipes are short, robust, and whitish. Fruiting bodies emerge singly and in small groups among green moss and leaf litter.

Cluster of small, rounded to irregular dark brown to blackish bodies with granular, slightly rough surfaces, scattered and slightly raised on a rough brownish background. Margins are indistinct and arrangement is irregular.

Yellowish, irregularly contoured surface with numerous small, dark brown to black, cup-like fruiting bodies clustered and scattered across the rough, uneven background. The fruiting bodies have well-defined margins and contrast sharply with the lighter substrate.
Numerous small, black, rounded, raised structures densely scattered across the tan to brown surface of an acorn, forming rough, granular patches that contrast with the smoother background.

Numerous small, circular to irregular patches with distinct white margins and yellowish to pale brown centers form crust-like growths. The patches vary in size, sometimes merging into larger groups, with smooth to slightly granular texture and well-defined, slightly raised edges.

A small, delicate mushroom with a conical to bell-shaped, pale brown cap featuring a fibrous, slightly scaly surface and striate, uneven margin. The slender, pale stem is covered in fine fibrils, supporting the cap above woody debris.

Two small mushrooms with grayish-brown, uneven caps featuring wavy, notched edges and slightly scaly surfaces. The slender, brown stipes are distinctly curved. The upturned specimen reveals pale brown, moderately spaced gills narrowly attached to the stipe.

Slender mushrooms with bell-shaped to conical, light to medium brown caps featuring striate margins and a finely hairy surface. Gills are pale, well-spaced, and attached beneath the caps. Stems are elongated, thin, slightly curved, and fibrous, ranging from whitish to pale brown.

Three rounded, compact pellets with a coarse, irregular texture and visible plant fragments. The surface is dry, fibrous, and dark greenish-brown, lacking any distinct fruiting bodies or reproductive structures.

Small, brown, gelatinous fruit body with a smooth to slightly uneven surface, scattered dark specks, and a lobed, undulating margin. The shape is roughly circular with a slight central nodule, appearing moist and flat next to a 1 euro coin for scale.

Numerous tiny, round, translucent to light brownish-white globose bodies densely clustered together, with smooth, slightly glistening surfaces, scattered irregularly across a dark, granular background. Some fruiting bodies overlap, and no stalks or differentiated margins are visible.

A resupinate, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, pale cream to ochre with some darker patches and scattered small dark specks. The surface appears felted to slightly granular, with an irregular, diffuse margin blending into the substrate.

Minute, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a granular, pebbly surface. Yellowish-brown to ochre, moist and somewhat translucent, with entire, non-raised margins. Closely grouped and emerging from a dark substrate, the surface is roughened by fine granules.

Dense clusters of pale greenish to whitish, branched structures, each tipped with small, irregular, lobed orange-brown fruiting bodies. The fruiting bodies appear moist, contorted, and granular, giving a gelatinous texture. Minute size is indicated by the scale below.

Clusters of mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, light brown to orange-brown caps, darker at the center. Caps have a dry, finely textured surface. Gills underneath are closely spaced and ochre to rusty brown. Stipes are cylindrical and match the cap color.

Highly branched, bushy structure with thin, irregular, pale grayish-green branches. Surface appears rough and slightly granular. Scattered small, rounded to disc-shaped brownish structures are visible along the branches, forming a loose, tangled mass.

Brown, uneven surface with numerous small, shallow, irregularly shaped depressions and slits scattered throughout. The texture is rough and granular, with the fruiting bodies blending subtly into the substrate and lacking prominent margins.

Pale cream to light tan, shelf-like fruiting body with irregular, undulating margins and a fibrous, moist-looking surface. Brownish tinges and lobed edges are visible, attached laterally to decaying wood. No distinct pores or gills are apparent.

Delicate mushroom with a slender, off-white to pale brown stem covered in shaggy, fibrous remnants. The hemispherical to bell-shaped cap is brownish and adorned with prominent, shaggy fibrillose material, especially around the margin. Soft, fragile appearance.
Broadly fan-shaped, semicircular fruiting body with a pale cream to light brown, rough and uneven upper surface. The margin is wavy and irregular, and the fungus is broadly attached to the wood.

Numerous minute, pale yellowish to light brown, cup-shaped structures with a somewhat translucent, granular surface are scattered across a dark, fibrous background. The fruitbodies are sessile, very small, and have even, unfringed margins.

Numerous small, black, rounded, and slightly raised spots are scattered across the pale, fibrous stem surface. The dark structures have a roughened texture and are embedded in the plant tissue, standing out against the lighter background.

Two minute, nearly black fruiting bodies with smooth, glossy, globose bases and slender, elongated necks extending upward. The surface is unornamented and the structures are spaced apart on a plain, light background.

Elongated, club-shaped to slightly flattened black fruiting bodies with smooth, matte surfaces and rounded or irregular tips. Sizes vary from slender to robust, and the arrangement is scattered to loosely grouped.

Dark brown, convex to slightly depressed caps with a subtle velvety texture and faint central umbo. Smooth, moist surface. Long, slender, fibrous brown stems with white mycelial remnants at the base. Pale to light brown, crowded gills attached to the stem.

Two mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, rusty brown, finely textured matte caps. Stems are robust, cylindrical, yellowish with brown streaks, and one base is covered in soil. Gills beneath the cap are closely spaced and brownish.

Numerous tiny, round to oval, translucent fruiting bodies with a granular, moist surface. They are pale to yellowish, closely packed, and have smooth, regular margins, forming a dense cluster without visible stalks.

A dark, nearly black, irregular patch with a smooth to slightly uneven, glossy surface spreads across exposed, lighter brown wood. The margin is distinct, and the fungal layer appears superficial without visible fruiting bodies.

Medium-sized mushroom with a smooth, moist, grayish-brown cap that is slightly depressed in the center. The cap margin is striate and somewhat translucent. The slender stem matches the cap in color and is slightly curved.

Three flat, circular mushroom caps with smooth, yellowish-green surfaces and darker olive-brown centers. The cap edges are slightly wavy and fringed, with some caps partially covered by green moss and forest debris.

Thin, crust-like layer tightly attached to the surface, whitish to pale cream with a finely porous texture. The margin is irregular and lobed, scattered with small plant debris and conifer needles. The surface is smooth to minutely porous, lacking any cap or stem structures.

Delicate, small mushroom with a pale tan, conical to bell-shaped cap showing faint striations. The slender, whitish stem is slightly curved and covered in fine, fuzzy fibrils. The overall texture appears fragile and thin.

Small, black, flask-shaped structures are embedded in the smooth brown surface, clustered irregularly. Each structure has several rounded, dark pores visible as tiny openings, giving a pitted appearance to the area.

Overlapping, semicircular shelves with concentric green, brown, and tan zones, wavy thin purplish margins, and a velvety texture. One fruiting body reveals a lilac to purple, finely porous underside. The fungi form a dense, layered cluster.

Cluster of slender mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate, grayish-brown caps featuring striate margins and papery texture. Broad, pale to light brown gills are prominently attached. Stems are elongated, off-white to pale tan, and fibrous.

Dense clusters of small, rounded, knobby structures with granular, uneven surfaces. Colors range from muted browns and grays to greenish tones. The growths are compact, irregularly margined, and covered in minute wart-like protrusions, blending into the intertwined substrate.

Round brown fruit covered with numerous small, black, rough, and slightly raised spots. The surface appears mottled with lighter and darker brown areas, and the fungal structures are granular and uneven, arranged irregularly. Some surface cracking is visible.

Brownish, uneven surface with scattered small dark speckles and subtle textural variations. No distinct reproductive structures or hyphal networks are clearly visible; fine details are unresolved in this magnified view.

Dense cluster of small, rounded orange to yellow fruiting bodies scattered across a bright yellow, lobed, and granular surface with radiating, uneven margins. The center shows deeper orange tones, and the surface appears moist and slightly glossy.

Clustered mushrooms with broadly convex to flat, light brown caps featuring darker centers and paler, grooved margins. Caps appear dry and slightly fibrous. Stems are long, slender, and similarly colored. Exposed gills are pale brown and attached.

Irregular, shelf-like fruiting body with a fuzzy, uneven white upper surface and jagged, undulating margin. The underside displays prominent, elongated, tooth-like white structures with a slight brownish tint near the base. Texture appears soft and fibrous.

Numerous tiny, bright orange, slender club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and rounded tips are scattered upright across a dark, mossy background, interspersed with dried grass and plant debris. The vibrant orange stands out against the green and brown surroundings.

Mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened greenish-yellow caps, darker and subtly fibrillose at the center, paler at the margin. Crowded, creamy white gills and robust, pale greenish stipes are visible, with moist, uneven cap surfaces.

Small mushrooms with brown, smooth, moist-looking convex to slightly flattened caps. Stems are long, slender, and somewhat translucent. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps. Fruiting bodies are scattered among green grass and moss, appearing delicate and fragile.

Small, dark, dot-like structures scattered on brown, dried leaves and conifer needles. The substrate is composed of overlapping, glossy, brown leaf litter and slender, tan needles, with the fungal elements appearing as tiny black specks.

Distinct, roughly circular to irregular brown spots with well-defined, slightly darker borders on a green leaf. The lesions appear dry, matte, and slightly sunken, with a uniform brown coloration and no visible reproductive structures.

Cylindrical, tan to light brown surface with a rough, fibrous texture. Scattered small, dark, circular to oval structures are slightly sunken, creating an irregularly pitted appearance across the coarse substrate.

A solitary mushroom viewed from below, showing crowded, creamy white gills with brownish stains and a robust, smooth, white stem that is distinctly curved. The cap surface is not visible, and some soil adheres to the stem base.

Dense, cottony white mat spreading irregularly over wood, with a soft, fibrous texture. Loosely attached filamentous tufts and patches are visible, and the diffuse margin blends gradually into the substrate. No distinct fruiting bodies are present.

Numerous small, dark brown to blackish, cup-shaped discs with smooth, rounded margins are scattered among dry, brown needles and twigs. The leathery fruiting bodies are inconspicuous but stand out due to their darker color and disc-like shape.

Pale, closely spaced, and brittle gills radiate from the attachment point, with a cream to pale yellow color. A yellowish spore print fans out on the white surface. The cap margin fragment is slightly uneven, and small soil particles are scattered on the gills.

Grayish, bell-shaped cap with a shaggy, striate surface and splitting margin. The cap appears slightly translucent at the edges. The white, smooth stem is upright and relatively robust, supporting the solitary fruiting body.
Broadly convex cap, pale cream to light brown with a slightly darker center and subtle markings. Smooth, even margin. Cylindrical, slender, pale stem with faint surface texture. Gills not visible.

Small to medium mushrooms with smooth, pale tan to ochre caps—one slightly depressed and irregular at the margin. The exposed underside shows closely spaced, decurrent, creamy to pale ochre gills. Stems are short and robust, partially obscured by soil.

Clustered mushrooms with broadly convex to flat, pale yellowish-brown caps and smooth, matte surfaces. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to light yellow, and attached to slender, cylindrical, pale stipes. Cap margins are even and not inrolled.

Small, densely clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate light brown caps, paler striate margins, and slender, pale fibrous stems. Some caps overlap, and the stems appear relatively long compared to the caps.

Dense, irregular cluster of white to cream fruiting bodies with lobed, deformed shapes. Surfaces are covered in soil and debris, giving a dirty appearance. Margins are uneven and not sharply defined, with no visible stems or gills.

Bright orange, contiguous patches with rough, textured surfaces and distinct yellowish-orange borders. The growth is flat, closely appressed, and irregularly lobed, standing out against the dark, cracked background.

Delicate mushrooms with thin, white stems and off-white caps featuring a distinct brownish center. The larger specimen shows creamy white, closely spaced gills and a slightly uplifted cap margin. Surfaces appear smooth with faint radial fibrils.

Numerous small, black, irregularly shaped fruiting bodies are scattered across a pale, cracked, and granular surface. The dark structures are embedded or slightly raised, with rough texture and uneven margins, contrasting sharply with the lighter background.

Broadly convex cap with a pale cream center and darker brown edge, smooth surface. Crowded, cream-colored gills attached to a slender, elongated brown stem. Needle litter clings to the stem, highlighting its earthy tones.

Cup-shaped to irregularly lobed fruiting bodies with smooth to slightly wrinkled inner surfaces, dull brown to dark brown coloration, and orange-brown wavy, uneven edges. Texture appears leathery, with some cups deeply cupped and others more flattened or contorted.

Numerous small, yellow to yellow-brown, smooth, spherical structures densely clustered in irregular masses along fibrous plant stems. The sporangia are tightly grouped, forming prominent, rounded aggregations without visible slime or gelatinous material.

Broad, crust-like patch with a rough, granular surface. Predominantly brownish-orange in color, with an uneven, slightly paler and irregular margin. Surface appears matte, dry, and closely appressed to the substrate.
Two pale tan, ovoid fruiting bodies with a granular surface, each topped by irregular, dark, filamentous appendages projecting outward. The structures contrast sharply against a dark, moist base.

Two small mushrooms with off-white to pale cream caps, each featuring a distinct brown central disc and a scaly, fringed surface. The gills are white and free from the slender, fibrous white stems, which show some soil adherence.

Mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, light brown caps featuring darker centers and striate margins. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to light brown. Stems are long, slender, white to pale gray, and fibrous, lacking a ring.
A small, loose deposit of pale yellow, powdery spores sits beside a color chart and razor blade. No fruiting body is visible; only the fine, granular spore mass is present.

Numerous tiny, black, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies are scattered across a pale, rough, cracked surface. The fruiting bodies are embedded or slightly raised, with a matte to granular texture, and are irregularly distributed without a clear pattern.

Dense mat of overlapping, irregularly rounded, leaf-like lobes with grayish-green to brownish tones. Lobes have distinctly outlined, pale or whitish edges and a slightly glossy to matte surface, tightly appressed to the substrate.

A solitary, cup-shaped fruiting body with a broadly rounded, flattened disc. The upper surface is dark gray to nearly black, matte, and finely velvety. The margin is even and slightly undulate, with a smooth, unornamented appearance.

Numerous tiny, pale cream to off-white, disc-shaped bodies with smooth, slightly glossy surfaces are scattered and attached directly to the surface. They are irregularly rounded, somewhat flattened, and lack visible stalks.

Minute, pale tan to yellowish globose bodies with a granular surface, each topped by radiating, rigid, dark bristle-like appendages forming a starburst pattern. The structures are closely clustered and sharply contrasted against the lighter background.

Two compact clusters of small, bright orange, glossy spherical bodies form rounded, irregular masses. The individual spheres are smooth, closely packed, and well-defined, with no visible stalks or supporting structures.

Clustered, irregularly shaped bodies with a rough, warty brown exterior. Cut specimens reveal a marbled, beige to light tan interior. Surfaces are uneven and lobed, forming a compact group among decaying leaves.
Shallow, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, leathery surface. Inner surface is muted brown, margin is paler orange-brown, irregular, and lobed with gentle folds and undulations.

Irregularly lobed, cup-like fruiting body with undulating, curled margins. Surface is smooth and matte, ranging from light to dark brown, with a slightly velvety texture. Robust and fleshy appearance, directly attached to the substrate.

Broad, shallow cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, matte, medium to dark brown inner surface. The margin is distinctly darker, almost blackish, and slightly thickened, giving a velvety appearance. The overall shape is irregularly rounded to subtriangular.

Leaves display numerous small, densely packed yellowish to brownish pustules, especially along margins and undersides. Many leaves are curled, wilted, and show brown necrotic patches, contrasting with healthy green foliage.
Numerous dark brown to nearly black, irregularly shaped, slightly raised pustules with a granular texture are scattered unevenly across a green leaf surface, disrupting its smoothness.
Tiny, dark, cup-shaped fruiting bodies sparsely scattered along brown, elongated, slightly curved structures. The apothecia are minute, smooth, and disc-like, each emerging singly from the surface.
Irregularly rounded, brown fruitbodies with a rough, warty surface clustered together. One is cut open, displaying a dense, waxy, marbled pale tan to light brown interior.

Thick, robust cup-shaped fruiting body with undulating, irregular margins. Upper surface is smooth, leathery, and medium to dark brown, with paler, minutely roughened edges. The fungus appears folded or crumpled, with curled edges and a slightly textured exterior.

Irregular, patchy growth with matted brown crust-like areas interspersed with dense, whitish zones. Texture varies from compact to diffuse, forming uneven patterns across the woody surface. No distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Small, dark, nearly spherical to slightly flattened fruiting bodies with a granular surface, clustered on a pale, fibrous background. Fine, hair-like structures are visible at the base. The fruiting bodies appear dry and range from dark brown to blackish.

Numerous small, black, rounded to irregular dots scattered and sometimes clustered on the cut surface of dead wood. The fruiting bodies are smooth, slightly raised, and somewhat shiny, lacking visible stalks or differentiated margins.
Numerous tiny, white to off-white, flat to slightly concave disc-shaped structures with distinct pale margins are scattered across the smooth, light brown stem, giving it a speckled appearance.
Dense cluster of small, oval to cylindrical, pale yellow fruiting bodies with a slightly rough, granular surface, tightly packed in an irregular, spreading patch.

A tiny, dark, glossy, irregularly shaped structure attached to a brown woody stem. The surface is smooth and shiny, with no visible fuzz or setae. The fruiting body is solitary and minute compared to the stem.

A single, cushion-shaped mass with a rough, cracked, and granular brown surface. The margins are rounded, and the form is compact, lacking any visible stalk or differentiated structures. The surface appears crusty and irregularly fissured.

Solitary mushroom with densely packed, broad ochre-orange gills and a fibrous, orange-brown cylindrical stem. The cap margin is even, and the underside displays rich warm tones. No veil remnants or ring are visible.
A solitary, globose fruiting body with a thick, rough, and cracked surface. The peridium is rusty brown, uneven, and warty, with a paler, weathered patch on top and an irregular margin.

Small fruiting body with an orange-brown, convex cap showing faint radial striations. Gills are pale and closely spaced. The stipe is long, slender, curved, and fibrous, matching the cap in color, with moss remnants at the base.

Small, delicate mushrooms with tawny to ochre-brown, smooth, striate caps. Undersides reveal pale brown, closely spaced gills. Slender, cylindrical stems match the cap color and appear slightly translucent. Fruiting bodies are scattered and diminutive among fine-textured moss.

Broad, irregular, fan-shaped fruiting body with a dense white to cream poroid underside. Margin is wavy and uneven, with crust-like, roughened patches and some fragmentation. Upper surface is soiled and debris-covered, giving a rugged appearance.

Cluster of slender mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate, smooth, matte caps in pale grayish-brown to dark brown. Stems are thin, cylindrical, and similarly colored with paler bases. Gills are closely spaced, pale grayish, and slightly decurrent.

Minute, spherical fruiting bodies about 1 mm wide, with smooth, brown, somewhat translucent surfaces partially coated in a fine, golden, dust-like spore layer. Each sphere sits atop a slender, dark stalk, and the delicate structures cluster closely together.

Clusters of small, bright orange, spherical fruitbodies with a smooth, slightly velvety surface and finely granular texture, densely grouped on a dark, moist background with scattered green moss and organic debris.

Leaves display numerous irregular, white to pale gray spots with defined margins, some coalescing into larger patches. The affected areas are slightly raised and rougher than the surrounding green tissue, with scattered and clustered distribution.

A small, delicate mushroom with a slender, straight light brown stem and a warm brown, convex cap. The cap displays pronounced radial striations along the margin and a smooth, dry surface. A tiny green organism rests on the cap.

A sinuous, chain-like mass of closely packed, irregularly shaped sporangia, pale cream to off-white with a powdery, chalky surface and rough, granular texture. The sporangia appear slightly flattened or angular, forming a loosely organized aggregation.

Minute, spherical sporangia with a granular, ochre to light brown surface, each less than 1 mm wide. The sporangia are borne on slender stalks, densely clustered, and covered in fine, dust-like material, with even margins and an upright arrangement.

A dense, white, fuzzy mat with an irregular, well-defined margin covers the surface. Numerous minute, dark specks are scattered across the cottony layer, creating a striking contrast against the white background.

Small, delicate mushrooms with slender, pale yellow-brown stems and light brown, convex caps featuring pronounced radial striations. Some caps reveal pale, widely spaced gills. The fruiting bodies are scattered and have a textured, corrugated appearance.

Two small mushrooms with convex, orange-brown, velvety caps. One shows densely packed, yellowish-orange gills and a slender, pale, slightly curved stem with a fibrous texture. The other cap is intact, displaying a uniform color and dry surface.

A dense layer of minute, white, spherical to subglobose structures forms a granular, powdery surface. The tightly clustered bodies create a beaded texture against a dark background, with no large fruiting bodies visible.

Moist, grayish to dark gray-brown caps with a glistening, smooth surface and irregular, wavy margins. Caps are centrally depressed or umbonate. Pale gray, closely spaced gills and slender grayish stems are visible beneath.
A dry, brownish leaf densely covered with numerous small, black, rounded fruiting bodies irregularly scattered and slightly raised above the smooth leaf surface, creating a striking contrast.

Cluster of slender mushrooms with smooth, grayish to gray-brown convex to flat caps and matching cylindrical stems. Pale gray, closely spaced gills are visible beneath several caps. Surfaces appear smooth, and cap margins are even.

Minute, moist, globose to irregular fruiting body with a smooth, glistening tan-brown surface. The margin is indistinct, and the structure appears closely appressed to the substrate, lacking a distinct cup shape. Arranged solitarily or in a small cluster.

Dense, irregular cluster of small, pale cream to off-white, granular sporangia forming a compact, lumpy mass. The surface appears moist and uneven, with closely packed fruiting bodies blending into the surrounding substrate. Margins are indistinct and merge with the decaying material.

A dark, nearly black surface densely dotted with numerous tiny, rounded, shiny black structures. The background is granular and subtly glistening, with uneven texture and hints of reddish-brown at the lower margin.

Elongated, lanceolate structure with mottled brown to olive coloration. Surface is rough and uneven, featuring numerous small, dark, dot-like spots scattered throughout. Margins are irregular and the texture appears leathery.

Clusters of small, bright orange, discoid to slightly convex fruiting bodies with distinctly granular surfaces and well-defined, even margins, emerging from a dark, moist background with scattered mineral grains.

Granular to minutely squamulose greenish thallus with numerous small, dark gray to blackish rounded structures scattered irregularly across a rough, uneven surface. The growth is closely appressed, forming a thin, patchy layer without distinct margins.

A continuous, crust-like patch with a white to off-white surface densely covered in minute, bead-like granules. The texture appears rough and uneven, with a diffuse margin blending gradually into the underlying surface.

Small, delicate mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate orange-brown caps, striate uneven margins, and closely spaced pale orange-brown gills. Stems are long, slender, and fibrous, matching the cap color. No veil remnants or annulus visible.

Numerous small, black, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered unevenly across a moist, dark brown surface. The fruiting bodies appear discrete, shiny, and subtly blend into the substrate without sharply defined margins.
A single, rounded, cushion-like structure with a smooth, moist-looking surface and pale pink coloration. The margin is even and the surface is unbroken, lacking any visible pattern or spore masses.

Leaves display numerous irregular, dark brown to blackish spots and blotches with diffuse margins, varying in size. Lesions are interspersed with lighter green areas, and the tissue appears mottled, discolored, and dry with some necrotic patches.

Numerous small, black, spherical bodies with a matte, subtly textured surface are clustered and scattered irregularly across a fibrous, plant-like background. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised and vary slightly in size.

Mushroom with a wavy, irregular cap margin, dark brown to black closely spaced gills, and a pale stem showing brown streaks and subtle blue-green bruising. The cap surface fades from light brown at the center to darker at the edge.

A dense layer of slender, dark, thread-like filaments scattered across a pale, fibrous background, each filament often ending in a small, rounded, dark head. The arrangement is irregular, with delicate, upright structures emerging from the surface.

Dense, fine, felt-like or tufted patches with a soft, fuzzy texture, grayish to olive-brown in color, forming irregular colonies on a brown, textured surface. Scattered small white specks are visible across the substrate.

Numerous small, pale beige to light brown spherical structures with a granular surface, densely clustered and supported on slender, dark stalks. The sporangia appear powdery and are arranged in scattered to gregarious groups.

Dense, irregular patches of minute, spongy fruiting bodies with a pale brown to off-white, net-like surface. Numerous fine, white, hair-like filaments extend outward, creating a delicate, airy texture. Fruiting bodies are closely packed and sometimes merge, forming a porous appearance.
Numerous tiny, white, circular discs are scattered irregularly along the brown, smooth stem. The discs are flat to slightly raised with well-defined margins, standing out against the woody surface.

Numerous small, dark brown to blackish, rounded structures with rough surfaces and pale centers are scattered irregularly across a yellowish-orange, granular, and shiny background. Some fruiting bodies appear slightly raised and clustered.

Small mushrooms with convex to flat, moist, pale brown to grayish-brown caps, some with subtle striations at the margin. Gills are pale gray and moderately close. Slender, curved stipes are grayish-brown with attached substrate at the base.

A tightly appressed, crust-like growth with a granular to minutely tuberculate surface. The color ranges from pale yellowish to light tan, with a diffuse margin blending into the wood. No distinct pores or gills are visible; the surface is covered in small, irregular granules.

Numerous tiny, spherical, button-like fruiting bodies scattered across dense green moss, ranging from light to dark brown. The sporocarps appear in loose clusters or singly, with a fine granular texture, contrasting against the vibrant moss and small leafy plants.

Convex to slightly flattened caps with a uniform rusty orange-brown color and dry, finely textured surface. Cylindrical stems are pale at the base, deepening to orange-brown near the cap. Gills are closely spaced, pale yellowish to tan, and radiate from the stem. Margins are even and uncurled.

Numerous tiny, black, disc-shaped fruiting bodies densely scattered and slightly raised on moist, fibrous dark brown wood. The discs have a matte to subtly shiny surface, some with a distinct margin, and vary slightly in size, creating a stark contrast against the substrate.

Dark, nearly black central area with a rough, granular texture. Margin shows brownish and greenish hues, appearing moist. Small, translucent to pale structures cluster at the edge, and the fruiting body outline is irregular.

Two small mushrooms with orange-brown, dry convex caps—one upturned to show closely spaced yellowish-ochre gills. The slender, pale, slightly curved stipe is smooth. Cap margins are even, and no ring or veil remnants are visible.

A tiny, disk-shaped fruiting body with a pale cream to light yellow color. The surface is matte and opaque, with a smooth, regular margin. It appears dry, delicate, and solitary, lacking visible reproductive structures.

Two small mushrooms with convex, orange-brown, finely velvety caps. One shows densely packed, deep orange-brown gills attached to a slender, pale orange-tan curved stem. The surface appears dry and slightly textured.

Slender branch with a rough, grayish-brown surface densely covered in tiny, dark, raised dots and a larger, irregular, darkened structure. The texture appears uneven with small bumps scattered across the bark.

Cluster of mushrooms with smooth, convex ochre to light brown caps, slightly paler at the margins. Stems are thick, pale brown to yellowish, with darker streaks and soil at the base. Gills are crowded, attached, and pale beige to light brown.

Two slender mushrooms with wavy, undulating brown caps and densely packed, rich brown gills. The caps have a moist, slightly glossy surface with lighter patches. Stems are pale brown, smooth, and cylindrical, emerging closely together from dark soil.

Two small mushrooms with light to medium brown, irregularly shaped caps, slightly depressed at the center and matte-fibrous in texture. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath. Brown, curved stems show fibrous surfaces and soil particles.

Robust, irregular fruiting body with a thick, crust-like surface. Upper side is yellowish to brownish with rough, cracked texture and greenish patches. Margin is uneven and wavy. Underside is whitish and porous, merging into a thick base.
Delicate, slender dark stalks support small, spherical to ovoid fruiting bodies with finely textured, brownish surfaces, clustered loosely and elevated above the substrate.

Numerous tiny, nearly black fruiting bodies scattered across a pale surface. They are round to slightly irregular, somewhat flattened, matte, and slightly rough, with mostly smooth but occasionally undulating margins. Some are clustered, others are solitary.
Tiny, pale tan cup-shaped structures with a distinct fringe of fine, hair-like filaments around the margin, sparsely scattered along a dark, smooth cylindrical surface.

Three mushrooms with brown, fibrous, slightly scaly caps and uneven margins. The largest shows pale, crowded gills beneath a convex cap. Stipes are slender, pale lilac to whitish with a subtle violet hue, and some soil clings to the base.

Slender mushrooms with elongated, pale tan to light brown stems and small, conical to bell-shaped caps. Caps are smooth, light brown, and slightly striate. Gills underneath are closely spaced and brown. Sizes range from 4 to 10 centimeters.

Thin, spreading crust tightly adheres to the wood, displaying a granular to finely nodulose surface. The coloration is whitish to pale yellowish with scattered light brown patches. The texture appears rough and uneven, with indistinct margins blending into the substrate.

Numerous small, globose heads with a dry, powdery or granular surface, pale beige to off-white, each atop a slender, dark brown to blackish wiry stalk. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped, some overlapping, with a distinctly granular texture covering each head.

Extensive, tightly appressed patch with a white to cream color. Margin is distinctly cottony and finely fringed, while the central area appears smooth to slightly granular. Irregular, spreading edges with no visible fruiting bodies.

Two mushrooms with slender, curved brownish stems and light brown, convex to plane caps. The gills underneath are closely spaced, pale to light brown, and slightly decurrent. Both cap and stem surfaces are dotted with small white granules.

Two small mushrooms with convex, light to medium brown caps showing irregular darker patches and subtle surface unevenness. Gills are closely spaced and pale to medium brown. Stems are slender, curved, whitish to pale brown, and fibrous with some darker streaks. Each measures about 2.5 cm tall.

Highly magnified view of a granular, glistening surface with a pale off-white to tan color. The margin is irregular and slightly scalloped, and the texture is densely packed with minute, bead-like structures.
Dense, continuous crust of tightly packed, small, cream to pale tan, wart-like projections forming a rough, uneven, and pebbly surface with irregular undulations.

Tall, slender mushrooms with conical to bell-shaped, moist reddish-brown caps featuring striate margins and slightly wrinkled surfaces. Stems are long, curved, reddish-brown, with soil clinging to the bases. Gills are brownish and closely spaced.

Numerous tiny, brownish, spherical to ovoid fruiting bodies with a powdery texture, each perched atop slender, dark, hair-like stalks. The sporangia are clustered and evenly scattered across the decaying wood surface, with smooth margins and slight size variation.

Thin, pale greenish to yellowish crust closely appressed to the surface, dotted with numerous small, rounded apothecia featuring pale margins and slightly darker central disks. Apothecia are embedded and loosely grouped. A lobed, pale bluish-green foliose lichen appears at the lower right.

A substantial, cushion-shaped fruiting body with a rough, cracked, and granular brown to tan surface. The center displays a lighter, slightly net-like patch. The margins are rounded and the structure is directly attached to the substrate.

Numerous tiny, black, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies densely scattered and partially embedded on a pale, fibrous stem. The fruiting bodies are shiny, firm, and arranged in irregular clusters across the surface.

Minute, brown, spherical fruiting bodies densely clustered, each on a slender dark stalk. Surfaces display a delicate, net-like lattice with a powdery, granular coating. The sporangia are tightly grouped, with intricate, cribrate textures visible at high magnification.

A continuous, pale yellowish to light tan crust tightly adheres to the wood, with a distinctly granular to finely warted surface. The margin is irregular, blending into the substrate, and some cracking and minor detachment are visible at the edges.

Small mushroom with a convex, rich orange-brown cap showing pronounced radial striations and a smooth surface. The long, slender stem is distinctly sinuous, lighter orange to yellowish, and slightly fibrous. No gills are visible from this angle.

Slender, elongated, white to translucent cylindrical fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and gentle curves, emerging upright in a scattered arrangement. Bases appear slightly darker or fibrous, contrasting with the delicate, minimalistic appearance of the upright structures.
Tiny, rounded fruitbodies with pale to light brown bases, each topped by a dense, dark granular spore mass. The clustered apothecia have smooth margins and a textured surface from the spore covering.

Large, irregular white patches with sharply defined dark brown to black margins disrupt the green leaf surface. The affected areas appear rough and leathery, with uneven distribution and visible leaf veins in unaffected regions.

White to cream, crust-like surface densely covered in short, tooth-like projections. Margin is irregular and wavy with brownish discoloration. Texture appears fibrous to spongy, closely appressed, lacking a distinct cap or stipe.

Clusters of minute, white, spherical bodies form dense, grape-like aggregations, interconnected and surrounded by fine, radiating, hair-like filaments. The texture appears powdery to granular, with compact groupings sharply contrasted against a dark background.

Numerous small, rounded, dark brown to blackish bumps scattered across a golden-brown, textured surface. The bumps are slightly raised, some with a tiny central opening, and are distributed irregularly, sometimes forming loose clusters.

A delicate, slender mushroom with a pale, elongated stem and a small, conical to bell-shaped light brown cap. The cap surface is smooth with a slightly darker center, and the underside reveals radiating gills.

Numerous circular to oval, pale gray to off-white lesions with sharply defined black borders scattered across the green leaf. Lesion centers appear slightly sunken and papery, with some coalescing at the edges. Leaf veins remain green and prominent.

Numerous minute, dark brown to nearly black, rounded or slightly irregular fruiting bodies with a granular surface are scattered and clustered on a pale, fibrous background. The fruiting bodies are very small, sessile, and lack a distinct margin at this magnification.

Small, disc-shaped fruiting body with a flat, finely granular white upper surface and a translucent, yellowish-brown margin and base. The margin is even, and the structure is delicate and sessile, directly attached to the substrate.

A solitary, cushion-shaped mass with a brown, mottled, and cracked surface. The texture appears dry and rough, with irregular fissures and a slightly lobed margin. The fruiting body is compact and hemispherical.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, dry orange-brown caps showing fine fibrils. Stems are slender, pale to dark brown with longitudinal streaks, and bases have soil and moss. Gills are closely spaced, attached, and pale ochre to light brown. No veil remnants or annulus visible.

Broadly convex cap with a rich orange-brown color, slightly darker at the center. The surface appears velvety and matte, with a mostly smooth margin and minor irregularity. Stipe and gills are not visible.

Crust-like fruiting body with a whitish, finely textured upper surface and a pale tan lower region. The surface features densely packed, elongated, irregular pores, creating a fibrous, torn appearance. The margin is diffuse and blends gradually into the substrate.

Extensive, tightly appressed patch with a granular to minutely nodular surface. Off-white to pale beige in color, with irregular, somewhat lobed margins and a powdery, cottony appearance formed by densely packed small granules.

Numerous small, black, spherical to subglobose structures densely scattered and clustered across a dry, fibrous stem. The fruiting bodies appear slightly raised with a rough, granular texture, contrasting against the brownish background of the stem.
A single, small, pale cream fungal patch with a flattened, irregularly rounded outline. The surface is granular and matte, with an indistinct margin blending into the substrate.

Small cluster of mushrooms with smooth, moist, caramel-brown convex caps, some with wavy margins. Caps are slightly translucent at the edges. Stems are slender, pale tan with fibrous texture. Gills are closely spaced and light brown.

A single, circular to oval fruiting body with a flat profile, frosted by fine granular structures. The center is pale beige, gradually darkening to a brownish, minutely roughened margin. The surface appears crystalline and the margin is well-defined.

Petite mushroom with a slender, straight, light brown stipe and a small, smooth, moist, reddish-brown convex cap. The cap margin is even and regular, and the overall appearance is delicate and upright.

Two small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat caps, pale to medium brown and mottled. Cap margins are even, adorned with tiny moisture droplets. Stems are short, curved, and match the cap color. Surfaces appear moist and smooth.
Minute, translucent to whitish, oval to nearly circular discs with smooth, glistening surfaces and slightly darker, well-defined margins, arranged in a loose row on a fibrous brown substrate.

Slender, cylindrical, pale branches with a bushy, irregularly branched structure. The surface is granular and covered in numerous small, round, whitish outgrowths, giving a distinctly filamentous and three-dimensional appearance.

Continuous, patchy mat with grayish to pale brown color and a distinctly granular to velvety surface. The texture is irregular, undulating, and bumpy, with scattered darker patches and a fine, fuzzy appearance.

Dense, bushy cluster of thin, hair-like, intricately branched segments. Branches are pale greenish-white to grayish, wiry, and filamentous, forming a tangled, airy mass with irregular branching and occasional slight swelling at the nodes.

Tightly adherent, flat crust with a pale gray to whitish, cracked surface. Numerous black, rounded spots are irregularly scattered and embedded within the smooth thallus, creating a striking contrast.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened pale pink caps, smooth margins, and closely spaced white gills tinged with pink. Stems are robust, cylindrical, white with faint pink mottling, and have a dry, finely textured surface.

A bushy, pale greenish-white tuft with finely branched, hair-like filaments hangs from a tree branch. The structure appears airy, delicate, and cottony, with intricately interwoven, slender branches forming a pendant mass.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened caps, pinkish-white and moist. Gills are closely spaced, pale pinkish to white, and attached to thick, white stipes with faint pink tones and a subtle fibrillose texture. Smooth cap margins and gentle pink blush are visible.
A small mushroom with a smooth, yellow-brown convex cap bearing a few dark specks, and a slender, pale, straight stem. The cap margin is even, and the fruiting body is solitary among plant debris.

Green needle-like surfaces are coated with a thin, powdery to granular pale greenish crust. Scattered across this layer are small, round, whitish, slightly raised disk-like spots, irregularly distributed and contrasting with the green background.

Small to medium mushrooms with pale tan to light brown convex caps, smooth to subtly textured surfaces, and closely spaced ochre gills. Slender, off-white to pale brown stems are straight to slightly curved, with soil and debris clinging to the bases.
Small mushrooms with convex, yellowish-brown caps showing a moist, wrinkled surface. Gills are densely spaced, broad, and tan to ochre. Stems are slender, elongated, brownish, and fibrous.

Slender mushrooms with thin, white stems and small, conical to bell-shaped caps. The caps are pale gray to grayish-brown with pronounced radial striations and a smooth surface. Young and mature fruiting bodies cluster together, with some white mycelium visible at the base.

Broad, convex to slightly depressed caps with purplish-brown to reddish-brown hues and lighter mottled centers. Caps have smooth, inrolled margins and faint radial streaks. Gills are closely spaced, cream to pale yellow. Stems are robust, cylindrical, and white with some soil attached.
Dense clusters of tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, translucent to opaque surfaces and slightly raised margins, scattered across decaying wood.
