A thin, cottony to slightly crustose, white to off-white mat spreads diffusely over a rough surface. The texture is finely fibrous and web-like, with patchy areas showing tan or brownish particles embedded in the mycelium. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.
A fine, white, powdery coating covers the green plant bud and stem, giving a dusty appearance without visible fruiting bodies or structural changes to the plant tissue.

Small, irregular, dark brown to blackish patches scattered across a dried leaf surface. The patches are slightly raised and lack distinct margins or visible fruiting bodies. Leaf venation forms a network of fine, polygonal cells.

Tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with translucent to whitish color, each featuring a distinctly fringed, hairy margin and a slightly darker central disc. The delicate, ciliate edges give a star-like appearance against the dark background.

A thin, pale gray crust forms a patchy, diffuse layer tightly appressed to the stone. The surface is relatively smooth with some granular or powdery areas, blending subtly into the rock without distinct margins or visible fruiting bodies.

Two globose fruiting bodies, one grayish-brown with a rough, warty surface and visible opening, the other smaller, off-white to cream with a smoother texture. Both have irregular margins and some adhering soil particles.

Minute, white, rounded tufts with a distinctly fuzzy, cottony appearance and fine, radiating hairs along the margins. The fruiting bodies are solitary and sharply contrasted against a dark background, highlighting their delicate, crystalline texture.

A tightly adhering, gray to dark gray crust with a rough, cracked, and granular surface. The texture appears powdery in places, with irregular, diffuse margins blending into the stone. No visible fruiting bodies.
Small, white, cup-shaped structures densely clustered on a brown surface, each with a pronounced fringe of long, delicate, hair-like projections around the rim, giving a soft, fuzzy appearance.

Crustose growth with scattered, dark, rounded to irregular rough-textured fruiting bodies partially immersed in the substrate. The surface is uneven, with indistinct margins blending into the surrounding green and brown material. Small, dark pits mark the perithecial openings.

Broadly convex cap with a slightly lobed margin, displaying a uniform golden-yellow color. The surface is smooth, matte, and subtly velvety, with the margin slightly paler than the center. No gills or stipe are visible from this angle.
Bright orange, shallow disc with a smooth, moist surface. The nearly circular margin is densely fringed with short, brown, hair-like setae, creating a distinct fuzzy edge.

Smooth, moist caps in yellow to ochre hues with wavy, uneven margins; one cap shows a large bite. Slender, yellow, slightly curved stems with attached debris. Pale yellow, closely spaced gills visible beneath the caps.

Numerous tiny, white to cream, cup-shaped bodies with conspicuous, fine, hair-like fringes along the margins. The cups are closely grouped, with smooth, matte surfaces and densely ciliate edges, scattered across a dark background.

A small, dark, nearly black spot with a slightly shiny, granular surface, embedded in pale wood. The fruiting body is low, irregular in outline, and lacks a distinct margin or visible reproductive structures.
Silvery-white cap with a smooth to slightly fibrous surface and inrolled margin. Densely packed, distinctly brown gills contrast with the pale, robust, fibrous stem.

Irregular, pale gray patch with a powdery, granular surface and fine cracks. The margin is uneven and slightly lighter, with a diffuse, lobate outline. The thallus is tightly appressed and lacks visible reproductive structures.

A grayish-brown, crust-like layer with a distinctly fuzzy, velvety texture, spreading irregularly. The surface is uneven and minutely bumpy, with scattered white mycelial tufts visible at the edges. No cap, stem, or margin structures are present.

A pale grayish-white, roughly circular patch with a cracked, areolate surface. The thallus is crustose, tightly adherent, with an irregular but well-defined margin and a rough, granular texture. No prominent reproductive structures are visible.

Tan to light brown fibrous surface with several small, dark, rounded, slightly raised spots scattered irregularly. The surface appears dry and subtly textured, with the dark spots contrasting against the lighter background.

Rusty to orange-brown caps with a dry, fibrillose surface and uneven margins. Caps are broadly convex to nearly flat. Slender, ochre-brown stems are slightly curved. Gills are yellowish to ochre and moderately spaced. Clustered among moss.
Broad, smooth cap with a dry, matte surface; light brown overall with a distinctly darker, slightly depressed central disc and a subtly wavy, even margin.

Viewed from below, the fungus displays densely packed, white, slightly decurrent gills radiating from a central, smooth to faintly fibrous, light brown stem. The cap surface is not visible in this image.

A dried brown leaf with prominent veins and serrated edges, covered in numerous small, irregular dark spots and mottled patches. The surface appears leathery and brittle, with minute dark speckles scattered across the tissue.
Small, globose fruiting body with a tan, rough, and cracked outer surface split open to reveal a dense, olive-brown, powdery spore mass. The peridium margins are irregular and torn.

Two mushrooms with medium brown, finely fibrous caps—one viewed from above, one showing closely spaced dull brown gills. Stems are slender, slightly curved, and pale brown to ochre with a smooth surface.

Dense clusters of minute, upright stalks topped with small, globular heads emerge from a compact, greenish-yellow, granular base. The surface is uneven and textured, with stalks of varying heights creating a moss-like appearance.

Tiny, cup-shaped fruitbodies with whitish to translucent coloring, each featuring a distinctly fringed, hairy margin. The delicate, shallow cups are scattered in small groups, with fine hair-like structures ornamenting their circular edges.

A continuous, gray, crust-like layer tightly covering the surface, with a granular, rough, and uneven texture. The surface is matte, slightly bumpy, and lacks visible reproductive structures or distinct margins.

Slender, dark brown stem with a slightly glossy surface, supporting a small, reddish-brown convex cap. The cap margin is even and slightly incurved. Closely spaced gills beneath the cap match its color. Approximately 10 cm long with a 1 cm diameter cap.

A brown, elongated, oval structure with a rough, textured surface and scattered dark patches. Some soil or debris adheres to the surface. No distinct fungal fruiting bodies or visible reproductive structures are present.

Medium to dark brown convex caps with a dry, finely fibrillose surface. Stems are slender, slightly curved, and fibrous, with white mycelial remnants at the base. Gills are closely spaced, broad, and dark brown.

Three mushrooms with convex, cream to pale yellow caps mottled with brown soil patches. Stems are thick, white, and slightly bulbous at the base. Gills are brownish-ochre, moderately crowded, and attached to the stem. Caps appear smooth, with no visible veil remnants.

Delicate, minute fruiting bodies with slender, translucent to whitish stems and tiny, pale, smooth, cup-shaped caps. The caps have slightly flared margins and are spaced apart, with the thin stems lying across a moist, brownish surface.

Hemispherical cap with bluish-green and brownish hues, smooth to slightly fibrous surface. Thick, white stem with fibrous material and debris near the base. Cap margin appears even; overall structure is robust.

A tiny, solitary fungus with a smooth, white, disc-shaped cap atop a slender, translucent stalk, emerging from a reddish, bumpy, catkin-like substrate. The fruiting body appears delicate and fragile, with a pale, unblemished surface and no visible gills or pores.

Bright orange, irregularly lobed structures with a moist, smooth, and slightly gelatinous surface, arranged in a compact, linear sequence along a thin, pale stalk. The margins are rounded and the segments closely connected, creating a striking, vibrant appearance.

Minute, granular to slightly nodular yellow-green patches closely appressed to the twig, forming irregular, discontinuous crusts with a rough, uneven surface. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible. The thallus appears as scattered, fine, olive-toned granules.
Tiny, white, disc- to cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, translucent to opaque surfaces, each borne on a slender, short stalk and scattered across a dark, moist, organic substrate.

Small mushrooms with slender, reddish-brown stems and rounded to conical, smooth, dark brown caps. Gills underneath are brown and moderately spaced. The fruiting bodies are about 6 centimeters tall, with some plant debris attached to the base.

Blue-green to gray-green, leaf-like lobes with irregular, upturned margins. Surface densely covered in small, granular outgrowths, giving a textured look. Occasional white undersides and blackened cracks are visible. Thallus forms overlapping, loosely attached patches.
A single, small, cup-shaped fungus with a smooth, matte brown upper surface and a thin, slightly translucent, irregular margin. It is attached laterally to a dark brown branch.

Irregular, globose to lobed yellowish-olive structures with a granular surface, arranged in a chain and connected by thin, translucent strands. The sporocarps appear slightly rough and clustered against a dark background.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, pale brown to beige caps and matte, subtly hairy surfaces. Gills are pale and closely spaced beneath the cap. Stems are slender, cylindrical, and similar in color to the caps.

Small, delicate, cup-shaped structure with a smooth, white to translucent surface and a finely defined, even margin. The profile is circular and slightly raised, with another similar structure blurred in the background.

A minute fungus with a slender, translucent whitish stem supporting a small, smooth, pale cup-shaped cap with a slightly incurved margin. The cap appears moist and gelatinous. White, cottony mycelium surrounds the base.
A minute, white fungus with a long, slender, translucent stipe and a small, cup-shaped, smooth apothecium at one end. The surface appears moist and glossy, and the structure is thin and fragile.

Yellowish, polygonal surface with a smooth, slightly glossy texture. Scattered dark patches contain clusters of minute black dots, contrasting against the lighter background. No distinct margins or large fruiting bodies are visible.

Two mushrooms with convex, light brown caps covered in small white warts. One cap shows a central bump, while the other reveals densely packed white gills and a smooth, white stem with a skirt-like ring.

Slender, unbranched, club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, pale brown to tan, slightly translucent and waxy surfaces. Tips are blunt and rounded. Arranged in a loose cluster, some upright and some gently curved, partially embedded in dark soil among decaying plant debris.

Tiny, cream to pale yellow disc-shaped structures scattered across a rough brown surface. The discs are flat to slightly concave, with smooth, delicate, almost translucent margins, and measure just a few millimeters wide.

Elongated green leaves display irregular yellowish to brownish lesions with clusters of small, dark, raised pustules. The affected areas are slightly elevated and disrupt the smooth leaf surface, with surrounding tissue appearing pale or chlorotic.

Numerous small, round to irregular, reddish-brown pustules densely clustered and slightly raised on a bright green leaf, with clear discoloration in affected areas and a smooth, healthy appearance elsewhere.

Medium to large mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed brown caps, subtly fibrous surfaces, and even margins. Stems are slender, pale whitish to light brown with faint surface fibrils and slightly bulbous bases. Gills are closely spaced, attached, and pale, clearly visible on upturned specimens.

Dense mat of overlapping, irregularly lobed, leaf-like structures with undulate, slightly crenulate margins. Upper surface is grayish-green, somewhat powdery in places, and closely appressed. No visible reproductive structures. Interspersed with green moss, forming a contiguous, clustered mat.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, light to medium brown caps featuring darker centers and subtle radial fibrils. Stems are pale with faint longitudinal striations. Gills are closely spaced, pale grayish to brown, and attached to the stem. Cap surfaces appear smooth and moist.

Irregular, lobed patches of moist, glistening yellowish-orange slime with a soft texture, scattered in linear clusters along dark organic debris. Margins are diffuse and blend into the substrate, lacking distinct boundaries or visible fruiting bodies.

Numerous tiny, pale, granular or powdery specks are scattered irregularly across the green, elongated leaf surface, giving it a slightly roughened texture. The specks are subtle but distinct against the leaf's background, with no large fruiting bodies visible.

Irregular, dark blackish patches with a rough, granular texture scattered unevenly along the light brown wood surface. The patches lack distinct margins and blend into the substrate, forming a crust-like appearance.

Delicate fungus with a slender, reddish-brown stem covered in fine hairs. The small, white, dome-shaped cap is semi-translucent and adorned with numerous long, dark bristles, giving it a spiny appearance.

Broad, smooth caps with muted brownish-lilac tones and darker mottling, slightly inrolled margins. Densely packed, yellow-brown gills and robust, off-white stipes with some brownish discoloration. Soil and leaf litter adhere to the base.

Irregular, patchy, pale yellowish to off-white masses with a granular, slightly rough surface. The growth is amorphous and loosely scattered across a dark, organic background, interspersed with fine roots and decaying plant debris. No distinct fruiting bodies or defined shapes are visible.

Branched, dried stems encrusted with irregular, lumpy patches of yellowish-brown to olive, granular material. The encrustations are unevenly scattered, dry, and powdery, forming discrete masses without a continuous layer or distinct margins.
Numerous small, circular, dark brown pustules are densely clustered and slightly raised on a smooth green and yellowing leaf surface, with yellow halos surrounding many of the spots.

Two mushrooms with convex, light brown caps—one showing a slightly darker center and velvety surface, the other displaying closely spaced, deep brown gills and a cylindrical, fibrous stipe. Cap margins are even, and no veil remnants are visible.

Dense, cottony mycelial mat with a velvety to fluffy texture, predominantly white with extensive pale pink to salmon patches, spreading over and partially enveloping dark granular clumps. No distinct fruiting bodies or spore masses are visible.

Clusters of small, irregular, bright orange to yellowish-orange fruiting bodies with a granular, frothy texture. Some are covered by a thin whitish membrane, appearing moist and glistening, with short stalk-like extensions and a scattered, patchy arrangement.

Dense, leafy thallus with overlapping, irregular lobes in blue-green to olive-green hues. The upper surface is granular and matte, with distinctly serrated, finely notched margins. The texture is rough and uneven, forming a rosette-like arrangement tightly appressed to the surface.

Three mushrooms with smooth, pale yellowish to cream convex caps, closely spaced pale gills, and sturdy off-white stems. Some caps have minor debris, and the stem bases show brownish soiling with white mycelium. The fruiting bodies appear fresh and robust.

Two mushrooms with convex, pale yellow to cream caps, smooth surfaces, and slightly incurved margins. Stems are thick, white, and adorned with brownish fibrils, ending in bulbous bases. Gills are pale, closely spaced, and clearly visible in the sectioned specimen.

Pale cream to light tan caps with small white warty patches, smooth margins, and dry surfaces. White cylindrical stems feature a skirt-like ring and slightly bulbous base. Gills are white, crowded, and free beneath the cap.

Numerous tiny, dark, nearly spherical to slightly elongated structures scattered irregularly across a pale, fibrous stem. The fungal bodies appear as minute, bristly black dots with a subtly roughened texture, lacking overt fuzziness or filamentous growth.

Delicate, translucent fruiting body with a slender, elongated stipe supporting a small, flat, whitish, somewhat triangular cap. The cap has a smooth surface and slightly pointed apex. A mat of white, fuzzy mycelium surrounds the base.

Pale green to bluish-green, leafy thallus forming a dense mat with broad, flat lobes. Margins are distinctly serrated or irregularly notched, some slightly upturned. Surface appears smooth to slightly granular, with powdery patches in places.

Clusters of small, irregular, bright orange lobed bodies with a moist, slightly shiny surface. Some are connected by thin, translucent strands, scattered unevenly across a dark, damp background. The texture appears granular to smooth, with irregular margins and cushion-like shapes.

Tiny, pale cream to whitish, disc-shaped fruitbodies are scattered across the dark, rough surface of a conifer cone. The minute apothecia have smooth margins and a slightly translucent, waxy appearance, clustered gregariously on the cone scales.

Two mushrooms with convex, dry, fibrous light brown caps and slender, striate stems. One specimen shows closely spaced, pale brown to beige gills beneath the cap. Surfaces appear matte and no veil remnants are visible.

Numerous small, round to irregular greenish-black colonies scattered across a pale, smooth surface. The colonies are slightly raised with a fuzzy or powdery texture and diffuse margins blending into the background.

Irregular, lobed, cushion-shaped structures with a yellowish to olive, distinctly granular or powdery surface. The texture appears dry and crustose, with irregular, somewhat fused margins and a contiguous, spreading arrangement.

Medium brown caps with a slightly scaly texture, convex to flat and uneven at the edges. Densely packed, light brown gills beneath. Slender, pale stems with faint fibrillose markings. No visible ring or veil remnants. Mushrooms vary from young to mature, some caps more expanded.

Slender, unbranched, cylindrical fruiting bodies with smooth, medium to dark brown surfaces. Tips are rounded, and stems vary from straight to arched. Bases are slightly paler and emerge directly from the soil.

Long, narrow leaf with densely clustered, rust-brown, powdery pustules forming elongated streaks along the veins. Infected areas show yellowing, while the rest of the leaf remains green. Pustules are small, raised, and granular, coalescing into extensive linear lesions.

A small, dark, star-shaped structure with rigid, sharply pointed spine-like projections radiating outward from a central point. The surface is dark brown to black and somewhat glossy, with evenly spaced spiky arms.

Numerous minute, upright, hair-like structures densely cover the surface. They are brownish with some tips appearing slightly darker or purplish, and exhibit a fine, filamentous texture at a microscopic scale.

A tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, rounded edge sits atop a slender, elongated stem densely covered in fine, fuzzy hairs. The stem emerges from a brown, oval object, accentuating the delicate structure.

Irregular, lobed orange masses with a moist, granular to smooth texture, scattered in small clusters and connected by thin whitish strands. Margins are uneven and diffuse, blending into the dark background.

Cap greenish-blue with brownish patches and a slightly wavy, damaged margin. Gills are broad, densely packed, and purplish-brown. Stipe is robust, bulbous at the base, distinctly bluish-green, and smooth, with soil remnants attached.

Numerous minute, rounded to slightly irregular grayish apothecia scattered across a granular, greenish to yellow-green surface. The apothecia are smooth to slightly roughened and less than 1 mm in diameter, appearing dispersed rather than clustered.
No visible fungal structures are present; only green, strap-like leaves and blue, star-shaped flowers are seen, with no discoloration, pustules, or sori apparent on the foliage or flowers.

Two small fruiting bodies with globose to subglobose caps, pale cream to light brown, covered in rough, warty scales. Slender stems share the same scaly texture and color, with soil clinging to the base. No gills are visible from this angle.

Small, white to cream-colored rounded discs with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces. Some fruiting bodies show irregular or wavy margins and are clustered together, closely attached to the substrate.

Irregular, lobed, and convoluted yellowish-green structures with dark mottled patterns. The surface appears granular and slightly rough, with undulating, irregular margins. Structures are closely grouped and connected by thin strands, suggesting a moist, gelatinous texture.

Two slender mushrooms with brown-speckled, elongated stems and small, rounded caps covered in darker brown scales. One cap is split open, revealing a white, membranous interior. Soil clings to the base, and the surface texture appears scaly and granular.

Greenish-gray, broad, overlapping lobes with irregular, upturned margins. The surface is densely covered in granular, isidiate outgrowths, giving a rough, matte texture. Margins are lined with these granules, and the thallus appears undulating and slightly raised in places.

Broad, overlapping gray-green lobes form a dense, leafy patch with a slightly wrinkled, powdery surface. The margins are rounded to irregularly notched, and the thallus appears tightly attached and somewhat brittle.

Mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, smooth, light brown to tan caps. Gills are closely spaced, attached, and pale brown. Stems are slender, pale to light brown, and fibrous, with some appearing torn or bent.

Dense, thick mat with frilly, overlapping grayish-green lobes. Margins are irregular and slightly crenulate. Surface appears rough, granular, and somewhat powdery, with a silvery-blue tint in some areas. Forms a clustered, continuous patch tightly attached to the substrate.

Small, hemispherical cap with blue-green and yellowish tones, smooth and moist in appearance. Long, pale stem with bluish hues, some soil clinging to the base, and fine mycelial threads visible near the bottom.

Tiny, pale, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with thin, delicate margins are scattered in loose clusters across a rough, brown surface, creating a striking contrast between the light fungus and the darker background.
Two mushrooms with thick, white stems covered in brownish granules, topped by conical to bell-shaped caps that are pale and speckled with fine brown scales. The bases are darkened by attached soil.

Tiny, delicate disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a translucent white surface, smooth even margins, and slender, slightly curved pale stipes. Some discs show fine yellowish or brownish specks. The overall appearance is fragile and semi-translucent.

Rounded, irregular structure with a cracked, fissured surface. The color ranges from beige to light brown, with darker lines accentuating the crevices. The form appears bulbous with a possible constriction at the base, highlighted against a dark background.

Two medium-sized mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, dry, fibrillose brown caps. The left cap is darker and more domed, while the right is lighter and flatter. Both have subtle radial striations and a slightly darker central umbo.

Sectioned fruiting bodies with yellowish-brown caps, blue-green staining in the flesh and stipe, purplish-brown gills, and fibrous white mycelium at the base. One specimen shows the cap surface, the other reveals the gills and internal tissue coloration.
Numerous tiny, pale cream to off-white, irregularly rounded fruiting bodies with a granular texture are scattered and loosely clustered on a dark, rough, scaly surface.

Numerous tiny, cream to pale yellow, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly wavy margins are scattered and clustered on a brown, textured surface. The apothecia appear round to irregular and have a delicate, translucent quality.

Mature mushrooms with broad, pale tan to ochre caps, some with brownish patches and leaf debris. Gills are crowded and pale brown to ochre. Stems are thick, white to pale, with brown stains and bulbous, soil-covered bases.

Moist, glossy fungal mass with dark, irregular shapes and several small, pale tan to light brown, globose to cup-like structures. The tissue appears soft and somewhat gelatinous, with fine debris and green filaments scattered nearby.

Tiny, white, bell-shaped caps sit atop extremely slender, reddish-brown, wiry stems. The caps are faintly striate and slightly translucent, with even margins. The delicate fruiting bodies cluster together, rising above a moist, dark brown leaf.

Two small mushrooms with off-white to pale tan, fuzzy-textured caps; one cap is slightly depressed in the center. Slender, pale brown stems support the caps, with the right specimen showing white, closely spaced gills underneath.

A small, solitary, shallowly cup-shaped fruiting body with a short, distinct stipe. The upper surface is smooth and brown, with a slightly paler, finely textured margin. The texture appears velvety to smooth, blending subtly with the branch.

Two mushrooms with convex caps, one large and yellowish-green with a smooth, moist surface and faint striations at the margin. The stipes are robust and blue-green, with white veil remnants near the top.

Bright orange, irregularly shaped masses with a moist, granular, and lumpy surface are arranged in a linear sequence along a thin, pale support. The margins are uneven and the overall form is amorphous and bulbous.

Irregular, lobed, bright orange masses arranged in a chain-like pattern along thin, branching twigs. The surface appears matte to slightly moist, with a scattered, linear growth habit following the contours of the underlying structures.

Irregular, contiguous fruiting bodies with yellowish coloration and a distinct cracked, netted surface pattern. Margins are uneven, with a crustose texture and translucent, slightly glossy areas. Structures are attached to thin twigs or debris.

Flat, leaf-like patch with overlapping, radiating lobes. Margins are distinctly serrated. Surface is pale green to grayish, slightly powdery, with scattered white spots. Some minor cracks and fissures are visible. Tightly appressed and interspersed with small moss tufts.

Two small, rounded to convex caps with off-white to pale cream coloration and scattered brownish scales. Stems are short, robust, and similarly scaled, with soil clinging to the base. Gills are not visible.

Small mushrooms with reddish-brown, moist, smooth caps and closely spaced brownish gills. Stems are thin, elongated, and display a mottled white and reddish-brown, slightly fibrous texture. Fruiting bodies are scattered and lying on green moss.
Numerous minute, erect, hair-like blackish to dark brown structures, each less than 1 mm tall, densely scattered in patches across the rough, textured woody surface.

Small, dark brown to black, fuzzy patches with a bristly texture are scattered irregularly along a light brown, weathered stem. The colonies are rounded, discrete, and distinctly textured, standing out against the smooth surface of the stem.

Tiny, dark, nearly spherical structures scattered along the pale stem, each surrounded by a fringe of fine, bristle-like hairs, giving a distinctly rough, hispid appearance. The fruiting bodies are spaced apart and appear as minute, bristly dots.

Two mushrooms with convex caps; the larger shows greenish-yellow tones, marginal splitting, and a moist sheen, while the smaller is blue-green. Both have robust, pale blue to blue-green fibrous stems. No gills are visible.

Two delicate, slender fruiting bodies with long, translucent whitish stems, each topped by a tiny, smooth, cup-shaped white cap. The caps are slightly flared at the margin and appear fragile. The arrangement is scattered, with both fruiting bodies close together.

Tiny, dark, rounded to cup-shaped caps with smooth surfaces, each atop a slender, pale to whitish, delicate stipe. The fruiting bodies are scattered and distinctly separated, with caps appearing slightly concave or flattened. Overall size is very small compared to the nearby twig.

Irregular, crust-like masses with lobed, uneven shapes cling to twigs. Surfaces are dry, powdery, and granular, colored pale grayish-white to dark olive-brown with some yellowish tinges. Structures range from a few millimeters to over a centimeter, scattered in a linear pattern.

Two small, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, thin margins sit atop slender, semi-translucent stems. The stems are fragile, slightly brownish in places, and the overall appearance is delicate and finely detailed.

Irregular, lobed masses of bright orange with a gelatinous, spongy texture. Translucent, slimy regions intermingle with more opaque areas, and the organism envelops twigs and debris with diffuse, blending margins.

Two slender, upright, unbranched fruiting bodies with a cylindrical to slightly club-shaped form. They are nearly black, smooth, and subtly lighter at the base, with rounded apices and no visible cap or branching.

Mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, smooth pale beige caps. Gills are closely spaced, broad, and light tan. Slender, elongated stipes show a faint lilac tinge and fibrous texture. Caps have smooth, even margins; fruiting bodies overlap in a clustered arrangement.

Elongated green leaves display numerous small, raised, rust-colored pustules scattered across the surfaces. The pustules are rounded to slightly irregular, often with yellowish halos, and cause minor leaf discoloration and deformation.

Seed capsules are swollen and deformed, filled with dark brown to black, powdery, granular spore masses. The spore masses completely occupy the interior, giving a rough, irregular appearance. Inset shows globose, dark brown spores under magnification.

Slender mushrooms with conical to bell-shaped, smooth ochre-brown caps, some showing a slightly darker center. Stems are thin, pale to medium brown, and fibrous. Gills are closely spaced and lighter brown, visible on upturned specimens. Arranged loosely on sandy soil with grass and small stones.

Numerous tiny, dark, rounded to slightly irregular spots scattered across a dry, pale brown, cracked leaf. The spots are slightly raised and embedded in the leaf surface, contrasting with the brittle, tattered leaf background.

Irregular, dark patch with a granular, powdery texture embedded in a pale, discolored area on the green leaf surface. The margin is diffuse and slightly fuzzy, with fine black specks concentrated in the center.

Compact, irregular black masses with a granular to powdery texture clustered on dried, brownish plant tissue. The fungal growth appears rough and crusty, closely adhering to the plant’s reproductive structures.

Densely clustered, ruffled, and lobed masses with a compact, cauliflower-like shape. Pale cream to light tan in color, with smooth, intricately folded surfaces and irregular, undulating margins, giving a frilled appearance.

Smooth, convex cap with a yellowish-brown hue and slightly darker center. Gills are closely spaced, broad, and medium to dark brown. Stem is pale cream to light brown, fibrous, and slightly curved with brownish patches.

Numerous small, rounded, reddish-brown to dark brown pustules scattered across a dried leaf, concentrated along veins. The pustules blend into the rough, matte-textured leaf surface, with subtle brown, gray, and black color variations.

Narrow green leaves display numerous small, brown, irregularly shaped spots and slightly raised pustules scattered across the surfaces, some merging into larger patches, indicating a rust-like infection.

Dark brown to nearly black, irregularly shaped, slightly raised pustules scattered along the green stem. Some pustules are elongated, others rounded, often surrounded by faint yellowish halos. The affected areas appear rougher than the surrounding smooth tissue.

Extensive, crust-like patch tightly appressed to the surface, densely covered with small, rounded to warty granules. Pale grayish to off-white in color, with a granular, uneven texture and diffuse, slightly fibrous margins. Irregular spreading pattern across the substrate.
Longitudinal section shows a light brown, fibrous stem and a pale tan cap with a thin, slightly incurved margin. The internal tissue appears fleshy, and gills are not distinctly visible in this view.

Irregular, dark brown to blackish lesions with lighter, possibly necrotic margins disrupt the green leaf surface. The affected areas appear rough and crusty, forming elongated patches that do not cover the entire leaf.

Broad, moderately spaced tan gills with a smooth surface radiate from a fibrous light brown stipe. The cap margin is wavy and undulate, matching the gills in color. The overall appearance is dry and even-toned.

Minute, rounded to irregular blackish spots scattered within a greenish and whitish matrix, appearing smooth to slightly granular. The dark fungal bodies are embedded or superficial, lacking prominent margins and blending subtly with the surrounding tissue.

Numerous raised, circular to irregular brown pustules scattered across a yellow-green leaf, some with a papery or powdery texture. The pustules vary in size and density, disrupting the leaf surface and surrounded by faint chlorotic halos.

Leaves display numerous small, irregular brown spots with pale yellow halos, scattered across the surface. Some areas show holes, curling, and edge discoloration, with a wilted, damaged texture and visible tissue necrosis.

Pale greenish-gray, crusty surface with a granular, uneven texture. Numerous small, round, brownish discs are scattered centrally. Edges are irregular and fragmented, with greenish patches along the margins. The overall appearance is rough and compact.
Dense clusters of small, yellowish-orange, powdery pustules cover the flower parts and nearby leaves, forming irregular, granular patches that stand out vividly against the green foliage.

A dense, white, fuzzy mat radiates outward with a diffuse margin, blending into the green surface. The center is darker and granular, dotted with small, dark specks within the filamentous, matted texture.

Large green, five-lobed leaves display numerous white, roughly circular spots scattered across their surfaces. Some spots have slightly irregular margins, and a few holes are present. The leaf texture is smooth and glossy.

Longitudinally sectioned mushroom with a medium brown, smooth, conical cap. Pale brown gills are visible beneath the cap. The stem is long, slender, light brown, and fibrous, with a slightly thickened base.

Dense, compact mass with numerous flattened, ruffled, and contorted lobes. Pale cream to light brown color, smooth and somewhat waxy surface. Irregular, undulating margins create a flower-like or cauliflower appearance.
Dense green foliage with smooth-edged, oval leaves and upright stems. Clusters of small, bright yellow inflorescences are scattered among the leaves. No distinct fungal structures are visible.

Tiny, upright fruiting bodies with slender dark stalks topped by globose to oval, brown, fuzzy heads. Arranged in loose groups, each head appears finely textured and powdery. Structures are minute, less than a few millimeters tall, standing out against the substrate.

Densely clustered, coral-like structures with multiple upright, irregularly branched, and flattened tips. Smooth, slightly waxy surface and bushy appearance, emerging from a thickened base with attached soil.

Slender, translucent stem with a granular surface supports a small, pale cream cap. The cap is convex with prominent radial striations extending to the even margin. Gills are not visible from this angle.

Two nearly spherical, dark brown to black fruiting bodies covered with irregular, star-shaped white patches. The surface appears rough due to these pale, angular scales. The sporocarps are closely grouped and attached to a greenish background.

Broadly convex to depressed caps with yellowish to yellow-brown tones and greenish-olive patches, irregular margins, and slightly sticky surfaces. Robust, white cylindrical stipes with adhering soil. Closely spaced, white to cream gills are clearly visible on one specimen.

A single, upright fruiting body with a dark, nearly black, rough-textured cap atop a slender, fibrous, light brown stalk. The cap appears shiny and globose, contrasting with the translucent, irregular stalk. The structure stands out against a blurred green background.

Small, delicate, white to translucent fruiting bodies with slender, upright stalks and slightly expanded, disc-shaped heads. The apothecia are spaced apart, varying in height, with smooth, thin stalks and rounded to slightly irregular margins.

Slender, moist orange stalk supporting a rounded, dark sporangium with prominent white, wart-like spots. The cap surface appears granular and uneven, contrasting with the translucent stalk. Background is blurred, emphasizing the detailed fruiting body.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with a vibrant light orange to peach color and finely granular surface. The margin is even and rounded, and the bodies are sessile, closely grouped on a green mossy background.

Small, globose fruiting bodies with a striking mosaic of silvery-white and dark brown patches on the surface, each elevated on a slender, fibrous brown stalk. The sporocarps are clustered and distinctly patterned.

Large, irregular brown lesion with a leathery texture, densely covered in tiny black raised dots. The margin is diffuse, blending into adjacent green tissue. The surface shows significant discoloration and necrosis, with numerous minute black fruiting bodies scattered throughout.

A sharply defined edge with a fine, crystalline or minutely hairy texture, transitioning from a pale, off-white surface to a darker background. No overall form or branching is visible at this magnification.

A green, curved stem with a brownish, sunken lesion and slight swelling. The affected area appears ruptured, with fuzzy surface texture and remnants of dried plant tissue attached near the damaged site.

Numerous small, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with pale gray to grayish-white centers and distinctly darker, almost blackish margins. Some discs have slightly undulating or irregular edges and smooth surfaces, often closely grouped or overlapping.

A delicate, small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, pale cream to translucent cap and a slender, fragile stipe. The cap margin is even and unornamented, standing upright and contrasting with the darker, fibrous plant debris.

Numerous small, brown, spherical fruiting bodies with a finely granular, slightly fuzzy surface are scattered and slightly elevated above a moist, dark background. The sporocarps are dispersed and stand separately, with no visible stalks in this close-up view.

Tiny, grayish to translucent disc-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, moist, and slightly reflective surfaces cluster densely on wet, decaying wood. The apothecia are small, with even, non-raised margins and a gelatinous appearance.

A small, delicate mushroom with a dome-shaped, light brown cap featuring fine radial striations. The cap is smooth and slightly translucent, supported by a slender, pale, and slightly translucent stipe.

A single, slender reddish-brown stalk topped with a rounded, moist, gelatinous head displaying a mottled pattern of white and brown. The surface appears glistening and smooth, with regular, rounded margins.

Numerous small, globose to irregularly rounded, translucent to yellowish-brown, gelatinous fruiting bodies cluster together, forming a bumpy, uneven, shiny surface. The texture appears smooth and moist, with indistinct margins blending into one another and no visible stalks.

Irregular, dark blackish patches and streaks spread across pale, fibrous plant stems. The growth is superficial, patchy, and lacks any prominent fruiting bodies or distinct elongated structures, blending with the rough texture of the substrate.

Densely clustered, upright coral-like branches with smooth, slender, pale cream to off-white surfaces. Tips are rounded to slightly pointed, and the robust base emerges directly from the soil, forming compact, intricate clusters.

Small mushrooms with smooth, moist, light brown to orange-brown convex caps, closely spaced pale tan gills, and slender, off-white stems covered in fine fibrils. Some stems show brownish discoloration and soil at the base.
White, widely spaced gills radiate from a central point beneath a cap, with a slender, translucent to pale yellowish smooth stem extending outward. The cap surface is not visible in this view.

Numerous tiny, black, elongated, slightly raised fruiting bodies scattered across pale, straw-colored, dried plant stems. The dark structures contrast sharply with the lighter background and are embedded in the plant tissue.

Crustose, grayish-white patch with densely packed, small round to polygonal areoles. Each areole has a central pale to whitish disc, creating a granular, cracked texture. Margins are irregular but distinct, contrasting sharply with the darker background.

Crustose greenish-gray patch with numerous small, bright orange to yellow-orange rounded discs scattered in irregular clusters. The discs have flat to slightly convex surfaces and distinct margins, contrasting against the smooth to slightly granular background.
Numerous small, circular, brownish to rust-colored raised spots scattered across the green leaf surface, disrupting the otherwise smooth texture and contrasting with the visible reticulate venation.

A single delicate mushroom with a pale beige, conical to bell-shaped cap showing pronounced radial grooves. The cap is smooth and slightly glossy. The long, slender stipe is translucent and uniformly pale, giving a fragile appearance.
A delicate mushroom with a long, slender, yellowish to pale brown translucent stem, fine whitish fibrils near the base, and a small cap showing well-spaced, white to pale gills from below.

Small, dark, oval to slightly elongated fruiting bodies scattered and loosely clustered on bark. Matte to slightly rough texture, dark brown to nearly black, embedded in the surface with indistinct margins. No prominent reproductive structures visible.

Small, cream to pale yellow fan-shaped caps with finely velvety texture and wavy, inrolled margins. Densely packed, radiating gills are visible on the underside. Fruiting bodies are sessile, overlapping in clusters, and lack a distinct stipe.

Tiny, vivid orange, shallow cup-shaped discs with smooth, slightly glossy surfaces. The minute fruiting bodies are scattered and sessile, with even, non-raised margins, nestled among dense, bright green moss.

A tightly appressed, crust-like layer densely covered with small, rounded, pale to cream-colored granules, creating a granular and uneven texture. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the substrate, with some whitish, cottony patches at the edges.

Numerous small, black, rounded to irregularly shaped fruiting bodies scattered across a pale, striated, dry surface. The dark structures are embedded or slightly raised, sharply contrasting with the lighter background.

A continuous, bright yellow to orange crust covers the fallen trunk, forming a granular, slightly roughened, adherent layer. The lichen appears patchy but dense, following the contours of the wood and providing a vivid contrast against the darker bark.

Thin, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, pale tan to off-white with densely packed, small rounded warts creating a granular, uneven texture. Some areas show yellowish or ochre tints and scattered whitish patches. The margin is diffuse and blends gradually into the substrate.
Brown, moist caps with striate, translucent margins; slender white stems with a powdery surface; densely packed, broad, pale brownish-gray gills. Surrounded by fallen leaves and decaying wood.

Several tiny, slender, upright white fruiting bodies with smooth, translucent surfaces emerge singly from a small piece of brown plant debris. Each structure is delicate, unbranched, and sparsely scattered.

A slender, green, slightly hairy stem arches into a hook shape, ending in a cluster of irregular, swollen, glossy green structures. The tip appears deformed and enlarged, with a few small, linear leaves or bracts along the stem.
A green, curved plant stem with a cluster of small, bulbous green structures at the tip. The stem shows distortion and slight discoloration, with a mostly smooth surface and some visible fine hairs.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened yellowish-brown caps, scattered darker patches, and smooth surfaces. White to cream, closely spaced gills are attached to robust, off-white stems. Caps show some adhering debris and entire margins.

Two small, oval to elongated bodies with semi-translucent whitish interiors and light brown exteriors. Surfaces appear moist, gelatinous, and smooth, with rounded margins blending into the dark, textured background. Fine pale fibers are present nearby.

Delicate fruiting body with a slender, slightly curved, pale to dark brown translucent stem. The cap is cup-shaped, smooth, pale, and has a slightly irregular margin. Attached to a partially split, darkened structure.

Numerous tiny, irregularly shaped, black to very dark brown granular patches scattered across a light brown, ridged surface. Most patches are less than 1 mm wide, appearing loosely clustered or isolated, with a slightly fuzzy texture.

Numerous tiny, white, translucent to opaque globose fruiting bodies with smooth, moist-looking surfaces are scattered and clustered irregularly on a fibrous plant stem. The fruiting bodies are sessile and lack visible stalks.

Tightly clustered, upright fruiting bodies with smooth, matte, pale pinkish-white to creamy branches. The branches are intricately divided, with blunt to slightly pointed tips and a soft, waxy appearance. No caps or cup-like structures are present.
Small, bright orange to reddish-orange cup-shaped bodies with distinctly fringed, hairy margins and a velvety surface, scattered loosely on dark soil.

Three mushrooms with smooth, moist, convex caps in light to reddish-brown, paler at the edges. Gills are closely spaced and pale cream. Slender, white stems show some soil and debris at the base. No veil remnants or ring visible.

Numerous small, round, dark brown to black dots scattered irregularly across a pale, striated, fibrous plant stem. The dots appear as discrete, superficial spots, contrasting sharply with the smooth background.

Clusters of small, round to oval discs with vivid yellowish-orange centers and pale, whitish to grayish raised margins, scattered across a granular, pale gray crust. The surface appears rough and the apothecia are tightly grouped.

Crustose lichen with a rough, granular, and bumpy surface. Predominantly pale grayish-white with yellowish to greenish tinges, forming irregular, compact, lumpy protrusions. Margins are indistinct, blending into the background. Texture appears powdery to granular, forming a continuous patch.
Slender, pinkish-red stalks topped with small, round, rough-textured heads. The heads are granular and lack white spots, with fruiting bodies spaced apart on decaying plant material.
Small, irregularly rounded, gelatinous patches that are translucent to whitish with a smooth, moist, glistening surface and indistinct edges blending into the substrate.

Numerous tiny, circular, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with slightly raised, well-defined margins and a dull grayish to brownish color, densely clustered and sometimes overlapping, with a granular surface texture.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, medium to dark brown caps, some with frayed or split margins. Gills are crowded and pale tan. Stems are long, thin, fibrous, and brownish, with soil clinging to the base.

Minute, clustered cup-like bodies with pale, translucent discs and distinctly granular, yellowish to golden margins. The surfaces appear smooth and moist, while the edges are textured and minutely fringed.

Cluster of small mushrooms with convex, warm light brown caps. Cap margins are distinctly paler, striate, and fringed, with dry, textured surfaces and visible radiating striations. Caps overlap slightly, and no gills or stems are visible from above.

Clustered mushrooms with convex, dark gray to nearly black caps and slender grayish stems, paler at the base. Gills are pale gray, closely spaced, and attached to the stem. Caps have a smooth, matte surface.

A tiny, pale cream to translucent cup-shaped structure with a smooth, moist inner surface and a thin, slightly wavy margin. The fruiting body appears delicate and shallow, standing out among moss and plant debris.

A rounded, grayish structure densely covered with long, stiff, dark bristle-like hairs radiating outward, creating a spiny, halo-like margin. The surface appears finely textured and compact, with robust hair-like projections giving a distinctive appearance.

Small mushrooms with smooth, moist, light brown to tan convex caps, some nearly flat. Gills are pale cream and closely spaced. Slender, elongated stems are fibrous, whitish-gray at the base, and brownish above. Cap margins are even, lacking striations or veil remnants.

Irregular, contorted fruiting body with pale pinkish to whitish coloration and a dry, rough surface. The structure appears collapsed and convoluted, lacking a distinct cap or stem, with uneven margins and no visible reproductive features.

Pale yellowish to off-white, crust-like layer with a granular, minutely tuberculate surface. The margin is diffuse and fibrous, with visible mycelial threads extending onto the substrate. The fungus forms a continuous, patchy sheet without distinct fruiting bodies.

Slender, pale brown stem supporting a smooth, light brown cap with a slightly darker edge. Underside shows widely spaced, well-defined gills radiating outward in a fan-like pattern. Subtle gradient from light to medium brown across the cap.

A magnified, dark, bulbous structure with a granular texture at the tip of a slender, elongated substrate. Lighter, rounded bodies are visible near the main mass, all sharply contrasted against a pale background.

Diffuse yellowish-orange patches and subtle granular texture are visible along the veins and edges of the green leaf, with scattered small dark spots. The discoloration is patchy and follows the venation, giving the surface a slightly irregular appearance.

Two mushrooms with smooth, convex to nearly flat tan caps. The gills are prominently visible—one set dark brown and closely spaced, the other paler and irregular. Stems are slender, cylindrical, and pale tan, matching or slightly lighter than the caps. Cap margins are smooth and even.

Clustered mushrooms with smooth, pale cream to light tan convex caps featuring a yellowish center. Stems are slender, off-white with brownish stains near the base. Gills are dark brown and closely spaced. Caps appear slightly moist and delicate.

Dark, irregularly textured mass with a compact, crust-like surface. Scattered small, bright yellow, globose fruiting bodies stand out against the uneven, granular background with vertical ridges and embedded debris.

Broad, flattened caps with tan to ochre tones and darker patches, slightly scaly surfaces, and irregular wavy margins. Thick, robust stems are pale with yellowish and brownish discoloration. Gills are pale grayish to lilac, visible on upturned specimens.

Dense cluster of mushrooms with smooth, moist, light brown to orange convex caps, faintly striate margins, closely spaced pale brown gills, and slender fibrous stipes showing darker fibrils and subtle bruising.

Small, bright yellow, gelatinous fruitbodies with a smooth, moist surface and rounded tips. Club-like to tongue-shaped, somewhat translucent, and scattered singly on dark wood. No visible gills or pores.

Two tiny, delicate mushrooms with long, slender, translucent white stems and small, glassy, slightly convex caps. The caps are faintly translucent, showing subtle gills beneath. The overall appearance is fragile and ethereal, with the fruiting bodies spaced apart.

A thin, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, with a granular to crystalline, whitish to pale, powdery texture. The growth is diffuse and patchy, blending seamlessly into the underlying material.

Slender, pale brown stem supporting a small, funnel-shaped tan cap with smooth surface. Gills beneath the cap are white to pale brown and moderately spaced. One specimen is sharply focused, another blurred in the background.

Two small mushrooms with centrally attached slender pale brown stems and smooth, undulating cap margins. The gill surfaces are prominently displayed, radiating, closely spaced, and uniformly light to medium brown with a dry, matte texture.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, dark brown to grayish interiors and paler, slightly fuzzy margins. The cups are circular to oval, closely grouped, and stand out among bright orange discs of another fungus.

A single, tiny, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, pale beige inner surface and a slightly darker, finely textured rim. The surface is matte and even, with no visible ornamentation or internal structures.

Numerous tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with dark brown to grayish-black centers and distinctly pale, whitish margins, scattered and clustered in linear groups. The apothecia are smooth, minute, and have thin, well-defined edges.

Tiny, round, pale yellow to white discs scattered across a dark leaf surface, each with a delicate fringe of fine, hair-like structures around the margin. The fruiting bodies are sessile and disc-shaped, forming loose clusters.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, matte, medium to dark brown upper surfaces and even to slightly undulate margins. Sessile and scattered among green moss, lacking visible stems.

Broad, orange-brown caps with smooth to slightly wavy margins, some with darker patches and soil debris. Stems are thick, yellowish to ochre, with brown streaks and soil at the base. Gills are pale, crowded, and visible on one specimen.

Slender, elongated stem with pale brown and whitish areas, partially obscured by grass. The cap appears as a pale, rounded blur in the foreground, with no clear surface details visible.

A dark, irregular mass densely coated with numerous tiny, bright yellow-orange, globose to slightly elongated structures. The surface is rough, granular, and uneven, with the yellow-orange elements forming a conspicuous clustered layer.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with dark brown, glossy inner surfaces and paler, velvety outer margins. The cups are sessile, with even, slightly rolled edges and a smooth, moist appearance inside, contrasting with a subtly textured exterior.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, brown interiors and paler, velvety margins. The cups are oval to nearly round, sessile, and scattered among moss and plant debris. The outer surface appears minutely hairy, especially at the rim.

Two small, cup-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, slightly granular tan exteriors and darker, smooth interiors. Margins are thin, irregular, and one cup shows a distinct split. Both are sessile on dark soil.
A single, smooth, oval-shaped spore with a light brown to tan hue, sharply outlined against a pale gray background. A black segmented scale bar appears above for size reference.

Tiny, dark, globose fruiting bodies on slender stalks, each densely covered with long, bristly hairs, creating a fuzzy, spiny texture. The surface appears rough and black to very dark brown, with no visible gills or pores. Fruiting bodies are only a few millimeters across.

Medium to large mushrooms with robust, off-white stems and slightly bulbous bases. Caps are broadly convex to flat, ochre to orange-brown with paler margins and a fibrillose texture. Gills are closely spaced, pale grayish to light brown, and attached to the stem.

Small, clustered, yellow gelatinous fruiting bodies with a glossy, translucent surface. Irregularly shaped, some club-like or lobed, grouped tightly along a dark surface. Texture appears smooth and moist, with rounded, undulating margins.

Beige to light brown spore sac with a pointed apex sits atop a star-shaped base formed by several reflexed, cracked rays. The sac is smooth and powdery, while the rays are fibrous and slightly curled downward.

Two robust fruiting bodies with thick, white stems and off-white to pale tan, funnel-shaped caps featuring wavy, irregular margins. The surface appears smooth, and the mushrooms are medium to large in size.

Solitary, upright, club-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, glossy, translucent yellow surface. The texture appears gelatinous and moist, with rounded margins and uniform coloration throughout. Unbranched and distinctly elongated.

Clusters of overlapping, fan-shaped caps in light pink to peach hues with a glossy, moist surface and fine striations along the edges. White, closely spaced gills are visible beneath some caps. Caps vary in size, with smaller ones above and larger below.

A thin, continuous, crust-like layer with a powdery to finely granular surface, predominantly whitish to pale gray, interspersed with darker brown and black patches. The margin is diffuse and irregular, blending gradually into the substrate.

Slender mushrooms with dark gray to black, matte, slightly velvety caps and pale gray gills. Stems are elongated, fibrous, and show a gradient from white at the base to dark gray near the cap, with some soil clinging to the base.

Broad, convex to flat caps with brownish-olive tones and darker streaks, moist and slightly viscid. Gills are pale brownish to gray, moderately crowded, attached to sturdy, pale to light brown stipes with brownish stains. Sectioned specimens show firm, fleshy interiors.

Large, irregular, lobed mass with pale whitish to grayish coloration. Surface is matte, rough, and thick with brownish patches and undulating, convoluted margins. No distinct stem or cap; overall texture appears leathery.

Large, irregular, lobed fruiting body with a dry, cracked, and uneven surface. Colors blend tan, ochre, brown, and grayish tones with darker patches. Margins are curled and irregular, giving a rugged, weathered appearance.

Cluster of mushrooms with pale, silvery-grey conical to convex caps and closely spaced, light gills. Slender, pale stipes emerge from among moss, leaf litter, and twigs at the base of a mossy tree.

Two mushrooms with convex to flat brown caps, dry and patchy surfaces, and striate, irregular margins. One cap is upturned, showing thick, white, frilled gills. Stems are cylindrical, fibrous, and pale brown to whitish.

Numerous tiny, rounded, orange-brown fruiting bodies scattered across a dark, rough surface, with several slender, dark, hair-like projections emerging irregularly from the substrate and fruiting bodies.
Broadly convex cap with a darker brown, slightly depressed center fading to a pale tan, dry and subtly fibrous surface, and an irregular, wavy margin. Stem mostly hidden by grass.

A tightly appressed, crust-like layer with a white to cream convoluted surface, featuring intricate, ruffled folds and ridges. The margin is irregular and undulating, with no distinct cap or stem visible.

Extensive, tightly appressed orange patch with a strikingly wrinkled, brain-like surface. The margin is distinctly white, fuzzy, and cottony, sharply contrasting with the dense, convoluted ridges and folds of the central area.

Sectioned fruiting bodies with convex, brownish caps showing darker mottling, smooth moist surfaces, and slightly inrolled margins. Gills are pale cream, moderately spaced, and attached to robust, pale stipes with soil remnants at the base. Fleshy interior is visible.

Large, cushion-like fruiting body with a whitish to pale gray, velvety or powdery surface. The structure is irregular, somewhat lobed, and has an undulating margin with subtle darker patches and uneven texture.

Convex to irregular pale tan caps with some darker patches, closely spaced pale grayish gills, and robust off-white stems with fibrous texture. One specimen is sectioned, showing the internal structure and uneven, upturned cap margins.

Tiny, bright white, round fruiting bodies densely clustered on a dark leaf surface, each displaying a spiky or hairy texture with radiating marginal hairs. The delicate structures sharply contrast with the substrate, appearing as minute, star-like tufts scattered across the leaf.

Two small mushrooms with slender, light brown stems and smooth, matte caps that are distinctly depressed in the center. The cap margins are slightly paler. Pale, moderately spaced gills are visible beneath one cap. Stems are cylindrical and darker at the base.

Small, brown, cup-shaped bodies with smooth, concave interiors and distinctly granular, whitish outer margins. The fruiting bodies are clustered, with the largest showing a well-defined, rounded edge and fine granulation especially along the rim.

A single, slender stalk supports a rounded, irregular head densely covered in fine, hair-like projections. The structure is darkly silhouetted, with a filamentous or setose texture visible on the head under microscopic view.

A solitary, shallow cup-shaped fungus with a light brown, wrinkled inner surface and a smooth, slightly paler margin. The outer surface matches the inner in color. The cup is open and sessile, lacking a visible stem.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed warm brown caps, smooth to faintly fibrillose surfaces, and even margins. Pale tan to light brown gills radiate from slender, cylindrical, cream to light brown stipes, some with soil at the base.

Two large, irregularly lobed fungal pieces with a pale creamy to yellowish surface, marked by extensive blue-green and rusty brown discolorations. The texture appears matted and felted, with undulating margins and areas of bruising or color change.
A crust-like, off-white to pale cream growth tightly appressed to wood, with a granular to minutely toothed surface and diffuse, irregular margins blending into the substrate.

A thin, widespread, whitish to pale cream layer with a cottony, velvety texture. Loosely interwoven, fibrous hyphal strands form an uneven, patchy surface with diffuse margins blending into the substrate.
Close-up of light to medium brown gills, moderately spaced and slightly wrinkled, radiating from a central slender, fibrous, pale brown stem. The cap is not visible in this view.

A tiny, cup-shaped fruiting body with a vivid orange to reddish-orange disc and a thin, pale whitish margin. The surface appears smooth and slightly gelatinous, nestled in the crevices of decaying wood.
A small, delicate, cup-shaped fungus with a smooth, light brown to tan inner surface and a slightly paler, minutely roughened, undulating margin. The texture appears smooth and somewhat translucent.

A small, irregularly shaped, nearly black mass with a granular, rough surface and indistinct margins blending into the surrounding material. The surface appears lumpy and uneven, with a subtle sheen and minute yellowish rounded elements nearby.

Clustered mushrooms with smooth, dark gray to nearly black convex caps and even, slightly inrolled margins. Gills are densely packed, pale to whitish, and attached to long, slender, grayish stems. Stems are straight, smooth, and match the cap color.

Two mushrooms with smooth, light brown caps—one convex, one slightly depressed—displaying darker, inrolled margins. Pale beige, widely spaced decurrent gills are visible beneath. Stems are long, slender, and match the gill color, with a smooth texture.

Smooth, convex orange-brown caps with paler margins; closely spaced pale grayish-brown gills; slender, pale, slightly fibrous stems. No veil remnants or annulus visible. Caps and stems are even and unstriate.

Small, bright yellow, club-shaped structures with smooth, moist, and slightly translucent surfaces. Fruiting bodies are scattered singly or in small groups, each with a rounded or tapered apex, standing upright on a woody surface.

Slender, elongated stems with small, rounded to broadly convex caps in shades of light brown to tan. Caps appear smooth to slightly striate, with subtle shading variations. Stems are pale, fibrous, and slightly curved. Gills are not visible from this angle.

Irregular, flat orange to ochre patches with a distinctly wrinkled, cerebriform surface and a broad, cottony white margin. The texture appears dry and fibrous at the edges, with fuzzy borders surrounding the vivid center. Patches are tightly appressed and confluent.

Two small, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with pale brown to tan, finely granular surfaces. The margins are distinctly fringed with long, dark, hair-like structures, giving a fuzzy appearance. The fruiting bodies are closely attached and gregarious.

Medium-sized mushrooms with convex to broadly convex caps, darker brown central discs, and lighter tan margins. Cap surfaces are smooth with subtle radial fibrils and occasional margin splitting. Gills are pale, moderately spaced, and attached to robust, white stipes with brownish bases.

Small, pale, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, light interiors and thin, slightly darker margins are scattered among moss and plant debris. Bright orange, spherical clusters are also present nearby.

Small mushrooms with dark gray to nearly black, smooth, rounded to conical caps, pale closely spaced gills, and long, slender bluish-gray fibrous stems. Caps show subtle striations and slightly wavy edges.

A small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, light tan to beige surface and a thin, slightly undulating margin. The texture appears moist and gelatinous, with an even, delicate edge and no visible fuzziness.

Delicate, translucent white mushrooms with long, slender stems and tiny, umbrella-shaped caps. The caps are thin, almost membranous, with slightly wavy or irregular edges. Fruiting bodies appear clustered and fragile.

Dense, cottony to felt-like surface with pale cream to light brown coloration. Texture is fibrous and granular, featuring numerous small, tufted projections that create a rough, uneven appearance. The margin is irregular and merges gradually with the substrate.

Brown, irregularly rounded fruiting body with a granular, rough surface. The base blends into the substrate, and no distinct stem or margin is visible. The overall appearance is somewhat blurred and solitary.
