Convex to slightly depressed caps with brownish to grayish-brown, matte surfaces. Cap margins are smooth and entire. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to light tan, and decurrent onto short, pale stems. No visible latex exudation.

Numerous small, rounded to irregular orange apothecia with pale, well-defined margins densely cover the cracked, pale bark. The patches are tightly appressed, with a whitish border visible at the edges. Surfaces are smooth and apothecia often cluster or merge.

Dense, white to pale, powdery mat with a fuzzy, granular texture. Small, round, slightly raised darker spots with radiating appendages are scattered across the surface, forming patchy but continuous coverage.
A thin, smooth, tightly adherent crust with a pale grayish to whitish color and subtle sheen. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the wood, and the surface is even and unbroken.

Small, white, fan-shaped fruiting bodies with a velvety outer surface and prominent, radiating gills. The caps are laterally attached, lacking visible stipes, and have even, unlobed margins. The surface appears finely hairy and delicate.

Convex to slightly flattened caps with light brown to grayish tones and subtle zonation. Gills are distinctly purplish to lilac, thick stems are white and robust, often with soil clinging to the base. Caps appear smooth to slightly fibrillose.

Small, thin-walled, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth ochre to light brown inner surfaces and slightly paler, minutely roughened, irregular margins. Arranged in small groups, the cups contrast with the dark substrate and scattered green moss.

Smooth, reddish-brown, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with pale, slightly wavy margins. The surface appears shiny and moist, with no visible stem, and the cups are clustered among dark debris and conifer needles.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, dry, fibrous caps in muted brown to purplish-brown. Stems are robust, pale with brownish or purplish tinges, and covered in soil. One specimen is cut to show pale internal tissue and faint purplish hues beneath the cap.

Two mushrooms with grayish-brown, finely textured caps; one shows crowded, decurrent, cream to pale yellow gills with a slightly undulating pattern. The cap surface is dry with subtle radial fibrils and a darker center.

A swollen, gall-like structure distorts the leaf, showing purplish to brown discoloration with a cracked, ruptured surface and rough, irregular margins. The surrounding leaf tissue remains green and healthy.

Dense aggregation of small, oval to polygonal, dark brown to reddish-brown structures with lighter, reticulate boundaries forming a honeycomb-like pattern. Surface appears slightly rough and granular. A prominent jagged vertical crack runs along the right side.

Irregular, angular patches of dark brown to nearly black tissue with leathery, cracked surfaces and distinctly uplifted, roughened margins. The patches are flattened, scattered, and closely adhere to the bark, creating a rugged, overlapping appearance.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, pinkish-red caps featuring faintly striate margins. The cap surface is smooth with subtle radial texture. White, closely spaced gills and robust, cylindrical white stipes are visible.

Two mushrooms with broadly convex to slightly depressed caps, reddish-brown with faint zonation and striate, wavy margins. White, closely spaced gills and robust, smooth white stipes are visible. The cap surface appears smooth and unblemished.

Thin, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the surface, pale cream to off-white with scattered pinkish and orange patches. Texture appears finely granular to powdery, with diffuse, matted margins blending into the substrate.

Bright white, nearly circular cap with a slight heart-shaped indentation at the base. Surface is densely velvety, especially along the fringed margin. Prominent radiating ridges create a fan-like pattern across the cap.

Cracked, creamy white to light gray surface densely covered with rounded, reddish-brown, slightly raised patches. The rough, areolate texture and matte apothecia create a striking mottled pattern across the tightly adherent crust.

Brown surface with a distinct honeycomb-like, netted pattern of polygonal, plate-like segments. A prominent longitudinal crack reveals a lighter interior. The texture appears dry and brittle, with fine, thread-like structures scattered across the surface.

A small, solitary, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth ochre interior and similarly colored exterior. The margin is distinctly paler, thin, and slightly scalloped, with a wide open hollow structure.

Delicate, small, pure white mushrooms with convex to nearly flat caps, fine powdery texture, and slender white stems. Gills are widely spaced and radiate from the stem. Some caps show a subtle central depression. Fruiting bodies range from globose immature forms to fully expanded caps.

Pale whitish to light gray, crustose patches with rough, cracked surfaces. Each patch features prominent, angular to rounded blackish structures slightly raised above the surface, surrounded by paler, cracked margins. The thalli are tightly grouped, forming a patchwork appearance.
Dense, irregular orange-brown mass with a moist, granular surface composed of tightly packed, small rounded structures, spreading across plant debris and moss.
Green, pinnately lobed leaves with some pale discoloration and minor browning at the edges. The leaf surfaces appear smooth, and no visible fungal structures or spore masses are present.

Dark, nearly blackish-brown upper surface with a distinct net-like texture. The lower region is tan to light brown, fibrous, and woody, with an irregular, eroded margin and a firm, crust-like appearance.

A sliced mushroom showing a smooth, brown to muted violet-brown cap with a slightly incurved margin. The gills are closely spaced, pale tan to beige, and regular. The cross-section reveals a firm, off-white to cream interior.

Irregularly rounded, pale off-white to light gray crusts with rough, cracked surfaces. Each thallus has a prominent, darkly outlined central opening surrounded by scattered dark speckles. Margins are uneven and slightly lobed, with thalli closely grouped but not overlapping.

Crustose thallus tightly attached to bark, with numerous small, rounded to polygonal, bright orange apothecia surrounded by pale margins. The grayish, cracked surface contrasts with the vivid apothecia, following the bark’s rough contours.

Convex brown cap with a slightly inrolled margin, smooth surface, and pale, closely spaced gills. The robust, cylindrical stem transitions from pale at the base to brownish near the cap, with soil and moss clinging to the base.

A cut section of a small to medium mushroom with a brownish, smooth cap margin and closely spaced, pale to light brown gills. The off-white to pale brown stem appears solid. The gill attachment and spacing are clearly visible.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with slender, slightly curved white stems and rounded caps densely coated in fine, powdery white scales. The gills are white, free, and radiate clearly from the stem on the upturned specimen. The overall texture appears fragile and almost translucent.

Small, white, fan-shaped fruiting bodies arranged vertically on a branch. Caps are flat to slightly convex with smooth surfaces. Gills are visible underneath, radiating outward from the point of attachment. No stem is present; fungi appear sessile.

Cluster of mushrooms with broad, pale cream to light tan caps, some with brownish patches and adhering soil. Caps are smooth with slightly inrolled margins. Thick, robust white stems show brownish discoloration, and closely spaced pale gills are visible on upturned caps.

Dense, white, powdery growth covers the green surface, forming a fuzzy mat of fine, filamentous hyphae. Some darker, thread-like structures are interspersed, creating a patchy but extensive appearance without distinct margins or visible fruiting bodies.

Numerous small, upright, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, light brown to ochre interiors and distinctly paler, cream-colored thin margins. Some cups have irregular or chipped edges. The cups are sessile and scattered among pine needles and bark fragments.

Irregular, dark brown to blackish patches closely appressed to decaying wood, with a matte, granular surface. The margins are diffuse, blending into the substrate, and the bodies vary from rounded to elongated, lacking visible stalks or distinct structures.

Crustose thallus with a pale gray to whitish, granular surface, densely dotted with numerous small to medium, bright orange, rounded apothecia. The apothecia are scattered or clustered, with flat to slightly convex discs and well-defined margins, contrasting sharply against the pale background.

Irregular, crust-like patches with pale grayish to light brown color, rough and granular surface, pitted texture, and undulating, scalloped margins. Compact and closely adherent to the underlying material.

Close-up of a brown, finely granular interior with prominent vertical ridges and partitions. The upper edge is darker and compact, while the lower area is loose and powdery. The structure is minute, with intricate, layered organization visible at millimeter scale.

Smooth, white to off-white caps with moist, slightly sticky surfaces; broadly convex to nearly flat with undulating margins. White, broad, decurrent gills run down robust, cylindrical stems. Stems are solid, white, and slightly tapering, with some adhering soil.

Two robust mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, pale cream to light brown caps, some brownish center tints, and dry surfaces. Stems are thick, white, and feature a distinct brownish ring. Gills are closely spaced and pale brown. Soil clings to the stem bases.

A green leaf surface densely coated with a fine, white, powdery layer. The coating appears granular and dusty, unevenly distributed, and contrasts sharply with the underlying green tissue. No distinct fruiting bodies or structures are visible.

Small, densely clustered, fan-shaped caps with white to cream coloration. Prominent, closely spaced gills radiate across the entire underside. Caps have smooth to finely hairy surfaces and slightly wavy margins. No visible stems; attachment is lateral.

Two robust mushrooms with large, pale tan to off-white convex caps, some brownish discoloration, and irregular margins. The thick, cylindrical stipes are pale yellowish-tan with fine brown reticulation. Olive-brown pore surfaces are visible beneath the caps.
A small, brown, rounded fruitbody with a slightly convex, finely textured, velvety surface and smooth margin, centrally attached by a short stem to the branch.

Large, irregular red cap with pale patches and a moist, textured surface. Thick red stipe shows yellowish-brown discolorations and faint net-like pattern. Exposed pore surface is yellowish, bruising blue-green where damaged.

Irregular, elongated, and coalescing vivid yellow-orange powdery patches with granular texture, forming dense, spore-laden pustules on the green leaf surface. Margins are diffuse and the distribution is uneven, with some larger aggregations visible.
Numerous tiny, round, brown to reddish-brown fruiting bodies densely scattered, some with a slightly roughened surface, on a pale, fibrous, moist background with visible plant debris.

Bright yellow-orange, disc-shaped caps with a moist, translucent surface and central dimples, each atop a slender, dark stem emerging from glossy, waterlogged wood. Fruiting bodies are scattered and spaced apart.

Small, yellowish-orange, elongated and irregularly shaped patches clustered on a green leaf surface. The structures are slightly raised, granular, and powdery, forming a linear arrangement with vivid contrast against the leaf.

Cluster of cup-shaped fruiting bodies with undulating, lobed, and folded margins. Upper surfaces are light to ochre-brown, smooth, and moist with a gelatinous sheen. Lower surfaces appear slightly darker. The fungus is laterally attached to a woody branch.

Numerous tiny, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies, yellowish to light brown, semi-translucent, and smooth-surfaced, are clustered together on a dark, moist background. Margins are entire and not lobed.

Striking blue mushroom with a smooth, pale blue cap and darker blue, closely spaced decurrent gills. The robust, cylindrical stem is blue with lighter patches and a slightly fibrous texture. Cap margin is slightly inrolled.

Tiny, white to off-white, cup-shaped structures with distinctly hairy margins are scattered loosely across a brown, textured surface. The fruiting bodies are circular, dry, and appear slightly fuzzy due to the conspicuous marginal hairs.
Numerous tiny, pale cream cup-shaped structures with slightly translucent, velvety surfaces and distinct, raised fuzzy margins, densely clustered together in a close-up view.

Crust-like, patchy growth with a granular to powdery surface, predominantly white with purplish-violet areas. The layer is irregular, slightly raised, and uneven, lacking distinct caps or margins, and appears densely concentrated in some spots.
Tiny, rounded, dark brown to black structures with rough, granular surfaces scattered across a green, granular background. The margins are indistinct, blending into the surrounding tissue.

Slender mushrooms with elongated, pale stems and convex to flat caps showing light brown to grayish tones with darker centers. Cap margins are uneven or wavy. Gills beneath are closely spaced and pale to grayish. Sizes range from 3 to 7 centimeters.

Densely packed, granular green to yellow-green surface with scattered small, cup-like brownish structures and uneven, crusty texture. The arrangement is compact, with fine and coarse textures blending together across the surface.

Green, healthy leaves with smooth margins and lanceolate to oblong shapes scattered among grasses. Surfaces appear smooth and glossy in sunlight, with no visible fungal fruiting bodies, lesions, or discoloration.

Medium brown cap with a slightly darker center, conical to convex shape, and wavy margin. Smooth cap surface. Pale tan to light brown gills beneath. Slender, elongated, light brown stem with some soil and mycelial threads at the base.

Thick, robust yellowish stipe with brownish reticulation and scattered darker spots, slightly rough and fibrous surface. Lower cap margin shows yellowish-brown pore surface with small, tightly packed pores. Cap edge appears velvety.

Solitary, delicate cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, translucent yellowish-brown surface. The margin is even and slightly undulating. The slender stem is dark brown to nearly black, tapering where it attaches to the wood.

Leaf surface shows numerous small, dark, irregular spots scattered across yellowed, chlorotic areas near the margin. Spots are slightly raised, disrupting the leaf’s texture, with some coalescing into larger necrotic patches.

Numerous small, round to irregular black spots densely scattered across a green leaf, with some yellowing visible around the affected areas. No prominent fruiting bodies or raised structures are apparent.

A single mushroom with striking blue, closely spaced gills radiating from a pale blue, smooth stipe. The gills show a gradient from deep blue at the edge to lighter blue near the center. The cap surface is not visible.

Viewed from below, the mushroom displays closely spaced, pale brown gills radiating from a slender, smooth, pale stipe. The cap margin is even and slightly incurved, with a light brown to tan coloration and a smooth texture.

Tiny, yellowish-orange, rounded to disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, moist surfaces and slender pale stalks are scattered along a wet, dark brown branch. The caps are even-margined and unlobed, standing out against the damp wood.

Numerous tiny, dark brown to nearly black, roughly spherical to slightly flattened fruiting bodies with a granular surface are scattered and clustered on a yellowish-white, fibrous background. The structures are sessile, lacking visible stalks or margins.

Numerous tiny, pale beige to light tan, cup-shaped structures densely clustered on a brown decaying stem. Each cup has a smooth, slightly raised margin and a central disc, forming irregular groups along the surface. The texture appears smooth and minute under magnification.

Small, slender, club-shaped fruiting bodies with a smooth, moist surface and yellowish to pale orange color, emerging upright from wet, dark brown bark. No distinct cap or gills are visible. Fruiting bodies are scattered along the branch.

Two slender mushrooms with light brown, fibrous-textured caps—one convex, one showing crowded pale brown gills—on thin, pale stems with soil at the base. Caps are slightly darker than stems, and margins are even. Each specimen is about 5 cm long.

Dense mat of minute, globose to subglobose granules with a beaded, rough texture. Predominantly dark reddish-brown with scattered lighter and whitish patches. Surface appears moist and uneven, lacking distinct margins in this close-up view.

A broad yellowish-green leaf covered with numerous small, dark brown to black spots, some merging into larger blotches. The leaf margin is slightly wavy, and the surface appears roughened and chlorotic around the spots.

Numerous small, dark, roughly circular to irregular spots cluster across a green surface, each slightly raised with a granular texture. The background shows green and yellowish tones with faint reddish discoloration near the dark fungal groupings.

A minute, dark brown to nearly black, irregularly shaped spot with diffuse, slightly raised edges and indistinct margins on a yellowish-green surface. The central area is darker, highlighted by a white arrow, and the structure is less than 0.5 mm in diameter.

Numerous tiny, dark spherical bodies with radiating, stiff, hair-like appendages scattered across a pale, granular green surface. The spheres vary slightly in size and appendage length, appearing embedded or resting on the surface.

Moist, brownish surface densely dotted with numerous small, dark, circular fruiting bodies. The texture is granular and uneven, with a glossy sheen and closely packed, slightly raised speckles scattered across the substrate.

Irregular, black, fuzzy patches spread across the wood surface, appearing velvety to hairy and matted. The growth is patchy, with indistinct margins that blend gradually into the substrate, lacking sharply defined edges or visible fruiting bodies.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a light to medium brown, finely velvety exterior and uneven, scalloped margin. The interior is smooth and paler. Short, dark central stem attaches it to the substrate.

Pale, rounded, slightly raised swellings are visible along the smooth green stem, contrasting with the healthy tissue. The swellings appear opaque and firm, with no distinct external fungal structures present.

Numerous tiny, pale gray to whitish, disc-shaped structures are scattered irregularly along a brown woody stem. The discs are slightly raised, smooth, rounded, and have a somewhat translucent or waxy appearance.

A solitary mushroom with a striking blue cap, faint concentric zones, and a slightly inrolled margin. The robust, cylindrical stipe and decurrent gills share the same blue hue, with subtle mottling visible on the stem.
A vibrant green leaf with a prominent central vein, slightly curled and pointed margins, and a smooth, healthy surface. No visible fungal structures or lesions are apparent in this close-up view.

Leaf surface shows multiple irregular, dark brown to black necrotic spots with yellowish halos. Lesions are scattered, vary in size, and some coalesce. Affected areas appear slightly sunken and discolored, with diffuse margins.

Numerous tiny, white to off-white, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and slightly translucent appearance. Each has a circular to irregular margin, some edged with fine, hair-like structures, and are scattered singly across the substrate.
Small, irregularly lobed fruiting body with undulate margins, granular and crustose surface. Mottled purplish, brown, and greenish tones, covered in a powdery or mycelial coating.
Smooth green leaf with a prominent central vein, showing faint pale linear discolorations and a single irregular hole. No visible fungal fruiting bodies or surface growths are present.

Numerous small, scattered yellow-orange to ochre pustules and powdery deposits on the leaf surface, some merging into larger irregular patches. The pustules are raised and granular, with slight discoloration of the surrounding leaf tissue.
Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, light brown to tan surfaces and thin, even margins. The cups are slightly shiny and attached laterally in a scattered arrangement along a woody branch.

Cluster of slender mushrooms with tan to brownish, moist, convex to slightly depressed caps featuring paler margins. Gills are closely spaced and pale, while stems are elongated and match the cap margin in color. Caps appear smooth and slightly sticky.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, rounded spots scattered irregularly across a greenish-brown, granular surface. The spots are slightly raised and vary in size, forming distinct punctuations against the lighter background.

Broad, pale blue cap with a slightly depressed center and smooth, inrolled margin. Cap surface is matte with faint concentric blue zones. Cylindrical stem matches cap color, showing darker blue speckling. Gills are blue and decurrent.

Small, nearly circular disc with a light to medium brown, finely velvety upper surface. The margin is slightly raised and paler, forming a distinct border. No gills or stipe are visible; the fruitbody is sessile and attached directly to the wood.

Single medium-sized mushroom with a convex, yellowish-brown, uneven cap. Crowded pale brown gills are visible beneath. The robust, pale stem shows brownish discoloration and soil clings to its base. Surface appears dry and slightly fibrillose.

Small, bright orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly glossy surfaces and flat to slightly depressed centers, closely grouped on a dark, wet substrate. Their vivid color stands out against the reflective background.

Numerous small, bright yellow-orange, cup- to disc-shaped fruiting bodies with slender pale stalks are scattered along dark, water-soaked branches. The vivid, smooth surfaces of the apothecia stand out sharply against the wood and green moss.

Medium-sized mushrooms with brown, slightly scaly caps showing darker centers and faint zonation. Gills are brown and closely spaced. Stems are pale with brown streaks, some showing veil remnants and soil at the base. Caps and stems display a fibrous texture.

A cluster of slender, upright, bright orange to reddish-orange cylindrical fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and slightly irregular, pointed tips, emerging closely together from a decaying brown leaf.

Numerous small, scattered, orange-brown pustules are slightly raised on the smooth green leaf surface. The pustules are irregularly distributed, creating a patchy appearance that contrasts with the surrounding healthy green tissue.
Tiny, round, orange-red pustules scattered and slightly raised on a smooth green leaf surface, some clustered and others isolated, standing out vividly against the background.

Small fungi with slender, translucent to whitish stems topped by smooth, bright yellow to orange, disc-shaped caps. The fruiting bodies are clustered together, their glossy stems and caps standing out against the dark, wet background.

A single mushroom with a pale, slender stem and a convex cap viewed from below. The light tan gills are well-spaced and prominently defined, with a smooth cap margin. Surrounded by moss and small green plants.

Green, pinnately lobed leaves display numerous small, dark brown to black circular spots scattered across the surface, with some yellowing or necrosis surrounding the lesions. No visible fruiting bodies or fungal growth clusters are present.
Small, white, irregularly shaped and slightly globular structures scattered along the midrib of a fresh green leaf, appearing slightly raised above the surface.

Irregular, crust-like growth with a granular to powdery texture. Surface shows rusty orange, yellow, brown, and purplish patches, with fine whitish crystalline granules scattered throughout. Margins are diffuse and blend into the substrate, lacking distinct fruitbodies.
Greenish, rounded, overlapping lobes with a smooth to slightly granular surface, scattered with numerous minute, black, dot-like structures irregularly distributed across the surface.
Numerous tiny, rounded to slightly irregular pale cream fruiting bodies with smooth, somewhat translucent surfaces and subtly raised margins, scattered and sometimes clustered on a dark background.

Dark, nearly black, globose to irregular sclerotia with a firm, compact, matte to faintly lustrous surface. Margins are well-defined, and the surface is dotted with adherent soil particles. Sclerotia are closely grouped and partially buried among mineral grains.
Elongated, pale green to whitish, smooth cylindrical structure lying horizontally across the frame, with a glossy surface and no visible fuzz or ornamentation.

Small, black, roughly spherical to irregular structures with a matte, slightly rough surface, scattered and partially embedded among green moss and organic debris. The compact bodies blend subtly with the surrounding material, lacking visible fruiting structures.

Numerous small, dark, nearly black circular spots with diffuse yellowish-green halos are scattered across the smooth green leaf surface. The spots are slightly sunken, irregularly rounded, and do not merge, with visible leaf veins in the background.

Elongated, diffuse yellow-orange streaks and irregular patches are scattered across the green leaf surface, forming linear to blotchy discolorations without sharply defined margins. No distinct fruiting bodies or pustules are visible.

Small mushrooms with slender, pale, slightly curved stems and brown, convex to flat caps showing a faintly scaly texture. Gills underneath are crowded and light brown. Caps measure about 1–2 cm wide. Soil clings to the stem bases.

Two small, nearly black, irregularly rounded bodies with hard, compact texture and rough surfaces marked by distinct fissures. Both appear dense and carbonaceous, with no visible reproductive structures, set against a plain white background.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a rounded, upright margin. The outer surface is yellowish-brown, moist, and slightly translucent, with a subtly wrinkled texture and uneven edge. Delicate appearance on bark-covered wood.

Two tiny, bright orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, glistening surfaces and slender brownish stems stand upright on moist, dark wood. The cups have slightly irregular margins and delicate proportions, each only a few millimeters wide.

Three small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, smooth, matte brown caps. Stems are slender, pale brown, and slightly fibrous. Gills are pale beige to light brown and moderately crowded. No ring or volva is visible.
Numerous minute, pale to light brown, granular or wart-like spots are scattered irregularly along the roughened surface of a dried plant stem.

Green leaf surface densely covered with small, dark, irregularly shaped, slightly raised spots. Some spots coalesce into larger patches, with diffuse margins and surrounding yellowed tissue. The overall texture is smooth except for the raised lesions.

A single mushroom with a broadly convex, pale beige cap featuring a darker, moist, and shiny center. The cap surface is smooth and slightly sticky, with an even margin. A slender, pale stem supports the cap above green moss.
No visible fungal structures are present; only broad, lance-shaped green leaves with minor spotting and discoloration are seen.

Two robust mushrooms with convex tan to ochre-brown caps, thick pale stems, and yellow pores. The cut surfaces and pores display a vivid blue staining reaction, and the stems show a subtle net-like texture.

Clustered, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, moist, brown surfaces and slightly undulating margins. The texture appears gelatinous to leathery, and the cups are attached laterally, overlapping each other on the wood.

A single, black, roughly oval sclerotium with a matte, slightly roughened surface. It is partially embedded among green mosses, appearing firm, compact, and with an irregular outline. No visible reproductive structures are present.
A minute, compact, dark, and irregularly shaped mass embedded within fragmented, fibrous brown wood. The sclerotium measures less than 1.5 mm across and contrasts with the lighter substrate.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a moist, light to medium brown cap. The thin margin is slightly translucent, showing subtle radial striations. The surface is smooth and the fungus is attached laterally, appearing sessile without a visible stem.

A dense, white, powdery layer covers the upper surfaces of several oval leaves, giving them a frosted appearance and obscuring their natural green color. Some leaf edges show slight discoloration and curling.

Two small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth tan to ochre inner surfaces and slightly darker, minutely hairy margins. The cups are sessile, closely clustered, and emerge directly from the bark, with a subtle velvety texture on the outer edge.

Small, black, roughly spherical to oval fruiting bodies with a granular surface, scattered or loosely grouped on a pale wood surface. The margins are entire and slightly raised above the substrate, creating a distinct contrast.

Numerous tiny, dark gray to black, cup-shaped structures with distinct rims and central depressions are scattered across the woody, fibrous surface. The fruiting bodies are minute, circular to slightly oval, and often clustered.
Small mushroom with a circular cap, beige to light brown margin, and a distinctly darker, moist-looking center. The cap surface is smooth and slightly shiny, with an even, unlobed edge.

A single, tiny, broadly rounded cap about 8.3 mm wide, light to medium brown with a smooth to subtly granular surface, faintly darker edge, semi-translucent margin, and finely textured base attached directly to the surface.
A close-up of a broad, crinkled green leaf with prominent veins and smooth, pale stems. The leaf surface appears healthy, undamaged, and free of visible growths or discoloration.

Small, shallow cup-shaped fruiting bodies with a yellowish-orange, smooth, and slightly translucent surface. The margin is thin and slightly raised, and the glossy apothecia are attached directly to dark, rough wood.

Numerous tiny, dark brown to blackish, disc-shaped fruiting bodies densely scattered and slightly raised on a moist, fibrous surface. The fruiting bodies are smooth to subtly textured, sessile, and closely grouped, with no visible stalks.

Numerous tiny, pale to off-white, disc-shaped to shallowly cup-like fruiting bodies densely cover a dark brown stem. The smooth, regular margins and slightly translucent appearance make them stand out against the substrate. The apothecia are closely packed and sometimes overlap.

Numerous tiny, dark, round disc-like structures are scattered across the surface of a decaying stem. The fruiting bodies are flat to slightly convex, smooth, and have subtle pale margins, blending into the substrate.

Numerous small, dark brown to nearly black, round to slightly flattened fruiting bodies with a minutely roughened surface are scattered and embedded among fibrous plant material. The fruiting bodies are sessile, discrete, and uniform in size, forming a scattered to loosely grouped pattern.

Two slender mushrooms with elongated, pale stems and small, convex to slightly umbonate caps. The caps are pale brown with a fibrous texture. Gills are crowded and attached, visible on the upturned specimen. Soil clings to the stem bases.

Elongated, orange, powdery and slightly raised spots scattered along the green leaf, forming irregular patches parallel to the veins. The pustules have a granular texture and contrast sharply with the smooth leaf surface.

Small, cup-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, light to medium brown exterior and paler inner surface. Margins are finely hairy, and the surface appears slightly translucent and moist. Fruitbodies are sessile or have very short stems, attached directly to the substrate.
Numerous small, circular to irregular yellow-orange pustules scattered across a green leaf, with a prominent, powdery, granular mass forming a dense cluster among flatter, diffuse spots.

Highly magnified view showing a rough, crustose surface with irregular, labyrinthine cavities and channels. Colors range from dark brown to black with lighter whitish areas and a moist, slightly reflective greenish zone. Texture appears uneven and granular, with diffuse, irregular margins.

Convex to slightly flattened light brown caps with paler, irregular patches; smooth to slightly fibrous surface. Robust, pale stipes with soil at the base. Brown gills visible on one specimen. Group includes both mature and younger fruiting bodies.

A small, irregularly rounded structure with a rough, granular surface. Predominantly brown with darker, almost black patches and minute, wart-like projections. The surface appears compact and crustose, lacking a visible stem or cap.

Small, dome-shaped fruiting bodies with pale beige to light brown coloring, scattered darker brown spots, and smooth, rounded margins. Surfaces show white granules and a slightly granular or warted texture. Fruiting bodies are irregularly lobed and closely attached in clusters.

Small, dark, oval to irregular rounded structure with a granular, roughened surface and a central depression. The surface is mostly dark brown to blackish, with lighter reddish-brown granules scattered on top. Margins are indistinct and blend into the background.

Moist, light brown surface scattered with numerous small, black, globose to ovoid structures. These shiny, smooth, slightly raised bodies are irregularly distributed across the granular, wet substrate. No fuzzy mycelium is visible.

Small, circular fruiting bodies with grayish to bluish centers, each bordered by a distinct white ring and a conspicuously hairy, fuzzy outer margin, scattered irregularly across a dark, rough surface.

Small, brown, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly flared margins and a matte to subtly velvety texture. The cups are sessile to short-stalked and upright, scattered among dead stems and green moss.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed caps, grayish-brown with darker centers and paler, wavy margins. The cap surface is smooth with faint radial streaks. Gills are closely spaced and pale grayish-brown. Stipe is slender, pale grayish-white, and slightly fibrous.

Minute, round to slightly oval white fruiting bodies with smooth, moist, glistening surfaces. They are sessile, clustered loosely, and have even, well-defined margins, standing out delicately against a heterogeneous background.
Irregular, partially broken cap with a moist, smooth grayish-brown surface. The margin is frilled and uneven, exposing pale, off-white gills beneath. The stipe is not visible.

Highly magnified view showing a dark, crusty, and irregular surface with numerous porous cavities and channels. The texture is granular and uneven, featuring a mix of brown, black, and white tones with lighter internal areas exposed.

Highly magnified view showing a rough, dark brown to black surface with a prominent cavity. The cavity margin is lined with a white, fuzzy or crystalline border, and the interior displays irregular, convoluted, lighter structures. Texture appears coarse and compact.

A single, delicate fungus with a slender, reddish-brown, slightly curved stalk topped by a small, globose, pale brown sporangium. The sporangium surface is granular and rough, with a crystalline, glistening appearance.

Small, dark brown to nearly black, hemispherical fruiting bodies with rough, uneven surfaces and central pale depressions. Some display yellowish patches and are scattered in clusters on a moist, decomposed surface.

Highly magnified view showing a central greenish, granular area with a crystalline sheen, bordered by rough, uneven brown and gray surfaces. Irregular margins and intricate textures are visible, with both smooth and bumpy regions highlighted.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to flat, moist, grayish to pale brown caps showing subtle zonation. Cap margins are smooth. Stems are slender and pale. Exposed gills are pale cream and closely spaced, attached to the stem. Surfaces appear slightly translucent.

A single, minute, golden-yellow spherical fruiting body with a delicate net-like surface, perched atop a slender, dark stalk. The textured sphere is less than 0.5 mm in diameter and distinctly elevated above the substrate.

Irregular, undulating caps with mottled pale tan, cream, and dark brown patches. Cap surfaces appear moist and slightly fibrous, with some weathered or damaged areas. Pale to light brown, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps. Clustered among grass and clover.

Numerous tiny, black, dot-like fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across the rough bark of a fallen trunk. The fruiting bodies are minute, slightly raised, and embedded, blending subtly with the bark’s surface.

Dark, crust-like structure with a rough, uneven margin and granular blackish-brown surface. A prominent cavity is lined with white, powdery or cottony material, contrasting sharply with the rugged, irregular exterior.

Numerous small, nearly black, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered across a pale, striated stem surface. The fruiting bodies are discrete, well-defined, and sharply contrast with the substrate.

Tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a slightly granular surface are spaced along a slender, dry brown stem. The structures are shallow and delicate, standing out against the darker background.

Two mushrooms with white to pale cream, closely spaced gills on the underside of their caps. The gills show subtle brownish tinges near the stem attachment. Stems are slender, pale brown, and moderately long. Only the underside is visible.

Tiny, spherical fruiting bodies with a yellowish to light brown hue, each perched atop a slender, dark stalk. The surface of the spheres appears net-like and perforated, giving a delicate, reticulate texture. Fruiting bodies are scattered and well-separated.

Irregular, crust-like patches tightly adhere to the surface, displaying a granular to powdery texture. The coloration is predominantly dark brown to blackish with scattered pale, whitish areas. Minute dark specks are visible, lacking any distinct stem or cap.

Numerous tiny, pale whitish to translucent disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across the surface, each with a smooth, matte texture and even margins. The delicate, fragile discs are directly attached to the substrate without visible stems.
A tiny, shallow cup-shaped fruiting body with a pinkish-white, minutely granular surface and a slightly raised pale margin, perched solitarily on a striated, speckled stem.
Numerous tiny, white, spherical structures with a powdery appearance are scattered across rough brown wood, interspersed with fine, black, hair-like threads emerging from the substrate.

A single, minute, nearly spherical to slightly flattened disc with a soft, velvety texture. The center is pale pinkish-peach, surrounded by a subtly lighter, smooth, off-white to beige margin. The surface appears finely granular.

Slender, elongated fruiting body with a smooth, moist brown surface, curving gently. One end forms a distinct cup-shaped hollow, while the other tapers to a thin point. Greenish material adheres along the surface.

Numerous tiny, dark, nearly black, rounded to slightly irregular discs scattered across a pale, fibrous, ridged surface. The fruiting bodies are matte, sessile, and distributed singly or in loose groups.

A single, translucent, globose structure perched on a slender stalk, with a smooth, glassy surface and delicate net-like patterning. Darkened patches are visible within the sphere, which stands out against a dark, blurred background.

A single, delicate sporocarp with a globose, pale ochre cap densely dotted with dark brown spots, supported by a slender reddish-brown stalk. The cap surface appears finely textured and moist, standing erect above the substrate.

Small, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies closely grouped on wood, medium to dark brown with a distinctly granular, bumpy surface. Margins are uneven, and the moist surface gives a glistening appearance.

A single, upright, delicate fruiting body with a slender dark stalk supporting a small, spherical head. The head is yellowish-brown and finely granular or reticulate in texture, standing out sharply against the blurred background.
A thin, white, crust-like layer tightly adheres to the surface, with a finely granular to minutely web-like texture and indistinct, patchy margins blending into the substrate.
A pale, woody twig with smooth surface, bearing several brown, ovoid to conical, bud-like structures at the tip and along the stem. No distinct fungal fruiting bodies are visible.

Highly magnified, rough, powdery surface with irregular, labyrinth-like cavities and ridges. Predominantly brown with lighter, whitish areas. Crustose, compact, and uneven, lacking any distinct stem or cap. Margins are irregular and blend into the surrounding material.
A tiny, pale pink, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, delicate surface and an even, slightly upturned margin, attached to a slender, speckled stem.

Irregular, spreading patches with a grayish to whitish, granular and powdery surface. The tissue appears crust-like, blending indistinctly into the substrate, with no visible stems, caps, or distinct fruiting bodies.

Longitudinal section of a curved fruiting body with a yellowish, fleshy interior, brownish outer surface, and pale gill structure at one end. The cut surface appears fibrous, and the margin of the cap is smooth.

Highly magnified view showing a rough, crustose surface with irregular, labyrinthine cavities and channels. The coloration is mottled brown, gray, and white, with darker regions. Margins are uneven and eroded, and the texture varies from smooth to granular.

Minute, white, cottony or granular tufts scattered across a brown surface, interspersed with fine, dark, hair-like filaments. The white structures are small and irregular, contrasting sharply with the substrate and the dark, thread-like elements.

Mushroom with a strongly curved, thick white stem showing yellowish-brown discoloration and soil at the base. Cap is broadly convex, yellow to orange, smooth and matte. Gills are closely spaced, thin, and pinkish-brown.

Convex to irregular cap with a pale, slightly wavy margin and subtle pinkish-brown hues. Gills are closely spaced, pale with a faint violet tint. The robust stem is mottled with darker and lighter patches, and both cap and stem appear smooth.

Highly magnified, uneven surface with a mix of white, brown, and black coloration. The texture is rough and granular, featuring scattered white patches and diffuse, irregular margins. No distinct fruiting bodies or horn-like projections are visible at this scale.
Broadly convex cap with a smooth, moist surface, grayish-brown in color with lighter whitish patches near the margin and a darker spot on one side. Margin is wavy and paler than the center.

A single, delicate fruiting body with a slender, brown stalk supporting a nearly spherical, translucent, net-like head. The head displays an intricate, reticulate surface with numerous dark, dot-like spore masses distributed throughout the lattice.

A single, small, irregularly cylindrical structure with a granular, uneven surface. The body is dark brown to blackish with lighter ashy patches, blending indistinctly into the rough background. No cap, pores, or gills are visible.

Small, irregularly rounded to cushion-shaped fruiting bodies closely attached to stems, pale cream to light brown with numerous darker brown to reddish-brown spots. Surfaces appear slightly moist or gelatinous, with indistinct margins blending into the substrate and a somewhat granular texture.

Irregular, thin, contorted whitish to grayish patches with a powdery or granular texture overlay a darker olive-green to brownish background. The surface appears chaotic and patchy, with indistinct margins and no clearly organized structures visible.

Long, slender, pale stems with fibrous texture and remnants of soil at the base. Caps are convex to nearly flat, brownish, with slightly striate margins. Crowded, pale to light brown gills are visible beneath the smooth caps. Size varies among the four specimens.

Small mushroom with a convex to slightly depressed tan-ochre cap, dry and subtly textured. Cream-colored, closely spaced gills run down a robust, pale yellowish stem. Soil and fine mycelial threads cling to the base. Another cap lies flat, showing similar color and texture.
A close-up shows a network of fine, translucent hyphae forming a delicate web, with several small, pale yellowish to whitish tufts scattered across a moist, reflective surface.

Two small, upright, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, light brown to tan exteriors and interiors. Margins are even and slightly thickened, and the surface appears velvety. The cups are closely positioned and well-formed.

Highly magnified view showing a rough, granular surface with irregular cavities. The texture is crustose and uneven, featuring brown, black, and greenish hues with powdery or crystalline patches and color transitions from dark to lighter greenish areas.

Irregular, lobed caps with pale brown to tan coloration and whitish mottling; dry, slightly velvety surface. Gills are close, decurrent, and creamy. Stipes are robust, off-white to pale tan, with soil and mycelium at the base. Largest cap about 3–4 cm wide.

Grayish to bluish-gray caps with a moist, slightly fibrillose surface; convex to slightly depressed shape. Slender, pale stems with bluish-gray hues and fibrous texture. Pale pinkish to tan, well-developed gills attached to the stem.

Two mushrooms with pale, fibrous stems and caps showing pronounced ruffled, striate margins. The left cap is light tan and moist, while the right cap is grayish-tan with a darker center and irregular, split edges. Broad, closely spaced pale tan gills are visible.

Minute, black, circular fruiting bodies scattered across a pale, longitudinally ribbed surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised, smooth-margined, and have a flattened profile. The substrate shows a fibrous texture with no visible gelatinous or translucent material.

A single, small, irregularly rounded structure with a rough, granular surface. The color is dark brown to blackish, displaying subtle iridescent or metallic reflections. Margins are indistinct, blending into the background, and the form is pulvinate to crustose.

Dark brown to nearly black, irregular mound-like structures with a rough, granular, and crystalline surface. Some areas glisten, likely from moisture, and the margins are uneven, blending into the surrounding material without clear separation.

Small, cushion-shaped fruiting bodies with a white to light brownish hue, scattered along dried stems. Surfaces appear granular with numerous tiny white dots, and margins are irregular and slightly lobed. Fruiting bodies are closely attached to the substrate.

Small, brown, hemispherical to subglobose fruiting bodies with a granular, roughened surface, scattered and clustered directly on moist bark. No visible stalks, and the fungi are embedded on the wood surface.

Broadly convex ochre to yellow-brown cap with a smooth surface and slightly incurved margin. Pale brown to cinnamon gills are moderately spaced. Robust, curved yellowish stipe with brownish stains, fibrous texture, and remnants of a web-like veil near the base.

Small, light brown to tan, cup- to disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and even margins, clustered together among dried plant stems. Their size is noticeably small compared to the surrounding debris.

Irregular, distorted caps with whitish to dirty cream coloration and thick, robust stems. Surfaces are rough, patchy, and covered in soil and debris. Margins are uneven and wavy, with some gills or underlying tissue partially exposed.
Rough, uneven surface with granular or crustose texture, displaying dark brown to black areas interspersed with lighter whitish patches and sparkly reflections.

Patchy, encrusting growth with a granular to powdery surface, displaying irregular whitish to grayish areas blending into the substrate. The colonies are discontinuous and crust-like, with diffuse, irregular margins and no prominent fruiting bodies visible.

Small mushroom with a light brown, densely fuzzy cap covered in fine, erect hairs. The cap margin is even and slightly incurved. The slender, straight stem is pale gray and smooth, maintaining a consistent thickness throughout.

Two small mushrooms with slender, white stems and tan to light brown, slightly convex caps. The cap surfaces appear finely fibrous or scaly, with even margins. The mushrooms rest on decaying wood amid green moss.

A single, delicate fungus with a slender reddish-brown stalk topped by a pale, globose, net-like sporangium. The surface appears granular and is adorned with tiny crystalline droplets, giving a fragile, sparkling appearance.

Two delicate mushrooms with thin, translucent stems and small, flat, grayish caps covered in fine, powdery scales. The gills are visible beneath the caps, and the overall appearance is fragile and dainty.

A single, minute, dark spherical fruiting body sits atop a slender reddish stalk. The surface is glossy and net-like, with fine, hair-like filaments radiating from the base, all standing above a moist, textured background.

Cluster of mushrooms with dry, orange-brown caps, some convex and others nearly flat with faint central depressions. Gills are pale to light brown and moderately spaced. Stems are robust, white to pale brown, with fuzzy, slightly bulbous bases and remnants of a web-like veil.

A single, minute fungus with a slender, translucent stalk topped by a small, globose sporangium. The sporangium is delicate, appearing netted with fine, thread-like structures at its edge. The stalk is pale yellowish-brown.

Two small mushrooms with light grayish-white, hairy caps—one showing a slightly darker, fringed center. The exposed gills are white, free from the stem, and closely spaced. Stems are white and fibrous.

A thin, white, cottony mat spreads patchily across the irregular surface, with a soft, filamentous texture and diffuse margins blending into the substrate. Small dark particles are scattered throughout the crust-like layer.

Cluster of dark brown to nearly black, irregular, rough-textured structures with granular surfaces and scattered small white specks. The compact mass forms uneven, somewhat pointed projections, lacking distinct stems.

Irregular, lumpy, and lobed forms with a rough, crusty surface. Color ranges from white to light brown, with darker soil patches and organic debris adhering. Margins are uneven and the overall appearance is compact and dense.

A small, dark, roughly spherical to bulbous structure with an uneven, granular surface. The coloration is predominantly dark brown to nearly black, with lighter brownish patches and minute surface protrusions visible.

Numerous tiny, whitish to translucent discs with smooth, even margins and a faintly granular surface are scattered irregularly across a dark, textured background. The delicate, shallow cup-shaped fruiting bodies appear both solitary and loosely clustered.

Highly magnified view showing a rough, irregular surface with convoluted, slit-like cavities. The coloration is a mix of white, brown, and black, with jagged margins and a granular or powdery coating accentuating the intricate, labyrinthine texture.

Broad, grayish-brown caps with prominent dark central blotches and scattered white patches. Cap margins are slightly wavy and irregular. Pale to light brown gills are visible beneath the caps. The mushrooms grow closely together among grass.

Tiny, pale tan to light brown disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded edges, each perched on a short, delicate stalk and scattered along a slender, dried stem. The upper surfaces are slightly convex to flat, giving a pin-like appearance.

Slender, curved, greenish gelatinous stem supporting a small, brown, moist, cup-shaped apothecium with a smooth, slightly flared margin. The surface appears glossy and semi-translucent, giving a delicate overall appearance.

Highly magnified view showing a rough, irregular surface with jagged, cavernous openings. The texture is coarse and granular, with dark brown to blackish-brown coloration interspersed with lighter brown and whitish patches. Some areas appear slightly lustrous under light.

Two rounded, dome-shaped fruiting bodies with a moist, glistening surface. The larger one is brown with numerous darker brown spots, giving it a textured appearance. The margin is smooth, and both sit directly on wet, decaying wood.

Tiny, white to translucent disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered along dry brown stems. The discs are flat to slightly concave, with smooth, regular margins and a matte surface, spaced apart and delicate in appearance.
Tiny, pale cream to white disc-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, slightly convex surfaces and well-defined margins, each on a short, barely visible stalk, scattered along a brown stem.

A solitary, globose fruiting body with a smooth, brown exterior and a partial apical split exposing a yellowish inner surface. The slender, glossy stipe is dark brown to nearly black, contrasting sharply with the apothecium.

Crustose surface with rough, irregular texture; predominantly brown, gray, and white hues. Features convoluted, labyrinthine cavities, granular appearance, and intricate folds with lighter whitish encrustations in some areas.

Dark, irregular fragment with a matte to slightly glossy surface, scattered with small, black, hemispherical to conical protrusions. The texture appears rough, and the specimen measures a few centimeters across.
A close-up shows a light brown, fibrous surface densely covered with numerous small, black, spherical to ovoid structures, giving it a rough, granular, and speckled appearance.

A small, irregular, granular mass embedded in a dark, rough surface. The structure is slightly raised, uneven, and matte, with muted earthy tones and a crustose, granular texture. No distinct cap, stipe, or visible reproductive structures are present.

Irregular, horn-like projections with rough, scaly surfaces emerge from decaying wood. The fruiting bodies are dark brown to grayish, uneven, and scattered, with rugged, raised margins and a coarse texture.

Grayish-brown cap with a conical to broadly convex shape, slightly undulating and faintly striate margin. Cap surface is smooth to finely fibrillose with minor debris. Slender, centrally attached stem matches the cap in color and appears smooth.
Numerous small, black, rounded to slightly irregular bumps scattered and clustered on a reddish-brown patch of bark, with some areas showing darker discoloration and peeling edges.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, light to medium brown caps, densely packed rusty brown gills, and whitish to ochre stems often curved and covered in brownish fibrils, especially near the soil-encrusted base. Caps show subtle zonation and a smooth to slightly fibrous texture.

Numerous small, white to cream, shallow disc-like fruitbodies with wavy, upturned, minutely fuzzy margins. Some display subtle brownish tinges at the edges. The fruitbodies are irregularly shaped, varying from nearly round to lobed, and are scattered densely across the dark substrate.

Dense clusters of white to off-white, fan-shaped caps with wavy, upturned margins and fine surface texture. Some caps show light tan tones and are scattered with small black specks. Gills run down short, lateral stems. Caps vary from fully expanded to emerging.

Small, shiny black nodules clustered and embedded in a reddish-brown, rough woody surface. Some nodules are exposed within a split in the bark, appearing as minute, dot-like structures with tiny black openings.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a bright orange to yellow-orange smooth inner surface and a paler, irregular, slightly lobed margin. The texture appears glossy and fragile, with the cup nestled among forest floor debris.

Robust, fleshy mushrooms with dark reddish-brown, conical to umbonate caps showing a dry, wrinkled texture. Gills are closely spaced and deep reddish-brown. Stems are thick, matching the cap color, and coated with sand.

Medium to dark brown convex caps with a smooth, matte surface. One mushroom shows widely spaced, pale grayish gills and a slender stipe that is white at the base, turning bluish-gray and fibrous upward.

Bright yellow, thin, cup-shaped structure with a smooth inner surface and an irregular, wavy, slightly lobed margin. The cup is delicate and partially filled with small debris, contrasting with the surrounding forest litter.

Numerous small, flattened, translucent to pale cream disc-like bodies with wavy, undulating margins cluster loosely on the surface. Some have darker, curled edges, and all appear thin, delicate, and smooth, lacking visible stalks.

Ochre to tawny-brown caps with darker centers, broadly convex to nearly flat, and distinctly jagged, radially split margins. Slender, pale stems with fine fibrils and attached soil. Gills are pale brown and moderately spaced. Fruiting bodies are scattered and irregularly shaped.

Patchy, crust-like layer tightly adhering to the branch, light brown to pinkish in color, with a cracked, slightly flaking surface and irregular, blending margins. Some areas are interspersed with green moss or algae.

Numerous small, black, naviculate to angular fruitbodies with a flattened, hard, carbonaceous appearance are scattered and partially embedded in a rough, pale surface. Their surfaces are smooth to slightly roughened, lacking visible fuzz or velvety texture.
Small, dark, irregularly shaped fruiting bodies with angular, flattened forms and rough, matte to slightly granular surfaces, scattered and partially embedded in a pale, uneven substrate.

A small, dark, irregularly oval fruiting body with a granular, uneven surface and indistinct margin, blending into the pale fibrous substrate. The structure is slightly raised and solitary, with a deep brown to black coloration.

A single, small, dark fruiting body with a rough, shiny surface and a central slit-like opening. The shield-like structure is slightly raised above the lighter, textured background, with distinct margins.

A ruptured, cup-shaped fruiting body with an irregular, broken margin reveals a dense, dark purple-brown spore mass inside. The outer surface is pale brownish to grayish and weathered, with remnants of the peridium clinging to the base.
Irregular, thin, crust-like patches with a dark greenish-black to brown color, featuring numerous minute black dot-like structures scattered across the surface and an uneven, slightly raised margin.

Small mushroom with a convex, pale grayish-brown cap, distinctly hairy at the margin. The cap edge is paler and slightly inrolled. The slender, curved stipe is finely fibrous and darker toward the base.

White to pale yellowish caps, some with wavy or irregular margins. Gills are closely spaced, pale, and run slightly down the robust, white stems. Surfaces appear dry and smooth, with visible size variation among fruiting bodies.

Two slender mushrooms: one with a smooth, moist, orange-brown hemispherical cap and pale fibrous stem; the other with a grayish, dry, conical cap and a curved, grayish-brown stem. Both emerge among dense green moss and grass.
Broad, convex cap with a pale cream to pinkish margin. Gills are closely spaced, decurrent, and white to pale cream, radiating from a robust white stem partially covered in soil and debris.

A globose to slightly flattened fruiting body with a deep purple coloration, smooth in some areas and cracked or flaking in others. The surface shows a powdery texture, especially on top, with irregular, broken margins indicating maturity.

A brown, dome-shaped surface with a rough, textured appearance, scattered with small, pale yellow to cream disc-shaped fruiting bodies. The discs are smooth, sessile, and appear singly or in small groups, with slightly lighter centers.

Two mushrooms with smooth, pale caps showing a brownish center; one cap is convex and the other slightly flattened. Crowded, pale brown gills are visible, along with moderately thick, white to off-white stems lacking any ring or veil remnants.

Irregularly lobed, lumpy fruiting bodies with a rough, warty, cracked tan surface and darker patches. A cut section reveals a dense, pale whitish interior with a marbled, veined texture and firm, convoluted appearance.

Numerous tiny, white to translucent, circular fruiting bodies densely cover the surface, each with thin, delicate, slightly wavy margins and a glassy appearance, forming scattered to gregarious clusters.

White to cream caps with smooth surfaces and slightly wavy margins. Slender, pale stems support well-developed, closely spaced gills that are white to pale cream, radiating from the stem and clearly visible underneath.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with pale whitish, circular caps displaying prominent radiating gills underneath. Caps are flat to slightly convex with even margins, supported by thin, elongated light brown stems scattered along a dead grass stem.

Numerous tiny, cup- to disc-shaped fruiting bodies with undulating whitish margins and brownish to tan centers, scattered densely across the dark, rough wood surface. The apothecia are smooth, waxy, and have irregular, wavy edges, appearing tightly clustered yet distinct.

Rounded, globose fruiting bodies with irregular, collapsed upper surfaces. The exterior and interior are deep purple, covered in a powdery, granular texture. Margins are broken and uneven, with no visible stipe or base.

Small, white, stalked, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly flared margins emerge irregularly from a brown, oval surface speckled with soil. The delicate, pale apothecia stand out against the dark background.

Tiny, delicate fungus with a thin, white to cream cap, nearly flat and displaying distinct radial gills beneath. The smooth cap margin and extremely slender, short stipe support the cap laterally. The fruiting body is solitary and diminutive.

Tiny, nearly spherical black fruitbodies with a rough, granular surface, clustered along a darkened line on a pale stem. The fruitbodies are closely grouped and appear slightly raised from the substrate.

Mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, pale cream to light brown caps, some bearing darker patches and adhering debris. Gills are densely packed and brownish. Cylindrical, pale stipes show remnants of soil. Caps have smooth margins, and the surfaces appear smooth with scattered organic material.

Tiny, white to translucent disc-shaped fruiting bodies with frosted, finely granular surfaces. Each sits atop a short, slender, translucent stalk. Margins are even, and the fruiting bodies are scattered on a fibrous brown substrate.

Large, globose fruiting body with a dark purple-brown surface, covered in irregular, peeling patches and scales. The surface appears dry and rough, with uneven margins on the patches. No stipe or base is visible from this angle.

Tiny, delicate fruitbodies with thin, whitish stalks and smooth, shallow, disc-like pale caps emerge in clusters from the side of a brown, rough-textured organic object. The caps are even-margined and unmarked.
A thin, spreading, gelatinous mass with a white to cream color. The surface is shiny, moist, and soft-looking, with an irregular, undulating margin and no visible fruiting bodies.

Small, nearly black, hemispherical to slightly flattened fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across a pale, fibrous stem surface. The fruiting bodies are embedded or partially immersed, with a rough, granular texture and indistinct margins.

Numerous small, bright yellow, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, waxy surfaces are scattered across a dark, rounded object, creating a striking contrast and a three-dimensional effect under strong lighting.

Slender mushrooms with bluish-gray stems, pale closely spaced gills, and smooth convex caps in muted brownish-gray tones with slightly paler margins. The stems show whitish bases and some darkening near the soil line.

Irregularly lobed, roughly globose fruiting body with a pale tan to light brown, cracked and uneven surface. Patches of adhering soil are visible, and the texture appears chalky or crumbly. No internal structures or stalk are visible.
Two small, pale tan to light brown, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with distinctly lobed, scalloped margins and smooth, moist surfaces, closely appressed to the substrate.

Medium-sized mushrooms with convex to irregularly expanded caps, pale yellowish to light brown and slightly scaly. Crowded, attached gills are pale cream to yellowish. Robust, cylindrical stipes are pale, with soil remnants at the base. Both cap and gill surfaces are clearly visible.

Irregular, crust-like patches tightly pressed to the wood, each with a brownish center and a dense, white, woolly margin. The edges are distinctly fuzzy, while the centers appear smoother and more compact.

Broadly convex to irregular caps with cream to pale yellow tones and scattered brownish patches. Gills are closely spaced, off-white to pale yellow. Stems are white with yellowish discoloration and soil remnants at the base. Cap surface appears dry and slightly fibrous.

Broad cap with creamy white background and wine-red streaks, moist surface speckled with soil. Thick, widely spaced, decurrent gills with a pale pinkish hue. Robust, cylindrical stipe with faint reddish streaks and fibrous texture.
Irregular, tuberous bodies with a light brown to tan, rough and bumpy surface, some with soil remnants. Cut specimens reveal a pale, marbled, dense interior with a firm texture.

Convex to slightly flattened caps in pale cream to light brown, smooth surface with minor debris. Cylindrical white stems with soil remnants at the base. Gills are closely spaced, pale, and attached to the stem. No ring or volva visible.

Small mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped, dark brown to grayish-brown caps and smooth, matte surfaces. Stems are long, slender, yellowish to brownish, fibrous, and often twisted. Gills underneath are closely spaced and grayish-brown.
A small, dome-shaped, glossy dark brown cap with scattered small white wart-like spots. The cap surface appears moist and smooth, with an even margin. No stipe or gills are visible from this angle.

Bright yellow-orange, thin, and fragile cup-like body with irregular, crumpled, and undulating lobed margins. The inner surface is smooth with some darker recessed areas. A delicate web-like structure is visible across part of the surface.

A single, small, nearly black, globose fruiting body with a rough, granular surface and a prominent, slightly raised ostiole at the apex. The margins are well-defined and the structure is compact and sessile.

Fan-shaped, creamy to off-white fruiting body with a wavy, irregular margin. Densely packed, strongly decurrent gills run down a short, indistinct stem. Surface appears smooth and slightly shiny, with delicate, fragile texture and minor insect activity at the base.

Convex to irregular pale cream caps with yellow staining, especially near the base and gills. Crowded, pale gills show yellow discoloration. Robust, white to yellowish stems, some with soil attached. Multiple specimens display cap and gill details.

Irregular, cup-like fruiting bodies with lobed and contorted shapes. Surfaces are vibrant orange with paler yellowish areas, especially along uneven, split margins. Texture appears leathery and brittle, with some damaged edges.

Small, cup-shaped structure with a smooth, pale tan inner surface and a distinctly fringed margin lined with coarse, spiky hair-like projections. The outer surface appears minutely hairy and granular, especially near the edge.

Small, dark, crust-like fruiting bodies scattered on bark, circular to irregular in shape with rough, cracked surfaces. Margins blend into the substrate, and the surrounding bark shows brown and greenish patches.

Three mushrooms with convex, dark brown caps showing subtle lighter patches and a dry, finely textured surface. One specimen reveals closely spaced, radiating brown gills and a slender, pale brown stem with soil particles attached.

A solitary, semicircular to irregular cap with a smooth, moist surface. The cap is light brown to tan, with a paler margin and a slightly darker center. No stipe or gills are visible; the margin is thin and even.

Fan-shaped, pale tan to light brown caps with wavy, irregular margins and smooth surfaces. Crowded, decurrent gills are pale cream to light brown, running down the lateral attachment. Fruiting bodies overlap in a clustered, horizontal arrangement.

Dense cluster of overlapping, fan-shaped caps with wavy, undulate margins. Predominantly white to off-white, some beige tones, and speckled with black particles. Smooth surface, irregular and lobed appearance.
Small, irregular, worm-like mass with a glistening, wet, gelatinous surface. Translucent grayish to bluish-white in color, smooth and undifferentiated margin, solitary and moist appearance.
Clustered fruiting bodies with light brown to tan, moist, glossy caps. The caps have irregular, wavy, and lobed margins with a smooth surface. Edges are undulate, and the stems are mostly obscured.

Tiny, delicate fruiting bodies with smooth, pale whitish convex caps, some showing faint wrinkles. Caps are attached directly to the stem by very short, barely visible stalks, and are scattered in a linear arrangement along the dead plant stem.

A thin, crust-like layer tightly attached to the surface, grayish to violet-gray in color, with a smooth to finely granular texture. The margin is irregular and blends into the substrate, with scattered minute bumps and small cracks visible.

Pale, pinkish-tan cap with a matte, slightly uneven surface and scattered debris. The margin is wavy and irregular. Underside shows closely spaced, thin, white to cream gills running partway down the cap. Stem is not visible.

Irregular, lumpy fruiting bodies with rough, uneven surfaces. Colors range from pale cream to light brown, mottled with darker brown and scattered white patches. Margins are convoluted and knobby, with compact, dense forms of varying sizes.

Bright yellow-orange, cup-shaped body with a distinctly irregular, jagged margin. Surface is matte with scattered dark specks and a visible perforation near the edge. Texture appears velvety, not waxy.

Pale, creamy to faintly pinkish fruiting bodies with densely crowded, decurrent gills. Caps have wavy, irregular, and somewhat lobed margins, with a smooth surface. A small brown twig rests on one cap. Stems are not visible.

Tightly packed, well-developed gills with a smooth, moist, waxy texture. The color transitions from deep orange at the base to lighter yellow at the edges, with small orange latex droplets exuding along the gill faces.

Broad, convex cap with a white to pinkish background, densely covered in reddish-brown to purplish speckles and blotches. The margin is smooth, slightly inrolled, and shows some irregularities and minor damage. Surface appears moist and somewhat sticky.

Tiny, pale cream to whitish, cup- or disc-shaped fruiting bodies with short, slender stalks emerge in a scattered pattern from the smooth, brown surface of a round fruit. The delicate structures contrast with the darker, earthy background.

Patchy, irregularly spreading growth with a granular to velvety surface. Predominantly muted brown and grayish-beige, interspersed with translucent and off-white granules. Surface appears slightly moist, uneven, and diffuse at the margins, blending into the background.

Numerous tiny, black, dot-like fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across a smooth, green-stained section of wood. The fruiting bodies are rounded and slightly raised above the surface, contrasting with the green and tan background.
