Convex, light brown to ochre caps with a felty, fibrillose surface; robust white to cream stems featuring prominent brownish scaly patches, especially near the base. Gills are crowded, pale, and attached. Thick, white flesh visible in sectioned specimens.

Mushrooms with convex to flat caps, featuring prominent brown, scaly centers on a pale background. Cap margins are slightly incurved and finely fringed. White, free gills and slender, smooth white stems, some with soil at the base.

A green, elongated leaf segment displays a prominent, slightly raised patch densely coated with fine, whitish to pale tan granules, giving it a powdery and textured appearance. The affected area contrasts with the surrounding smooth leaf tissue and has an irregular margin.

Small, scattered yellowish to brownish spots form irregular lesions on the upper leaf surface, following the veins. The affected areas are diffuse, lacking distinct pustules or raised structures, and the surrounding tissue remains mostly green.

A tightly adhering, crust-like layer with a rough, uneven, and granular surface. The coloration is predominantly grayish to brownish with lighter and darker patches. The texture appears dry and cracked, with an irregular margin blending into the substrate.
Dark, cylindrical surface with a rough, matte texture, scattered with tiny white specks and a few irregular pale patches. No prominent fruiting bodies or margins are visible.

Elongated, club-shaped fruiting bodies with slender, curved stipes and ovoid to cylindrical caps. The surface is dry and powdery, colored brown, with some caps partially split. A dark brown spore mass is visible on the white background.

Dense, bushy mat of pale grayish-green, flattened, strap-like lobes with irregular, perforated margins. Lobes are branched, overlapping, and display fine, frilly outgrowths at the tips. Surface appears matte and slightly rough, forming a loosely tufted structure.

Small, circular to irregular yellowish-brown spots scattered along leaf veins and interveinal areas, some with faint central depressions or pale halos. The surrounding tissue shows mild yellowing, and the leaf surface appears smooth with minute lesions.
Dense clusters of small, smooth, glossy yellow-orange spheres tightly packed and emerging from decaying plant debris, forming irregular masses with some spheres extending outward from the main group.

Numerous tiny, pale yellow to off-white, cup- or cone-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded margins and slender stalks, scattered across a brown surface. The texture appears slightly granular and translucent, with delicate, minute structures loosely grouped.

Densely clustered, small, spherical sporangia forming irregular patches. Colors range from yellow to brown, with yellow areas fresher and brown more mature. The surface is smooth, and the margins of the colony are uneven, compact, and closely packed.

Long, slender green leaves display irregular white patches and streaks, mainly at the tips and along the edges, creating a sharp contrast with the healthy green tissue. The leaves overlap in a delicate, intricate pattern.

Mushroom with a pale pinkish-brown, smooth cap showing irregular, wavy margins and some discoloration. White, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the cap, and the short, stout stem is also white.
Two mushrooms with convex to flat caps, medium to dark brown centers, paler scaly margins, white free gills, and slender pale stems with brownish streaks and a faint membranous ring.

Broad, pale yellow underside with a thick, rounded, irregular margin and a distinctly bumpy, granular surface. The robust stem is brown and soil-covered at the base, fading to whitish near the cap attachment.

A solitary mushroom with a convex, brown, scaly cap and irregular margin. The slender, curved stem is granular, fading from pale at the top to dark brown at the base. Pale gills are visible beneath the cap.

Thin, crust-like layer spreading irregularly over wood, displaying a patchwork of reddish-brown, pinkish, and creamy white tones with a granular, slightly rough texture. The diffuse margin blends into the substrate, with some areas covered by soil and leaf debris.

Overlapping, irregular brown to dark brown scales with uneven, slightly lobed margins. The matte surface is mottled with lighter and darker areas and scattered with small, pale granules. The patch is dense and closely appressed.

A crust-like, tightly adherent patch with a pale tan to light brown surface, covered in numerous small, round to angular pores. The texture is finely granular and slightly rough, with diffuse margins blending into the substrate.

Robust fruiting bodies with thick, fibrous brownish stems and convex to irregularly flattened caps. Caps are off-white to pale yellow, with a rough, granular texture and powdery, yellowish undersides.

Elongated green leaf with yellowish discoloration and subtle speckling, especially along the midrib. The surface appears matte and slightly wrinkled, with visible tears and missing sections along the margin. No distinct fungal structures are visible.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, smooth light brown caps, robust white to cream stems, and closely spaced pale gills. Some caps show minor blemishes. Two specimens are cut lengthwise, displaying a white, fleshy interior.

Dense tufts of pale greenish-gray, strap-shaped, irregularly branched lobes form bushy, matte, and slightly powdery patches scattered across the stone. The lobes are erect to spreading with smooth to slightly undulate margins.

Fruiting bodies with pale brown, leathery rays radiating outward in a star shape, surrounding a central, round, dull brown spore sac with a wrinkled surface and a distinct apical pore. Ray number and arrangement vary among specimens.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened caps, light brown to ochre with darker patchy or scaly markings. Cap margins are smooth and slightly inrolled. Gills are dense, closely spaced, and yellowish-brown. Stipes are robust, pale yellow-brown, with soil at the base.

Close-up of a thick, robust stem merging into a yellowish-white cap with a rough, bumpy, uneven surface and scattered small white nodules. The cap margin is slightly curled, highlighting coarse surface details.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, translucent white caps and finely striated margins. Stems are thin, elongated, and translucent, with widely spaced white gills visible beneath the caps. The overall appearance is smooth, fragile, and ghostly.

Extensive, thin, crust-like patch tightly covering wood, displaying pinkish to pale orange coloration with irregular, diffuse whitish margins. Surface appears smooth to slightly uneven, spreading flatly without visible cap, stem, or pores.

Broken mushroom with a pinkish-red to yellowish-brown cap, slightly striate margin, and brittle texture. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to yellowish. The robust, white stipe and exposed white, crumbly flesh are visible.

A single, delicate fruiting body with a slender, translucent stalk supporting a tiny, smooth, pale pink cup-shaped cap. The margin of the cap is even, and the overall structure appears minute and fragile.

Tiny, pale yellow to translucent goblet-shaped structures with thin, short stalks and smooth margins, scattered across a textured surface. The delicate, moist-looking tissue appears slightly granular under magnification.

Dense, powdery to granular surface with vivid yellow to yellow-orange coloration, interspersed with irregular white patches. The crust-like texture appears undulating and uneven, forming a thick, friable coating without distinct fruiting bodies.

Two mushrooms with flat to slightly convex brown caps, darker at the center and paler, textured edges. Stems are slender, off-white with irregular brown bands, and slightly curved. Gills are crowded, free, and pale cream to light brown.

White stem with brown speckles, slightly curved and fibrous. Cap is brown, partially broken with an irregular, tattered margin. White, crowded gills are exposed beneath the cap, free from the stem. Surface shows scattered brownish scales.

Patchy, crust-like covering of minute, irregular yellow-green to olive granules scattered across the soil surface, blending with mosses. The texture appears rough and uneven, with no distinct margins or visible fruiting bodies.

Mushrooms with brown, patchy, scaly convex to flat caps, white free gills, and slender white stems adorned with brown flecks. Cap margins are slightly irregular. Multiple fruiting bodies are clustered together, showing distinct surface textures and coloration.

Round, light brown fruiting bodies with rough surfaces; mature forms display star-like rays peeled back, revealing a central grayish-brown spherical sac with a distinct apical pore. Rays are pale tan and smooth to slightly fibrous.
Rounded, irregular fruiting body with a thick, brownish stem. Surface is off-white to pale yellow, densely warty and uneven, with a lobed, contorted margin and compact structure.

Numerous tiny, pale cream to translucent, cup-shaped to triangular fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly flared margins are scattered in clusters across a reddish-brown fibrous surface. The fruiting bodies appear sessile or with very short stalks and have a waxy texture.

Small, densely clustered, cup-shaped bodies with smooth, grayish to olive-brown inner surfaces and distinctly fringed margins covered in fine, whitish to pale brown hairs. Many cups have sand grains and debris adhering to their surfaces, enhancing their fuzzy appearance.
No visible fungal structures or symptoms are present; only thin, feathery green leaves with slightly pale tips are seen.

Broad, dark brown to nearly black cap with a matte, dry surface. Irregular white patches where the surface is damaged. Cap is convex to slightly depressed in the center, with a smooth, uneven margin and scattered debris.
Numerous small, round to slightly oval, pale cream fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and well-defined margins, densely clustered and scattered across a dark, charred substrate.

Crust-like, tightly appressed fruiting body with a porous, maze-like surface. Pores are small, angular to irregular, and densely packed. Coloration varies from pale cream to ochre and light brown, with whitish patches and a spongy, uneven texture.

Mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, dark brown caps with a reddish tinge and smooth, moist surfaces. Margins are slightly inrolled on younger specimens. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to ochre, and stipes are cylindrical, lighter brown, fibrous, with white mycelium at the base.

Large, fleshy mushroom with a smooth, convex, light brown cap bearing a shiny, wet surface. Thick, white stem is densely speckled with black. Pale gills are visible beneath the cap. The cap margin is smooth and the fruiting bodies are solitary to paired.

Flat, crust-like surface with dense, small, angular to slightly elongated pores. Colors range from pale to reddish-brown, with diffuse, whitish margins and patches of white mycelium. The texture is finely porous and the surface appears mostly flat with some undulating areas.

Crustose, lumpy thallus with a predominantly brown surface, interspersed with lighter and darker patches. The texture is rough and granular, with scattered small white particles and irregular, indistinct margins blending into the substrate.

Mushrooms with convex, light brown caps covered in darker brown scales, slightly inrolled margins, thick yellowish stems with bulbous bases, and closely spaced ochre gills. Soil clings to the stem bases, and the surface appears smooth to slightly fibrillose.
Pale grayish-green, strap-like lobes radiate loosely from the center, with wrinkled, granular surfaces and uneven, upturned margins. The thallus appears irregular and directly attached to the rock.

Smooth, convex white caps with faint brownish tints and subtle striations near the margin. One cap shows a patch of missing cuticle. Thick, white stems with remnants of substrate. Pale, crowded, free gills visible on the smaller, curved specimen.
Long, narrow green leaves with scattered pale yellow spots and irregular holes. Some leaf edges are curled or dried, but no visible fungal fruiting bodies or pustules are present.

Smooth, elongated green leaves display irregular, pale whitish patches or lesions. No visible fruiting bodies or external fungal structures are present; discoloration appears as subtle, diffuse areas on the leaf surface.

Irregular, collapsed caps with pale off-white to yellowish tones and uneven, slightly fuzzy surfaces. Thick, upright stalks are rough and granular, showing some blue-green discoloration and embedded bases. The fruiting bodies appear scattered and distorted.

Dense, bushy, pale green to grayish mats with branched, tufted filaments cover the upper rock, contrasting with bright yellow, granular, tightly adherent patches forming irregular crusts on the lower surfaces.

Radiating cluster of elongated, transparent, thread-like structures extending from a central point, each containing several small, oval bodies. The overall appearance is delicate, gray, and translucent with a subtle sheen.

Extensive, crust-like layer tightly attached to wood, pale pinkish to salmon in color with irregular, lobed edges and a thin whitish border. Surface appears smooth to slightly uneven, merging into darkened wood areas.

Upright, slender, pale green stalks with distinctly cup-shaped tops, covered in a granular, powdery texture. The cup margins are irregular and adorned with small, bright red dots, giving a striking contrast.

Mushrooms with broadly convex to flat caps, pronounced brown centers, and paler, scaly margins. Cap surfaces are dry with scattered white to cream scales. Stems are slender, white to cream, with remnants of a ring. Gills are white and free. Varying maturity is visible.

Numerous small, nearly black, globose fruiting bodies with rough, textured surfaces are densely clustered on a yellow, granular background. Some fruiting bodies are adjacent to patches of whitish, fuzzy growth. The margins are well-defined and rounded.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to flat caps, central brown discs, and paler, scaly margins. Slender white stems show brownish fibrils, and some have veil remnants. Gills are white to cream, visible on upturned caps amid wet leaf litter.

Dark, nearly black, crustose surface with a rough, uneven texture. Scattered across are numerous tiny, rounded, pale to light brown structures, slightly raised and embedded in the thallus, forming irregular patches among plant debris.

Elongated, cylindrical stems with rough, woody texture; one has a bulbous, cracked, granular cap, while the other is slender and tapering. Both are dark brown to blackish with a dry, brittle appearance.

A patch of orange-brown, granular growth with a crystalline, powdery texture forms an irregular, raised mass on a greenish surface. The fungal area is amorphous and patchy, with golden to reddish-brown hues and visible surface texture.

Green leaf with numerous yellowish-brown, powdery spots and irregular patches. The affected areas are granular, slightly raised, and mottled, with some necrotic regions and small holes visible along the surface.

Numerous blackish, metallic-glossed, globose structures scattered across a densely perforated, honeycomb-like surface of rusty to orange-brown granular tissue, creating a striking contrast between the dark spheres and the lighter, regularly pored background.

Clustered mushrooms with large, golden-brown funnel-shaped caps, darker centers, and slightly inrolled, wavy margins. The exposed underside shows closely spaced, decurrent yellow gills. Stipes are robust, yellowish, and soil-stained at the base. Cap surfaces appear dry and velvety.

Crustose growth tightly adheres to a cracked surface, densely covered with small, black, circular fruiting bodies. The pale to grayish-brown tissue is rough and fissured, with granular, stippled patches where the fruiting bodies are embedded.

Green cylindrical stem densely covered with small, white, oval to elongated raised pustules arranged in irregular rows, giving a speckled appearance. Some fine, web-like growth is visible around the lesions.

Numerous small, black, rounded fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across a dried, striated plant stem. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised with a matte to subtly shiny surface, lacking visible openings or spore masses at this magnification.

Tiny, rounded fruiting bodies with pale whitish to light gray discs and slightly raised, possibly fringed margins. The surfaces appear smooth with a subtle granular texture, scattered across the decaying leaf.

Numerous tiny, brown, speckled pustules scattered irregularly across a bright green, veined leaf surface. The pustules are slightly raised with indistinct margins, disrupting the otherwise smooth texture of the leaf.
Dense clusters of tiny, black, circular to cup-shaped structures embedded in and slightly raised above a pale, cracked, woody surface, forming granular dark patches on the rough, fissured background.

Elongated, cylindrical black fruiting bodies with a matte, slightly textured surface. Each structure is upright, some with a gentle curve at the tip, and uniformly dark with smooth margins, emerging from the ground among grass and moss.

Numerous tiny, black, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with central depressions are scattered and clustered across a pale, fibrous wood surface. Some discs show a lighter center. The texture appears smooth to slightly rough.

Numerous tiny, pale yellow to ochre, disc-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces and rounded to irregular margins are scattered across the moist, dark surface of the log. The apothecia are sessile and mostly solitary or loosely grouped.

Small, clustered fruiting bodies with hemispherical to convex caps densely coated in fine, whitish, hair-like structures, giving a fuzzy appearance. Stems are similarly pale and covered in fine hairs. Margins of the caps are even, and the overall color is pale white to off-white.
A thin, white, powdery to fuzzy coating covers the green leaf surface, forming a delicate, filamentous layer with some denser patches and small pale spots. The texture appears cottony and diffuse.

Numerous small, round, dark blue to black fruiting bodies with distinct central dots are densely clustered across a cracked, pale, rough surface. The fruiting bodies are embedded or slightly raised, forming irregular groups on the substrate.

Green stem with numerous small, white, blister-like pustules scattered irregularly. The pustules are raised, rounded, and slightly granular, varying in size and forming patchy clusters along the stem.

Green stem densely covered with numerous white, slightly raised, irregularly shaped pustules arranged in longitudinal rows. The pustules vary in size, appear somewhat flattened, and have a waxy or powdery texture.

Dense, mat-like thallus with a finely granular texture, forming a continuous, low, greenish-grey layer. Some areas show a yellow-green tint. The surface is uneven, compact, and closely adheres to the substrate, with no visible upright structures or distinct margins.

Small, delicate mushroom with a slender, whitish, slightly fibrous stem and a pale grayish, nearly flat cap. The cap is distinctly pleated with deep radial grooves and a scalloped margin, giving it a textured, almost papery appearance.

A dense, white, cottony mass with a rounded, irregularly lobed shape emerges from the spider's back. The surface is adorned with numerous small, yellowish granules, creating a striking contrast against the reddish-brown spider exoskeleton.

Light green leaf with a prominent vein network, scattered with numerous minute, round, dark brown to blackish spots evenly distributed across the surface. The leaf margin is entire and slightly undulate, and the surface appears smooth and matte.

Clustered, overlapping caps with smooth, pale off-white surfaces and irregular, slightly ruffled margins. Some caps show splits and scattered debris. Crowded, pale gills are visible beneath the caps, while the stems are mostly hidden by the tight grouping.

Dense, contiguous mat of small, rounded to subglobose structures tightly packed together, ranging from pale cream to light brown with some pinkish or tan hues. The surface is distinctly granular, forming an irregular, low, spreading crust interspersed with green moss.

A pale, finely granular surface scattered with numerous minute, dark, roughly circular to irregular spots, unevenly distributed and appearing as isolated or loosely grouped dark structures. No large fruiting bodies or distinct margins are visible.
Granular, uneven, grayish-green surface with a rough, crust-like texture. Scattered across are small, dark brown to blackish, pin-like fruiting bodies protruding distinctly above the thallus.
Numerous small, round to slightly irregular brown spots densely cover the green leaf surface, each forming a discrete, raised pustule that contrasts sharply with the prominent reticulate venation.

Cluster of four mushrooms with smooth, convex to nearly flat ochre-brown caps, paler at the edges. Stems are slender, pale yellow to white, and finely fibrillose, with soil clinging to the base. Gills underneath are pale and closely spaced.

Erect, unbranched fruiting bodies with a deep black color, club-shaped to slightly spatulate, featuring a velvety, minutely hairy surface and smooth, rounded to slightly pointed tips. Arranged in a scattered, loosely grouped manner above light green foliage.

A tiny, rounded to slightly angular fruiting body with a matte, brownish-tan surface and a subtly raised margin. The texture appears dry and somewhat rough, with no visible shine or sliminess. Solitary and very small in size.

Small mushrooms with convex, light brown caps showing faint striations near the edges and slightly darker centers. Slender, pale stems support closely spaced, pale gills with a subtle pinkish hue. Surfaces appear smooth and slightly fibrous.

Two delicate mushrooms with slender, fibrous light brown stems and reddish-brown convex caps. One cap shows fine grooves along the margin and a smooth, slightly moist surface. The other reveals closely spaced, pale brown to grayish gills beneath the cap.

Dense, compact patch with a dark brown to nearly black, granular surface. The thallus is rough and uneven, covered in small, wart-like projections and embedded mineral particles, creating a distinctly textured appearance.

Numerous tiny, rounded blackish spots are scattered irregularly across a tan, fibrous surface with greenish patches. The spots are slightly raised and granular, contrasting with the uneven, subtly colored background.

Vibrant yellow-orange disc with a finely granular surface. The margin is distinctly lined with dense, dark, outward-projecting hair-like setae, creating a striking fringe around the edge. The texture appears dry and matte.

Numerous tiny, rounded to slightly flattened yellowish-orange to light brown discs with a translucent, gelatinous texture, irregularly grouped on decayed wood. Some fruiting bodies appear more cup-like, others more disc-shaped, all with a moist, delicate surface.
A compact cluster of minute, irregularly shaped, dark brown to blackish granules with a rough, lumpy surface. The structures are closely grouped, forming a granular mound with no distinct margins.

Numerous small, black, spherical fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across a pale, fibrous surface, giving it a pebbled and textured appearance. The fruiting bodies are matte to slightly shiny and partially embedded in the substrate.

Small, delicate mushrooms with pale gray to white, pleated caps and slender white stems. The caps are convex to nearly flat, displaying pronounced radial striations and a smooth to slightly granular surface. Clustered in groups, emerging from crevices in decaying wood.

Irregular, slightly raised off-white to pale cream patches scattered along the green surface, with a granular or mealy texture and indistinct margins. The patches coalesce into larger areas, causing localized swelling and a crustose appearance embedded in the tissue.

Numerous small, oval to rectangular, white to pale yellowish patches are slightly raised and densely scattered in rows along the green stem. Each patch has a fuzzy, powdery texture with diffuse margins, creating a patchy, irregular pattern.

Dense, continuous mat of pale green to greenish-gray, granular to squamulose structures with a rough, irregular surface, tightly appressed to the substrate and covering a large area. No upright structures visible.

Tiny, round to oval, pale cream fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces and irregular fringed margins. Scattered across the leaf surface, some appear slightly sunken. Fine hyphal threads are visible around the fruiting bodies.

Medium to dark brown, smooth convex caps with moist surfaces; white to cream, closely spaced gills; cylindrical, pale stems with substrate remnants at the base. Caps have even, non-striate margins and lack veil remnants or rings.
Numerous small, bright orange, shallow cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, moist surfaces and margins, scattered in loose clusters across a muddy, leaf-littered surface.

Dense, white, cottony mycelium overlays dark, lobed, leathery patches with undulating margins. The white, fuzzy growth forms irregular mats and tufts, often concentrated along the edges and upper surfaces, creating a frosted appearance.
Numerous small, dark brown to black, rounded pustules densely scattered across a vibrant green leaf, each slightly raised and sharply contrasting with the smooth leaf surface.

Numerous small, white, blister-like pustules densely cover the green leaf surface. The pustules are irregular, slightly raised, and often split open, revealing a granular or powdery interior. Their bright white color contrasts sharply with the surrounding green tissue.

A green leaf with brown, slightly curled edges is coated in a fine, white, powdery layer, giving it a fuzzy appearance. The powdery coating is uniform across the leaf surface, with no visible fruiting bodies.

Dense, powdery whitish growth covers the surface, interspersed with numerous small, dark, spherical structures. The matted, granular layer contrasts with scattered black fruiting bodies, creating an uneven texture with visible fine threads and compact spots.

Clusters of cream to pale tan mushrooms with broad, irregular, wavy-edged caps. The cap surface is smooth to slightly fibrous. Undersides show crowded, pale brown to grayish gills and robust, white cylindrical stems.

Numerous small, circular to irregular brown lesions with slightly raised, mottled surfaces and yellowish halos are scattered unevenly across the green, textured leaf. The darkened spots vary in size and density, forming distinct pustules.

Small, delicate mushroom with a pale gray, radially striate cap that is convex to flat and slightly scalloped at the margin. The slender, elongated stem is coated with a fine, powdery or fibrous texture.

Elongated green leaves display numerous small, white, slightly raised spots scattered across their surfaces, giving a speckled and powdery appearance. The leaf margins remain smooth and entire, with the white lesions clearly contrasting against the healthy green background.

Dense, white, cottony to powdery mycelium radiates across a brown, wavy, crinkled surface. The thick mat has a fibrous, granular texture and irregular margins that follow the contours of the underlying tissue.

Slender, black, club-shaped fruiting bodies with a slightly swollen, rounded apex and a cylindrical, minutely rough or setose stipe. One specimen is attached to soil and moss, the other is separated, both small and slightly curved.

Numerous irregular, pale cream to off-white pustules densely scattered across the green leaf surface. The pustules are slightly raised, granular, and powdery, with some showing central openings or ruptures. Leaf veins are clearly visible among the patchy, crustose formations.

Dense, white, cottony or fuzzy growth overlays a darker, convoluted surface. The fine, filamentous texture creates a soft, powdery appearance, with irregular, diffuse margins and some brownish and pale areas beneath the overgrowth.

Numerous green leaves display irregular, diffuse white powdery patches on their surfaces. The coating appears fine and evenly spread, giving the leaves a slightly dusty look. Some leaves show yellowing and minor dark spots, but the powdery layer is the most prominent feature.

Two small, bright orange, disc-shaped bodies with a distinct fringe of fine, hair-like structures around the edges. The surface is matte and finely textured, and the discs are closely set and partially embedded in a moist, earthy matrix.

Elongated green leaves with distinct yellow-orange spots and patches, mainly along the margins and tips. Some areas show diffuse discoloration and subtle raised lesions, contrasting with the healthy green tissue.

Slender, black, club-shaped fruiting bodies with elongated, slightly flattened or grooved heads tapering smoothly into thin cylindrical stipes. Surfaces appear matte to slightly velvety, and the heads blend seamlessly into the stipes. Bases show attached soil and fine rootlets.

Delicate mushrooms with slender, whitish stems and thin, pleated caps. Caps are grayish-brown with a darker central disc, showing pronounced radial grooves. Fruiting bodies range from conical in youth to broadly expanded when mature, with a translucent, fragile appearance.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat brown caps, slightly darker at the center, and a matte, finely fibrillose surface. Pale, crowded gills are visible on upturned specimens. Slender, smooth, white to pale stipes complete their delicate appearance.

Irregular, patchy colonies with a granular to slightly foliose texture and pale greenish-gray color, tightly attached to the wood. Margins are diffuse, blending into the substrate, with no prominent upright structures or visible fruiting bodies.

Two mushrooms with convex, light brown caps featuring slightly darker centers and finely textured surfaces. The smooth, slender stems are pale brown to off-white, and the caps have even, dry margins. No rings or volvas are visible.

Tall, slender stem with a fibrous texture supports a broad, flat brown cap featuring a slightly darker center. Even cap margin and prominent, radiating gills are visible beneath. The specimen stands solitary with a straight stem and fully expanded cap.

Small, pale grayish to whitish mushrooms with deeply grooved, bell-shaped caps and slender white stems. Fruiting bodies cluster in crevices of decaying wood, with some button-like immature forms and others fully expanded. Moss surrounds the base.
Bright orange, circular, flattened discs with smooth, moist surfaces and a distinct fringe of fine, dark, hair-like structures around the edges. Fruiting bodies are clustered closely together.

Dense, irregular mats of white, cottony mycelium form thick, fluffy, fibrous patches over a dark brown, convoluted, lobed surface. The white growth adheres closely, filling crevices and creating a striking contrast with the underlying undulating substrate.
No visible fungal structures are present; only a tall plant with deeply lobed green leaves and clusters of pale, fluffy seed heads is seen.

Patchy, greenish-gray crust tightly appressed to rough wood, forming irregular, granular to finely scaly areas with a mottled, uneven distribution. No distinct upright structures are visible; the lichen blends seamlessly with the wood’s fissures and grain.

Dense, carpet-like mat of small, scale-like structures in greenish-yellow to light brown hues. The surface is intricately granular, with tightly clustered, overlapping squamules forming a continuous, compact texture. No distinct reproductive structures are visible.
Single mushroom with a broad, nearly flat off-white cap, closely spaced pale gills, and a thick, fibrous stem featuring a prominent ring. The stem base is covered in soil and root debris.

Leaf surface densely covered with minute, irregular brownish spots and speckles, forming scattered aggregations. The lesions are small and unevenly distributed, giving the leaf a mottled appearance. Leaf margin is serrated with fine hairs visible along the edges.

Scattered, irregular brown lesions or pustules on a green surface, each spot slightly sunken with diffuse margins and surrounded by a granular, glistening texture. The brown areas vary in size and do not merge together.

Dense, greenish-gray, granular mat tightly appressed to the surface, forming irregular, crust-like patches with a finely roughened, powdery texture and slight surface elevations. No upright structures or distinct reproductive bodies are visible.

Slender, upright blackish stalks topped with small, rounded, granular brownish heads. Stalks are smooth, sometimes slightly curved, and spaced apart on a pale, crystalline-looking surface. Fruiting bodies are minute and solitary or occasionally paired.

A dense, white, cottony mass with a granular, uneven surface envelops the body of a spider, obscuring its features. The compact fungal growth stands out against the brownish background, displaying a spongy, crust-like texture.

Slender, elongated orange-brown stem with a slightly fibrous texture supports a broadly convex, light orange cap. The cap margin is wavy and irregular, with attached orange gills visible underneath. The overall stature is delicate and solitary.

Dense cluster of pale tan to cream mushrooms with broadly convex to slightly depressed, smooth caps and inrolled to wavy margins. Crowded, pale gills are visible on upturned specimens. Cylindrical, white to pale stems emerge from the grass at the tree base.

Irregular, spreading patches of white, cottony to web-like growth tightly appressed to the surface. The texture appears fibrous or powdery, with uneven, slightly raised margins and no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Clustered fruiting bodies with smooth, pale off-white to light tan convex caps and slightly wavy edges. Well-developed, closely spaced gills run down the short, mostly hidden stems. Mushrooms overlap in a shelf-like arrangement along a vertical split in the wood.

A diffuse, whitish, powdery coating covers patches of the green leaf, giving it a fine, granular texture. The fungal growth appears patchy and lacks visible fruiting bodies, blending subtly with the leaf’s surface.
A compact, white, irregularly rounded mass with a granular to warty texture and lobed outline, densely covering the dorsal surface of a brown spider.

Numerous small, irregular yellow and orange-brown spots scattered along the leaf veins, some coalescing into larger patches. The affected areas are slightly raised and rough, with diffuse margins and surrounding yellowed tissue.

A solitary, slender, dark stalk rises vertically, topped with a rounded, olive-brown to dark brown head. The head is distinctly granular or powdery, with irregular margins. The minute structure appears delicate, and the stalk surface is smooth to slightly roughened.

Dense, irregular white cottony patches with a soft, fluffy texture cover the leaf surface, often following the veins. The patches are granular or filamentous, with diffuse, poorly defined margins, and appear to erupt through the leaf tissue.

Clustered mushrooms with pale cream to light tan, broadly convex to flat caps, dry and finely textured surfaces, and slightly undulating margins. Long, white, slightly curved fibrous stems and crowded, pale gills are visible on upturned fruiting bodies.

Dense, muted green mat with a granular, crustose to squamulose texture. Surface is uneven, featuring small, irregular squamules and a powdery appearance, closely appressed and spreading in patchy, irregular patterns across the wood.

A tightly packed, crust-like surface of pale gray to off-white, composed of small, rounded to irregular polygonal areoles. The texture is granular and uneven, with scattered tiny disc-like structures and indistinct margins blending into the background.

Irregular, elongated dark brown to black mass composed of tightly packed, pebble-like structures. The surface is rough, granular, and crustose, lacking visible stalks or distinct shapes, and is directly attached to a green plant stem.

Numerous tiny yellowish to brownish spots and clusters scattered across the green leaf surface, some slightly raised with a granular or powdery texture, creating patchy and irregular aggregations distinct from the leaf’s fine, velvety appearance.

Brownish surface densely dotted with numerous minute, dark, rounded to slightly irregular bumps. The dark structures are scattered but evenly distributed, contrasting with the lighter, dry, and subtly textured background.

Numerous tiny, black, rounded fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across the surface, each slightly raised with a matte to subtly shiny texture. The fruiting bodies are minute and discrete, contrasting against the mottled brown and greenish background.

A small, irregularly shaped whitish mass with a granular or powdery surface tightly envelops part of a spider’s body. The fungus appears compact and closely attached, with no distinct reproductive structures visible.

Numerous irregular, raised, whitish to cream pustules with a granular, slightly fuzzy texture are scattered unevenly across the green leaf surface. The pustules vary in size and shape, with rounded to angular outlines, standing out against the healthy green background.

Dark, nearly black fruiting bodies with tongue- to club-shaped forms, some with flattened or lobed tips. Surfaces appear smooth to slightly roughened, and slender stipes are visible, one with attached root material. Each specimen measures a few centimeters long.

A single mushroom with a convex, reddish-brown cap featuring fine striations at the margin and a dry, matte surface. The slender, pale stipe is slightly curved and smooth, with soil clinging to its base.

Tiny, scattered, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with yellowish to brownish tones, finely granular surfaces, and translucent edges. Some appear slightly irregular or flattened, with a subtle color gradient from yellow margins to browner centers.

A fine, powdery, whitish coating forms a diffuse, mealy layer across the green leaf surface. The fungal growth is subtle and even, lacking dense patches or visible fruiting bodies, with a few scattered brownish spots present.

Dense, intricate mat of delicate, feathery mycelium with numerous thin, thread-like filaments. The texture is soft and cotton-like, forming a complex, interwoven network. Coloration is pale, almost white, with a diffuse, fluffy, cloud-like appearance and no visible fruiting bodies.

Dense, white, cottony mat with a distinctly fuzzy, filamentous texture. The growth is irregular and layered, forming a thick, soft coating with diffuse margins that blend into the background. No visible fruiting bodies are present.

Microscopic cross-section showing a dark brown, granular outer layer encasing a lighter, fibrous interior. Several round air bubbles are present around the section, highlighting the contrast between the dense margin and the paler, textured core.

Patchy, greenish thallus with a granular to slightly foliose texture, interspersed with blue-green, lobed patches. The surface is uneven, with small rounded lobes and granular areas forming an irregular mosaic across the bark.

Three mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped caps, pale grayish to off-white and smooth. Gills are free, pinkish, and crowded. Stems are slender, white, and smooth, with a volva visible at the base. Soil and leaf debris cling to the bases.

Elongated, cylindrical, dark brown to nearly black structures with a moist, glistening surface cluster irregularly on a woody twig. The margins are uneven, and the fungal bodies are directly attached, forming scattered to grouped patches.
The surface appears smooth to slightly rough with a brownish hue, scattered greenish and dark specks, and no distinct fruiting bodies or visible fungal structures.

A patchy, grayish to olive-brown roughened surface densely dotted with tiny, black, flask-shaped bumps. Numerous minute black dots mark the slightly raised fruiting bodies, giving a granular, mottled appearance across the bark.
Several small, black, rounded to slightly irregular smooth structures are scattered and partially embedded in a yellowish-brown and greenish rough substrate, viewed under magnification.

A delicate, wispy mat of fine, thread-like, hyaline to pale brownish filaments forms a loose, cobweb-like network across the woody surface. The texture appears fragile and minutely branched, with no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Small mushrooms with slender, pale brown stems and convex to slightly flattened pinkish-orange caps. The gills underneath are well-spaced, radiating outward, and pale to pinkish. Cap margins are smooth, and the surface appears faintly textured.

Numerous black, flask-shaped structures with pointed openings are densely clustered and partially embedded in the rough, woody surface. The angular to elongated bodies have slightly raised ostioles, creating a textured, scattered pattern across the bark.
A decaying tree trunk with a weathered, cracked surface and some darkened patches; no distinct rounded or cushion-shaped fungal bodies are clearly visible at this scale.
Irregular, closely appressed patches with brown surfaces and paler, whitish wavy margins. Fruiting bodies are smooth to slightly velvety, merging into larger colonies without distinct caps or stems.

Dark gray to brown, irregular patches with a rough, granular texture and small, overlapping lobes with undulate margins. The surface is matte and uneven, contrasting with bright yellow, broader-lobed patches nearby.

Bright yellow to yellow-orange caps with finely striated margins, smooth and slightly moist surfaces. Slender, elongated white to pale yellow stems. One mushroom lies on its side, revealing closely spaced, pale gills. Group scattered among dark organic debris.

A minute, dark, globose to subglobose fruiting body with a shiny, rough surface and a prominent tuft of stiff, dark hairs at the apex. The background is light and featureless, highlighting the solitary structure.

Small, bracket-like growth tightly attached to the surface, light tan to pale brown with an irregular, lobed margin. The underside features prominent, uneven, maze-like pores and a soft, fibrous texture.

Granular, uneven surface with a pale yellowish-tan background, scattered with numerous small, dark, rounded to irregular spots. The texture appears finely granular and mottled, with subtle variations in tone and no visible margin.

Dark, roughened bark with numerous small, black, globose to subglobose bumps scattered across the surface. The bumps are partially embedded, giving a granular, uneven texture. Lighter woody tissue is exposed where the bark is split.

Extensive, leathery patches with light brown to grayish tones, irregular and undulating lobed margins, and a matte to velvety surface. Reflexed edges and scattered small, round whitish structures add to the complex, uneven appearance.

Broad, irregular mat with a brown, granular to warty surface. Thallus is closely attached, uneven, and displays lobed, somewhat wrinkled margins. Small, tightly packed granules cover the surface, giving it a rough, textured appearance.

Tiny, delicate white fruiting bodies with cup-shaped to shallowly funnel-shaped caps. Prominent radiating pleats create a textured, ruffled appearance. Margins are thin and slightly undulate. The mushrooms are clustered closely together, appearing fragile against the green moss background.

Dense, contiguous thallus with a granular to minutely squamulose surface, olive-brown to grayish-green in color. Tightly appressed, uneven, and cushion-like with small rounded structures and some lobate margins at the edges.

Rounded, smooth fruiting body with a shiny, varnished appearance. Dark grayish-brown overall, covered in numerous small reddish-brown speckles. A moist, darker patch is visible on the upper surface. Margin is rounded and structure is sessile.

A sharply defined, nearly circular dark brown to black spot on a green leaf, with a small white speck at the center. The lesion contrasts distinctly with the surrounding healthy tissue, and leaf veins remain visible.

Small, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth to slightly granular yellowish to orange-brown surfaces and darker, well-defined margins. The apothecia are sessile, closely grouped, and measure a few millimeters across.

Numerous slender, erect, blackish, spine-like fruiting bodies with a glossy surface emerge singly or in small groups from a pale, rough, woody background. The sharply pointed structures contrast distinctly with the lighter substrate.

Pale tan to light brown cap with a smooth, irregular, and slightly depressed center. The surface is heavily encrusted with soil and debris, with some radial striations or cracks and a wavy, uneven margin. Stem is not visible.

Tiny, white, shell-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, slightly translucent caps and thin, delicate margins. They are laterally attached and scattered across moss and leaf litter, blending subtly with the surroundings.

Minute, dark, sharply pointed spine-like structures protrude erectly from the wood surface, scattered and rigid, contrasting against the lighter, slightly textured substrate. No rounded or colony-forming bodies are visible; only stiff, hair-like projections are present.

Medium to dark brown convex caps with a matte, fibrous surface. Cylindrical, beige stems with soil at the base. Gills are closely spaced and pale to light brown. Caps range from 4 to 7 cm wide, with even margins.

Crust-like, resupinate fruiting bodies with wavy, irregular margins. Surface is zonate, rough, and patchy, displaying pale pinkish, tan, and brown tones with darker, almost charred areas. Texture varies from smooth to granular and cracked.

Dense, intricate network of white to off-white mycelial threads forming a fuzzy, cottony, filamentous mat. The texture is web-like with a diffuse margin blending gradually into the surface. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Clustered, rounded fruiting bodies with a smooth, glossy, dark brown to nearly black surface. Sizes vary from small to medium, with the largest at the top and smaller ones below, forming a stacked, compact arrangement. Margins are rounded and regular, and the texture appears hard and polished.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, muted brown caps showing subtle fibrillose or scaly texture and lighter patches. Cap margins are uneven and slightly split. Gills are beige to light brown and moderately crowded. Slender, off-white to pale brown stems with fibrous texture and soil adherence.

Globose, cushion-shaped fruiting body with a dark, almost black, smooth and shiny surface. The exterior is mottled with small brownish speckles and has a slightly uneven texture. Margin is rounded and continuous.

A dark, nearly black, crust-like patch embedded in wood, with a rough, uneven surface and several small, rounded openings. The fungal tissue is thin, tightly adherent, and distinctly contrasts with the yellowish-brown surrounding material.
Numerous tiny, black, nearly spherical to slightly irregular fruiting bodies with a matte, fuzzy texture are scattered singly and in loose groups across a pale, striated, fibrous surface.

Small, soft, and closely appressed fruiting body with a fibrous to matted texture. Pale cream to pinkish-buff coloration, blending into reddish-brown at the margins. Irregular, uneven pore surface merges subtly with the rough bark.

Cluster of small mushrooms with convex to flattened brown caps, some with paler striate margins. Caps appear dry and fibrous. Slender, off-white to pale yellowish stems, with closely spaced pale brown gills. Soil clings to stem bases.

Two mushrooms with smooth, convex to slightly flattened grayish-brown caps and white, cylindrical stems. One shows densely packed, broad, pinkish gills underneath. Cap margins are smooth, and the overall texture is even and unadorned.

Clustered, globose to irregular fruitbodies with a dark, nearly black matte surface. The texture appears rough and firm, with some visible surface cracking. The fruitbodies are densely packed and abut each other along the wood.
Single mushroom with densely packed, pinkish-brown gills and a long, white stem thickened at the base. The cap margin is slightly wavy, and some soil clings to the lower stem.
Small, pale gray to whitish, disk- to cushion-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth to slightly wrinkled surfaces and irregular, lobed margins, closely attached in scattered groups along a dark branch.

Small, white, delicate caps with pronounced radiating pleats, mostly flat to slightly depressed centers, and gently upturned or rolled margins. The fruitbodies appear fragile, almost translucent, and are scattered in clusters without visible stems.

Three slender mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate, light to medium brown caps showing a subtle fibrillose texture. Gills are closely spaced, white to cream, and the pale, fibrous stems have soil clinging to their bases.

Clusters of small, rounded to slightly irregular black fruiting bodies with a smooth, somewhat shiny surface are scattered on the charred, cracked wood. The dense, globose structures vary in size and are grouped closely together.

Green leaves display numerous dark brown to black, irregularly shaped spots and lesions of varying size, some merging into larger patches. The spots are scattered across the leaf surfaces, creating a mottled appearance.

Dense, contiguous mat with dark olive-brown to brownish-green coloration. Surface appears irregular, granular to minutely lobed, and tightly appressed, with diffuse margins blending into the bark. No distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Dense, tangled mat of pale yellow-green, hair-like branches forming a web-like, fruticose structure. The fine, flexible segments create a delicate, lace-like appearance with smooth surfaces and even, tapering margins. No visible reproductive structures are present.

Flattened, lobed thallus with a rough, irregular surface covered in granular material. Predominantly pale grayish-brown with darker patches and greenish hints near undulate, irregular margins. Texture appears coarse and brittle, with fragmented areas.
Irregularly shaped, pale tan to yellowish mass with a rough, undulating surface and lobed, convoluted margins. The texture is uneven, featuring shallow depressions and a somewhat porous interior.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, pale cream caps showing light brown patches and adhering debris. Smooth, inrolled cap margins on younger specimens. Gills are closely spaced, pale, and decurrent. Stipes are robust, cylindrical, and pale, with soil attached.

A small, wedge-shaped fruiting body with a moist, fibrous texture and soft pinkish coloration emerges from a bark crevice. The margin is irregular and ragged, and the surface appears fleshy and pliant.
Small, rounded, dark brown to blackish fruiting bodies with smooth, subtly shiny surfaces are clustered and scattered along the charred, decaying surface of a large log.
Irregular, compact patch with gray to dark gray, lobed margins. Surface is uneven and textured, featuring numerous small, pale disk-like structures concentrated near the center.

Crust-like, irregular fruiting body with undulating, leathery surface. Colors range from pale brown to tan with whitish patches. Margin is uneven and closely attached, showing some zonation and rough texture.

Tightly clustered, wavy fruiting bodies with pale beige to light brown color and irregular, frilled margins. Surfaces appear moist and glossy, with a convoluted, lobed, and somewhat shelf-like appearance. Moss is interspersed among the layers.
A small, rounded fruiting body with a dark, smooth, glossy exterior. The cut surface reveals a shiny, black, lacquered interior with distinct concentric zones and a gelatinous texture.

Irregular, crust-like bodies with rough, zoned upper surfaces in dark brown to tan shades, some greenish patches, and pale, wavy margins. Texture appears hard and woody, with no visible stem or cap. Interior is pale and fibrous.

Small, scattered yellowish to olive discs and granular patches dot the woody surface, interspersed with numerous short, black, spine-like protrusions. The fruiting bodies are minute, discrete, and do not form a continuous mat.

Irregular, crust-like fruiting body with undulating, thin, lobed margins. Surface shows mixed brown and whitish tones, subtle zonation, and a rough, uneven texture. Firmly attached, with no visible spines, pores, or gills.

Numerous minute, dark, upright, spine-like or cylindrical fruiting bodies emerge sparsely from a pale, uneven surface. The structures vary slightly in height, have a smooth to slightly roughened texture, and stand out sharply against the background.

Grayish-green, foliose thallus with a rough, granular, and bumpy surface. Irregular, lobed margins and a compact, uneven texture. Some areas appear slightly raised and coral-like, with no visible reproductive structures.

Numerous small, bright yellow-orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, matte surfaces and slightly undulate or lobed margins, densely clustered and scattered across dark, charred debris. The apothecia are sessile and vary from round to irregularly oval in shape.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, pale cream to light brown caps, some with subtle orange tints. Smooth, moist surfaces with soil debris. Gills are closely spaced, pale, and decurrent, running down robust, pale stipes.

Two mushrooms with smooth, pale gray to grayish convex caps and white cylindrical stems. Each stem emerges from a prominent, membranous volva at the base, partially covered with soil and organic debris. Gills are not visible from this angle.

Dense, greenish-brown granular surface with numerous small, round, cup-like structures. Some blue-green, slightly upturned lobe margins are visible, and the thallus appears closely appressed with a rough, uneven texture.

Extensive, irregular, undulating shelf-like growths with wavy, frilled, and lobed margins. Surfaces are moist, rough, and uneven, colored brownish-pink to tan with darker, almost black patches. Fruiting bodies overlap in closely attached tiers, lacking distinct caps or stipes.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, dark brown, fibrous caps, some showing splitting at the edges. Gills are densely packed and pale cream, stems are cylindrical and off-white, with soil clinging to the base.

Semicircular, thin cap with a pinkish-brown to reddish, finely velvety surface, scattered dark specks, and a wavy, irregular margin. The cap appears soft, with subtle zonation and a slightly paler edge.

Numerous small, round to irregular dark brown to blackish spots with well-defined margins are scattered across the green leaf surface. The spots are slightly sunken, some with darker centers, while the surrounding tissue remains green and smooth.

Minute, dark, erect, spine-like fruiting bodies scattered sparsely, each sharply pointed and rigid with a glossy surface, protruding distinctly from a granular, greenish-brown substrate. No cushion or fuzziness is visible; the structures are well-defined and isolated.

Extensive, crust-like growth with glossy, dark brown to black central areas and pale, undulating cream margins. The surface appears moist and slightly wrinkled, forming irregular, shelf-like projections with convoluted edges. Small green moss patches are interspersed among the fungus.
Numerous hard, globose to irregularly rounded, dark brown to blackish-gray bodies clustered and scattered along the tree bark, with rough, somewhat shiny surfaces and sessile attachment.

Dark, irregular, layered growth with thin, wavy, lobed margins. Pale edges sharply contrast the moist, darker upper surface. Fruiting bodies overlap in shelf-like clusters beneath moss and melting snow.

A dense, white to off-white, fuzzy and web-like mat spreads irregularly across the surface, forming a granular, reticulate pattern with diffuse margins blending into the substrate. No fruiting bodies or sclerotia are visible.

Numerous small, pale yellow to ochre, disc-like to shallowly cup-shaped fruiting bodies with slightly raised, minutely fringed margins, densely clustered and often coalescing on a blackened, ashy substrate.

A thin, irregular patch of white to off-white crust with a granular, powdery texture spreads across dark wood. The surface is densely packed with fine granules, forming a discontinuous, amorphous layer with diffuse, uneven margins.

A single, irregular brown spot with diffuse margins and a slightly sunken appearance is visible on a smooth green leaf. The lesion is centered along a prominent vein, with surrounding tissue remaining green and healthy.

Tiny, delicate white fruiting bodies with thin, somewhat translucent caps and slightly wavy margins. The caps are smooth and attached to short, slender stems, appearing scattered and nestled among green moss. Their small size and fragile appearance stand out against the mossy background.

Delicate, white, web-like mycelial mat forming a fine, lace-like network with visible reticulation, tightly appressed to a brown, decaying leaf. The texture appears cottony to membranous, with a diffuse margin blending into the substrate.

Three tiny, delicate mushrooms with slender, translucent white stems and small, bell-shaped, slightly striated caps. The caps appear fragile and almost see-through, with a smooth texture and faint lines along the margins, emphasizing their dainty structure.

Flat, thin fruiting body with a light pinkish-brown hue. The pore surface is densely covered in small, round pores. Margin is even and slightly wavy, with a soft, velvety, spongy texture. No visible stem.
Mushroom with an upturned, pale brown cap and closely spaced, light brown gills. The cap margin is irregular and partially covered in soil. The robust stipe is also encrusted with soil.

Slender, upright, spike-like fruiting bodies emerge from the wood surface, dark and nearly black with a rough, granular texture. The pointed or slightly curved tips vary in height, and the structures are scattered across the substrate.

Several minute, dark, slender spine-like structures protrude from a moist, glistening greenish-yellow surface. The bristles are elongated, pointed, and scattered, standing out sharply against the blurred, shiny background.

Dense, white to pale tan, powdery to fuzzy mat spreading irregularly across organic material. Surface appears granular to velvety, forming patchy, crust-like areas with diffuse margins. No distinct fruiting bodies or reproductive structures are visible in this close-up view.

Irregular, spreading patches tightly appressed to the surface, with a granular to finely warted texture. Pale beige to light brown in color, the margin is diffuse and blends gradually into the substrate. The surface lacks any obvious fuzziness or distinct structures.

Dense clusters of small, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly raised margins. The surfaces are matte to subtly velvety, yellowish to orange-brown, and tightly packed, each disc just a few millimeters wide.

Dense, irregular patch with dark brown to nearly black coloration, tightly appressed to bark. Surface is granular, uneven, and powdery, with indistinct margins blending into the substrate. No visible reproductive structures.

Patchy, crust-like mycelial mat with a granular to powdery texture, predominantly off-white to pale brown. Dense, fuzzy patches are irregularly distributed, forming uneven, slightly raised areas without distinct fruiting bodies or defined margins.

Broad, convex to flattened cap with dark brown to grayish-brown striate surface and irregular white patches. Densely packed, pale gills are free from the slender, off-white, slightly curved stem, which ends in a bulbous base with volva remnants.

Cylindrical structure with yellowish-brown to olive coloration, uneven granular surface, and numerous scattered dark spine-like protrusions extending outward. Some areas appear moist, and the spines create a distinctive roughened texture against a plain white background.

Several slender, dark, upright cylindrical structures emerge from the surface, each with a slightly pointed or rounded tip bearing a pale or whitish apex. The fruiting bodies are scattered and vertically oriented, standing out against a blurred background.

A thin, patchy layer of white to off-white, finely granular to powdery growth spreads irregularly across dark wood, forming a diffuse, crust-like mat with uneven, gradually blending margins. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Dark, nearly black, globose to subglobose bodies with a matte, rough, and cracked or pitted surface. Fruiting bodies are clustered and solitary, emerging directly from charred wood, lacking any visible gloss or wetness.

Four mushrooms with convex to flat, wavy-margined caps in light to medium brown, showing a fibrillose to scaly texture. Cylindrical, pale stipes with soil at the base and crowded, pale brown gills beneath the caps.

Numerous tiny, round to slightly irregular, yellowish-white to cream, smooth and somewhat glossy fruiting bodies scattered across dark decaying wood. The soft, gelatinous structures are grouped loosely and vary slightly in size, mostly just a few millimeters wide.

Numerous minute, erect, dark spine-like fruiting structures scattered sparsely in a linear arrangement along the smooth, light-colored wood surface. Each structure is slender, sharply pointed, and contrasts distinctly with the substrate.
Small, dark, nearly spherical to slightly flattened bodies with prominent, stiff, dark hairs radiating from their rough surfaces, scattered across a pale, moist-looking background.

Dense, contiguous mat of small, rounded to irregular lobes forming a crust-like surface. The texture is granular to finely roughened, colored olive-green to brownish-green, with irregular margins blending into the substrate. No upright or bushy structures are visible.

Two tiny, pale cream to white, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces and even margins, attached directly to a dark, ridged, glossy substrate. The delicate cups are sparsely distributed and appear fragile.
Several minute, dark, brush-like tufts are clustered near the joint of an insect leg, appearing as tiny, irregular, spiky projections attached to the exoskeleton.

Large, roughly circular fruiting body with a dry, cracked, pale to light brown surface. Finely porous texture is visible, with some areas covered by leaf litter and debris. Margin is even and not prominently curled.

Dense clusters of small, irregularly rounded to lobed bodies form a continuous, pale yellow to ochre surface. The texture is granular and matte, with indistinct margins merging together. No stalks or prominent structures are visible.

Sectioned ovoid structure with a pale, fibrous outer layer and a densely packed, granular, purplish-brown powdery interior. The exposed surface is uneven, showing fine particulate texture and some debris.
Heart-shaped, light brown cap with a rough, fibrous surface and uneven margin. Prominent radial cracks are visible, giving the cap a split appearance.
Dark brown to black, irregularly rounded truffle-like bodies with a rough, warty surface, held in the person's hand. The texture appears firm and knobby, with uneven contours and a compact form.

Green, deeply lobed leaves display numerous small, dark brown to blackish, slightly raised spots scattered irregularly across the surfaces. The spots are discrete and contrast with the otherwise smooth, healthy-looking leaf tissue.
Irregularly shaped, dark brown bodies with a rough, deeply cracked, warty surface. One specimen is cut open, revealing a marbled interior with a network of lighter and darker veins.

A compact, dark, fuzzy central mass with several slender, translucent stalks, each topped by a small, greenish, globular head. The surface appears hairy, and the globular heads vary slightly in size and color intensity.
Irregular, dark brown to nearly black powdery mass with a rough, crumbly texture sits at the tip of a smooth green fruit, sharply contrasting in color and texture.

A tight cluster of minute, rounded fruiting bodies with vivid orange-red coloration and a rough, pebbly surface. The surfaces are dusted with yellowish to orange granular material, and the margins are smooth and well-defined.
A dense, white, thread-like mycelial network forms a fine, cobweb-like pattern across a green surface, with scattered small, dark, spherical structures embedded within the mat.
A single, slender, translucent stalk with a slight swelling near the tip, ending in a cluster of small, rounded, clear spore-like bodies.

Small mushrooms with convex, pinkish-orange caps showing striate margins. Gills are pale and well-developed, radiating from a slender, finely textured stipe that fades from light at the top to darker brown at the base.

Clusters of dark, nearly black, globose to subglobose structures embedded in a pale, fibrous, matted substrate. Smooth-surfaced fruiting bodies are scattered and partially immersed, interwoven with white, thread-like mycelium. The overall texture is dense and cottony with contrasting dark and light elements.

Broad, grayish to light brown caps with a velvety texture and irregular, wavy margins. Pale gray, closely spaced gills are visible beneath. Slender, elongated stems support the caps above moss and leafy ground cover.
Sturdy mushroom with a thick, pale stem and a convex, light brown cap showing darker spots and a slightly moist surface. The cap margin is smooth, and some soil and debris adhere to the stem.

Slender, elongated stems with small, conical to convex caps in pale to orange-brown hues. Caps have slightly wavy margins and fine radial striations. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath some caps. Bases show attached soil and green moss. Mushrooms reach about 2 inches tall.

Medium-sized mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, rich brown caps featuring a lighter central disc and finely fibrillose surface. Gills are closely spaced and brownish. Stems are slender, pale to light brown with longitudinal fibrils and white mycelial remnants at the base.
Two mushrooms with smooth, light brown convex caps; one intact with a straight, pale stem, the other cap flattened and marked by two prominent holes. Both rest among dense, brown fallen leaves.
Small, black, rounded bumps with a rough, granular texture are scattered irregularly across a smooth, greenish-gray surface, forming wart-like projections that contrast with the background.

Leaves show irregular, patchy yellow discoloration along veins and between leaflets. The yellowing is diffuse, lacking sharply defined spots or visible pustules. Leaf surfaces appear smooth, with the discoloration as the most prominent feature.

Convex to slightly flattened caps in pale cream to light tan with subtle brown mottling and scattered dark specks. Smooth, moist surfaces. White, broad, widely spaced gills run slightly down the smooth, cylindrical white stipes. Varying sizes, some with soil at the base.

Numerous green leaves display a thin, whitish, powdery coating on their upper surfaces, forming irregular, diffuse patches that give the foliage a dull, frosted appearance. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.
Irregular, warty, and lobed dark brown bodies with a rough texture. One specimen is cut open, revealing a firm, marbled interior with intricate white veins against a pale to light brown background.

A tiny, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, pale yellow, slightly translucent surface. The margin is gently flared and even, and the fungus appears delicate and diminutive, accentuated by the close-up view.

Numerous tiny, yellow, disc- to shallow cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded to slightly irregular margins. Surfaces appear smooth and somewhat translucent, scattered singly and in small groups across decomposing leaf and needle litter. No visible stipes.

Bluish-gray, slimy caps with a prominent rusty-brown center. Pale lilac, closely spaced gills beneath. Slender, smooth white stem with faint bluish tinges. Caps are convex to slightly depressed, surface moist and glossy.

Four slender mushrooms with elongated, pale stems and conical to bell-shaped caps. The caps are light brownish to tan, fading toward the edge, with faint grooves and slightly uneven, scalloped margins. Soil clings to the stem bases. Caps appear smooth to slightly fibrous.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate, light to medium brown caps featuring a matte, fibrous texture and inrolled margins. Stems are elongated, slender, whitish to pale brown with longitudinal fibrils and minor brownish stains, bases showing soil remnants.

Greenish-brown, slimy mass with numerous slender white to yellow stalks, each topped by a bright yellow, powdery spherical head. The vivid yellow structures contrast sharply with the dark, mucilaginous base, creating a scattered, irregular arrangement.
Numerous dark, oval to slightly elongated, raised structures densely cover a pale tan cylindrical stem, forming irregular rows and giving the surface a rough, textured appearance.

White to cream mushrooms with smooth, moist, convex to slightly depressed caps. Gills are white, closely spaced, and run down thick, fibrous white stems. Some caps show faint beige discoloration and are partially covered by brown leaf litter.

Dense, crust-like surface with a granular, uneven texture. Predominantly gray with a subtle greenish tint, covered in minute, rounded granules that create a rough, bumpy appearance. No visible margins or distinct reproductive structures.

Dome-shaped, darkly pigmented structure embedded within layered plant tissue, displaying a smooth, curved outline and compact form. Some greenish material is present nearby, and the fungal body is integrated within the host tissue, lacking external ornamentation.

Small, irregular, ear-shaped fruiting bodies with dark gray to nearly black, velvety caps and paler margins. White to cream gills are closely spaced and run down the short lateral attachment. Clustered in a shelf-like arrangement with undulating, tough-looking edges.

Small, cup- to shell-shaped fruitbodies with dark, rough, fibrous exteriors and pale, smooth inner surfaces. Margins are uneven and slightly curled. The fruitbodies are scattered and intermixed with yellow and white lichen patches.

Three medium-sized mushrooms with smooth, convex light to medium brown caps and slightly inrolled, irregular margins. Pale brown, closely spaced gills are visible on one specimen. Stipes are robust, white to off-white, slightly curved, with soil remnants at the base.

Crustose, pale gray surface with a cracked, granular texture and scattered small blackish dots. Irregular, brittle edges reveal an orange-brown, fibrous layer beneath, with a greenish margin at the interface.

Numerous tiny, yellow-green, spherical fruiting bodies on slender stalks emerge from a dark, moist, slimy mass. The globose structures are slightly translucent and scattered irregularly, with fine whitish threads visible among the wet, fibrous substrate.

Slender mushrooms with pale yellow-brown, convex to flat caps showing pronounced radial striations. Stems are thin and cylindrical, matching the cap color. Gills are widely spaced, pale, and clearly visible from below. The texture appears smooth and delicate.

Cluster of mushrooms with smooth, matte brown caps, some slightly depressed at the center. One upturned specimen reveals crowded, pale creamy-tan gills and a cylindrical, pale to light brown stem with a fibrous texture.

Upright, slender plant inflorescences bearing irregular, blackish-brown, granular to powdery masses along the floral axes. The dark patches contrast with remaining pale floral tissue, creating a patchy appearance on the vertical stems.

Clusters of elongated, cylindrical green structures with smooth, glossy surfaces and dark brown to blackish tips. The tips show discoloration and darkening, contrasting with the bright green tissue. The arrangement is compact, with closely packed units.

Irregular, compact clusters at stem tips, dark brown to black with interspersed pale whitish patches. The surface appears granular or powdery, with lobed, uneven shapes and some web-like material between clusters.

Dense, irregular clusters of dark brown to nearly black granular masses with a rough, lobed, and crumbly surface, borne on slender stalks. The structures appear powdery and compact, lacking distinct caps or gills.

Compact, crust-like surface densely covered with minute, rounded, pale grayish-white granules, creating a rough, powdery texture. Irregular margins blend into the background, with a patch of brownish discoloration visible in one area.
