Numerous small, rounded, dark fruiting bodies with a shiny, moist surface are scattered irregularly across a fibrous, striated brown stem. Some appear slightly sunken into the substrate.

Cluster of dark, nearly black, irregularly shaped bodies with slender, pale yellow to white rod-like projections radiating outward. Surface appears granular and compact, with fine web-like mycelial threads at the base and irregular margins.

Green, pinnately divided leaves with numerous small dark spots and prominent yellowish, elongated, blister-like swellings along veins and petioles. The swollen structures are rough and pustulate, causing leaf distortion and contrasting sharply with the green foliage.

Elongated, yellowish, slightly raised patches with numerous small, wart-like, yellowish-white sori cover the leaf surface. Scattered, round, dark brown to black spots are also present. The sori appear granular and uneven, forming linear or curved patches tightly adherent to the leaf.

Mushrooms with convex to broadly flattened, smooth, moist brown caps; cap margins slightly inrolled on younger specimens. Densely packed brown gills are visible beneath. Stems are robust, cylindrical, and pale brown to tan, with some soil at the base. Flesh is firm and pale.

Irregular, crust-like patches with a rusty reddish-brown upper surface and distinctly orange, rough, undulating margins. The texture appears granular, with lobed edges and angular fragments, each about 3–5 cm across.

The leaf surface is densely coated with a powdery, white to grayish-white, fuzzy layer that obscures much of the natural color and venation. The fungal growth appears as a continuous, fine, dust-like covering.

Convex to broadly convex caps with smooth, moist brown to grayish-brown surfaces. Gills are closely spaced, pale gray to light brown, and attached. Cylindrical, fibrous stems match cap color, with soil and organic debris at the base. Cap margins are slightly wavy.

Mushroom with a scaly, dark brown cap featuring lighter patches and an uplifted margin revealing white gills. The long, slender stem is twisted, fibrous, and transitions from pale to dark brown, ending in an irregular, bulbous base with attached debris.

Dense clusters of small, brown, spherical bodies closely packed together, each sphere covered with conspicuous, fine, white, hair-like filaments projecting outward, creating a fuzzy, textured appearance along the surface.

Small, circular to irregular brown spots scattered across a green, serrated leaf. The lesions are slightly raised, disrupting the smooth, slightly hairy surface, with some spots merging into larger patches.

Three delicate mushrooms with light brown, moist, slightly shiny caps showing striate margins. Slender, pale fibrous stems support closely spaced, pale grayish gills. The caps are convex to bell-shaped, and the overall appearance is subtle and fragile.

Small, round, dark grayish-brown discs with smooth to slightly velvety upper surfaces, each outlined by a conspicuous white, hairy margin. Fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly grouped on moist wood.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex yellow to yellow-brown caps, scattered brownish spots, and smooth surfaces. Gills are pale cream to light yellow and closely spaced. Stems are sturdy, white at the base with yellowish-brown discoloration and soil remnants.

Numerous tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across a rough surface. The discs are translucent to orange-brown, smooth, gelatinous, and circular to slightly irregular, with some more opaque and others more translucent, grouped in small clusters.

Two mushrooms with long, slender, fibrous stems that darken toward the top. Caps are convex to nearly flat, brown, and densely covered in coarse, dark scales. Gills are pale cream, broad, and free to slightly attached. Cap margins are uneven and scaly.

Tiny, white, powdery spheres perched atop slender, dark stalks, arranged in a loose row. The sporangia have a fuzzy, cottony texture and well-defined margins, standing out sharply against the red background.
A single, minute, dark green to olive ovoid structure with a granular, slightly hairy surface and a rounded apex, standing out distinctly against a blurred background.

Dense cluster of small, pale cream to white mushrooms with conical, deeply grooved caps and finely scalloped margins. Slender, off-white stems support the caps, which are tightly packed. Gills are pale and closely spaced, and the caps have a smooth, fluted texture.

Convex to slightly depressed caps with pale brown, grayish, and greenish hues, some with darker patches and irregular markings. Stout, white cylindrical stems and closely spaced cream to pale yellow gills. Cap margins are smooth to slightly wavy, with some caps showing age or damage.

Clusters of small, brownish to reddish spheres densely coated in white, fuzzy mycelium. Numerous slender, white filaments extend outward, each ending in a tiny, globose tip. The overall texture is distinctly fuzzy and compact, with intricate surface detail and delicate, thread-like outgrowths.
Numerous tiny, round, pale tan to light brown disc-like structures scattered across a plant stem, each slightly raised with smooth margins and a fine granular surface texture.

Clusters of small, dark, spherical bodies densely covered in fine, white, radiating hair-like projections, creating a distinctly fuzzy, spiky appearance. The spheres are closely grouped, each separated but forming a dense, contiguous patch with a velvety texture.

Small, round, dark brown to olive-black discs with a velvety surface and distinct pale, slightly raised margins. The fruiting bodies are sessile, tightly appressed to the wood, and vary in size, appearing solitary or in loose groups.

Small, rounded fruiting bodies densely clustered, with a velvety, hair-like surface. Light brown to tan coloration with darker mottling. One body features a slender, pale, stalk-like projection emerging from its surface.

Slender, elongated white stems with slightly bulbous bases and smooth, conical to narrowly bell-shaped pale whitish caps. Some caps show faint surface fibers. The mushrooms appear delicate and fragile, with remnants of soil on the bases.

Green leaves interspersed with yellowed ones, many showing irregular brown to black spots and sharply defined lesions. Some leaves display extensive yellowing and necrosis, with scattered dark spots across the surfaces.

Three specimens with slender, curved stems covered in patchy brown scales. The caps are convex to flat, dark brown with pronounced scales and irregular, uplifted margins. One cap is cut to show closely spaced, pale gills. Stems appear fibrous and roughened.

Small, dark olive to nearly black disc-shaped fruitbodies scattered across decaying wood. The discs are smooth, matte, and sessile, with even margins and varying in size from minute dots to larger rounded discs.

Slender, white stems support delicate, bell-shaped caps with striate margins. Caps are pale to whitish, some with a grayish tint at the apex. Several fruiting bodies show signs of self-digestion, and the mushrooms appear fragile and clustered.

Two tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with pale, irregular margins and central discs densely covered in dark purple-brown granules, giving a textured, dotted appearance. The cups are closely grouped and stand out against a fibrous background.

A compact fruiting body with a brown, textured cap covered in coarse, prominent scales and an irregular margin. The cap surface displays intricate ridges and a slightly depressed center. The lighter stem above is also adorned with scaly ornamentation.
Irregular, crust-like reddish-brown patches with a granular, uneven surface and distinct orange borders. The margins are lobed and diffuse, tightly appressed to the darkened wood substrate.

Clustered, dark brown to blackish, irregular masses line a thin stem, with numerous long, pale, thread-like filaments radiating outward. The fungal growth appears compact, granular, and rough-textured, clinging closely to the stem.
A large green leaf with a thin, diffuse, whitish powdery coating on its upper surface. The powdery layer appears patchy and lacks visible fruiting bodies, blending subtly with the leaf’s texture.

Irregular, lobed fruiting bodies with a whitish to grayish surface, darkened patches, and rough, granular texture. Margins are wavy and eroded, with pitted areas and some soil or debris adhering. Clustered growth on the forest floor.

Convex to slightly depressed yellowish caps with brownish patches, smooth surface, and adhering debris. Gills are closely spaced, yellow, and attached to robust, pale yellow cylindrical stipes. Bases show soil and organic matter.

A dark, continuous, granular to powdery coating covers the branch surface. The texture appears matte, with an irregular margin that blends into the wood. The coloration is predominantly dark brown to black, lacking distinct fruiting bodies.

Small, delicate mushrooms with slender, pale stems and smooth, light brown conical to bell-shaped caps. The caps are slightly translucent with even margins, and the fruiting bodies are upright and fragile, scattered loosely on the forest floor.

Two mushrooms with convex, smooth, moist brownish-ochre caps. Gills are pale to light brown and closely spaced. Cylindrical, slightly curved stems are whitish with brownish spots and fibrous texture, bases covered in soil and moss.

Numerous tiny, white, spherical fruiting bodies with a powdery texture are scattered irregularly, each perched atop a slender, dark stalk. The globose heads contrast sharply with the thin, dark stems, creating a delicate, scattered appearance across the moist surface.

Small, clustered fruiting bodies with granular, brownish nodules atop slender reddish-brown stalks, each cluster adorned with fine white filamentous projections. The fruiting bodies are tightly grouped and scattered across a moist, dark surface, with the white filaments contrasting sharply against the darker background.

Mushrooms with convex, medium to dark brown caps bearing patchy lighter areas and soil debris. Cap margins are slightly inrolled on younger specimens. Stems are robust and brownish, with soil clinging to the bases. Gills are pale lilac to light brown and closely spaced.

Several elongated, slender, slightly curved structures with smooth surfaces, mostly white with a faint reddish tinge, are dispersed against a dark, moist background. The unbranched, cylindrical forms have uniform thickness and rounded ends, with no visible grouping or additional structures.

Granular, uneven surface with a predominantly white to light gray coloration, scattered with darker speckles and patches. A brownish-tan area appears on the left. The texture is rough and powdery, with irregular, indistinct margins and no defined shape.

A patch of pale, angular lesions outlined by leaf veins, with numerous tiny, dark, rounded specks embedded in the tissue. The lesions are slightly lighter than the surrounding leaf, and the surface remains smooth.
Small, cup-shaped fruiting body with irregular, undulating margins. Surface is smooth, pale greenish-yellow, and appears moist and fleshy with a slightly gelatinous texture.

Slender, upright fruiting bodies with intricate, coral-like branching. Main stems are pale yellow, transitioning to translucent, whitish tips. Surfaces appear smooth and slightly glossy, with branches tapering to fine points. Bases are narrow and slightly thickened.

Irregular, pale yellowish to brownish granular patches appear within red-circled areas, contrasting with the surrounding dense clusters of small, bright yellow, cup-shaped structures on a crustose mat over a cracked, stony surface.

Numerous small, rounded, nearly black structures densely clustered together, each with a granular to slightly fuzzy surface. The fruiting bodies are compact and closely packed, interspersed with pale fragments of organic material.
Dense patches of small, rounded, greenish-yellow cup-like structures tightly clustered together, forming an irregular, leafy-textured mat with uneven, lobed margins and a granular surface.

Large, fan-shaped fruiting body with a broad, smooth, pale cream cap and slightly wavy margin. Prominent, closely spaced white gills radiate from the cap edge toward the base. The cap appears firm and fleshy, with overlapping growth and no visible stipe.

A whitish, cottony mycelial mat encircles the base of the plant stem, with a brownish lesion visible at the soil line. The affected stem appears discolored and slightly sunken, contrasting with the surrounding dark, moist soil.

Tiny, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with pale grayish to whitish discs and distinctly darker, fringed, hairy margins. The apothecia are scattered and sessile, each displaying a fuzzy edge that contrasts with the smooth inner surface.

Delicate mushrooms with slender, pale brown stems and broadly convex caps featuring a darker, central umbo. The caps are tawny to ochre, paler at the striate margin. Gills are closely spaced, pale tan, and smooth-edged. No veil remnants or ring are visible.

Two mushrooms with convex, smooth, ochre to tawny brown caps and robust, curved, off-white stems with brownish streaks. Gills are closely spaced, brownish, and attached. Cap surface is matte with an even margin.

Dense clusters of small, bright yellow to yellow-green cup-shaped structures with rounded margins, tightly packed on a granular, slightly rough surface. The cups are prominent and scattered across a similarly colored, lobed background, creating a compact, intricate pattern.

Golden-yellow surface densely covered with fine, hair-like fibers, creating a distinctly fuzzy, velvety texture. The margin is slightly undulate, and the coloration is uniform without visible scales or warts.

Small mushrooms with convex to hemispherical, smooth, light yellowish-beige caps and slender, pale stems. Some caps show finely granular surfaces. Darker gills are visible beneath a few caps. Arranged loosely in sandy soil.

A tightly-adhering, pale gray to white crust with a rough, granular texture. Numerous small, rounded, slightly raised structures dot the surface, giving it a pitted, areolate appearance. The patch has irregular margins blending into the substrate.

A small, hemispherical to nearly spherical cap with a uniform warm brown color and a fine, velvety matte surface. No stem or gills are visible, and the fruiting body emerges directly from the substrate.

Two white mushrooms with convex to nearly flat caps, slightly fibrous or scaly surfaces, and irregular margins. Caps are speckled with soil and debris. Stems are short, robust, and white, with soil clinging to the base and a faint ring zone visible on one stem.

Small, pale to whitish caps with fibrous, slightly shaggy surfaces and wavy, irregular margins. Undersides show pale, well-spaced gills attached to slender, whitish stems. Fruiting bodies are loosely grouped.

Mushrooms with ochre to tan, wavy-margined caps, some with darker patches and soil debris. Gills are pale and closely spaced. Stipe is robust, distinctly pale lilac to violet, and slightly bulbous at the base.

Dense, yellow-orange powdery patches and granular clusters cover a surface with long, fine, white hairs. The fungal growth forms irregular, rough-textured areas, with spore masses giving a distinctly granular appearance.

Pale greenish-gray, crust-like patch tightly appressed to the surface, with an irregular, cracked, and granular to minutely warty texture. Margins are diffuse and blend into the background, lacking visible fruiting bodies. Distinct from surrounding moss.

A small, solitary, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth olive-brown inner surface and a paler, slightly translucent, even margin. The cup is shallow, delicate, and has a subtle sheen, suggesting a rubbery texture. The exterior is lighter in color.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, yellowish-brown caps and finely textured, matte surfaces. Cap margins are slightly wavy. Gills are closely spaced, pale yellow-brown, and attached. Slender, brownish, slightly fibrous stems support the caps above the substrate.

Small, smooth, golden-brown caps with convex to hemispherical shapes, some slightly flattened or umbonate. Slender, pale to light brown stipes. Gills are closely spaced and brownish. Fruiting bodies are scattered in loose groups, with both mature and immature specimens visible.

Clustered, shallow to moderately deep cup-shaped fruitbodies with irregular, slightly lobed margins. Surfaces are matte, medium to dark brown, and collect sand and debris. Inner surface appears smooth, while the outer surface is subtly roughened. Cups vary in size and shape.

Dense, compact surface with uneven, rough texture. Greenish and brownish hues dominate, with minute, darkly pigmented, granular elements scattered across irregular patches. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible; granules appear rounded to irregular in shape.

Numerous tiny, pale to whitish, circular cup-like structures densely scattered on dark soil. The cups are shallow, smooth, and slightly translucent, with smooth, slightly raised margins. They vary slightly in size, mostly a few millimeters wide, and are closely packed together.

Highly magnified, irregularly contoured section with a granular, uneven margin. Muted yellowish and brownish tones dominate, and the surface appears textured. No distinct reproductive structures or clear margins are visible in this microscopic view.

Small to medium mushrooms with pale, off-white convex to bell-shaped caps, featuring a distinctly scaly or shaggy surface. Some caps appear slightly flattened or irregular, and a few slender stems are partially visible among wood chips.

Irregular, crusty patches tightly attached to the stone wall, pale gray to whitish in color, with a rough, granular texture. The patches are scattered and discontinuous, following the contours of the stone surface.

Medium-sized mushrooms with pale brown, smooth convex caps, one showing a darker center. The upturned specimen reveals crowded, white, slightly decurrent gills and a smooth, white cylindrical stem with soil at the base. Cap margin is entire and not striate.

Small, densely clustered cup-shaped bodies with conspicuous dark, hair-like fringes on the margins. Inner surfaces range from pale grayish-white to vivid orange, appearing granular or slightly glistening. Granular texture is enhanced by adhering soil particles.
Clusters of small, rounded to irregularly lobed yellow-orange nodules with a granular, rough texture are scattered across a mottled surface, forming short, uneven projections.

Clustered mushrooms with dark brown, moist, shiny caps, some broadly convex and others slightly depressed. Cap margins are smooth and inrolled in younger specimens. Gills are pale brown to ochre, moderately close, and attached. Stipes are pale, cylindrical, fibrous, with darker brown bases.

Small, black to very dark brown cup-shaped structures with minutely hairy, irregular margins. The fruiting bodies are scattered and stand out against a greenish, granular background. The inner surfaces of the cups are smooth and dark.

Small, bright orange, disc-shaped fruitbodies with smooth, moist surfaces and a dense fringe of short, fine hairs outlining the margins. The discs are round to slightly oval and closely grouped, with vivid, saturated coloration.

Dense, white, cottony to foamy mat with scattered translucent to beige globose droplets of varying sizes. Surface appears uneven and granular, with droplets irregularly distributed and some coalescing into larger beads.

Pale, powdery bands with irregular margins encircle the fly’s swollen abdomen, showing a dry, granular texture. The fungal growth is concentrated at the intersegmental membranes, giving a distended appearance while the wings and legs remain intact.

Small, bright orange, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly depressed centers and distinctly fuzzy, hairy margins. The apothecia are circular to irregular, clustered closely together, and stand out sharply against the dark, granular substrate.

Small, solitary cup-shaped fungus with smooth, pale beige to light tan surfaces inside and out. The margin is even and unlobed, and the texture appears smooth and slightly waxy. The interior is hollow and open upward.

Pale greenish-gray, crust-like patch with a dense, granular to warted surface. The thallus is compact, cracked, and areolate, forming an irregular, continuous area with rough texture and indistinct margins blending into the background.

Crustose, granular surface with tightly packed, wart-like brown projections. The texture is rough and uneven, with scattered tan and lighter granules. The surface appears matte with subtle glistening in some areas, compact and closely appressed.

Delicate, coral-like structures with slender, intricately branched arms. Pale yellow and slightly translucent, the smooth, thin branches taper to rounded or slightly pointed tips. The surface appears moist and glossy, giving a fragile, airy impression.

Delicate, highly branched, coral-like fruiting bodies with slender, upright, pale yellow to whitish branches. The texture appears smooth and fragile, with clusters scattered among herbaceous debris. No distinct cap or stem, just antler-like projections.
Granular, uneven patches with a rough, powdery texture in brown, olive, and greenish hues scattered across the surface. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible at this magnification.

Irregular, orange-brown crust-like patches with a rough texture closely adhere to the lower edge of the log, blending into the decaying wood. The fruiting bodies lack caps or stems and form a linear distribution along the underside.

Dense clusters of small, rounded to irregular, yellow-orange to brownish granular structures cover a branching surface. The texture is crustose and uneven, with some wart-like, slightly raised formations. Coloration ranges from bright yellow-orange to dull brown, contrasting against a blue background.
Two small, dark, nearly black cup-shaped bodies with rough, bristly, irregular margins. The surface appears matte to slightly shiny, and the fruiting bodies are closely grouped together.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate, greenish-brown, velvety caps. Gills are broad, pale, and frilled, radiating from smooth, pale stipes, some with slightly bulbous bases. One specimen shows upturned cap and attached soil debris.

Medium brown cap with pale, creamy radial streaks and slightly striate margin. Gills are closely spaced, tan to light brown, and attached to a slender, pale beige stem with faint brown speckling. Cap surface appears smooth to slightly fibrous.

Patchy white, cottony to fuzzy mat with scattered, tiny, pale, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies. The texture is soft and filamentous, forming irregular patches with minute fruiting bodies lacking obvious cup or gill structures.

Vivid light orange to yellowish-brown surface densely covered with small, elongated, interconnected pores forming a honeycomb pattern. The texture appears dry and spongy, with an irregular, slightly lobed margin. The fruiting body is resupinate and large, as shown by the ruler for scale.

Crust-like, yellowish to yellow-green surface with a granular to warty texture. The thallus is compact, matte, and closely attached, showing irregular cracking and an uneven, rough appearance. No distinct lobes or visible fruiting bodies.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, medium brown caps showing a subtle gradient toward the margin and a finely fibrillose surface. Stems are long, slender, mostly pale with brownish streaks and patches, and have a smooth to slightly fibrous texture.
A small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, pale off-white exterior and a darker grayish-brown inner surface. The margin is even and slightly thickened, forming a shallow, matte bowl.

Small, bright orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly glossy surfaces and rounded, raised margins. Scattered in small groups, each disc less than a centimeter wide, standing out vividly against the dark, moist soil.

Large mushrooms with convex to irregularly flattened caps, covered in rough, grayish-white scales. One specimen shows crowded, white to pale cream gills and a thick, solid white stipe, slightly bulbous at the base.

Small, slender mushrooms with smooth, conical to bell-shaped light brown caps, some showing faint grooves. Gills are closely spaced and tan, stems are long, thin, pale, and slightly curved. Clustered together.

Numerous small, circular to slightly irregular, dark brown to reddish-brown raised pustules scattered across a green leaf surface, some surrounded by faint yellowish halos. The pustules disrupt the smooth texture of the leaf.

Mushrooms with broadly convex to flat ochre-orange caps, some with darker patches and subtle zonation. Cap surfaces appear dry and slightly scaly. Gills are pale to light brown and closely spaced. Stems are robust, pale to lilac-tinged, with soil adhering at the base.

Two mushrooms with smooth, moist yellow-orange caps, some with splits exposing white gills. Densely packed brownish-purple gills are visible on one specimen, with a thick stem showing a lilac tint near the top and soil clinging to the base.

Numerous small, pale gray to whitish, cup-shaped discs with finely fringed brownish margins, densely clustered and irregularly scattered across dark soil. The inner surfaces are smooth, while the edges appear distinctly hairy. No visible stipes are present.

Tiny, cup-shaped fruitbodies with pale, smooth interiors and distinctly dark, rough, hairy outer margins. The cups are only a few millimeters wide and scattered across the surface, with a strong contrast between the whitish disc and nearly black, textured rim.

Dense, dark brown crust with a rough, granular surface composed of tiny, wart-like structures. The texture appears matte and dry, spreading irregularly without distinct margins or visible reproductive bodies.

Two slender mushrooms with white, convex to bell-shaped caps featuring fine, powdery or slightly scaly surfaces and faintly striate margins. Stems are smooth, white, and slightly swollen at the base, with remnants of substrate attached.

A thin, white, crust-like layer tightly covering the surface, with a powdery to fuzzy texture. The surface is irregular and scattered with tiny black specks. The margin is diffuse, blending gradually into the underlying material.

Three nearly spherical, dark fruiting bodies with a powdery white coating on their upper surfaces, clustered together on a piece of plant material. The surfaces appear matte and dry, with well-defined margins.

Cream to pale tan caps with broad, irregular, wavy margins and slightly fibrous surfaces. White, widely spaced gills and robust, slightly curved stipes. One cap is shown from above, the other from below, both surrounded by brown leaves.

Extensive, crust-like fruiting body tightly attached to wood, with an irregular, undulating surface. Rusty orange to ochre in color, featuring darker patches and a granular, rough texture. Margins are diffuse and blend into the substrate.
A thin, continuous, pale cream to whitish crust tightly covering the surface, with a smooth to finely granular texture and scattered embedded debris. No visible fruiting bodies or distinct margins.

A broad, orange, crust-like patch tightly adheres to the wood, with a granular to finely porous surface and uneven, slightly raised paler margins. The lower region displays a subtle labyrinthine texture.
Close-up of a crust-like surface with pale yellow to off-white, granular to warted texture. The surface appears cracked in places, with compact, uneven granules forming a rough, powdery appearance.

Thick, white, fuzzy bands encircle the insect’s abdomen, with a diffuse, powdery halo of spores radiating outward. The fungus appears as cottony growths, sharply contrasting with the insect’s natural coloration and translucent wings.

Cluster of irregular, lobe-like structures with yellowish to pale ochre color, densely speckled with brownish spots. Surface appears granular, uneven, and convoluted, resembling a brain-like texture. Compact grouping highlights rough, bumpy details.

Dense, continuous mat of small, rounded to angular white-gray areoles, each with a central depression. Surface appears pitted and cracked, with slightly raised margins on each areole, forming a tightly adherent, textured layer.

White mushrooms with slender stems and convex to flat caps, some with uplifted or split margins. Caps have a subtle brownish center and a dry, slightly scaly surface. Gills are white and crowded, and soil clings to the stem bases.

Two small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with thin, undulating, irregularly lobed margins and smooth, light brown to olive-brown surfaces. The inner surface appears slightly darker and moist, with scattered soil particles adhering. No stem is visible; the fungi are directly attached to the ground.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, pale to whitish interiors and distinct, short, brown, hairy margins. The margins are densely fringed with fine brown hairs, giving a fuzzy appearance. Cups are closely grouped and slightly irregular in outline.

Numerous small, scattered, raised brown pustules with a granular or powdery texture dot the green leaf surface. The pustules are rounded to slightly irregular and distributed irregularly, with surrounding leaf tissue appearing healthy.

Slender mushrooms with smooth, conical to bell-shaped cinnamon-brown caps and finely striate, paler margins. Stems are thin and light brown, with fruiting bodies clustered together. Caps appear moist and gills are not visible from this angle.

Dense clusters of small, rounded to irregular yellow and yellow-green structures tightly appressed, forming a granular to warted, patchy mat with indistinct margins blending into the surface. Some areas appear slightly powdery or roughened.
Pale, convex cap with a faint brownish tinge and smooth surface, supported by a thick, white stem that tapers upward. The base is bulbous, coated with soil, and shows a partial veil remnant.

Large, overlapping caps with smooth, pale tan to light brown surfaces and slightly undulating margins. Prominent, closely spaced gills radiate from a short, off-center stipe. The fungi form a shelf-like, layered cluster emerging from a tree trunk.

A thin, continuous, finely granular to powdery layer with a whitish to pale gray color, evenly covering the surface. The texture appears delicate and uniform, with no distinct fruiting bodies or visible margins.
Dense, white, cottony mycelial growth with a fibrous texture covers the lower plant stem at the soil line, forming an irregular patch at the base.

Numerous tiny, bright orange, cup-shaped discs are scattered in loose, irregular lines across deeply cracked, grayish-brown bark. The vivid orange apothecia stand out sharply against the rough, muted background, often following the bark's fissures.
A diffuse, brownish stain with faint radiating lines on a smooth white surface, lacking visible fruiting bodies or distinct structures.

Irregular, patchy colonies with a white, powdery to slightly cottony surface. The texture appears granular and fibrous, with diffuse margins blending into the substrate. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Clustered mushrooms with convex, pale tan to light brown caps displaying a striking cracked pattern of white fissures. Caps are smooth-margined and slightly incurved, with short, thick stems attached laterally. Fruiting bodies overlap closely, showing a firm texture.

Medium brown caps with darker centers and paler, striate, irregular margins. Cap surface appears dry and fibrous. Pale cream, moderately crowded gills are visible. Off-white stems show faint striations and brownish discoloration near the base, with soil adhering to the lower portion.

Small, scattered mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, light brown to tan caps showing a slightly granular surface. Cap margins are smooth. Underside reveals pale brown, moderately close gills. Stems are short, slender, and pale, partially covered by sand.

Small, bright orange, circular to slightly irregular discs scattered across a rough, cracked, white to grayish granular surface. The discs are well-defined, mostly under a millimeter wide, and often appear in loose clusters or singly.
A flat, extensive, orange crust tightly adheres to the wood, with a granular to finely warty surface and irregular, diffuse edges blending into the substrate. No cap or bracket is visible.

Irregular tan to brown necrotic lesion on a green leaf, with numerous minute black dot-like structures scattered across the surface, often aligned with veins. Lesion margins are diffuse, and the area appears slightly sunken and dry with a granular texture.

Clustered fruiting bodies with convex to inrolled caps, pale cream to light tan, fibrous and velvety surface. Gills are closely spaced, decurrent, and the robust stipe matches the cap in color and texture.

A tiny, round, purplish disc-shaped fruiting body with a finely granular surface stands out against a coarse, pale, granular background. The margin is even, and no stalk or additional structures are visible. The fruiting body appears solitary and distinctly colored.

A single, tiny, rounded fruiting body with a purplish color and scattered dark speckles on its smooth, somewhat glossy surface. It appears compact and sessile, standing out against the pale, granular background.
Numerous tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a smooth, flat, orange to reddish-orange surface and sharply defined margins are densely scattered across green moss, creating a striking contrast.

A tiny, cup-shaped fruiting body with a yellowish-orange hue and slightly textured surface, nestled among bright green, spiky moss fronds. The margin is even and the fungus appears solitary, contrasting with the surrounding foliage.

Small to medium mushrooms with convex, light brown caps showing faint radial striations and wavy margins. Pale, broad gills run slightly down slender, smooth stems that darken toward the base. Caps appear smooth to slightly velvety.

Patchy crustose surface with a mosaic of green, brown, and whitish areas, densely dotted with small, black, rounded to slightly elongated structures. The texture ranges from granular to velvety, with irregular color zone margins and unevenly clustered black fruiting bodies.

Numerous tiny, black, upright, bristle-like structures densely scattered across decaying wood. The fruiting bodies are cylindrical to clavate, rigid, and rough-textured, emerging directly from the wood’s surface and cracks. Pale patches of wood contrast with the dark fungal growth.

Irregular, closely appressed patches with a rough, fibrous surface. Pale orange to yellowish centers blend into whitish, shaggy margins. Texture appears bristly, with no visible pores or gills, forming crust-like growths on wood.

Dense, cottony white mass with a soft, fuzzy texture envelops a central form, with thin, thread-like hyphal extensions radiating outward. The structure is irregular and finely filamentous, obscuring the underlying shape.

A dense network of thin, filamentous, greenish-yellow branches radiates from a central stem. The branches are matte, slightly rough, and irregularly branched, with minute granular outgrowths and a flexible, thread-like appearance.

Small, white to grayish tuft with a cottony texture and fine, hair-like filaments radiating outward. The central mass appears dense and matted, with some granular or powdery areas. Substrate stem tissue is visible beneath the growth.

Dense, amorphous mass of whitish to pale greenish material with a fuzzy, filamentous texture. The structures appear irregular and lack sharply defined margins or visible reproductive bodies, giving a soft, indistinct appearance under high magnification.

Cylindrical cross-section showing a pale, solid central core surrounded by a thin, greenish outer layer. The margin is smooth and continuous, with clear separation between the inner and outer tissue zones.

A spider suspended in its web, completely enveloped by a dense, white, cottony and powdery coating. The fungus forms tufts and filaments radiating outward, giving the spider a distinctly fuzzy, obscured appearance.

A single, irregularly rounded cap with a reddish-brown, moist, and glistening surface. The center is slightly depressed, and the margin is smooth and subtly undulating. The cap appears slimy and viscid.
Dense cluster of slender, bright yellow stems topped with smooth, convex to bell-shaped light brown caps, some with darker centers and faint striations near the margins.

Cluster of small mushrooms with convex, light brown caps showing faint radial striations and darker centers. Margins are smooth and slightly incurved. Slender yellow stems and pale, closely spaced gills are visible on some specimens.

Clustered mushrooms with pale tan to ochre, convex to slightly flattened caps, smooth to slightly undulating margins. Gills and robust cylindrical stipes are striking violet to lilac. Some caps show subtle darker spots; gills are closely spaced and attached.

Crustose lichen forming tightly appressed, rounded to sub-circular gray to dark gray patches with cracked, areolate surfaces. The patches are closely clustered, separated by fissures, and have irregular but well-defined margins with a matte, slightly granular texture.

Numerous small, rounded to slightly irregular, dark brown to black fruiting bodies scattered and clustered on light brown, fibrous wood. The fruiting bodies have a matte to slightly rough texture and are embedded or superficially attached to the bark.

Tightly adherent, pale gray to whitish crust with a cracked, areolate surface. Numerous small, black, rounded apothecia are scattered across, slightly raised and contrasting sharply with the lighter, hard, crusty background.

Convex to nearly flat, warm brown caps with slightly upturned, irregular margins and a dry, granular surface. Light brown, fibrous stems. Closely spaced ochre-brown gills visible beneath one cap. Sand particles adhere to the caps.

Dense clusters of minute, dark brown to nearly black, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with pale, slightly raised margins. The surface appears finely granular, and the apothecia are tightly packed, irregularly following the contours of the woody crevice.

Two mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, smooth pale tan to cream caps, irregularly covered in soil. The robust stipe is pale with a faint lilac tint, especially near the base. Gills are pale to light lilac. Caps lack a distinctly darker margin.

Tightly appressed, pale gray crust forming a continuous, cracked mosaic of small, angular areoles with fine dark fissures between them. The surface is matte and finely granular, with slightly darker margins outlining each areole. No visible fruiting bodies.

Tiny, rounded, cup-like fruiting bodies with smooth, orange to yellowish surfaces are scattered among dense green moss. The apothecia are sessile and less than a few millimeters wide, standing out distinctly from the moss.

Tiny, vivid orange, cup-shaped fruitbodies with finely granular surfaces and distinct central depressions are scattered among green moss leaves. The margins are even and smooth, highlighting their minute size against the moss.

Elongated, crust-like fruiting body tightly attached to the surface, pale cream to off-white with a dense, maze-like pattern of small, irregular pores. The margin is even and blends smoothly into the substrate, and the surface appears firm and slightly undulating.

Two mushrooms with smooth, brownish-red caps about 6–7 cm wide, lighter at the margin. Gills are closely spaced, white to cream, and run slightly down the sturdy, pale to light brown stipe. The white, firm flesh is visible in the cut specimen.

Tiny, vivid orange to reddish-orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered among lush green moss. The smooth, shallow cup-like surfaces have even, regular margins and are minute in size, standing out against the mossy background.

Two large mushrooms, one showing crowded white to cream gills and a thick, soil-covered stem, the other with a pale, tan, convex cap mottled with brown patches, irregular margins, and exposed white flesh. Cap surfaces appear dry and roughened by debris.
A single mushroom with a light brown, shiny, and slimy cap. The cap is broadly rounded with a central depression and a smooth, slightly inrolled margin. No gills or stipe are visible from this angle.
Crustose, greenish-gray surface with a rough, cracked texture. Scattered small, round, pale disks with slightly raised margins and lighter centers are visible across the granular, patchy thallus.

Small, pale ochre to light brown mushrooms with ruffled, striated cap margins and smooth, slightly translucent surfaces. Slender, cylindrical stems match the cap color. Caps show irregular edges and some soil particles. Clustered among dark soil, dry grass, and twigs.

Two mushrooms with convex, dark brown, fibrillose caps featuring pale radial striations. Gills are closely spaced and pale, stems slender, white to cream, slightly fibrous, with a subtle bulbous base and soil attached.
Tiny, dark, cup-shaped structures scattered on wood, each with a shallow, smooth surface and a distinct fringe of fine, spiny hairs around the rim, giving a bristly appearance.

Minute, black, dot-like structures densely scattered in irregular clusters across a brown, fibrous woody surface. The tiny rounded fruiting bodies create a stark contrast against the substrate, with no other visible fungal features.

Pale gray, crust-like patches tightly adhere to the stone, displaying a cracked, areolate surface. Numerous small, black, rounded dots are scattered across the thallus. Margins are irregular and blend gradually into the rock.

Delicate, slender reddish-brown stalks each support a tiny, spherical head with a pale, finely granular or powdery surface. The globose structures are scattered and elevated individually above the dark substrate.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate, light to medium brown caps and paler, striate margins. Gills are well-spaced, pale cream to light tan, and attached to slender, pale yellowish stems. Caps appear smooth and slightly moist.

A dense, white, cottony mass envelops a suspended spider, with fibrous, matted fungal growth partially covering the legs and obscuring much of the body. The texture appears soft and tangled, with no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Dense, highly branched, fruticose structure with long, slender, cylindrical filaments forming a tangled mass. Pale greenish-gray coloration with a matte, finely textured surface. Irregular branching with occasional short side-branches; no visible reproductive structures.

Numerous small, spherical bodies with a metallic purple to blue-gray sheen, each elevated on slender dark stalks. The smooth, slightly iridescent spheres are densely clustered, creating a pin-like appearance across the surface.

Solitary mushroom with a smooth, light brown cap featuring a scalloped margin and a slightly darker center. The thick, upright stem is vivid light yellow, contrasting sharply with the cap. No gills are visible from this angle.

Bright orange, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces. Margins are minutely hairy and somewhat inrolled. Multiple cups of varying sizes cluster together, their interiors smooth and vivid.

Pale gray, crust-like surface cracked into small, angular patches forming a mosaic pattern. Irregular margins blend into the background. Scattered tiny black dots are visible across the dry, rough texture.

Tiny, spherical fruiting bodies densely clustered on decaying wood, ranging from pale cream to light and dark brown. Each globose head is perched atop a slender stalk, with a smooth texture and scattered to gregarious arrangement along wood crevices.

Highly magnified view showing a pale, fibrous structure with a distinct central reddish-brown axis, surrounded by lighter, whitish to greenish tissue. The texture appears rough and irregular, with visible branching and a possible cortex.

Small, brown, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth to slightly wavy margins, each on slender, dark to pale brown stalks. Attached to dark, irregular sclerotia, the cups are smooth and range from light tan to medium brown. Specimens are scattered and diminutive in size.

Bright orange, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, moist surfaces and thin, even margins. Some cups show minor notches or irregularities along the edge. The centers are slightly depressed, and the fungi are closely clustered together.

Upright, slender, pale greenish-gray structures with a distinctly scaly surface, irregularly branched and topped with small, bright red tips. The tufts vary in height and form loose clusters emerging from the ground.

Thick, clavate stem with a yellow base and reddish upper portion, covered in fine reticulation. Cap is irregular, yellowish, and shows blue-green bruising. Pore surface is yellow, also stained blue where damaged. Texture appears velvety to slightly rough, with multiple specimens clustered together.

A single, small, globose fruiting body with a white to pale pinkish, finely powdery surface. Delicate, thread-like hyphae radiate from the base, blending into the surrounding mycelium. Margins are indistinct, giving a soft, fuzzy appearance.

Dense mat of fine, thread-like hyphae with a wispy, filamentous texture. Off-white to pale yellowish coloration, forming a delicate, tangled, and fuzzy network. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible in this highly magnified view.

Crusty, tightly appressed patch with a finely cracked, areolate surface. Predominantly gray with subtle brown and pale undertones, matte and slightly granular. Irregular but sometimes well-defined margins, lacking visible fruiting bodies.

Small, clustered mushrooms with pale tan to ochre, convex caps featuring striate and scalloped margins. Slender, yellowish stipes support the caps. Some caps have soil particles adhering to their smooth surfaces. Gills are not visible in this view.

Crustose patch with a cracked, mosaic-like surface, displaying pale gray, white, and rusty-brown tones. Numerous small, black, rounded spots cluster centrally. The irregular margins blend into the background, and the texture is tightly adherent and areolate.

Dense, bushy tuft of finely branched, thread-like filaments forming an intricate, tangled mass. The color is greenish-gray with a matte, finely textured surface. The base shows attachment to a small piece of bark, and no visible reproductive structures are present.

Medium to dark brown caps with a moist, fibrillose surface and uneven, slightly split margins. Gills are closely spaced, pale to light brown, and attached to off-white, fibrous stipes with soil at the base.

Three mushrooms with reddish-brown to yellowish velvety caps, thick stems showing yellow bases and reddish upper parts with a net-like pattern, yellow pores, and vivid blue staining on cut or bruised areas.

Slender, pale greenish-grey cylindrical branches with a rough, matte surface. The branches are irregularly contorted, segmented in appearance, and loosely branched, with tips that are slightly pointed or curved.

Numerous small, black, upright fruiting bodies densely clustered on a light brown woody surface. The structures are slender, cylindrical, somewhat hair-like, with some slightly bulbous bases and a rough, textured surface. They are irregularly grouped and project vertically from the substrate.

Small, spherical fruiting bodies with a granular surface and striking metallic iridescence in blue, purple, and pink hues. Each is perched on a slender, dark stalk, with some showing split or open tops revealing inner contents. Structures are minute and delicately clustered.

Dense white, cottony mat with numerous slender, upright black projections emerging irregularly. The black structures are elongated and slightly curved, contrasting sharply against the pale, filamentous background. Surface appears matted and textured with fine, fuzzy filaments.
Two slender, reddish-brown stalks each support a single, round sporangium with a sparkling, silvery surface and smooth, well-defined margins. The fruiting bodies are spaced apart and appear delicate.

Broad, slightly inrolled cap margin with beige to light brown and pinkish hues. Closely spaced, smooth, decurrent gills run partway down the robust, cylindrical stipe. Cap and stipe surfaces appear smooth and moist, with soil and moss adhering to the stipe base.

Elongated, slender structure with a rounded, bulbous base tapering to a fine point. The surface is densely covered with fine, dark, hair-like projections along its length, giving a bristly appearance under the microscope.

Pale gray, crust-like surface cracked into small angular areoles, with scattered black, rounded fruiting bodies. Texture appears rough and granular, tightly pressed against the stone. Some areas show color changes due to chemical spot tests.

A small, vivid orange fruiting body with a cushion-like shape and distinctly granular, bumpy surface. The margin is even and well-defined, and the texture is highlighted by close proximity to green moss leaves.

Crust-like, tightly attached patches with a poroid surface, showing a gradient from pale cream at the margin to yellowish-brown centrally. The margin is irregular and diffuse, blending into the wood. No cap or stem present.
Numerous small, black, roughly oval to irregularly rounded structures with a textured surface are clustered in loose groups on a light brown, decayed woody surface.

Slender, upright, pale greenish-gray branches with a rough, granular to squamulose surface. Irregular branching and uneven, lobed outgrowths are visible along the cylindrical axes. The base is attached to a clump of soil and organic debris.

Numerous small, raised, dark gray to black pustules scattered irregularly across a yellowing, browning plant surface. The pustules are granular, rough, and often coalesce into larger clusters, rupturing the epidermis and contrasting sharply with the lighter background.

Delicate, thin reddish-brown stalks each support a single, round, grayish, powdery-looking head. The spherical heads are evenly spaced and finely textured, standing upright above a dark, moist surface.

Thick, robust stems with yellow bases and reddish upper portions. Broad, irregular caps are reddish-pink with darker mottling and bruising. Yellow pore surface shows blue-green staining, especially on the upturned specimen. Cap margin is slightly inrolled, texture velvety to rough.

A single, translucent green, leaf-like structure with a pointed tip, rounded base, and smooth margins. The surface displays a fine, reticulate network of cells and a prominent central vein. The texture appears delicate and membranous.

Small, orange-brown mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, dry, textured caps. Gills are closely spaced and pale orange to ochre, clearly visible on upturned specimens. Cylindrical stems, some partially covered with soil, and no visible ring or veil remnants.

Broadly conical to convex cap with a light brown, slightly fibrous surface. The margin is even, not striate. The white, smooth, slender stem emerges from the soil, with some soil and debris adhering at the base.

Disc-shaped fruiting body with a pale orange-peach hue, matte and slightly granular surface, dotted with small dark specks. Margin is even and the profile is gently convex, with a regular, smooth outline.
Clusters of tiny, spherical to slightly elongated fruiting bodies with a metallic blue-black, iridescent sheen, each perched on a slender dark stalk atop moist, rough, decaying wood.

Dense, tangled network of slender, cylindrical, highly branched filaments. Branches are gray-green to pale greenish, matte, and slightly roughened, with small granular or wart-like outgrowths scattered along their surfaces. No prominent reproductive structures are visible.

Thick, irregular fragments with a greenish upper layer and exposed interior showing dense, elongated, tooth-like or lamellate structures in cream to yellowish-brown hues. Texture appears tough and fibrous, with jagged, uneven cut margins.

Crust-like patches tightly adhere to the surface, displaying a maze of small, angular, interconnected pores. Color transitions from pale cream at the margin to yellowish tones centrally, with a dry, finely granular texture.

Pale gray to whitish, cracked surface forming irregular, closely packed areoles with deep fissures. Numerous small, black, rounded discs are scattered across the crust, some immersed and some slightly raised, giving a rough, mosaic-like texture.
Small, round fruiting bodies scattered on a dark surface, ranging from white to pale lilac and deep purplish-violet, each with a distinctly fuzzy or hairy texture and well-defined margins.

Small, tan to medium brown cup- and disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth to slightly granular surfaces, each borne on slender, curved stalks emerging from irregular, dark, compact bases. Margins are even and unlobed. Sizes are uniformly small, as shown by the ruler for scale.
A tiny, vivid yellow-orange globose fruiting body with a minutely granular, moist-looking surface and an uneven margin, shown perched on the tip of tweezers.

Thin, white, crust-like layer spreading in a continuous patch with a granular to minutely warty, uneven surface. No distinct margins or fruiting bodies are visible. The fungus closely adheres to the underlying surface, forming a subtle, granular texture.

Slender, elongated mushrooms with pale yellow to brownish curved stems and smooth, convex beige to pale brown caps. Well-developed, widely spaced pale gills extend down the stem. Caps have subtly darker margins. Fruiting bodies are arranged in a row with soil clinging to the bases.

Minute, upright fruiting bodies with slender reddish-brown stalks topped by globose, white heads. The heads display a distinct net-like, granular surface texture. The structures are delicate and well-separated, emerging from a flat, brownish surface.

Dense, intricately branched mass with slender, filamentous, pale greenish-white to grayish branches. Surface appears rough and fibrous, with irregular, tangled branching and no visible reproductive structures.

Tiny, bright orange-yellow cup-shaped fruiting body with a granular surface, nestled among green moss leaves. The margin is smooth and even, and the fungus is notably minute compared to the surrounding moss.

Numerous small, thin, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, dark brown to tan upper surfaces and slightly paler, even margins. The cups are scattered and clustered among decaying leaves, twigs, and moss, blending into the forest floor debris.

Numerous tiny, spherical fruiting bodies scattered across a dark, fibrous surface. They range from white to pale lilac and deep purple, with a finely textured, powdery appearance. Each sphere is well separated and arises directly from the substrate.
Irregular, lobed cap with a moist, smooth surface and brownish to reddish-brown coloration. The cap margin is uneven and slightly cracked, with most of the stem obscured by moss and grass.

Small, vibrant orange, disc-like to shallowly cup-shaped fruiting bodies with thin, slightly irregular margins and smooth surfaces. The edges appear faintly scalloped, and the fungi are scattered among dark forest floor debris.

Two nearly spherical, transparent bodies with thickened outer walls are visible alongside a single elongated, septate structure containing granular brownish material, all set against a pale blue, granular background.

Tiny, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, moist, orange to light brown surface and rounded margin, partially embedded among dense, green moss leaves. The apothecium appears slightly flattened and glistening.

Numerous tiny, pale pinkish to light brown, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and lighter, well-defined margins, densely clustered among bright green moss leaves. The apothecia are small, cup-like, and appear moist.

Numerous tiny, dark brown to black, cup-shaped structures are scattered across a rough, reddish-brown surface. The cups are minute, rounded, and somewhat embedded, with smooth margins. Greenish granular patches are interspersed among the dark fruiting bodies, adding contrast to the coarse background.

A small, pale cream fruiting body with a cup-like shape and distinctly lobed, folded margin. The surface appears finely granular or minutely fuzzy, and the outline is irregular. The fungus is closely attached and sessile.

Minute, delicate cup with an opaque white, finely granular disc. The margin is distinctly fringed with long, fine, translucent hairs, giving a feathery appearance. Several spherical droplets cling to the hairs. The short stipe is also covered in fine hairs.

Slender, elongated stipe with brownish streaks and a slightly bulbous, dirty base. Cap is pale tan to light brown, nearly flat with a smooth, darker margin. Gills are closely spaced, off-white to pale cream, and free to narrowly attached.
Numerous tiny, brown, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with distinctly hairy or fringed margins and pale, whitish inner discs, densely clustered and scattered across a moist, pale wood surface.

Bright red-orange convex cap with smooth surface, widely spaced deep red-orange gills underneath, and a slender stem fading from orange near the cap to yellow at the base. Distinctive vivid coloration and prominent gills.

Slender mushroom with a smooth stem fading from pale yellow at the base to bright orange near the cap. The underside shows densely packed, deep red gills. The surface appears moist and slightly glossy, with soil clinging to the base.

Two mushrooms with convex brown caps, slightly scaly surfaces, and inrolled margins. Stems are thick, pale with brownish scales, and bulbous at the base. The cut specimen reveals pale, closely spaced gills attached to the stem.

Single, slender, curved yellowish stipe with brownish areas and adhering soil, ending in an irregular, lobed, dark brown, granular terminal structure. Stipe is smooth and slightly shiny, transitioning from yellow to brown toward the base.

Tiny, pale yellow to yellowish-white, rounded to slightly flattened discs with smooth to finely granular surfaces, closely attached and scattered in small clusters across a dark brown leaf surface.

Slender, elongated white stems with small, conical to convex light brown caps. Caps have a distinctly velvety texture and slightly incurved margins. Fruiting bodies measure about 4 centimeters long, with some soil adhering to the base.

Small, delicate mushroom with a convex to slightly umbonate cap, light brown with a darker center. The cap surface is finely striate and granular, with a thin, striate margin. Slender, light brown stem supports the cap centrally.

Numerous tiny, black, rounded spots densely scattered across light brown, needle-like plant debris. The dark fruiting bodies are slightly raised and evenly distributed, contrasting with the smooth, tan surface of the needles.
White caps with brownish tinges and irregular, wavy margins. Smooth surface, with one upturned cap showing closely spaced, pale gills. Slender, pale stems blend into the surrounding grass and moss.

Stout mushrooms with pale brown, convex to slightly flattened caps and subtle fibrillose texture. Gills are broad, closely spaced, and pale, attached to thick, white, solid stems with slightly bulbous bases, some stained by soil.

Slender, unbranched, pink fruiting bodies with smooth, moist surfaces and rounded tips. Cylindrical and slightly curved, these fungi stand out against the green moss and grass, showing no visible branching or external reproductive structures.

Numerous small, black, nearly round to irregular fruiting bodies densely scattered and loosely clustered on a pale, veined surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised with a matte, subtly textured appearance.

Tiny, pale yellow to cream, disc-like structures with a finely granular, powdery surface. The fruiting bodies are rounded to slightly irregular, with even margins and a soft, matte texture, scattered and clustered on the substrate.

Tiny, delicate mushrooms with slender, translucent stems and conical to bell-shaped, pale brown caps. Caps show pronounced striations along the margin. Pale, widely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps. The overall texture appears smooth and fragile.

Numerous small, black, rounded fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly raised on a smooth, brown surface. The fruiting bodies are discrete, appearing embedded or superficially attached, and are arranged in a somewhat linear pattern along the margin.

Small, slender mushrooms with pale cream to light tan, convex to bell-shaped caps, some showing a subtle velvety texture. Stems are thin, white to pale brown, with soil remnants at the base. Size varies among specimens, all with delicate stature.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, light brown to tan caps featuring a finely velvety surface. Stems are sturdy and pale, with some soil attached at the base. Gills are crowded and pale brown, visible on the upturned specimen.

A single mushroom with a circular, reddish-brown cap featuring a matte to slightly velvety texture, shallow central depression, and subtle radial striations. The margin is even, and the partially visible stem is bright orange.

Small, delicate mushrooms with pale brown, radially striate caps and distinctly darker central discs. The cap margins are thin, slightly undulate, and not frilled. The mushrooms are clustered, showing a subtle gradient from the center to the edge.

Slender, cylindrical stipe with a smooth surface, showing a gradient from pale yellow at the base to orange above. The base is coated with clinging soil, and no cap or gills are visible in this close-up.

Reddish-brown to pinkish-red crust with a granular, slightly rough texture. Scattered small, irregular bumps and ridges, some with dark embedded structures in fissures. Patchy distribution, blending into the bark, with no distinct large fruiting bodies visible.

A thin, pale greenish-yellow, crust-like layer tightly adheres to the surface, forming a continuous, finely granular texture that follows the wood’s natural grain and fissures. No distinct fruiting bodies or margins are visible, giving a uniform, slightly roughened appearance.
Small, bright orange, disc-shaped fruitbodies with moist, glossy surfaces and distinctly fringed dark hairs along the margins, clustered together on a wet, fibrous substrate.

Pale, beige to light brown surface with faint, branching, hair-like filaments forming diffuse tufts. The texture appears granular and uneven, with no distinct margins or discrete fruiting bodies visible. Filamentous structures blend subtly into the background matrix.
Slender, pale brown stem supporting a small, light brown convex cap with smooth margin. Underside reveals closely spaced, pale to whitish gills. Cap and stem surfaces appear smooth and moist.

Small mushrooms with convex to hemispherical, pale tan to light brown caps showing a velvety, minutely scaly surface. Slender, white to cream stems are slightly fibrous and soil-encrusted at the base. Largest specimen is about 6 centimeters long.

Tiny, rounded, black dot-like fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across brown, leathery, overlapping leaf surfaces. The fruiting bodies are minute, slightly raised, and lack any prominent stroma or large structures.

Two small mushrooms with vibrant orange convex caps edged in red, well-spaced red-orange gills, and slender, smooth orange stems fading to yellow at the base. The surface appears moist and slightly waxy.

Two small mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened reddish-orange caps, one showing a subtle brownish center. Stems are slender and match the cap color. The upturned specimen reveals pale orange, widely spaced, thick gills. Cap surface appears dry and finely textured.

Small, white fruiting bodies with thin, irregularly shaped caps and wavy or lobed margins. Some caps show a slightly depressed center. Surfaces are smooth and uniform in color. Stems, where visible, are slender and white. Mushrooms are loosely clustered.

Small, dark, nearly black, irregularly shaped raised fruiting bodies embedded in a reddish-brown, rough, granular surface. The structures are scattered, slightly sunken, and punctate, contrasting with the surrounding bark.

Extensive, crust-like growth with a pale cream to yellowish color, irregular and porous surface, and a rough texture. The margin is diffuse and uneven, with small, rounded pores scattered across the closely appressed fruiting body.

Slender, upright, club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, brownish to yellowish surfaces. One specimen is split lengthwise, showing a solid, pale yellow interior. Surfaces appear dry and matte, with no distinct cap or helmet.

Small, dark brown to nearly black, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies with a granular texture, slightly elevated and scattered across a greenish, mossy surface. The margins are indistinct and the surface appears minutely roughened.

Circular, flat thallus with a distinct dark, scalloped margin. Surface is grayish and densely covered with small, granular or pebbly structures, giving a textured appearance. Tightly appressed to the substrate and contrasting with the lighter background.

Club-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, brown to reddish-brown heads and paler, yellowish-tan stems. The surface is moist and slightly glossy, with fibrous texture on the stem and a hollow interior visible in the fallen specimen.

Two slender mushrooms with translucent white stems and small, convex, light pinkish-beige caps. The cap margins are striate and slightly frilled, with a moist, glossy surface. Pale, well-spaced gills are visible beneath the caps.

Pale beige to tan cap surface with a moist, slightly glossy look, covered in rounded, bubble-like polygonal patterns. Scattered small fragments of organic debris rest on the thick, fleshy, smoothly curved margin.

Clusters of mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, light brown caps featuring darker centers and finely fibrillose surfaces. Slender stems are white to pale brown, with yellowish tones near the top and some soil remnants at the base.

Small, black, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a slightly shiny, granular surface and a central depression. The margins are well-defined, and the structures are closely grouped together on the substrate.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, light brown caps featuring darker, slightly scaly centers and smooth margins. One upturned specimen shows a white stem with brown speckles and crowded, dark brown gills beneath the cap.

Two mushrooms with convex, warm brown caps and slightly paler, wavy margins. Gills are closely spaced and reddish-brown. Stipes are long, slender, fibrous, and brownish with whitish mycelial remnants and soil at the base.

Small, white to pale yellow mushrooms with flat, irregularly wavy caps and undulating margins. The gills are well-developed, radiating outward and decurrent on short, slender stems. Surfaces appear smooth and slightly translucent.

Small, delicate mushrooms with pale brown to tan caps featuring pronounced radial striations and slightly scalloped margins. The gills are pale and moderately spaced, and the slender, pale stipes blend with the surrounding dried plant material.

Tiny, fragile mushrooms with thin, translucent whitish stems and small, smooth, conical to bell-shaped caps in pale brownish to tan hues. The fruiting bodies are scattered and attached to bits of dried plant material, each measuring only a few millimeters tall.

Small mushrooms with slender, pale stems and finely velvety caps ranging from conical to convex. Cap color varies from white to light brown. Gills are closely spaced and pale. Some caps show even margins. Soil clings to the stem bases.

Small, delicate mushroom with a light brown, radially striate cap that is slightly convex and darker at the center. The cap margin is straight and finely lined. The slender, pale stem is smooth and centrally attached.
