Tiny, cup-shaped fruitbodies with bright yellow-orange interiors and pale, whitish margins, clustered and scattered across dark, moist wood. The cups are delicate, dry, and have smooth to slightly fuzzy edges.
Two irregularly oval bodies, one with a light brown, rough, soil-speckled surface, the other cut open to reveal a pale, whitish, slightly marbled interior.

Numerous tiny, translucent to olive-green, disc- to button-shaped fruitbodies with a smooth, glistening, jelly-like texture are scattered irregularly across moist, decomposing material. The fruitbodies are sessile or have very short, indistinct stalks and appear soft and gelatinous.

Small, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies with a striking metallic sheen, displaying iridescent silvery to bronze hues. Surfaces are smooth and reflective, with some appearing matte or dusted. Fruiting bodies are scattered among layered organic fragments.
A small, roughly spherical truffle with a pale brown to off-white, granular and slightly rough surface, partially exposed among moist soil, dead leaves, and twigs.

Tiny, scattered fruiting bodies with slender, semi-translucent stems topped by small, smooth, white disc-like caps. Some caps appear slightly irregular or wavy at the margin, and the overall look is delicate and sparse on the wood surface.

Irregularly rounded, tuberous bodies with a pale brown to beige, slightly rough exterior dusted with soil. One is cut open, displaying a white, marbled, veined interior. Surfaces are uneven with subtle lobes and indentations.

Small, nearly spherical, dark brown to black fruiting bodies with smooth, shiny surfaces are scattered on a green background. Some display fine, radiating, hair-like appendages. The structures are loosely grouped and distinctly outlined against the surface.
A dense cluster of blue-stained, thin, filamentous hyphal threads radiates from a central mass. The hyphae appear delicate, branching, and intertwined, with no visible macroscopic structures.

Small, round, dark brown to nearly black globose structures with slightly roughened surfaces, scattered across a pale, greenish-white, powdery background. Fine, hair-like appendages radiate from each structure, giving a delicate, spiky appearance.

Dense clusters of small, round to irregular, white to light brown fruiting bodies embedded in a fuzzy, cottony mat. The surface appears granular or powdery, with closely packed structures creating a textured, uneven appearance.

Numerous tiny, translucent to whitish, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across decaying wood. The discs are smooth, glistening, and sessile, each less than a few millimeters wide, appearing in loose, irregular groups.

A tiny, translucent greenish fruiting body with a slender, cylindrical stem and a small, rounded to slightly convex cap. Both cap and stem appear granular or velvety, with delicate, subtle coloration highlighted against a blurred background.

Irregular, spreading patches with a cottony to fibrous texture; predominantly white mycelium with yellowish to cream areas at the center. Thread-like strands radiate outward from denser, crusty zones, blending diffusely into the dark wood substrate.

Small, delicate mushrooms with pale cream to off-white convex caps bearing brownish scales, especially at the center. Caps have striate margins and upturned edges revealing crowded, frilled gills. Slender, smooth, pale stems with soil at the base.

Two pale to light brown, subglobose to irregular fruiting bodies with a slightly rough, bumpy surface. The larger specimen is rounded, while the smaller is more irregular. Both are partially embedded in dark, granular soil and show some darker surface patches.

A white, crust-like patch tightly appressed to the surface, with a granular to minutely porous texture and irregular, uneven margins. Some areas show yellowish-brown discoloration, and the surface appears pitted and patchy.

A single, small, globose fruiting body with a smooth, lustrous, metallic surface. The sporocarp is reflective and uniform, attached to a brown, textured structure. No visible ornamentation or additional structures are present.

Extensive, crust-like patches with a pale cream to off-white color, closely adhering to the surface. The texture is fibrous and striate, with irregular, undulating areas and diffuse margins blending into the dark background.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate, smooth, moist brown caps darker at the center. Gills are closely spaced and pale ochre to light brown. Slender, cylindrical stems match the cap color, with some soil and moss at the base.

Numerous tiny, rounded to slightly irregular, cream-colored fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces are scattered and clustered on the dark, rough, fragmented wood. The minute apothecia are sessile and pale, standing out against the substrate.

Scattered clusters of club-shaped fruitbodies with broad, flattened tops and smooth to slightly wrinkled surfaces. Color ranges from pale tan to ochre, with a dry, fibrous texture. Bodies taper gradually toward the base, some upright, others curved or leaning.

A single, minute, spherical fruiting body with a metallic, pearly gray, slightly granular surface sits atop a short, dark, rough-textured stalk. The sporocarp subtly reflects light, giving it a faint iridescence.

Pale, off-white to light tan crust tightly attached to the surface, with a finely fuzzy, granular texture. The surface shows irregular cracks and fissures, and the margin is slightly raised, roughened, and brownish with a broken, fibrous upper edge.

A small, solitary, disc-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, matte, dark brown upper surface and an even, slightly raised margin. The fungus is sessile and directly attached to the soil, with a uniform texture and no visible reproductive structures.

Numerous tiny, black, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with matte to slightly granular surfaces are scattered in loose clusters. They are mostly circular, some with irregular or lobed margins, and sit directly on a fibrous plant stem.
A grassy field with a central path of compacted, bare soil. The grass is green and healthy, with no visible fungal growth, discoloration, or distinctive structures present.

Delicate, hair-like stalks rise upright from the surface, each topped with a small, rounded, dark head. The stalks are thin, translucent to whitish, and sparsely distributed, with a striking contrast between the pale stems and the nearly black, globose apices.

A tightly appressed, crust-like patch with a pale greenish-yellow color. The surface is granular to finely warted, showing fine fissures and an uneven texture. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible.
Narrow, elongated green leaves and stems radiate from a central point, with small pale flowers at the tips. A fine, whitish, powdery coating covers the surfaces, giving a subtle frosted appearance.

Numerous tiny, pale grayish, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with distinct fringes of fine, hair-like structures, giving a fuzzy appearance. The discs vary in size and are tightly clustered, scattered across the woody surface.

Seven small mushrooms with brown, convex to slightly flattened caps, some showing striate margins. Light brown to tan gills are visible on several specimens. Slender, fibrous brown stipes with soil and mycelium attached at the base. Sizes range from 2 to 12 centimeters.

Convex to slightly depressed light brown caps with subtle radial fibrils and inrolled margins. Creamy white, closely spaced decurrent gills are visible on the upturned specimen. Stems are pale, with some adhering debris at the base. Texture appears dry and matte.
A thin, crust-like layer tightly adheres to the wood, displaying a pale gray to whitish, finely textured, velvety surface with irregular margins. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Minute, club-shaped fruiting bodies with a golden-yellow to orange hue, dry and granular surface, and subtle iridescence. Each structure sits atop a short, slender stalk, tightly clustered and emerging from a dark substrate.
Thin, patchy crust with a granular to powdery texture, displaying rusty-brown to lighter grayish areas. The surface appears irregular, lacking distinct fruiting bodies or prominent margins.

Numerous tiny, black, spiky tufts with fine, hair-like projections radiate outward from a pale, smooth surface. The clusters are irregularly scattered, creating a punctate, bristly texture that stands out sharply against the background.

Irregular, diffuse patches of dense white powdery coating cover the upper surfaces of multiple green leaves. The powdery growth appears soft and evenly distributed, forming conspicuous, patchy areas without visible fruiting bodies.

Dark, irregular patch about 2–3 mm wide on a green leaf, with a nearly black center, lighter brown to yellowish diffuse margin, and a granular, slightly glossy surface blending into the surrounding tissue.

Small, delicate mushrooms with slender, smooth, pinkish to rosy-brown curved stems and convex to slightly depressed pale pinkish-brown caps. Gills are closely spaced, pale pinkish, and slightly decurrent. Cap margins are faintly paler, and surfaces appear finely textured and moist.

Small mushroom with a convex to nearly flat, muted brownish-pink cap featuring a slightly darker center. The margin is smooth and even. A slender, straight, pale brown stipe emerges from the soil. No gills are visible from this angle.

Tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a conspicuous fringe of fine, hair-like structures around the margin, closely grouped on a brownish surface. The texture appears delicate and slightly translucent, with the marginal hairs giving a fuzzy appearance.
White, crust-like patches with smooth to slightly uneven surfaces and thin, wavy, irregular margins. The growth is compact, closely adherent to the substrate, and lacks any distinct cap or stem.

Delicate, erect fruiting bodies with slender, dark, thread-like stalks topped by small, ovoid to teardrop-shaped, matte brown sporangia. The sporangia have a slightly granular surface and are scattered singly or in loose groups.
A tiny, vivid orange, cup-shaped structure with a smooth to minutely granular disc and a fine, whitish, slightly fuzzy margin. It sits nestled among green moss leaves and scattered mineral grains.

Small mushrooms with pinkish-brown, convex to slightly depressed caps showing faint radial striations and wavy margins. Decurrent, widely spaced pinkish gills extend down slender, smooth, off-white to pale pinkish stems. Clustered among green leaves and moss on soil.

Clustered, dark brown to blackish fruiting bodies with rough, granular surfaces. Shapes range from ovoid to subglobose, some slightly elongated or pointed at one end, closely attached to decaying wood and irregularly arranged.

Small mushrooms with convex, pale brown to tan caps covered in fine fibrils or scales. Gills are closely spaced and beige to light brown. Slender, fibrous stems are off-white to pale brown, with some darkening and soil at the base.

Three small, nearly spherical fruiting bodies with finely granular, powdery surfaces and muted olive-brown coloration. The structures are closely grouped, sessile, and slightly roughened, lacking visible stalks or prominent outer layers.
Numerous tiny, white to off-white disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and distinctly fringed, hairy margins, scattered in small clusters on a brownish background.

A single, slender, pale to light brown stalk with a fibrous texture, expanding at the apex into a funnel-shaped, disc-like top fringed with fine, hair-like projections. The base is attached to a small mass of plant debris.

Smooth, pale tan to light brown caps, some with a slight central depression, sit atop slender, off-white stems. Gills are closely spaced and pale. Caps vary from convex to nearly flat, with even margins; one cap is split, revealing the gills beneath.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, light brown caps featuring subtly darker, scalloped margins. The cap surface is dry and finely textured. Slender, pale brown stems support the caps above the soil. Multiple individuals are present at various stages of growth.

Numerous tiny, translucent to whitish, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across dark, textured wood. Each appears as a shallow, glassy cup with smooth, well-defined margins, closely appressed to the surface and lacking visible stalks.

Semicircular, overlapping fruiting bodies with pale tan to whitish, slightly velvety upper surfaces and thin, even margins. The underside features a dense, white pore layer with small, regular pores. Some light brownish zones are visible on the caps.
A fine, whitish, powdery or downy coating covers the elongated green leaves and stems of the plant, forming a subtle, even layer without distinct structures or prominent reproductive bodies.

Tiny, smooth, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a yellowish to pale orange hue and slightly translucent appearance. The apothecia are circular, sessile, and scattered, with some smaller, paler discs nearby.

Minute, urn-shaped golden-yellow structures with slender stalks, densely clustered. The tops are covered in a fine, powdery mass, with some ruptured to reveal granular contents. Surfaces appear finely granular and powdery, each sporangium standing upright and less than 1 mm tall.

Thin, white to cream fruiting body with ruffled, irregular margins and a smooth to slightly textured surface. Closely appressed to the substrate, with some white, web-like mycelial threads visible above the main structure.

Numerous tiny, pale to translucent gray disc-shaped structures with distinct circular margins are scattered and slightly clustered across the dark, fibrous, decaying stem surface, appearing flush and embedded within the substrate.

Spreading, crust-like patch with a spongy, honeycomb surface of small, irregular pores. Colors range from pale cream to ochre and light brown, with a thin, whitish margin. The fruiting body is closely appressed and uneven in texture.

A sharply defined, irregular dark patch with brownish undertones and a moist, glistening texture on the leaf surface. Fine, whitish threads are visible at the lesion’s margin, contrasting with the surrounding green tissue.
Numerous small, black, spiky tufts scattered across a pale surface. Each cluster has a dark, rounded base with fine, hair-like projections radiating outward, creating a bristly, rough texture.

Numerous tiny, circular, pale white discs with distinctly fuzzy, hair-fringed margins are scattered in loose clusters. Each fruiting body has a velvety surface and radiating fine hairs, creating a delicate, frosted appearance on the woody background.

A thin, patchy, crust-like layer with a predominantly white surface, interspersed with beige areas. The texture is distinctly fuzzy or velvety due to dense, fine, hair-like structures. The margin is irregular and diffuse, blending into the background.

Numerous tiny, black, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, matte surfaces and well-defined rims are scattered irregularly across a pale, fibrous, striated plant stem. Some cups are clustered, while others are isolated, creating a striking contrast against the background.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, pale beige caps and smooth surfaces. Gills are closely spaced and light cream, clearly visible on one specimen. Slender, cylindrical stems are off-white to pale grayish, with remnants of soil and moss at the base.

Convex to slightly depressed caps with smooth, matte, light to medium brown surfaces. Margins are entire and not wavy. Gills are white to pale cream, closely spaced, and decurrent onto slender, pale stems. Some moss adheres to the base.

Leaf surface shows extensive yellowing and brown discoloration with numerous dark, irregular spots and blotches. Lesions are flat, mottled, and follow the veins, creating a patchy pattern of necrosis and chlorosis. No visible fruiting bodies.

Slender, translucent, hair-like filaments with slightly bulbous tips rise upright from the surface. The structures are sparsely spaced, smooth, and glassy, with a pale whitish coloration. The background is blurred, highlighting the delicate, filamentous appearance.

Thin, crust-like patch with a whitish to pale gray color, featuring a powdery to granular, uneven surface. The margins are diffuse and blend gradually into the surrounding bark, lacking distinct reproductive structures.

Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat ochre-brown caps, finely fibrillose surfaces, and closely spaced yellow-brown gills. Slender, cylindrical stems match the cap color, and the caps have even, non-striate margins. Fruiting bodies are clustered together.
Dense cluster of small, cylindrical to oblong, light brown to yellowish sporangia with open, cup-like tops and a distinctly powdery texture, tightly packed and emerging from decaying wood.

A single, delicate fungus with a slender, shiny dark stalk supporting a smooth, teardrop-shaped brown sporangium. The sporangium has a subtle sheen and well-defined, smooth margins. The entire structure appears minute, upright, and fragile.

Numerous tiny, bright orange to yellow, disc-shaped structures with slightly raised, well-defined margins and a granular surface, densely clustered on a pale, granular background. The discs are closely grouped, forming a compact arrangement.

Small, delicate mushroom with a round, slightly domed cap in muted brownish-pink, featuring a subtly darker center. The cap margin is smooth and even. The slender, straight stem matches the cap’s subdued color.

Numerous small, bright orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly irregular margins are scattered among dense, spiky green and brown moss. The discs are flat to shallowly depressed and have a moist, smooth surface, standing out vividly against the moss.

Two delicate, erect fruiting bodies with slender, dark, hair-like stalks each support a single, teardrop-shaped, brownish sporangium. The sporangia have a finely granular, powdery surface and stand well-separated from each other.

Several roughly spherical to oval structures with granular, textured interiors and distinct, slightly thickened borders. The coloration is yellowish-brown to olive, and the elements are grouped closely together, sharply outlined against a blurred background.

Fine, velvety beige to light brown surface with scattered, minute dark dot-like structures irregularly distributed. Subtle greenish hues are present, and the texture appears slightly uneven with a hairy appearance.

Numerous tiny, yellow-orange to ochre disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered singly across a dark surface. The discs are smooth, flat to slightly concave, with regular margins. White, powdery patches are interspersed among the minute apothecia.
Pale greenish-white to gray, broad, curled lobes form a dense, foliose mat. The surface is uneven, with granular clusters and overlapping, radiating margins tightly attached to the substrate.

Long, narrow green leaves are coated with a dense, powdery white layer, giving a frosted appearance. The white mycelial growth is continuous and fine, most prominent on upper surfaces. Some leaves show curling and distortion.

Three mushrooms with smooth, moist, light to medium brown convex caps, white to pale cream robust stems, and dark brown, closely spaced gills. One cap shows a crack, and the stems are slightly bulbous at the base with soil attached.

Numerous small, black, bristly round clusters densely scattered on a smooth, light brown surface. Each cluster has prominent stiff, dark hair-like projections radiating outward, creating a spiky appearance and strong contrast with the background.
Numerous tiny, vivid orange, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with slightly irregular, scalloped edges are scattered in clusters among dense, spiky green and brown moss, creating a striking color contrast.

A single mushroom with a rounded, convex cap that is light brown and covered in fine, fibrous hairs, giving it a textured, fuzzy appearance. The cap margin is even and not prominently striate. The stem is mostly hidden by leaves.

Dense mat of pale gray, flattened, irregularly lobed structures with incurved margins. Surface appears uneven and granular, with some lobes showing a powdery texture. Lobes radiate outward, tightly attached to the dark stone, creating a striking contrast.
Extensive, flat white patches with smooth to slightly uneven surfaces, spreading irregularly along the surface. Some areas show thin, undulating, bracket-like margins, giving a shelf-like appearance.

Leaf surface densely coated with a white, powdery, felt-like layer. Scattered across this mat are numerous tiny, dark, spherical structures, unevenly distributed and contrasting against the pale fungal growth.

Delicate, erect sporophores with slender, dark, hair-like stalks each support a single, ovoid to teardrop-shaped, light brown sporangium. The sporangia have a smooth to slightly textured surface and appear fragile and translucent.

Small, delicate mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed pinkish-brown caps, paler whitish margins, and finely textured surfaces. Gills are widely spaced, pinkish, and radiate from slender, similarly colored fibrous stipes.

Delicate, erect fruiting bodies with slender, dark stalks tinged red at the base, each supporting an ovoid to ellipsoid, pale brown sporangium with a granular, powdery surface. Structures are spaced apart in small groups, each only a few millimeters tall.

Tiny, vivid orange cup-shaped fruiting body with a paler, slightly granular margin. The surface appears roughened, not jelly-like, and the margin is lighter in color. Nestled among green moss stems and leaves.
Small, nearly black spherical bodies with rough surfaces scattered on a white, powdery mat. Some spheres are encircled by radiating, filamentous appendages, all set against a green background.

Numerous tiny, pale whitish to light gray, translucent discs densely clustered on wood, each with a pronounced fringe of fine, hair-like structures around the margin, giving a delicate, fuzzy appearance. The surface is smooth and glassy.

Two elongated, contorted fruitbodies with a firm, convoluted white surface, deep furrows, uneven lobate margins, and some brownish discoloration. The upper specimen shows patches of greenish material. Both exceed 5 centimeters in length.

Leaves display numerous irregular, dark brown to blackish spots and blotches with yellowish halos. The lesions are scattered and sometimes merge, appearing smooth and integrated into the leaf tissue without visible fruiting bodies.

Leaves exhibit irregular, dark brown to blackish spots and blotches on a yellow-green background, with some areas showing necrotic black patches. No visible fruiting bodies; lesions are scattered across the leaf surfaces.

Slender, elongated green stems display scattered, fine whitish to grayish powdery patches along their surfaces. The powdery areas are minute and irregularly distributed, giving a subtle, slightly roughened appearance without prominent fruiting bodies.

Semicircular to fan-shaped fruiting bodies with white to light brown upper surfaces, some showing darker brown patches. Margins are thin and even, texture appears smooth to slightly velvety. Fruiting bodies are attached laterally and arranged singly or in small, overlapping clusters.

A small, dark, rounded structure with a matte, rough surface, partially embedded in a granular matrix. The margins are irregular and blend into the surrounding material, with no visible hair-like projections or distinct reproductive features.

Mushroom with a pale yellowish-brown, smooth, slightly undulating cap, grayish-brown gills, and a thick white stem featuring a distinct rusty-brown ring near the top. The base is covered with soil and plant debris.

A single, delicate fruiting body with a slender, dark, hair-like stalk topped by a smooth, brownish, ovoid sporangium. The structure stands solitary and upright, with a fragile, minimalist appearance.

Irregularly cylindrical, slightly curved structures with blunt, rounded ends. Surface is dry, matte, and finely granular, colored muted brownish-tan. Sporocarps are closely grouped and sessile, lacking visible stalks.

Leaves are coated with irregular, diffuse white powdery patches, giving them a silvery or grayish appearance. The powdery layer is most prominent on the upper surfaces, obscuring the natural green color of the elongated leaves.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a vivid orange, granular surface and a thin, pale, irregular margin. The texture appears matte and powdery, with the structure nestled among moss and plant debris.

Cluster of small, round to polygonal, yellowish-orange discs with well-defined, slightly raised margins and granular surfaces. The apothecia are tightly grouped, vivid in color, and stand out against a pale, granular background.

Numerous tiny, black, dot-like structures densely scattered across a dried, brown leaf surface, especially along the veins, creating a granular, punctate pattern that contrasts with the lighter background.

Smooth, pale tan to light brown caps with gently undulating margins, some slightly depressed in the center. Slender, white to pale brown stems and closely spaced pale gills are visible on one upturned specimen. Caps appear moist and vary in size.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, rounded fruiting bodies scattered across a pale, fibrous wood surface. The fruiting bodies are discrete or loosely grouped, matte, and slightly rough in texture, contrasting sharply with the light background.

Numerous small, sharply defined, dark brown to black spots with slightly raised, roughened texture scattered irregularly across the green leaf surface. Each spot is circular to slightly irregular, remaining discrete and not merging together.

Numerous small, dark, round to oval bodies scattered across a pale surface, each with fine, dark, hair-like setae protruding. The structures are slightly raised, giving a rough texture and contrasting sharply with the lighter background.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened ochre-brown caps, some with paler patches and subtle fibrillose texture. Stems are thick, white to cream, with brownish discoloration and soil at the base. Cut specimen reveals white flesh and pale gills darkening toward the edge.

Numerous tiny, whitish to translucent disc-like structures scattered irregularly along a dark, decaying stem. The discs are circular, slightly raised, and have a moist, gelatinous appearance with well-defined margins contrasting against the substrate.

A tightly appressed, crust-like patch with a pale whitish to light gray color and a finely granular, powdery surface. The margin is irregular and blends into the substrate, lacking prominent lobes or visible reproductive structures.

A pale, granular to powdery whitish coating covers the upper surface of a slightly curved stem. The coating appears unevenly distributed, with some areas showing denser accumulation, giving the stem a frosted appearance.

A single, delicate fungus with a long, slender, dark stalk topped by a teardrop-shaped, brownish sporangium. The sporangium has a fine, slightly granular texture and stands upright, distinctly separated from the stalk.

Mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened caps, featuring a darker brown center fading to a lighter edge and a frosted texture. Stems are slender, off-white with brownish bases. Gills are pale to pinkish-brown and moderately crowded. Cap margins are smooth and slightly incurved in younger specimens.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, pale brown caps featuring a fibrous or finely scaly texture and some darker spots. Slender, elongated stems are pale with brownish fibrils. Gills are pale tan to light brown and moderately crowded.

Three small mushrooms with pinkish-brown, smooth, moist caps—one convex, one upturned, and one flat. Caps have finely scalloped margins. Gills are broad, decurrent, and pale pinkish. Slender, cylindrical stipes match the cap color and appear slightly fibrous.

Convex, smooth caps in yellow to golden-brown with a moist, shiny surface. Stems are thick, white, and soil-stained at the base. Gills are pale lilac to purple, and cap margins are slightly inrolled and entire.

Numerous tiny, black, rounded dots scattered across a pale, fibrous wood surface. The fruiting bodies are minute and slightly raised, appearing as embedded black specks against the lighter background.
